title: js: enforce one 30-second deadline for the entire tool invocation
description:
## Observed behavior
The canonical Phase 6 contract requires one 30-second total request deadline covering authorization, queueing, startup, IPC, JavaScript, and parent effects. `JsTool::call` first performs a permission check with its own timeout, then starts a fresh skill-preparation deadline, then a fresh grant expiry. `execute_bound` enters a supervisor that starts another watchdog; the shared production watchdog is `STEP_TIMEOUT + 30s` grace. Effect services also receive fresh `STEP_TIMEOUT` durations.

## Impact
A single JS tool call can consume substantially more than 30 seconds before returning, contrary to the security invariant and user-visible “30s limit” errors. Permission/skill preparation can be used to extend resource occupancy before worker execution begins.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Delay the initial permission response near its timeout.
2. Delay skill-manifest preparation near 30 seconds.
3. Delay supervisor lease/startup/execution/effects.
4. Observe each phase receives a new budget rather than sharing an absolute deadline from tool-call entry.

## Evidence
`docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md` lines 97-104 and 113-121; `src/extras/js/tool.rs::call`; `src/extras/js/supervisor.rs::{shared,invoke_interactive}`; effect-service constructors.
design: Create one checked absolute deadline at `JsTool::call` entry. Thread that same deadline (or strictly shorter derived remaining budgets) through initial permission authorization, skill preparation, grant expiry, broker/effect services, supervisor lease/startup/IPC, and worker runtime. Add a supervisor entry point that accepts the caller deadline rather than resetting it. Distinguish semantic completion from bounded post-deadline process reaping: cleanup grace must not permit more JS/effect execution or delay the tool result under a misleading 30-second contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- One absolute 30-second deadline begins before the first permission check and governs every invocation phase.
- No permission, skill, grant, supervisor, worker, or effect path can reset or extend the semantic deadline.
- Deterministic fake-clock/short-deadline tests compose delays across phases and prove total elapsed time is bounded, including queue contention and cancellation races.
- Timeout returns the existing bounded typed diagnostic and invalidates/reaps the worker/effects according to Phase 6 invariants.
- Canonical Phase 6 tests and `cargo test` pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: btw: bound side-question concurrency, lifetime, and shutdown
description:
## Observed behavior
Every `/btw` command immediately spawns a separate up-to-eight-turn provider run. There is no in-flight cap or whole-run deadline. `App` stores Tokio join handles, but ordinary `App::teardown` does not cancel or await them; dropping a `JoinHandle` detaches the task. Explicit retirement exists only for Ctrl-C targeting `/btw` and a git-worktree cleanup path.

## Impact
Repeated side questions can create unbounded concurrent inference cost and memory/network work. Normal exit or an unrelated TUI error can leave detached runs and scoped child work alive after the owning UI is gone.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Submit many `/btw` commands quickly, including while a main run is active.
2. Observe `btw_inflight` grows without admission control and each run can retry/use multiple turns without one enclosing deadline.
3. Exit normally or force a TUI error; ordinary teardown drops the handles without `retire_scoped_task`.

## Evidence
`src/ui/app.rs::{run_btw,teardown,retire_workspace_owners_before_cleanup}`, `src/agent/builder.rs::BTW_MAX_TURNS`, and `src/agent/runner.rs::spawn_btw`.
design: Make `App` the explicit owner of a bounded `/btw` task set. Add a small configurable/default in-flight limit with reject-or-queue semantics, one absolute whole-run deadline covering retries/streaming/tool turns, and a shared retirement routine used on normal exit, every error path, workspace rebind, and explicit cancellation. Abort, close the event stream, await task completion, and wait for scoped blocking children within a bounded cleanup budget. Avoid a separate issue for theoretical `u32` wrap; allocate IDs collision-safely while touching lifecycle ownership.
acceptance_criteria:
- `/btw` cannot exceed the configured concurrent-run limit or whole-run deadline.
- Normal exit, Ctrl-C, TUI errors, terminal lifecycle errors, and workspace changes cancel and settle all owned side-question tasks and scoped children.
- No detached provider/task work or late UI events remain after teardown returns.
- Tests cover saturation, timeout across retries, cancellation races, shutdown with blocking scoped work, and ID reuse/collision behavior.
- `cargo test` passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: compaction: never delete history omitted from bounded summarizer input
description:
## Observed behavior
`bounded_recent_conversation` keeps only a bounded tail when the serialized selected prefix exceeds `conversation_budget * MAX_COMPACTION_REQUESTS`, prepending an “older history omitted” marker. Callers still invoke `Session::compress(summary, cut_idx, ...)`, which drains the entire selected prefix.

## Impact
Messages that were never sent to the summarizer are permanently deleted while the generated summary falsely stands in for them. This is silent context/data loss.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a selected compaction prefix larger than the maximum retained conversation bytes.
2. Run bounded compaction and record which source bytes/messages reach the fake summarizer.
3. Observe that only the tail is represented, while `Session::compress` removes all messages through the original `cut_idx`.

## Evidence
`src/provider.rs::bounded_recent_conversation`, `src/startup.rs::compact_headless_session_with`, `src/ui/slash/mod.rs::handle_compress`, and `src/session/mod.rs::compress`.
design: Make the bounded serializer return provenance at message boundaries: the exact first/last represented message indexes and whether any record was partially represented. Compact only a fully represented contiguous prefix. If the chosen prefix cannot fit within the bounded request count, either move the cut to the representable boundary or fail without mutation; never summarize a tail and delete its unseen prefix. Compute token savings and compaction metadata from the actual removed records.
acceptance_criteria:
- No message is removed unless its full canonical serialized representation was supplied to the successful summarizer reduction.
- Oversized selected-prefix tests prove omitted older messages remain in session or the operation fails atomically.
- Interactive, headless, manual, between-turn, and mid-turn compaction use the same represented-range contract.
- UTF-8 boundaries, message boundaries, previous summaries, token savings, and persistence metadata remain correct.
- `cargo test` passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: compaction: isolate untrusted transcript data from summarizer instructions
description:
## Observed behavior
Compaction serializes messages as raw `[Role]: content` text and interpolates that text into predictable prompt delimiters. The summarizer's operative instructions and the untrusted conversation share the same user prompt. User text and tool output can therefore emit delimiter text, fake role records, or instruction sections that are indistinguishable from host framing.

## Impact
An attacker-controlled repository/tool response can steer the rolling summary, become durable System recap state, and influence every later turn after the original evidence has been deleted.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Put compaction-template delimiters, fake `[System]` records, and instructions such as “ignore the summary contract” in a user message or tool result.
2. Trigger compaction.
3. Inspect the summarizer request: attacker text is embedded without structural escaping or a stronger instruction/data boundary.

## Evidence
`src/provider.rs::{serialize_conversation,summarize_conversation_bounded,run_summarizer}` and `src/agent/prompt.rs::COMPACTION_PROMPT`.
design: Move the immutable summarization policy/output contract into the summarizer system preamble. Encode transcript records in a structured, length-bounded form whose framing cannot be terminated or role-spoofed by content, and label all transcript/tool payloads as untrusted data. Keep previous summaries and optional user compression instructions in distinct typed sections with explicit precedence. The summary itself must distinguish reported untrusted instructions from host instructions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adversarial messages containing every delimiter, fake role labels, JSON/control characters, and prompt-injection text cannot escape their data field or alter section precedence.
- The system-level summarization contract is separate from transcript data and optional user compression guidance.
- Rolling/multi-request compaction preserves the same framing and trust labels on every request.
- Tests inspect the exact summarizer messages and cover user, tool-result, prior-summary, and instruction injection cases.
- `cargo test` passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: session: persist canonical provider interactions for resumable tool transcripts
description:
## Observed behavior
Completed runners already construct canonical `Vec<rig::completion::Message>` interactions with provider tool-call IDs, structured arguments, and paired tool results. Interactive `AgentEvent::Done` discards that vector, while the live session stores only display summaries. Headless `run_print` returns only response text and usage, so `dispatch_print` persists no tool interactions at all. On resume, `convert_history` converts persisted System/ToolCall/ToolResult/SubagentToolCall records into assistant prose.

## Impact
A continued session cannot replay the causal transcript the provider originally saw. Structured arguments and role/provenance are lost, headless tool work disappears entirely, and a model can misinterpret tool evidence as prior assistant claims.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Complete an interactive or `-p` turn that invokes one or more tools.
2. Inspect the saved session and resume it with `--continue`.
3. Observe that interactive calls are formatted summaries and resumed as assistant text; in headless mode only the user prompt and final response were persisted.

## Evidence
`src/event.rs`, `src/ui/event_handler.rs`, `src/agent/runner.rs::convert_history`, `src/session/mod.rs::{add_tool_call_with_id,add_tool_result_with_id_and_artifact}`, and `src/startup.rs::dispatch_print`.
design: Add a versioned provider-neutral interaction representation to the durable session schema. Commit completed-turn interactions transactionally on both interactive and headless paths; preserve provider call IDs, tool names, structured arguments, result role/correlation, and bounded result content. Make `convert_history` replay valid call/result pairs rather than flattening them to assistant prose. Derive UI summaries from canonical records instead of treating summaries as the source of truth. Migrate legacy sessions conservatively as explicitly marked transcript prose; never invent structured arguments or authority that were not stored.
acceptance_criteria:
- Interactive and headless tool-bearing turns persist equivalent canonical causal interactions after successful completion.
- Resume replays valid paired tool-call/tool-result messages with exact IDs, names, structured arguments, ordering, and bounded result content.
- Parallel tool calls, multiple continuation turns, cancellation/failure rollback, compaction, and long-result artifact handling have regression tests.
- Legacy sessions remain loadable without fabricating canonical tool records.
- `cargo test` passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(agent): decouple cumulative turn token budget from max_tokens response cap
description: max_tokens (default 16384; documented in CONFIG.md:338 as 'Maximum response tokens' and sent to the provider as the per-response output cap) is also enforced by exhausted_token_budget (src/agent/runner.rs:731) against usage_ledger.total — the cumulative sum of input+output tokens across every completion call in a turn (observed_tokens = max(input+output, total_tokens)). Each call's input is the full prompt, so any multi-tool-call turn on a real session exceeds 16384 cumulative after 2-3 calls and aborts with 'Agent exhausted its cumulative token budget (X/16384) before completing.' Check sites: runner.rs ~1729 (per CompletionCall), ~1801 (before continuation), ~2063, ~2137 (EOF paths). Introduced in 3a78bcd 'fix(agent): fail closed on accounting edge cases'. The error text advises 'increase max_tokens', but that also raises the per-response cap sent to the provider, which providers can reject. This is the primary cause of the observed token-limit-exhaustion failures.
acceptance_criteria: Cumulative fail-closed budget has its own knob (e.g. turn_token_budget, defaulting to a value derived from context_window, or None) and max_tokens is used only as the per-response output cap. Exhaustion error message no longer suggests raising max_tokens. Tests cover a multi-call turn whose cumulative input+output exceeds max_tokens but completes normally.
close_reason: Fixed in d18f8da: turn_token_budget knob added (default None), runner no longer reuses max_tokens as cumulative budget, message updated, regression test added.

title: R3: add a VS Code extension job to ci.yml
description:
editors/vscode/ is new in v1.8.0: ~1,320 lines of TypeScript plus a 7,774-line package-lock.json. .github/workflows/ci.yml contains zero occurrences of 'vscode', 'npm', or 'node' (verified with grep -ci).

Every check the extension has — npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test — lives in release.yml inside the vscode-vsix job (lines ~390-396), which only runs on a release. A type error or failing vitest introduced on main stays invisible until someone cuts a tag, at which point the release build is what breaks.

Coverage inside the extension is also uneven. Tests exist for chat, config, conversation, and platform. There are none for:
- src/session.ts (339 lines, the ACP session lifecycle)
- src/extension.ts (216 lines)
- src/trust.ts (104 lines, the workspace trust gate)

Findings R4, R5, and R9 are all in those three untested files.
design:
Add a 'vscode' job to ci.yml: actions/setup-node with node-version-file: editors/vscode/.nvmrc, then npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test in editors/vscode. Single ubuntu-latest runner, no Rust toolchain needed. Gate it with the same 'if' guard the other non-scheduled jobs use.

Follow-up (can be a separate issue): add unit tests for session.ts lifecycle transitions and extension.ts session management.
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript compile error or failing vitest in editors/vscode fails CI on a pull request, not only on a release tag.
close_reason: Added a pinned VS Code CI job running npm ci, typecheck, lint, tests, and high-severity audit.

title: R2: structured Git mutations advertised to model and users but not implemented
description:
docs/specs/structured-git-mutations.md is marked 'Status: accepted (2026-08-14)' and specifies stage, unstage, and commit. The permission layer implements all three verbs; the tool does not.

Shipped:
- src/permission/mod.rs:37-42 — git/stage, git/unstage, git/commit as serialized config fields
- src/permission/checker.rs:144-146 — each wired to a config lookup
- src/config/mod.rs:624-626 — each accepted as a valid verb name

Missing:
- src/git/tool.rs:20-27 — GitOperation is Status | Diff | Log | Show. No mutation variant.

The tool ships enabled by default (git-worktree is a default feature; src/agent/builder.rs:533).

Three consequences:
1. The model is told it can write. description() says 'Inspect and update the bound Git repository' and parameters() advertises "message": "Commit message for commit only" (src/git/tool.rs:365) — but operation: 'commit' fails serde deserialization on the 4-variant enum, so the model burns turns on a capability that cannot exist.
2. GitArgs.message (src/git/tool.rs:35) is never read.
3. The mutation branch of validate_paths — the symlink-operand rejection at src/git/tool.rs:145-156 — is unreachable; all three call sites (lines 232, 258, 314) pass None for permission_verb.

A user who reads the ADR and sets git/commit = 'allow' gets a silently inert setting.
design:
Pick a direction and make the surfaces agree.

Option A (narrow the contract for 1.8.0, smaller): drop 'message' from parameters() and from GitArgs; change description() to 'Inspect the bound Git repository...'; re-mark the ADR as 'proposed' rather than 'accepted'. The permission verbs may stay reserved if the ADR notes they are not yet honored. Consider #[allow] or removing the dead permission_verb parameter of validate_paths.

Option B (land the feature): implement Stage/Unstage/Commit per the ADR, using the already-present infrastructure — acquire_process_git_mutation(), LOCAL_MUTATION_LIMITS, run_with_input, and the symlink rejection branch.
acceptance_criteria: No model-facing string or JSON schema field describes a capability the enum cannot accept; docs/specs/structured-git-mutations.md status matches what ships; either the git/* mutation verbs are honored by a real code path or the ADR says they are reserved.
close_reason: Implemented contained Stage, Unstage, and Commit operations with exact permissions, validation, observed outcomes, documentation, and tests.

title: UI: incremental markdown layout for streaming agent blocks (O(n^2) -> O(n))
description:
WHAT: While an agent block streams, agent_block_lines() re-parses the ENTIRE completed prefix every time a line completes: the MdCache key is (width, parsed_len) (src/ui/feed.rs:400-446), so each newline changes parsed_len, misses the cache, and calls markdown_to_styled(&block.text[..completed_len]) on the whole prefix (feed.rs:423). event_handler.rs:98-106 triggers render_viewport on every completed line, so a long streamed response costs O(n^2) total parse work and visibly burns CPU during streaming.
HOW: Make the parse incremental. Cache laid-out lines for a stable prefix and re-parse only from the last stable markdown block boundary (NOT just the last newline — a new line can retroactively change the enclosing construct, e.g. closing a fence or continuing a list). Practical approach: track the byte offset of the last top-level block boundary that markdown parsing already finalized; on a new completed line, re-parse only text[stable_boundary..completed_len] and append, keeping the previously laid-out lines for [0..stable_boundary]. Alternatively parse per finalized markdown block and concatenate cached per-block layouts. Keep the existing plain-text tail rendering for the unfinished line (feed.rs:433-444) unchanged.
VERIFY: (1) Use the existing test-only layout_computes counter (feed.rs:260-264) or add a parse counter to assert that streaming N lines into a block performs O(1) amortized markdown parses per appended line instead of one full-prefix parse per line. (2) Add a correctness test streaming a fence that opens in one append and closes in a later one — output must equal a from-scratch parse of the final text. (3) cargo test; manual: stream a long response and watch CPU.
close_reason: Implemented, regression-tested, reviewed, and committed.

title: New agent: rust-unsafe-code-audit
description:
Create a specialized agent for validating unsafe Rust blocks, SAFETY comments, FFI contract correctness, and UB categories. Critical for mini-agent: Phase 6 invariants (JsTool must never hold Runtime or Context, worker boundary must not leak grants) are enforced through unsafe code in src/extras/js/ and src/sandbox/. A generic code-reviewer sees unsafe and checks style; this agent validates soundness.

Where: Create /Users/ahrens/.claude/agents/rust-unsafe-code-audit.md

Activation trigger: Use when reviewing unsafe blocks, validating SAFETY comments, auditing FFI bindings, checking for UB, or verifying mini-agent Phase 6 invariants (JsTool Send+Sync, no Runtime/Context in parent, worker boundary grant lifetimes). Invoke after any change to src/extras/js/, src/sandbox/, or any file containing unsafe.

Core expertise to encode:
- UB categories: data races, invalid pointer dereference, alignment violations, use-after-free, uninitialized memory reads
- SAFETY comment standards: must state the exact precondition the caller upholds
- FFI contracts: calling convention (cdecl vs stdcall), struct layout (#[repr(C)], #[repr(transparent)]), null pointer handling, error code semantics
- Interior mutability soundness: Cell/RefCell/Mutex invariant preservation across unsafe boundaries
- Lifetime validity across unsafe: can the pointer outlive the referent?
- mini-agent-specific: JsTool must be Send+Sync, all grants are parent-created and invocation-bound, worker stdout is protocol-only
- Tooling: miri for UB detection, loom for concurrency testing

Draft prompt: You are a Rust unsafe code auditor specializing in soundness validation. For mini-agent: the critical invariants are that JsTool is Send+Sync (verified in src/extras/js/), no QuickJS Runtime/Context ever lives in the parent process, and all effect grants are invocation-bound and parent-created. For every unsafe block: (1) Identify what safety invariant is being relied upon. (2) Verify the SAFETY comment states the precondition explicitly. (3) Check pointer lifetime: can it outlive the data? Is there a concurrent write? (4) For FFI: confirm calling convention, struct layout, and allocation ownership. (5) Suggest miri or loom tests. Never approve an unsafe block without tracing its full precondition chain.

How to verify: Read the created file. Confirm it covers: UB categories, SAFETY comment standards, FFI contracts, mini-agent Phase 6 invariants, miri/loom tooling.
notes: Artifact audit on 2026-08-16 found the previously closed rust-unsafe-code-audit.md missing. Restored and verified UB categories, SAFETY preconditions, FFI layout/ownership, pointer lifetimes, Miri/loom, and Phase 6 parent/worker/grant invariants.
close_reason: Closed

title: New agent: vscode-extension-developer
description:
Create a specialized agent for VS Code extension development. This is needed RIGHT NOW — the VS Code extension implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-15-vscode-windows-distribution.md) has 7 tasks. typescript-expert knows TypeScript types; it does not know VS Code API semantics, webview security models, activation lifecycle, or vsce publishing.

**Where**: Create /Users/ahrens/.claude/agents/vscode-extension-developer.md

**Activation trigger**: 'Use when building or debugging VS Code extensions: webview panels, command registration, extension activation, sidebar views, status bar items, vsce packaging, marketplace publishing, per-platform .vsix builds. Also use for: postMessage security model, CSP nonce generation, .vscodeignore configuration, extension manifest (package.json) structure.'

**Core expertise to encode**:
- VS Code activation lifecycle: onStartupFinished, onLanguage, onCommand — which to use and why
- WebviewView vs WebviewPanel — sidebar views use WebviewViewProvider, floating panels use WebviewPanel
- Webview CSP: nonce-based script allowlisting, cspSource for local resources, why external CDNs are blocked
- postMessage protocol: extension → webview (webview.postMessage), webview → extension (onDidReceiveMessage)
- ExtensionContext: extensionPath, extensionUri, subscriptions cleanup, SecretStorage, globalState
- vsce per-platform packaging: --target flag, .vscodeignore negation patterns for bin/, marketplace target names (win32-x64, darwin-arm64, linux-x64, etc.)
- esbuild for extensions: --external:vscode, CJS format, why tree-shaking cannot remove the vscode import
- Contribution points: views, viewsContainers, commands, configuration, keybindings
- OutputChannel for diagnostics, StatusBarItem for connection state

**Draft prompt** (to include verbatim):
'You are a VS Code extension development specialist. You know the VS Code Extension API deeply. Key patterns: (1) Webview CSP: always use a nonce for scripts, cspSource for local stylesheets, never allow unsafe-inline. (2) WebviewViewProvider for sidebar panels — resolveWebviewView fires once, rebuild HTML if needed. (3) postMessage is the only safe webview communication — validate all incoming messages. (4) ExtensionContext.subscriptions: push every disposable (commands, panels, output channels) so they clean up on deactivate. (5) vsce --target builds per-platform .vsix — .vscodeignore must exclude all other platforms bin/ dirs using negation: !bin//**. (6) esbuild bundles with --external:vscode --format=cjs — vscode is a peer provided by the host. (7) Activation: onStartupFinished for agents/helpers, onLanguage for language features — avoid * which blocks startup. Reference: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-15-vscode-windows-distribution.md for the mini-agent extension design.'

**How to verify**: Read the created file. Confirm it covers: webview CSP/nonce, postMessage model, per-platform vsce packaging, esbuild config, activation events, subscription cleanup. Invoke on a question about webview CSP and confirm it gives a concrete nonce-generation answer.

Restored and verified CSP/nonce, message validation, activation lifecycle, subscription cleanup, Chat/webview contribution points, per-platform VSIX packaging, and current mini-agent trust/ACP invariants.

title: New agent: rust-async-concurrency
description:
Create a specialized agent for Tokio async runtime, Send/Sync reasoning, and Future invariants. This is the highest-ROI new Rust agent — mini-agent's ACP protocol, JS worker supervisor, and message routing are all Tokio-based, and Send/Sync failures are the #1 pain point the generic debugger misses.

**Where**: Create /Users/ahrens/.claude/agents/rust-async-concurrency.md

**Activation trigger**: 'Use when debugging async deadlocks, Send/Sync bound failures, Tokio runtime issues, pin/unpin errors, channel mismatches, Future cancel-safety issues, or async lifetime errors. Also use proactively when reviewing code that spawns Tokio tasks or crosses async boundaries.'

**Core expertise to encode in the prompt**:
- Tokio runtime semantics: blocking vs async tasks, current_thread vs multi_thread, block_in_place
- Pin/Unpin invariants and when to use Box::pin vs stack pinning
- Send/Sync bound failures: how to trace the non-Send value backward through closures and type chains
- Cancellation safety: can a Future drop mid-await without leaking? Are receivers still polled after cancel?
- Channel patterns: mpsc (fan-out), oneshot (single response), broadcast (pub/sub) — when each applies
- select! macro semantics and polling behavior
- Async trait workarounds (async_trait crate vs RPITIT in Rust 1.75+)
- tokio-console and cargo-flamegraph for profiling async code

**Draft prompt** (to include verbatim):
'You are a Rust async concurrency specialist for the mini-agent codebase (Tokio multi-thread runtime, ACP protocol over stdio, JS worker supervisor pattern). When you see an async issue: (1) Check if the failing type is Send — trace the non-Send value backward through closures and Arc wrappers. (2) Verify Tokio executor context — is this code running in a blocking context that needs block_in_place? (3) For Future errors, check Pin requirements and whether stack vs Box pinning is appropriate. (4) Examine cancellation safety: if a task is dropped mid-await, are resources cleaned up? Is the receiver still trying to poll? (5) For channel errors, confirm mpsc/oneshot/broadcast matches the use case. (6) Use cargo-expand on select! errors. Default to compile-time proofs over runtime guards. Suggest timeout + graceful shutdown patterns. Use tokio-console for runtime diagnostics.'

**How to verify**: Read the created file. Confirm it covers: Send/Sync tracing, Pin/Unpin, cancel safety, channel selection, tokio-console. Invoke the agent on a synthetic async Send bound error and confirm it identifies the root cause correctly.
notes: Artifact audit on 2026-08-16 found the previously closed rust-async-concurrency.md missing. Restored and verified Send/Sync tracing, Pin/Unpin, cancellation safety, channel selection, select semantics, tokio-console, and cargo-flamegraph guidance.
close_reason: Closed

title: src/git/ module has zero test coverage before release
description: The new src/git/ module (tool.rs, runner.rs) introduces 6 pub(crate) functions (capture, discover, executable, verify_contained, command_result, command_failure) with no #[cfg(test)] module anywhere in the directory. The module is included in the default feature set and used in production agent builds. Before releasing v1.7.2 this module needs unit tests covering at least: happy-path capture, error propagation when git is unavailable, and the field-parsing logic in tool.rs.
close_reason: Added #[cfg(test)] modules to runner.rs (9 tests: command_result variants, command_failure, git_environment keys, unavailable runner) and tool.rs (7 tests: hardened_args invariants). All 17 pass.

title: git/runner.rs:95 panics when executable metadata is unavailable
description: src/git/runner.rs line 95 calls .expect("current executable identity must be available") on a metadata lookup. This path is reached via the unavailable() fallback; if the metadata query fails (e.g., /proc/self/exe unreadable, unusual install layout), the agent process panics instead of returning a graceful error. Should propagate an Err instead of unwrapping.
close_reason: Changed unavailable() to return Result<Self, String> with ? propagation; Default::default() uses .expect() at the call site (unavoidable for Default trait).

title: Add a read-only structured Git tool
description:
## Why
The agent needs repository context on Windows even when shell execution is unavailable. Read-only status, diff, history, and object inspection cover the common coding loop with materially less risk than arbitrary Git commands.
design: Register a typed `git` tool with fixed operations `status`, `diff`, `log`, and `show`. Do not accept raw subcommands or argv. Use porcelain v2 `-z` for status; disable optional locks, external diff, text conversion, submodules, pager, lazy fetch, and prompts. Validate revisions with `rev-parse --verify --end-of-options`; pass validated paths only after `--` with literal pathspecs. Return structured status/history data and bounded diff/show text with explicit truncation. Register and advertise only when the shared Git capability is available for the current binding.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tool works without the general shell on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Schema permits only status/diff/log/show and rejects raw command/argv fields.
- Tests cover option-like revisions and paths, invalid revisions, Unicode, rename/copy status, binary files, submodules, hostile config, external diff/textconv/filter hooks, prompts, lazy fetch, and output truncation.
- No read-only operation creates locks, contacts remotes, launches helpers/editors/pagers, or writes repository/worktree state.
- Permission prompts and audit events identify the Git operation and normalized repository-relative targets.
- TUI, headless, ACP, and subagents share registration behavior and model guidance.
- Relevant tests and the debug install gate pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract and harden a shared workspace-bound Git runner
description:
## Why
Git process creation is currently duplicated, while the worktree implementation already contains most of the safe direct-process pattern. A single runner is needed before a model-visible Git tool can have consistent containment, cleanup, and Windows behavior.
design: Move the reusable execution boundary from `src/extras/git_worktree/mod.rs` into a documented `src/git/runner.rs` module and keep worktree callers on it. Resolve and pin the Git executable identity for the captured WorkspaceBinding. Invoke it directly with `-C <bound-root>`, the existing process-creation guard, bounded stdout/stderr, deadline and process-tree cleanup. Clear redirecting and interactive Git environment, including repository/object/worktree overrides; set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, no pager, and literal pathspec policy. Return a closed capability result when Git or containment is unavailable. Do not expose this runner directly to the model.
acceptance_criteria:
- Worktree functionality uses the shared runner with no behavior regression.
- Tests cover missing/replaced executable identity, Unicode and spaced workspace paths, hostile `GIT_*` environment, bounded output, timeout/cancellation, and child cleanup.
- Windows tests use canonical and ordinary path spellings for the same WorkspaceBinding.
- No runner path invokes a shell, searches a model-controlled PATH after capture, or accepts an unvalidated workspace root.
- New module documentation states containment and environment invariants.
- Relevant tests pass serially on Windows and normally on macOS/Linux; `cargo install --path . --debug` succeeds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Native structured Git client without shell grammar
description:
## Why
Users expect mini-agent to inspect and update Git repositories even when no general shell is available. A typed Git capability gives Windows, macOS, and Linux equal Git features without asking the model to compose shell commands or exposing arbitrary process execution.
design: Build on the existing direct `git` process pattern rather than adding git2/gix initially. Share one hardened workspace-bound runner, then expose fixed structured operations with no raw argv, shell, remote network, or unsandboxed fallback. Register the tool only when the exact Git executable and workspace containment boundary are available. Deliver read-only operations first; admit mutations only after a separate threat-model decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- Child issues deliver a shared hardened runner, read-only structured Git operations, and an explicit mutation security decision.
- The model can inspect a repository on Windows, macOS, and Linux without a general shell tool.
- No operation accepts arbitrary command strings/argv or invokes a shell.
- Capability registration is truthful for the current WorkspaceBinding and fails closed.
- Documentation explains supported operations, permission boundaries, output limits, and unavailable states.
close_reason: All 4 children complete (shared runner, read-only tool, mutation security decision, stage/unstage/commit); shipped on feat/windows-shell-native-git

title: Gate model-visible shell access on the bound Windows workspace
description:
## Why
On Windows, mini-agent can resolve PowerShell and advertise the compatibility tool as `bash` even though the production AppContainer helper cannot launch for the actual workspace. The screenshot reproduces helper setup stage 2 / exit 162 after the model has already claimed shell and Git access. Executable discovery and a process-wide preflight are not sufficient evidence that the bound workspace can execute.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start mini-agent in a Windows workspace whose AppContainer policy cannot be constructed, such as a workspace/cache overlap or another bound-root setup failure.
2. Ask which tools are available.
3. Observe that the model advertises `bash`.
4. Invoke `bash echo yes` or `bash git status`.
5. Observe `Windows AppContainer sandbox helper failed at closed stage 2` and exit code 162.
design: Capture one execution-capability result after the canonical WorkspaceBinding and exact sandbox roots are known. On Windows, validate root-role policy and perform a bounded no-op through the same production helper/profile/job boundary used by the shell tool, or a demonstrably equivalent setup-only probe. Cache only against the binding identity and invalidate on rebind. If unavailable, omit the tool schema and all model guidance that claims shell access, while retaining a closed diagnostic for the user. Never fall back to an unsandboxed process. Keep JS worker capability independent.
acceptance_criteria:
- A Windows fixture where the executable resolves but bound helper setup fails registers neither the compatibility `bash` name nor the future `shell` name and emits no shell guidance.
- A valid Windows PowerShell/AppContainer binding registers and executes the bounded no-op.
- Workspace rebind recomputes capability; results are not reused across roots.
- TUI, headless, ACP, and subagent rebuild paths consume the same captured capability.
- Failure leaves no helper/process residue and exposes no workspace secrets.
- Windows regression tests cover setup stage 2 / exit 162; relevant tests run serially and `cargo install --path . --debug` succeeds.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enforce VS Code Workspace Trust and remote-root authority
description:
## Why
Starting a coding agent can read files and execute tools. VS Code Restricted Mode and remote workspaces must control whether and where mini-agent starts, and workspace settings must not substitute an attacker-controlled binary.
design: Declare capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces and virtualWorkspaces as unsupported. Gate spawn and all agent commands on workspace.isTrusted and a file-scheme folder. Resolve executable configuration from user/remote-user scope only, not workspace/folder settings; run in the workspace extension host so remote paths and binaries are co-located. For multi-root, require explicit folder selection and create one ACP primary-root session; do not claim additional-root support.
acceptance_criteria: Untrusted workspace tests prove no process, network, config migration, or workspace read occurs and commands explain how to trust. A workspace setting cannot override executable/arguments. Local, Remote SSH, WSL, and Dev Container tests bind the selected canonical root; sibling and second-root access remains denied unless separately selected; trust revocation closes the session and reaps the process.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scaffold a Node VS Code workspace extension and supervised ACP stdio client
description:
## Why
VS Code desktop and remote Node extension hosts can spawn the agent; web extensions cannot. The base extension needs reliable discovery, protocol framing, logging, cancellation, and complete child cleanup before richer UI.
design: Create editors/vscode/ with a pinned TypeScript toolchain and official stable @agentclientprotocol/sdk. Declare extensionKind [workspace, ui], no browser entry point, no virtual-workspace support, and lazy command/chat activation. Resolve an explicit configured executable or the approved packaged artifact on the same host as the workspace; validate --version/ACP support. Spawn directly with shell:false and --acp, bind cwd to one selected workspace folder, bound stdout framing/stderr diagnostics, and own the child tree through deactivate/restart/crash.
acceptance_criteria: Local desktop plus SSH/WSL/container extension-host tests initialize a session and prompt through stdio; paths with spaces/Unicode work; no shell is invoked; absent/wrong/non-ACP binaries give actionable errors; malformed/oversized output closes safely; cancellation, extension deactivation, window reload, agent crash, and dropped request leave no process. Web and virtual workspaces show an unsupported diagnostic without activation side effects.
close_reason: Closed

title: Publish an ACP-enabled mini-agent artifact and registry metadata
description:
## Why
The acp Cargo feature is optional and absent from both current full and lite release archives, so an editor cannot assume that downloaded mini-agent supports --acp.
design: Choose one explicit artifact contract: add acp to the supported full release feature set, or publish distinctly named ACP artifacts for every supported target. Never silently make lite feature claims. Add a machine-verifiable feature/capability smoke using --acp initialize, preserve the four-file GPL archive contract and exact Corresponding Source, and submit/update ACP Registry metadata with canonical executable, stable stdio arguments, version, checksums, and platform coordinates.
acceptance_criteria: For x86_64 Windows, x86_64/aarch64 macOS, and supported Linux targets, the documented artifact launches --acp, completes stable v1 initialize/new/prompt/close smoke, and rejects version/feature mismatch. Release expected-set/checksum/source checks cover it; registry metadata validates and never points to the unrelated crates.io mini-agent package; install instructions work from a clean machine.
close_reason: Full release/default builds now include ACP; each platform VSIX packages that full artifact and verifies --acp plus initialize/new/prompt/cancel/close. Existing v1.7.2 registry metadata remains canonical.

title: Bridge ACP permission requests to editor clients without weakening headless defaults
description:
## Why
Current ACP construction is deliberately non-interactive: Ask fails closed. A useful guarded VS Code session needs an explicit client approval channel, but the server must never silently start with --accept-all or broaden permissions when no capable client is present.
design: Add ACP client requestPermission wiring behind negotiated client capabilities. Convert only typed mini-agent permission prompts into bounded ACP requests; map allow-once/allow-always/deny to the existing PermissionChecker without broadening paths/commands, persist only through existing policy mechanisms, and cancel/deny on disconnect, timeout, malformed reply, session close, or unsupported client. Preserve existing headless stdio/TCP fail-closed behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Interop tests prove allow-once affects one exact operation, allow-always uses the existing narrow durable rule, deny blocks it, concurrent sessions cannot answer each other's request, cancellation/disconnect/timeout deny and reap, and clients without permission capability see the current immediate denial. No extension launch path passes --accept-all implicitly; permission prompt content contains no secrets or unbounded tool output.
close_reason: Closed

title: Refresh mini-agent's stable ACP v1 lifecycle and TypeScript interoperability
description:
## Why
The implementation uses agent-client-protocol 2.0.0 with schema 1.5.0 and truthfully omits session/load, but current docs still claim ACP has no session-close notification. ACP v1 stabilized session/close in April 2026, so long-lived editor processes otherwise retain sessions until the 64-session cap.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build mini-agent with --features acp and start mini-agent --acp over stdio.
2. Repeatedly send session/new through a long-lived client without restarting the process.
3. Observe there is no handled session/close path and the 65th retained session is rejected as capacity full, even though current stable ACP v1 clients can send session/close.
design: Audit the current stable ACP v1 schema/SDK without importing experimental v2. Upgrade the Rust ACP dependency only as narrowly required. Implement session/close to generation-safely cancel an active turn, remove process-local history/skill services/read trackers, and release sandbox ownership; repeated/unknown close must be deterministic. Keep load/resume/delete/additionalDirectories/usage/message IDs unadvertised unless actually implemented. Add a locked Node test fixture using the official stable TypeScript SDK over stdio.
acceptance_criteria: Official stable TypeScript SDK initializes, creates, prompts, cancels, and closes a session against cargo test --features acp; closing active/idle/unknown sessions is bounded and leak-free; 65 sequential create/close cycles do not hit capacity; no closed session can be prompted; protocol-version mismatch and unadvertised methods fail truthfully; docs no longer claim close is absent. Full cargo test and debug install with acp pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Choose dedicated VS Code extension versus ACP registry/client compatibility
description:
## Why
A community VS Code ACP client already exists and the ACP Registry can describe install/configuration. A branded extension is justified only if mini-agent-specific UX, distribution, or support outweighs maintaining another editor client.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Publish ACP Registry metadata and a tested setup recipe for a maintained generic client.
2. Contribute mini-agent support upstream to an existing VS Code ACP client.
3. Maintain a dedicated mini-agent extension using the stable ACP TypeScript SDK.
4. Expose mini-agent as a Language Model Chat Provider; reject by default because mini-agent is an agent with tools, permissions, sessions, and effects, not merely a model endpoint.
design: Write an ADR comparing: registry metadata plus documentation for a generic ACP client; contributing mini-agent support to an existing client; and a dedicated extension. Evaluate ownership, UX, permissions, bundled-versus-external binary, Marketplace identity, Remote/WSL/SSH/Codespaces behavior, update cadence, telemetry/privacy, GPL implications, and support cost.
acceptance_criteria: ADR selects one path and states MVP/non-goals, binary acquisition policy, target VS Code version, local/remote/web support, UI surface, success metrics, and maintenance owner. Conditional dedicated-extension children are either activated by the decision or closed with rationale; ACP conformance/registry work remains independently actionable.
close_reason: Resolved: chose ACP registry/generic-client path (implemented in ny65.2–ny65.4 and ny65.9)

title: Integrate mini-agent into VS Code through stable ACP v1
description:
## Why
mini-agent already exposes an ACP stdio agent, making a Node-based VS Code workspace extension feasible without duplicating agent logic. Coordinate protocol lifecycle, permission UX, an ACP-enabled artifact, remote/workspace behavior, UI, and publication.
design: Use stable ACP v1 and the official @agentclientprotocol/sdk stable entry point; experimental v2 and draft remote transports are out of scope. Prefer stdio child-process transport in the workspace extension host. Keep mini-agent authoritative for provider config, tools, sandbox, sessions, and filesystem effects.
acceptance_criteria: The integration decision is recorded; approved implementation children are complete; local and remote desktop VS Code can run a trusted workspace prompt, stream tool/status output, request permissions, cancel, and close/reap the session; untrusted/web/virtual workspaces fail closed; signed/versioned VSIX and ACP metadata are reproducible.
close_reason: Stable ACP v1 VS Code integration, local platform VSIX packaging, trust/permission/cancellation behavior, and reproducibility are complete; online Marketplace/Open VSX publication remains deliberately deferred in mini-agent-ny65.10.

title: Decide whether Tauri is a product surface and freeze its installer matrix
description:
## Why
Tauri is not required to install the current CLI. Adding it creates a second UI, web frontend, signing identities, WebView dependencies, update policy, and support matrix. Make the go/no-go and scope explicit before implementation.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Keep the existing CLI/TUI archives and package-manager channels only.
2. Prioritize editor integrations such as ACP/VS Code without a desktop GUI.
3. Build a Tauri v2 shell that embeds an ACP-enabled mini-agent sidecar.
4. Build a native GUI by linking agent internals directly; reject by default because it duplicates lifecycle/security authority and couples UI delivery to the core crate.
design: Write an ADR under docs/decisions/ covering target users and workflows, why a desktop GUI is preferable to the TUI/editor integrations, MVP screens, sidecar-over-ACP architecture, binary bundling, data/config ownership, offline behavior, update policy, supported OS/architectures, and installer choices. Default proposal: DMG per macOS architecture, deb plus AppImage on x86_64 Linux, and NSIS x86_64 on Windows; MSI and ARM targets require explicit demand.
acceptance_criteria: ADR records go/no-go, measurable success criteria, supported OS/architecture/installer matrix, install/update/uninstall behavior, signing ownership, and whether MSI/ARM are required. A no-go closes the conditional Tauri implementation children with rationale; a go decision supplies every value needed by those children.
close_reason: No-go decision recorded in docs/decisions/2026-08-15-tauri-product-surface.md. VS Code ACP integration covers the primary user need; Tauri adds WebView dependency, second signing identity, and update policy overhead without measurable user value at this stage.

title: Keep AppContainer control-root authority handle-bound through journaling
description: src/sandbox/windows.rs validates and attests the private AppContainer control root, then drops the directory handle and continues stale-journal sweep plus intent/journal creation through a bare PathBuf. A same-user filesystem mutator can rename or replace the control directory or an ancestor after attestation, reintroducing overlap with an authorized root or redirecting recovery records. The process-wide profile lock coordinates mini-agent instances but not external filesystem mutation.
design: Replace the bare PathBuf result of profile_journal_root with a handle-bound control-root authority retained through sweep, profile creation, intent publication, full journal publication, cleanup and rollback. Deny rename/delete sharing where compatible with cleanup, or perform child opens relative to the retained directory handle. Bind canonical path and Windows volume/file identity and revalidate immediately before any unavoidable path-based operation. Reject ancestor reparses throughout. Preserve closed diagnostics and existing five-second recovery deadlines.
acceptance_criteria: Barrier-driven Windows tests swap the control root and separately an ancestor after DACL attestation but before stale sweep/intent creation; both fail closed with no profile, external journal, DACL mutation or residue. Normal stale recovery and concurrent launch serialization still pass. Ordinary/verbatim/8.3 and volume-alias cases cannot bypass identity checks. Run focused AppContainer tests serially, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and cargo install --path . --debug.
notes: Adversarial review of mini-agent-wbat.3 found this after the smaller ancestor-reparse regression was fixed. Primary symbols: profile_journal_root, protect_and_attest_control_root, sweep_stale_profiles_until_locked, create_profile_intent, create_profile_journal, create_appcontainer_profile.
close_reason: Merged in PR #23 after all 65 CI checks passed, including native Windows AppContainer, platform-path, MCP stdio, and worker-containment gates.

title: Recover preserved Windows AppContainer preflight journals on later startup
description: The bounded general AppContainer preflight correctly preserves its unique temporary root when profile/ACL recovery cannot finish before the cleanup deadline, because deleting the intent/journal could orphan authority. A later process does not currently discover these preserved roots, so transient cleanup failure can leave a profile, ACE, journal, and temp tree indefinitely.
design: Before a new general preflight, enumerate only the exact mini-agent-windows-sandbox-preflight-<UUID> namespace under the canonical local temp root. Open roots without following reparse points, verify owner/private DACL/link policy and the existing control-root schema, then use the existing bounded full-journal-before-intent sweep. Delete a root only after cleanup attestation succeeds. Bound count, bytes, lock wait, and total sweep time; malformed or unverifiable entries fail closed without deleting evidence or arbitrary temp data.
acceptance_criteria: Windows tests inject recovery deadline failure, restart through a child process, and prove the next startup removes the exact profile, Job, ACEs, journal/intent and temp root; malicious symlink/junction, owner/DACL, hardlink, malformed-name/schema, excess-count and concurrent-owner fixtures are rejected without mutation; sweep timing is bounded and failure remains cached closed. Run focused sandbox tests serially, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and cargo install --path . --debug.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reap timed-out Windows JS worker preflight work before caching failure
description: src/sandbox/worker/windows.rs::production_preflight uses a bounded caller receive but the helper thread can remain detached inside ACL mutation or CreateProcess after timeout. The process-local failure may be cached while that thread still owns process-creation or executable-ACL state, delaying later launches and allowing late side effects.
design: Make the probe operation itself deadline-aware and owned. On timeout, cancel or terminate every helper/process it started, join/reap the probe worker within an absolute cleanup ceiling, restore/revoke transient ACL state, and only then publish the cached fail-closed WorkerContainmentStatus. Serialize executable DACL mutation with the general AppContainer ACL transaction or otherwise prove concurrent updates cannot lose ACEs.
acceptance_criteria: Windows deterministic delay/failure tests prove the caller and cleanup return within documented ceilings, no probe thread or helper remains, the process-creation lock is immediately reusable, executable ACLs match their pre-test state, unavailable status is cached once, and a late success cannot overwrite the cached failure. Run focused worker tests serially, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and cargo install --path . --debug.
notes: Implemented in PR https://github.com/sebahrens/mini-agent/pull/25. Replaces detached Rust preflight thread with a Job-supervised fixed-function helper; parent holds exact executable/DACL rollback authority. Local fmt, strict Clippy, full serial cargo test (1561 + 7), and debug install pass. Awaiting native Windows CI.
close_reason: Merged PR #25 after full CI passed, including targeted rerun of the isolated Windows config-lock flake.

title: Bound Windows startup preflights and skip unused capability probes
description:
Windows startup synchronously runs the default AppContainer production preflight through Startup::validate_sandbox_availability and Sandbox::policy; run_production_preflight uses blocking output_guarded without an explicit deadline. Agent construction separately runs the Windows JS worker live preflight with a five-second deadline before build_agent_inner can honor --no-tools, then initializes skills. These independent child-heavy checks repeat on every new process and explain platform-specific cold-start stalls.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On Windows, cold-start a new mini-agent process with default sandboxing.
2. Observe synchronous general AppContainer production preflight, followed later by the independent JS worker preflight and skill initialization.
3. Repeat with --no-tools and observe JS containment is still reached before tool suppression; a delayed general helper has no explicit preflight deadline.
design: Give the general AppContainer production preflight an explicit deadline and bounded descendant cleanup while keeping its process-local OnceLock and fail-closed result. Resolve intended tool capabilities before probing: skip shell, JS containment and skill initialization when tools or those capabilities are ineligible. Run independent eligible general and worker probes concurrently only if their separate fail-closed contracts and process-creation serialization remain intact. Add closed phase timing suitable for diagnostics. Do not persist cross-process success or weaken either live preflight.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic Windows delay/counter tests prove at most one general and one eligible worker probe per process; a timed-out general helper and complete descendant tree are reaped within a documented ceiling; --no-tools performs no shell, JS worker or skill probe; unavailable results are cached; ACP and normal startup consume the same resolved result; no helper, profile, journal or temp-tree residue remains. Measure cold installed debug startup with PowerShell Measure-Command for normal and --no-tools headless runs and record bounded timings. Run focused Windows startup/sandbox/worker groups serially, full serial cargo test and debug install.
notes:
Primary paths: src/startup.rs::validate_sandbox_availability/init_features, src/sandbox.rs::policy, src/sandbox/windows.rs::is_available/run_production_preflight, src/provider.rs::build_agent_in_workspace, src/sandbox/worker/windows.rs. Reported latency is real; exact phase magnitude still needs Windows measurement.
Implemented capability-driven shell/JS/skill/general-sandbox/MCP startup gating, concurrent joined Windows general+worker preflights, closed timing, a five-second run deadline with bounded whole-tree reap and a fresh bounded profile/ACL recovery window, durable pre-profile intent, cross-process intent-transition locking, and deadline-aware ACL cleanup. Added source contracts, deterministic overlap/cache/deadline tests, and docs/benchmarks/windows-startup.md. macOS verification: full unrestricted serial suite passed (1550 + 7 bootstrap), focused startup/inventory/source tests passed, cargo fmt and cargo install --path . --debug passed. Keep open pending native Windows regression groups and recorded PowerShell timings. Preserved-root restart recovery remains mini-agent-prju; timed-out JS worker probe cleanup remains mini-agent-p522.
Integration gate 2026-08-10 after terminal/AppContainer/pricing followups: full serial suite passed (1561 + 7 bootstrap) and debug install passed. Windows timing/native evidence remains.
Implementation is merged on main through PR #22 (commits 49303a9 and 94cf4b3 within merge 53d5e73), with follow-up preflight recovery in PRs #23 and #25. Validate only the combined main build; no individual branch remains to merge. Keep open for native Windows timings/evidence.

title: Probe and truthfully register the Windows shell capability
description:
Cli::resolve_shell returns an unchecked string, Sandbox::with_shell applies -Command to every Windows executable, build_agent_inner always registers BashTool, and its description always claims Bash. A missing shell is advertised to the model and fails only when called; configured Git Bash or sh receives the wrong argument contract.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On Windows, configure a missing shell or Git Bash/sh.
2. Build an agent with tools enabled.
3. Observe bash is still advertised; missing shell fails only on call, while Git Bash/sh receives PowerShell -Command and the tool description still claims Bash regardless of dialect.
design: Resolve one closed ShellCapability from the captured workspace and PATH: canonical executable identity, supported dialect, and exact literal command argument. Support PowerShell/pwsh with -Command and Bash/sh with -c; reject missing or unsupported executables. Thread the same capability through UI, headless, ACP and rebuilds. Register and mention the tool only when capability exists; keep the permission/tool identity bash for compatibility but make the description dialect-correct. Never launch an unprobed fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Missing configured shell is absent from model tool definitions and the generated tool guidance; PowerShell and Git Bash PATH-shim fixtures receive the correct literal flag; unsupported executable is not registered; UI, headless and ACP expose the same result; rebuilds do not re-probe or change identity; --no-tools probes/registers no shell. Run focused shell_mode, builder and ACP tests serially, full serial cargo test, debug install, and a Windows installed-binary harness with PATH shims recording argv.
notes: Primary files: src/cli.rs, src/permission/mod.rs, src/sandbox.rs, src/agent/builder.rs, src/agent/prompt.rs, src/agent/tools/bash.rs and provider/ACP plumbing. The model prompt must be derived from the actual registered capability set.
close_reason: Implemented one-time truthful shell capability discovery across UI, headless, ACP, loop, and rebuilds; pinned validated Windows executable identity/bytes; aligned argv, tool schema, prompt guidance, and overhead accounting; full serial suite and debug install pass. Windows-native harness remains covered by Windows-only regression tests and CI because this host is macOS.

title: Keep active workspace authority across resume, session load and import
description:
Serialized Session.working_dir can diverge from the active UI workspace binding. Startup resume and SlashCtx::replace_session can install a saved or imported directory while context, permissions and tools retain another root; shell, MCP, hooks, add, statusline and file tools then disagree. JSONL import already retaining the active workspace is the safer reference.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Keep active workspace binding A.
2. Resume, slash-load, or native-import a session whose serialized working_dir names B.
3. Observe session-based consumers such as shell/MCP/hooks/add disagree with tools and permissions about whether A or B is authoritative.
design: Make the retained UiContext WorkspaceBinding authoritative. On resume, slash session load and native import, overwrite incoming Session.working_dir with the active binding root. Permit workspace transitions only through the explicit transactional worktree rebind path. Derive shell, MCP, hooks, add and status display from the binding rather than trusting serialized session input. Roll back all state if a provider/agent rebuild fails.
acceptance_criteria: With active workspace A and saved/imported session naming B, resume, slash load and native import retain A; native and JS relative reads/writes, shell pwd, add, hooks and MCP command CWD all use A; B remains untouched; failed provider rebuild restores both session and workspace-facing state. Run focused resume/import/session tests, cargo test worktree -- --test-threads=1, full serial cargo test and debug install.
notes:
Primary files: src/startup.rs, src/ui/slash/mod.rs::SlashCtx::replace_session, src/ui/slash/session.rs, src/ui/slash/add.rs and MCP wiring. Depends on the canonical WorkspaceBinding composition-root change.
Implemented active WorkspaceBinding authority across startup consumers, slash session replacement/import, worktree/add/init/review operations, hooks, welcome/status display, and undo. Provider changes are staged before session/client/agent commit. Added stale-session-path regressions and documented the serialized-path boundary. Verified focused tests, cargo fmt, strict clippy, cargo test worktree -- --test-threads=1, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1 (1562 passed, 5 ignored; worker bootstrap 7 passed), and cargo install --path . --debug.
close_reason: Merged as PR 26 (ded2285): active WorkspaceBinding now remains authoritative across resume, load, import, runtime consumers, and transactional provider rebuilds; all CI passed.

title: Retry transient locks in descriptor-relative Windows atomic writes
description:
src/fs.rs::atomic_write_platform::rename_open_file calls NtSetInformationFile(FileRenameInformation) once. Converted sharing and lock violations 32/33 abort native and brokered JS atomic-write consumers even though verified directory and staging handles remain valid.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On Windows, hold an existing supported atomic-write target without delete sharing.
2. Trigger a native or brokered JS write path that reaches atomic_write_platform replacement.
3. Observe the single NtSetInformationFile call map sharing/lock violation 32 or 33 directly to failure.
design: Retry only the final NtSetInformationFile call for converted Win32 errors 32/33, using the same open staging file and verified directory handles. Bound the total wait to at most one second and honor AtomicWriteCancellation without reopening or revalidating through mutable ambient paths. Preserve descriptor-relative atomic publication, complete-value semantics and existing cleanup; never delete and rewrite. This does not claim to solve destination identity compare-and-swap.
acceptance_criteria: Windows primitive and end-to-end tests prove transient locks succeed; persistent locks preserve prior content and leave no .zswrite residue; cancellation interrupts retry safely; non-32/33 errors call once; native and JS supported writes expose only complete old/new values. Run cargo test atomic_write -- --test-threads=1, cargo test tools_mod -- --test-threads=1, cargo test worker_broker -- --test-threads=1, full serial cargo test and debug install.
notes: Primary symbol: src/fs.rs::atomic_write_platform::rename_open_file. Relate to mini-agent-51p3, which separately tracks the unsolved existing-target compare-and-swap contract.
close_reason: Implemented bounded descriptor-relative Windows lock retry with cancellation and transient/persistent/error-class regression coverage

title: Reuse bounded private publication for Windows MCP OAuth credentials
description:
src/extras/mcp/oauth.rs::windows_private::atomic_write duplicates MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING and immediately fails on errors 32/33. OAuth token save, refresh, migration and migration-marker writes therefore have the same transient-lock failure as configuration persistence.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On Windows, create an existing MCP OAuth credential file and hold it without FILE_SHARE_DELETE.
2. Trigger token save, refresh, or migration.
3. Observe the duplicated MoveFileExW call fail immediately with error 32 or 33.
design: After the private configuration publisher has bounded lock retry, delegate OAuth secure_atomic_write to crate::fs::private_atomic_write_sync or extract one shared private final-publication primitive. Remove duplicated Windows rename logic while retaining credential-specific lock handling, private DACL enforcement, identity-checked temp cleanup and storage_error sanitization.
acceptance_criteria: Windows OAuth tests prove transient delete-denying handle release permits complete credential publication; a persistent lock preserves old JSON and DACL and leaves no .oauth temp residue; normal save/refresh/migration succeeds; diagnostics contain no token, serialized content or raw path. Run cargo test mcp_oauth -- --test-threads=1, cargo test config_persistence_permissions -- --test-threads=1, full serial cargo test and debug install.
notes: Primary file: src/extras/mcp/oauth.rs::windows_private::atomic_write. This child should reuse rather than fork the private retry policy.
close_reason: Reused shared private publisher and added Windows OAuth transient/persistent lock tests

title: Add Unicode-native Windows clipboard and truthful copy outcomes
description:
copy_to_clipboard pipes UTF-8 through clip.exe and treats a successfully written OSC 52 sequence as confirmed copy. Ctrl+Shift+C is consumed by the generic Ctrl+C interrupt path, while Ctrl+V falls through InputEditor and inserts a literal v. OAuth and selection callers can therefore claim copied when no clipboard operation was acknowledged.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In the Windows TUI, select text and press Ctrl+Shift+C; observe it enter the generic Ctrl+C interrupt path.
2. Press Ctrl+V with clipboard text; observe a literal v instead of clipboard insertion.
3. Copy Unicode through clip.exe/OSC 52 and observe callers report copied without a confirmed Unicode clipboard write.
design: Add a tested Windows CF_UNICODETEXT abstraction using the minimum Win32 clipboard/global-memory APIs, bounded retry for transient OpenClipboard contention, strict ownership transfer, NUL/size validation, and Unicode read/write. Route Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+V before generic Ctrl+C; keep plain Ctrl+C cancellation. Return an explicit Confirmed versus FallbackRequested outcome. Keep OSC 52 as terminal fallback but never label it confirmed. Share the same copy path for keyboard, mouse selection and OAuth; preserve selection on confirmed failure.
acceptance_criteria: Windows tests round-trip ASCII, non-BMP Unicode, empty and multiline content; embedded NUL and oversize data fail closed; transient clipboard contention succeeds and persistent contention exhausts boundedly without leaks; Ctrl+Shift+C never cancels, plain Ctrl+C still does, Ctrl+V inserts the full clipboard once at the cursor, and mouse/keyboard copy agree; OSC 52 emits the exact payload but UI/OAuth wording says requested rather than copied. Verify in Windows Terminal and ConHost with Unicode and multiline copy/paste after cargo test renderer_tests -- --test-threads=1, focused UI key tests, full serial cargo test, and debug install.
notes:
Primary files: src/ui/renderer.rs::copy_to_clipboard, src/ui/app.rs::handle_user_event and handle_key_event, src/ui/input/mod.rs, src/tests/renderer_tests.rs. Add only the needed windows-sys features. This issue depends on transactional console lifecycle.
Implemented CF_UNICODETEXT clipboard read/write with GMEM_MOVEABLE ownership transfer, strict UTF-16/NUL/4 MiB validation, CRLF boundary normalization, and bounded OpenClipboard retries. Routed exact Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+V before generic Ctrl+C, rejected AltGr aliases, unified keyboard/mouse/OAuth outcomes, and made OSC 52 wording explicitly unconfirmed. Added cross-platform unit coverage plus serial ignored Windows native round-trip/contention tests invoked by CI. Local verification: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings -A dead-code; cargo test -- --test-threads=1 (1578 + 7 passed, 5 ignored); cargo install --path . --debug; workflow YAML parse; git diff --check. Three focused reviewer passes are clean. Manual Windows Terminal/ConHost evidence remains required before final acceptance.
First native CI run exposed a headless-runner-only fixture failure: GetConsoleWindow was null and AllocConsole was unavailable. Reworked the Windows tests to create and own a message-only STATIC window for OpenClipboard/EmptyClipboard ownership, leaving production behavior bound to the real TUI console HWND. Focused renderer tests, Clippy, fmt, and diff checks remain green.
Merged via PR #31 on 2026-08-12 (merge a8fc9abb8a57547a0a5eb02b2f88a97df3d7bdf6). Corrected CI attempt passed the native Windows CF_UNICODETEXT round-trip/contention job and the full 65-job workflow; an unrelated existing macOS fetch-timeout flake passed on isolated rerun. Implementation is complete. Keep open only for manual Windows Terminal and ConHost Unicode/multiline keyboard+mouse copy/paste evidence.
Clipboard implementation is already merged on main through PR #31 (merge a8fc9ab). It must be validated together with the terminal lifecycle on the combined main build; no individual branch remains to merge.

title: Make TUI console attachment transactional and restore Windows UTF-8 code pages
description:
TerminalGuard::new mutates alternate screen, mouse, bracketed paste, keyboard enhancement and raw mode before a guard exists, so an intermediate failure leaks terminal state. Five manual suspend/resume paths restore only a subset. Adding Windows code-page changes without fixing this lifecycle would leak UTF-8 mode into child programs or fail to restore the console.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Attach the TUI to Windows Terminal or ConHost with non-65001 input/output code pages.
2. Render UTF-8 text, then suspend for editor/lazygit/help or force TerminalGuard initialization to fail after an early mode change.
3. Observe mojibake or leaked/asymmetric raw, alternate-screen, paste, mouse, enhancement, or code-page state.
design: Implement one stateful terminal backend/guard in src/ui/terminal.rs. On attached Windows console handles, snapshot GetConsoleCP and GetConsoleOutputCP, set both to 65001 transactionally, and restore originals on suspend, failed init, normal/error/panic drop; reapply UTF-8 on resume. Detect attachment with console-handle capability such as GetConsoleMode and skip code-page mutation for redirected/headless streams without failing. Replace manual editor, lazygit, init/help and input transitions with shared suspend/resume RAII preserving symmetric order for raw mode, alternate screen, mouse, bracketed paste and keyboard enhancement.
acceptance_criteria: Injected failures after every attach step restore all prior state; repeated suspend/resume is idempotent; editors/lazygit/help/init run with original console modes and code pages and the TUI resumes with UTF-8 plus bracketed paste/mouse/keyboard enhancement; redirected stdin/stdout makes no code-page calls and succeeds; normal, error and panic exits restore original values. Native Windows tests assert GetConsoleCP/GetConsoleOutputCP restoration. Manually verify Unicode output in Windows Terminal and ConHost plus external-tool and exit cycles. Run focused terminal tests serially, cargo test -- --test-threads=1, cargo install --path . --debug.
notes:
Implemented transactional TerminalGuard ownership for alternate screen, raw mode, mouse, bracketed paste, keyboard enhancement, and attached Windows console UTF-8 code pages. Added bounded Drop restoration retries and typed fatal lifecycle propagation before provider cache work. Focused terminal tests: 9 passed; slash-init and slash groups passed. Native Windows console and manual Windows Terminal/ConHost acceptance plus full integration gates remain.
Integration gate 2026-08-10: cargo test -- --test-threads=1 passed (1561 passed, 5 ignored; worker bootstrap 7 passed); cargo install --path . --debug passed. Remaining: native Windows console test and manual Unicode/suspend/resume verification in Windows Terminal and ConHost.
Implementation is merged on main through PR #22 (commit c6693e2 within merge 53d5e73). Validate only the combined main build; no individual branch remains to merge. Keep open for Windows Terminal/ConHost code-page and suspend/resume evidence.

title: Report AppContainer root-role conflicts before profile creation
description:
src/sandbox/windows.rs correctly rejects workspace/read-only-cache and configured read/write overlaps, but validate_explicit_root_policy emits generic errors with no overlap direction or recovery. A configured read root containing the private AppContainer control sibling can also be detected only after profile/storage creation, causing avoidable rollback and residue risk.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On Windows, start mini-agent with sandboxing enabled from C:\\Users\\<user>.
2. Leave the default cache under %LOCALAPPDATA%\\zerostack\\cache.
3. Trigger a sandboxed command and observe the expected overlap rejection with only a generic message and no recovery guidance.
design: Classify overlap over already-canonical, component-aware paths and report only closed role names plus direction. For workspace containing cache, advise using a project subdirectory or setting ZS_CACHE_DIR outside the workspace; provide the converse guidance when workspace lies inside cache. Name configured read/write roles for their conflicts. Preflight deterministic cache-parent/control-root conflicts before any AppContainer profile creation. Keep every overlap rejected; never grant both roles to the same tree and never include raw user paths in the diagnostic.
acceptance_criteria: Windows integration tests prove a project workspace with default cache succeeds; C:\Users\<user> containing the default cache is rejected before launch with workspace, read-only application cache, contains direction, and both remedies; cache containing workspace reports the opposite direction; configured overlapping roots report both roles/direction; configured read containing the control root is rejected before profile/journal creation; ordinary/verbatim aliases normalize consistently and reparse/UNC paths remain denied. Run the focused AppContainer tests serially, cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and manually verify sandboxed pwd from a project plus the home-root diagnostic with and without external ZS_CACHE_DIR.
notes:
Implemented closed root-role/direction diagnostics, both workspace/cache remedies, configured-root conflict reporting, pre-profile control-root checks, repeated post-create checks, and ancestor reparse rejection. Added Windows-native policy tests plus macOS source-contract coverage; focused source test passed. Adversarial re-review is clean within this bead. Deeper handle-lifetime TOCTOU is tracked as mini-agent-wbat.12. Native Windows and manual acceptance remain.
Integration gate 2026-08-10: full serial suite and debug install passed. Remaining: native Windows AppContainer integration and manual project/home-root diagnostic verification.
Implementation is merged on main through PR #22 (commit 099ff11 within merge 53d5e73). Validate only the combined main build; no individual branch remains to merge. Keep open for the documented native/manual Windows AppContainer scenarios.
