title: [AUDIT] Bound subagent concurrency, aggregate output, prompt count, and cost
description:
## Problem / security impact
`src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:104-172` truncates individual results but does not bound concurrent fan-out, aggregate output, number of prompts/tasks, duration, or cost. One tool invocation can exhaust runtime/memory or create uncontrolled spend.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:104-172`
- subagent task argument/schema types and configuration
- cancellation/accounting APIs used by subagents
- task-tool tests and user documentation

## Required implementation
Define explicit per-call limits for child count, concurrently running children, aggregate returned bytes/tokens, wall-clock duration, and budget/cost units available from the provider. Validate the complete request before starting work. Use bounded scheduling, propagate cancellation to every child, and stop launching queued work after failure/budget exhaustion. Specify deterministic partial-failure semantics and output ordering. Per-result truncation remains defense in depth, not the aggregate control.

## Acceptance criteria
- Requests over the child/prompt limit are rejected before any child starts.
- Runtime concurrency never exceeds the configured maximum.
- Aggregate output/cost/deadline bounds stop/cancel remaining work and return explicit partial status.
- Cancellation leaves no child task running.
- Mixed success/failure output ordering and accounting are deterministic.

## Validation
Run `cargo test task_tool_limits` and the existing subagent test module. Use a fake executor with concurrency counters, controllable output sizes/delays/cost, and cancellation probes. Assert peak concurrency, number started, aggregate bytes/cost, deadline behavior, deterministic ordering, and zero live children after return. Run the relevant feature combination used by CI plus `cargo test`.
acceptance_criteria: Subagent task invocations enforce preflight count, bounded concurrency, aggregate output/cost/deadline limits, cancellation, and deterministic partial failures.
close_reason: Implemented: bounded subagent prompt count and concurrency, aggregate output/cost/deadline enforcement, cancellation-safe deterministic partial results, provider usage accounting, fake-executor limit tests, and documentation

title: [AUDIT] Prevent hook pipe deadlock and bound hook subprocess resources
description:
## Problem / security impact
`src/extras/hooks/subprocess.rs:89-129` can wait on one pipe while a child fills the other, causing deadlock. Hook processes also need explicit time/output limits and descendant cleanup because hooks execute during agent control flow.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/hooks/subprocess.rs:89-129`
- hook configuration/documentation for limits
- hook subprocess tests

## Required implementation
Drain stdout and stderr concurrently, enforce independent and combined byte caps, and apply a finite default deadline. On timeout, cancellation, cap breach, or consumer failure, kill and reap the complete process tree. Define whether capped output is a hard failure or a truncated hook result; it must not be silently accepted as complete. Preserve required hook stdin and exit-code semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
- A child filling stderr while stdout is idle cannot deadlock; the inverse also holds.
- Infinite and forked hook processes are terminated and reaped.
- Captured output remains within configured/documented limits.
- Timeout/truncation/nonzero-exit results are distinguishable to the hook caller.

## Validation
Run `cargo test hook_subprocess_limits` and `cargo test extras::hooks`. Add deterministic local helper processes for stdout fill, stderr fill, mixed fill, infinite sleep, forked child, and normal hook. Assert wall-clock and byte bounds and no surviving descendants. Run `cargo test`.
acceptance_criteria: Hook subprocesses concurrently drain bounded pipes, time out, clean process trees, and return deterministic timeout/truncation results.
close_reason: Implemented: concurrent bounded hook output draining, finite deadline cleanup, explicit timeout/output-limit statuses, process-tree termination and focused subprocess limit tests

title: [AUDIT] Bound Bash subprocess runtime and streaming output
description:
## Problem / security impact
Bash subprocess execution can run forever or produce unbounded stdout/stderr. Waiting for full output risks memory exhaustion and pipe deadlock, and timeout without process-tree cleanup leaves descendants alive.

## Scope / files
- `src/sandbox.rs:205-279`
- `src/agent/tools/bash.rs:142-197`
- shared subprocess/streaming helpers used by Bash
- Bash tool tests

## Required implementation
Apply a mandatory finite default deadline with an optional lower configured limit, byte caps for stdout, stderr, and combined output, and concurrent draining of both pipes. Stream or buffer incrementally rather than `wait_with_output` on unbounded data. On deadline, cancellation, output cap, or receiver loss, terminate the process group/job object and reap all descendants. Return deterministic timeout/truncation metadata without presenting partial output as complete success. Bounds must apply even when the child emits on only one pipe.

## Acceptance criteria
- Infinite commands terminate within the configured deadline and leave no descendant process.
- Unlimited stdout, unlimited stderr, and mixed output stay within the documented byte cap without deadlock.
- Exit code, timeout, cancellation, and truncation are distinguishable.
- Output order/encoding behavior is documented and stable enough for callers.

## Validation
Run `cargo test bash_resource_limits` and `cargo test agent::tools::bash`. Tests launch an infinite process, a process that forks a persistent child, stdout-only and stderr-only flooders, and a mixed-output process. Assert wall-clock bounds, bounded captured bytes, deterministic status, and that descendant PIDs are gone. Run `cargo test`.
acceptance_criteria: Bash has mandatory deadlines, bounded concurrent stdout/stderr handling, deterministic truncation/error semantics, and process-tree cleanup.
close_reason: Implemented: added mandatory Bash deadlines, bounded concurrent stdout/stderr capture, deterministic timeout/truncation/cancellation statuses, and process-group cleanup; fixed verification dead-code warning

title: [AUDIT] Make atomic writes race-resistant and symlink-safe
description:
## Problem / security impact
The atomic-write helper in `src/fs.rs:34-88` relies on path-based checks and predictable filesystem operations that can be raced or redirected through symlinks. An attacker controlling a writable directory can precreate temporary names or swap parent/final targets between validation and rename.

## Scope / files
- `src/fs.rs:34-88`
- callers that use atomic writes for config/session/tool output
- Unix-focused filesystem security tests; documented non-Unix behavior

## Required implementation
Use descriptor-relative operations and no-follow semantics where the platform supports them. Create the temporary file exclusively in the destination directory with unpredictable names and restrictive permissions, write/sync as required by the existing durability contract, revalidate the approved root and parent immediately before mutation, and atomically rename without following a hostile final symlink. Define replacement behavior for existing regular files, symlinks, directories, and cross-filesystem paths. On platforms lacking equivalent primitives, fail closed for security-sensitive callers or document and test a conservative fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

title: [D2] Enforce full immutable skill identity and lifecycle-safe CRUD
description:
## Outcome
Define full immutable learned-JS artifact identity and lifecycle-safe CRUD so metadata/tests/capabilities cannot drift under one ID and tampered rows never execute.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/artifact.rs`: versioned canonical serialization, full SHA-256 identity, capability/tag/export normalization and typed validation.
- `src/extras/js/skills/store.rs`: identity-validating insert/read/list, embedding persistence, optimistic retire, explicit privacy purge/tombstone APIs.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_store_identity.rs`: canonical vectors, mutation, tamper, collision, lifecycle, and purge fixtures.

`mini-agent-yxy` owns schema/migrations; `mini-agent-y8n` verifier; lifecycle promotion/rollback is Phase 4/5.

## Required implementation
1. Use versioned unambiguous length-prefixed exact UTF-8 encoding over source, ordered embedded tests, ordered exports/signatures, description, normalized ordered tags, full capability tier/allowed-host manifest, and identity schema version.
2. Compute full 64-hex SHA-256 in trusted domain/store code. Operational status/time/telemetry/lineage/row-version/embedding metadata remains outside identity.
3. Reject caller ID mismatch and same-ID/different-payload collision; byte-identical insertion is idempotent. Identity-bearing fields have no update API and legacy short IDs never activate without explicit migration.
4. Recompute identity at insert, active read, and index-load boundaries. Tampered/corrupt rows fail closed before source leaves the store and become diagnosable for quarantine.
5. Implement typed `insert_verified`, `get`, `list_retrievable`, model-versioned embedding persistence, optimistic `retire`, and explicit privacy `purge`. Retirement preserves bytes/lineage; purge removes dependencies and creates a non-secret anti-resurrection tombstone.
6. Return typed non-panicking not-found/stale/database/corruption/collision/capability errors.

## Non-goals
Do not define SQLite schema, run verification tests, generate embeddings, rank results, promote/canary/rollback, or mutate identity-bearing fields.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Canonical test vectors are stable; changing any identity field/order changes ID, while operational changes do not.
- Caller mismatch, row tamper, legacy short ID, malformed capability/metadata, and simulated collision never return executable/retrievable source.
- Byte-identical insert is idempotent; retire is optimistic and reversible only through authorized lifecycle; purge removes dependencies and tombstones identity.
- Active/index reads return only identity-valid lifecycle-eligible rows with exact immutable bytes.

## Verification
Run:
```bash
cargo test --features js,skills skill_store_identity
cargo test --features js,skills skill_store_crud
cargo test --features js,skills skill_store_tamper
cargo test --features js,skills
cargo install --path . --debug
```
Fixtures must cover every identity field/order/normalization/version, operational mutations, caller mismatch, duplicate/collision, DB tamper, legacy IDs, malformed JSON/capability, embedding model metadata, stale retire, purge/tombstone, round trip, and active/index exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: SkillStore recomputes a full SHA-256 over versioned canonical identity data including source and tests, rejects caller/tamper/collision mismatches, and covers the complete CRUD contract including delete.

title: [D2] Enforce SSRF-safe fetch authorization on every destination
description:
## Problem / security impact
A URL-glob permission check alone does not prevent SSRF. Approved hostnames can resolve to loopback/private/link-local/metadata addresses, redirect to them, or change DNS answers between check and connect. Embedded credentials and unsupported schemes create additional ambiguity.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` fetch URL parsing/authorization
- JS permission bridge and `src/permission/checker.rs` `js/fetch` policy
- URL/network policy config and Phase 2 spec
- deterministic resolver/redirect tests

## Required implementation
Parse URLs with one trusted parser; allow only explicitly approved schemes (normally `https`, optionally `http` by policy), reject embedded credentials, fragments/options that are not supported, and malformed/ambiguous hosts. Resolve all addresses before connect and reject loopback, private, link-local, multicast, unspecified, reserved, and cloud metadata destinations for IPv4/IPv6, including mapped forms. Bind connection to authorized resolution results or revalidate at connect to address DNS rebinding. Send `js/fetch` permission for the normalized URL and exact resolved destination policy. Disable automatic redirects and repeat scheme, credentials, resolution, destination, allow-list, and permission authorization at every hop with a finite hop count. Define proxy behavior so it cannot bypass destination policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Localhost, RFC1918, link-local, IPv6 local, multicast/reserved, and common metadata endpoints are denied by default even via hostname.
- Embedded credentials and non-approved schemes are denied.
- DNS answer changes and redirects to denied destinations cannot bypass checks.
- Every hop has a finite permission wait and denial starts no request to that destination.
- Public allowed destinations work under explicit policy.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_fetch_ssrf_policy` with an injected fake resolver and local servers. Cover all address classes, IPv4-mapped IPv6, decimal/alternate host forms accepted by the parser, rebinding, redirect chains/loops, credential URLs, schemes, proxy configuration, Allow/Deny/Ask/timeout/channel closure, and an allowed public-test address without Internet access. Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox`.
acceptance_criteria: Fetch authorizes allowed schemes and every resolved/redirect destination, rejects credentials and non-public/metadata addresses including DNS rebinding, and handles permission outcomes with deterministic local tests.

title: [D2] Implement bounded fetch transport with redirect control
description:
## Problem / security impact
The proposed `reqwest::blocking::Client::new()` plus `resp.text()` has no connect/read/total deadline or body bound and follows redirects implicitly. It can hang the JS thread, exhaust memory/decompression, or bypass authorization at a redirect.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `FetchResult` and fetch transport
- `Cargo.toml` reqwest features
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` cancellation/result state as needed
- deterministic local HTTP test fixtures

## Required implementation
Construct/inject a configured blocking client with finite connect, per-read, and total host-call deadlines. Disable automatic redirects; return each redirect target to the authorization layer for revalidation before the next request. Bound request body, headers, response headers, compressed bytes, decompressed bytes, and returned text. Stream incrementally rather than unbounded `text()`. Support only explicitly documented methods/options and reject invalid headers/encodings as typed JS errors. Propagate cancellation and ensure a fetch failure does not kill the JS thread. Do not use public Internet in tests.

## Acceptance criteria
- Slow connect/read and endless bodies terminate within limits.
- Compressed and decompressed response limits are both enforced.
- Redirects are not followed by the transport without authorization of the new target.
- Returned status/body/truncation-or-error semantics are deterministic.
- Cancellation/channel errors leave the JS thread usable.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_fetch_transport` against local TCP/HTTP fixtures for normal response, slow headers/body, endless body, oversized headers/body, compression bomb, redirect, cancellation, malformed response, and recovery. Then run `cargo test --features js,sandbox` and `cargo test --features js`.
acceptance_criteria: Fetch transport uses an injected bounded client, finite connect/read/total deadlines, compressed/decompressed/body caps, manual redirect handoff, cancellation, and deterministic local tests.

title: [D2] Enforce JS file allow-lists at final read/write operations
description:
## Problem / security impact
Checking an allow-list before `std::fs::read_to_string`/`write` leaves a check/use race and can follow a swapped symlink. Compile-time signature differences also risk a safe sandbox build but unsafe plain-JS build.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `make_read_file`, `make_write_file`, and registration
- JS engine/tool configuration plumbing
- filesystem host integration tests

## Required implementation
Thread one `AllowConfig` policy through production host registration whenever file globals exist; do not create a parallel unrestricted signature. Apply the Phase 1 `js/read_file`/`js/write_file` permission check and Phase 2 allow-list, then revalidate containment immediately at descriptor-relative/no-follow open or mutation. For writes, use the race-resistant atomic-write contract and safely handle nonexistent targets. Treat allow-list as an additional restriction: permission approval cannot override a denied root unless an explicitly designed higher-level policy says so. Handle policy/config/channel errors as JS errors with no I/O.

## Acceptance criteria
- In-root authorized reads/writes succeed; either permission denial or allow-list denial prevents I/O.
- Final/parent symlink swaps between check and operation cannot escape the root.
- Plain `js` and `js,sandbox` feature rows do not expose an unrestricted alternate closure.
- Empty lists and malformed config follow the deny-safe policy.
- Errors do not panic or kill the JS thread.

## Validation

Integration tests race final/parent symlink swaps, exercise nonexistent targets and sibling-prefix paths, combine Allow/Deny with allowed/denied roots, and assert no outside file is read or changed. title: [D2] Define canonical, symlink-safe JS file allow-list policy
description:
## Problem / security impact
The proposed allow-list uses raw glob/prefix matching and treats an empty list as unrestricted. Traversal, sibling prefixes, symlinks, and nonexistent write targets can escape the intended roots.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/host.rs` `AllowConfig` and policy helper
- config schema/loading for JS read/write roots
- `docs/specs/phase-2-sandbox.md`
- path-policy unit tests

## Required implementation
Define an explicit base directory for relative configuration and normalize policies into absolute component-aware roots at load/startup. Decide containment using canonical paths and path components, never raw string prefixes or raw glob matches. For nonexistent write targets, canonicalize the nearest existing parent and validate the remaining relative components. Define final/parent symlink behavior and reject ambiguous paths. Empty or invalid lists must deny all; unrestricted access requires an explicit documented opt-in and still remains permission-gated. Separate read and write roots, and return typed reasons safe for JS/user display.

## Acceptance criteria
- `/safe` does not allow `/safe-evil`, `../` escapes, alternate separators, or symlink escapes.
- Relative policies resolve against one documented base, independent of process CWD.
- Nonexistent write targets under an approved canonical parent can be represented safely; escaping targets cannot.
- Empty/malformed policy denies rather than grants unrestricted access.
- The helper returns an authorization decision only; final operations revalidate separately.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox js_file_allow_policy`. Tests cover exact root, descendants, sibling-prefix, traversal, relative root/CWD changes, existing and dangling symlinks, parent symlink, nonexistent target, empty list, malformed path, and explicit unrestricted opt-in if provided. Run `cargo test --features js,sandbox` and `cargo test --features js`.

  1. Create oneshot channel: (reply_tx, reply_rx)

     - Timeout → Ok("JS error: execution timed out (30s limit exceeded)".into())
     - OomKilled → Ok("JS error: out of memory (64 MiB limit exceeded)".into())

Note: Error and Timeout/OomKilled return Ok(...) — errors are surfaced as tool output for LLM self-correction, not as Rust errors.

title: [D2] Map JS timeout, OOM, jobs, and exceptions without panics
description:
## Problem / security impact
The bead's proposed OOM rule—classifying a later `Runtime::new()` failure—does not identify OOM in the runtime that exhausted memory. Exception handling can also assume an object exception and panic on primitive thrown values. Promise jobs and endless microtasks need the same deadline as eval.

## Scope / files
- `src/extras/js/engine.rs` `run_step` and pending-job drain
- `src/extras/js/types.rs` `JsOutcome`
- `src/extras/js/tests/`
- rquickjs 0.12 behavior documented in code comments/tests

## Required implementation
Determine and encode the verified rquickjs 0.12 signal emitted by the current runtime when its memory limit is exceeded; construct `JsOutcome::OomKilled` from that signal. Do not infer prior OOM from the next runtime construction. Set memory/stack limits and the interrupt handler before eval. Drain pending jobs with the same overall deadline and a bounded job/turn policy so endless microtasks time out. Extract object exception stacks when available, but safely stringify primitive throws and rejected-Promise reasons. Map timeout, OOM, syntax/runtime error, and rejected job deterministically without message-substring ambiguity where typed APIs are available. Always drop the runtime and keep the JS thread alive.

## Acceptance criteria
- A current-runtime allocation limit produces `OomKilled`.
- Infinite eval and endless microtasks produce `Timeout` within the configured bound.
- `throw 'x'`, `throw 1`, `throw null`, syntax errors, and rejected Promises return safe errors without panic.
- Stack/line information is included when available.
- A fresh step after every OOM/timeout/error evaluates `1+1` to `2` with no leaked globals.

## Validation
Run `cargo test --features js js_outcome_mapping` and `cargo test --features js`. Add deterministic tests for OOM, infinite loop, endless microtasks, primitive/object throws, rejected jobs, syntax errors, and post-failure recovery/state isolation. Expected variants must be asserted directly, not by broad string matching. Run `cargo test` for feature-gate cleanliness.
acceptance_criteria: Current-runtime OOM, timeout, rejected jobs, primitive throws, syntax/runtime errors map deterministically to JsOutcome variants, never panic, and a fresh runtime succeeds afterward.
close_reason: Implemented: deterministic current-runtime OOM, timeout, pending-job, exception, and Promise rejection outcome mapping with bounded microtask draining and recovery tests

- pub(crate) fn run_step(code: &str) -> JsOutcome: creates fresh Runtime::new() EVERY call (never reuses)
  - set_memory_limit(MEMORY_LIMIT) and set_max_stack_size(STACK_LIMIT) on every new Runtime
  - deadline = Instant::now() + STEP_TIMEOUT; set_interrupt_handler BEFORE ctx.eval()
  - calls register_host_globals(&ctx) (implemented in host.rs, imported here)
  - ctx.with(|ctx| ctx.eval::<Value, _>(code)) — NOT eval::<(), _>
  - Maps Err(rquickjs::Error::Exception) → timeout detection → JsOutcome::Timeout or JsOutcome::Error with stack trace
  - Maps Ok(v) → JsOutcome::Value / JsOutcome::Void
  - RAII order: Context dropped before Runtime (enforced by local scope)

run_step is pub(crate) — NOT pub — because Phase 3 verify_skill() calls it cross-module (src/extras/js/skills/).

Invariant 1: Fresh Runtime per step — no Runtime struct field, no static/thread_local Runtime.
Invariant 3: set_interrupt_handler deadline before ctx.eval() in every code path.

title: Group diff rows into multi-line feed blocks instead of one Block per row
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: memory
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: Every edit/write diff row (default `max_diff_lines` = 200, cap `MAX_DIFF_LINES` = 1000) and every `/git` observation line becomes its own feed `Block` inserted with `place_after_anchor`, which does a reverse scan of all blocks for the anchor, a forward `any(running)` scan, a `VecDeque::insert` shift, a layout `touch` and a prune check — per row. A `Block` is ~510 B inline (24 B String + ~170 B `MdCache` slot + ~70 B `TokenCache` + two render caches + reasoning/anchor fields) plus its own `Arc<Vec<LineEntry>>` segment; 200 rows cost ~120 KB and ~1.6 M block visits per edit at the 4096-block cap, versus ~15 KB and one insert when grouped. Worse, `MAX_FEED_BLOCKS` = 4096 means roughly 20 edits fill the feed and older transcript starts being pruned ("[earlier feed content omitted]") even in a short session.
- WHERE: src/ui/events.rs:144-157 `push_mutation_diff`: `for row in diff.rows.iter().take(limit) { ... feed.place_after_anchor(anchor, style, format!("{prefix}{}", sanitize_for_review(&row.text))); }`; src/ui/app.rs:5101-5118 `drain_git_observations`: `for line in observation.text.lines().take(limit) { ... self.renderer.feed_mut().place_after_anchor(&observation.id, style, sanitize_output(line)); count += 1; }`; src/ui/feed.rs:709-726 `place_after_anchor` -> 819-837 `anchor_insert_position` (`rposition(...)`, `skip(position).any(|block| block.running)`) -> `self.blocks.insert(position, block); self.prune_completed_prefix();`; `Block` struct feed.rs:147-182; `MAX_FEED_BLOCKS` feed.rs:16; default 200 at src/config/mod.rs:730-733; `MAX_DIFF_LINES` src/agent/tools/mutation_diff.rs:10.
- HOW: In both loops accumulate consecutive rows of the same `BlockStyle` into one `String` joined by `'\n'` and call `place_after_anchor` once per style run (a `DiffHunk` row starts a new run). Rendering is identical: `push_plain_rows` (feed.rs:1626) splits on `'\n'`, wraps each line separately and colours by block style, so row text, order, wrapping and colour do not change. Optionally add `Feed::place_blocks_after_anchor(anchor, impl IntoIterator<Item=(BlockStyle, String)>)` that computes `anchor_insert_position` once and inserts the run sequentially. Keep the "(+N more diff rows omitted)" / "clipped" notices as their own blocks. title: Compile QuickJS C sources at opt-level 3 in the dev install
description:

- WHAT: The daily build is `cargo install --path . --debug`. `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 1` applies to `rquickjs-sys`, whose build script compiles the QuickJS C sources with `cc::Build` and no explicit optimisation flag, so `cc` takes `OPT_LEVEL=1` from Cargo and the entire JS interpreter, parser, GC and bytecode loader run at -O1. title: Stop the skills admission worker polling SQLite at 10 Hz while idle
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: In every proposal-enabled `skills` session the `skill-admission` thread wakes every 100 ms forever and runs two `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions (sweep + claim), each with a freshly parsed statement: 20 write-lock acquisitions and 20 SQL compiles per second, ~0.3-0.5% of a core continuously, plus write-lock churn against the telemetry writer which runs with `busy_timeout(0)` and retries at 10 ms (src/extras/js/skills/telemetry.rs:745-750, :27-28), so idle polling can cause spurious busy retries. Run `sweep_exhausted_proposals` only when `claim_due_proposal` returned `None` and at most once per fallback period. Switch the sweep/claim statements to `prepare_cached`. title: Make `--continue` peek `working_dir` from the file head instead of reading and parsing whole foreign sessions
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: io
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: `find_recent_sessions_for_workspace` walks sessions newest-first and, for every file until `limit` matches, reads the ENTIRE file (up to 8 MiB) and runs `serde_json::from_str::<WorkspacePeek>` over the whole document (serde still tokenises every byte to skip unknown fields) just to compare `working_dir`. `working_dir` is serialized at struct position ~40 (session/mod.rs:915), after `messages` (:840) and `compactions` (:847), so the head-peek technique already used for `name` (NAME_PEEK_BYTES = 4 KiB, storage.rs:756-787, mini-agent-hf54t) cannot apply. A user with N recent sessions from other workspaces pays N full reads+parses (N x up to 8 MiB) on every `--continue`.

Generalise `peek_session_name` into `peek_session_head(path) -> Option<(Option<String> name, Option<String> working_dir)>` that stops once both keys are seen (or at the 4 KiB cut); in `find_recent_sessions_for_workspace` use the peeked `working_dir` and fall back to the existing full read only when the head did not contain it (legacy files). title: Stop deep-cloning and double-encoding the Session on every native-bearing turn-end save
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: memory
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: For an Anthropic native session (`startup_requires_publication(.., matches!(&client, AnyClient::Anthropic(_)), ..)` startup.rs:1392), every settled turn does: (1) a full `Session::clone()` on the UI task (`PreparedSave::Native(Box::new(session.clone()))`), (2) in the blocking writer a full JSON encode + SHA-256 (`checked_publication_encoded`), then (3) if the publication phase is `Active`, a SECOND `session.clone()` and a SECOND full encode for the in-flight projection, and the first encoding is discarded (`encoded.filter(|_| !in_flight)`). Session JSON is bounded at 8 MiB (`storage.rs:8 MAX_SESSION_BYTES`), `messages` up to 100k entries, plus `native_history` (up to 4 MiB, native_replay.rs:321) is inside the clone. Worst case per turn ~ 2 deep clones (tens of MB of heap) + 16 MiB of JSON + one 8 MiB SHA-256, repeated every turn of a long session.
- WHERE: `src/session/storage.rs:243-247` (`prepare_save`: `return Ok(PreparedSave::Native(Box::new(session.clone())));`), `src/session/storage.rs:303-309` (`save_session_deferred`: `deferred::Snapshot::Native(Box::new(session.clone()))`), `src/session/native_publication.rs:429-438` (`checked_publication_encoded` -> `serialize_bounded_session` + `Sha256::digest`), `:571-596` (`save_snapshot_inner` -> `write_projection_with(session, phase == Phase::Active, Some(encoded))`), `:604-620` (`let snapshot = if in_flight { let mut copy = session.clone(); copy.native_frontier = session.native_frontier.in_flight_projection(); ... let json = match encoded.filter(|_| !in_flight) { Some(encoded) => encoded, None => super::storage::serialize_bounded_session(snapshot)?,`). The writer uses the Session only for: owner checks (`checked_publication_owner` :440-456: `lease.matches(session)`, `Arc::ptr_eq(cell, session.native_frontier.publication_cell())`), `validate_native_persistence()`, and `publish_checkpoint(session, bytes)` (`lock.rs:303-314` reads `self.matches(session)` and `session.id`).
- HOW: (a) In `write_projection_with`, replace the clone with a thread-local serialization override for `native_frontier` (same pattern as `SharedObservations::install_frozen_serialization`, `background_observation.rs:268`, used in `serialize_bounded_session` to avoid cloning for mini-agent-hcb3s): serialize `session` once with the projected frontier installed; the `encoded` argument then becomes unnecessary for the in-flight case. (b) Replace `PreparedSave::Native(Box<Session>)`/`Snapshot::Native(Box<Session>)` with a capture struct built on the caller side: `{ id: CompactString, encoded_current: String (for the digest check), encoded_projected: Option<String>, publication: NativePublication (clone of the small handle), frontier: NativeFrontier (Arc clone), lease: Arc<...> }` so the writer can run the same owner/revision/digest checks and `held.publish(&id, bytes)` without a Session; `validate_native_persistence` runs on the caller before capture (it already does for Legacy). Keep the superseded-revision drop logic (`drop_superseded`). Note the serialization then runs on the UI task unless moved to the blocking writer with the frozen-serialization pattern; measure both.
- VERIFY: `src/session/native_publication.rs::native_publication_turn_end_save_is_deferred_off_the_calling_thread` (:1841), `native_publication_deferred_snapshot_never_overwrites_a_newer_checkpoint` (:1886), `native_publication_current_progress_seals_counters_and_rejects_old_clones` (:2680), `src/session/storage.rs::prepared_save_of_a_legacy_session_is_the_exact_serialized_bytes_without_a_clone` (:1403), `serialization_with_bound_observations_matches_the_frozen_clone_exactly` (:1386). New test: extend the test-only `SERIALIZE_BOUNDED_CALLS` counter (storage.rs:50) to assert exactly one `serialize_bounded_session` per deferred native save, and assert no `Session::clone` via a test-only clone counter.
close_reason: Removed the in-flight projection's deep Session clone (thread-local encoding guard). The caller-side clone stays because deferring it would move the full encode onto the UI task, against turn_end_save_is_deferred_off_the_calling_thread.

title: Drop reqwest's `rustls-no-provider` feature from patched google-cloud-auth (dead second TLS client stack)
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: binary-size
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: The normal build links two TLS client stacks: native-tls (root `reqwest` feature) AND rustls' TLS layer (`hyper-rustls`, `tokio-rustls`, `rustls-platform-verifier`, `rustls-platform-verifier-android`) pulled solely by the patched google-cloud-auth's `reqwest` feature `rustls-no-provider`. So the rustls TLS layer is compiled, linked and its platform-verifier/security-framework glue initialised for nothing. google-cloud-auth needs the `rustls` crate only for RSA JWT signing (`credentials/service_account.rs:87 use rustls::sign::Signer;`, `crypto_provider.rs:17`).
- WHERE: `patched-deps/google-cloud-auth/Cargo.toml:128-136` (`[dependencies.reqwest] features = ["form","json","query","rustls-no-provider"]`). `cargo tree -e normal -i hyper-rustls` -> only parent `reqwest v0.13.4`; `-i rustls-platform-verifier` -> only `reqwest`. Root `Cargo.toml:124-130` (reqwest `native-tls`), `Cargo.toml:170` (`rustls = { ... features = ["ring"] }` kept for signing), `src/provider_vertex.rs:135` (`rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider().install_default()`).
- HOW: Remove `"rustls-no-provider"` from that feature list (keep `form`, `json`, `query`); keep the `[dependencies.rustls]` entry. Update `Cargo.lock` only via `cargo test`/`cargo install --path . --debug`. Expected: 4 crates (hyper-rustls, tokio-rustls, rustls-platform-verifier, rustls-platform-verifier-android) out of the build and the rustls client/handshake code paths out of the binary; TLS behaviour unchanged (native-tls was already the active backend). CAVEAT: CLAUDE.md says dependency changes edit only the root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock; this bead needs an explicit decision to touch `patched-deps/google-cloud-auth/Cargo.toml` (record it in `patched-deps/google-cloud-auth/UPSTREAM.md`). It is the small alternative to the larger "unify production on one TLS stack (rustls only)" bead in this epic — pick one direction, not both: this one keeps native-tls as the single client stack; the other removes native-tls instead.
- VERIFY: existing `src/provider_vertex_tests.rs::vertex81_config_adc_typed_token_and_custom_isolation`, `vertex81_real_sdk_adc_and_declared_token_stream_tools_usage_and_exact_native_view` (service-account JWT signing path still works via ring). `cargo tree -e normal -i hyper-rustls` must print nothing; `-i rustls` must list only google-cloud-auth and mini-agent. Measure: `ls -l target/debug/mini-agent` before/after and `cargo tree -e normal --prefix none | sort -u | wc -l` (497 -> 493).

title: Validate the `/add` walk's workspace binding every ~1000 entries, not every 25-entry batch
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: io
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: The blocking walk calls `workspace.validate()` before every batch send, i.e. once per 25 entries. `validate` (paths.rs 918-945) = `canonicalize` (lstat per component) + `checked_path_metadata` + `checked_file_metadata` + two `ensure_same_file` ~ 10-15 syscalls, so a 20k-entry walk performs ~800 validates ~ 10k extra syscalls, a sizeable share of the walk's own syscall budget. Same pattern in `load_files_sync`.
- WHERE: `src/ui/pickers/file.rs` 401-406: `workspace.validate().is_ok() && walk_entries_streaming(workspace.root(), &cancel, |batch| { all.extend(batch.iter().cloned()); workspace.validate().is_ok() && tx.send(batch).is_ok() })`; 413-416 `remember_walk`; 426-432 `load_files_sync`.
- HOW: Keep the validate before the first batch; inside the closure validate only every N batches (counter, N = 40 -> 1000 entries); add `&& workspace.validate().is_ok()` to the `finished` condition before `remember_walk` so a replaced root is never remembered. The UI side still validates on every poll (`try_finish_loading` 465-469, 50 ms tick while loading) and on accept (`selected_path` 652-657), so retirement latency is unchanged.
- VERIFY: `busy67_add_walk_drops_results_when_captured_root_is_replaced`, `busy67_finished_add_picker_rejects_replaced_root_before_enter`, `every_press_shows_the_cached_walk_and_revalidates_it_once`. New: with the test-only `VALIDATE_CALLS` counter (paths.rs 920) assert a 2,000-file `/add` walk performs <=4 validates instead of ~80.
close_reason: Implemented on main in the 2026-10-20 vb5vw wave (perf/<lane> merge), with the bead's pinning tests.

title: Share walk entries by Arc so `@`/`/add ` activation and the walk thread stop deep-cloning every entry
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: memory
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: Each `CacheEntry` owns `path: PathBuf` + `lower: String` (2 heap blocks). Activating the picker from the snapshot cache deep-clones the whole list on the UI task while holding the global mutex, and the walk thread clones every batch again into `all`. At the 20k-file cap that is ~40k allocations + ~3 MB memcpy per `@` press, plus ~40k allocations per walk, with three copies (snapshot, picker, `all`) alive during a walk (~10 MB).
- WHERE: `src/ui/pickers/file.rs` — `struct CacheEntry` 138-147; `cached_walk` 110-117: `(snapshot.finished.elapsed() <= WALK_REUSE_STALE).then(|| (snapshot.entries.clone(), snapshot.finished))`; walk closure 398-417: `all.extend(batch.iter().cloned());` (404 and 409); `filter_from` 611-618; constructors 164-177; `walk_entries_streaming` 778-786.
- HOW: Change the fields to `text: Arc<str>` (the relative path as shown) and `lower: Option<Arc<str>>` (None when `text` is already lowercase, which is most repo paths), keep `is_dir`, `kind`, `description`. Clone becomes two refcount bumps; `filter_from` matches on `entry.lower.as_deref().unwrap_or(&entry.text)` and pushes `PathBuf::from(&*entry.text)` only for the <=50 matches; `walk_entries_streaming` builds `Arc::from(rel)`. Optionally precompute the virtual rows once in `InputEditor::set_mcp_resources`/`set_agent_mentions` (`src/ui/input/mod.rs` 524-539) as `Vec<CacheEntry>` and clone them in `start_file_picker` (660-690) instead of running `format!` + `to_lowercase` per resource/persona on every `@`.
- VERIFY: file.rs tests `char_input_on_a_20k_cache_scans_once_and_matches_a_naive_filter`, `every_press_shows_the_cached_walk_and_revalidates_it_once`, `streamed_batches_filter_only_new_entries_with_the_rescan_result`, `draw_uses_the_cached_directory_flag_without_touching_the_filesystem`, `opaque_resource_completion_preserves_the_operand_without_opening_a_walk`; input/mod.rs `pasting_into_an_open_file_picker_extends_the_query_in_one_edit`; app.rs `busy67_*` picker tests. New: test-only accessor asserting `Arc::ptr_eq` between a snapshot entry's `text` and the activated picker's entry; time `cached_walk` on a synthetic 20k snapshot (<1 ms vs several ms).
close_reason: Implemented on main in the 2026-10-20 vb5vw wave (perf/<lane> merge), with the bead's pinning tests.

title: Build the aarch64-musl release artifact on the native ARM runner instead of QEMU
description:

- Dimension: ci-cost
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: release.yml builds `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` on `ubuntu-latest` (x86_64) through `cross` + `docker/setup-qemu-action`, so the C toolchain (vendored OpenSSL from `Cargo.toml:174-175`, the embedded Git 2.56 build, ring, rusqlite is optional) and the whole 380-crate release build at `opt-level = 3`, `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1` run twice (full and `--no-default-features`, lines 224 and 249) under CPU emulation. title: Run the Linux `test` rows with the parallel test runner (serial is duplicated by `parallel-test-smoke`)
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: test-cost
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: all 14 Linux `test` rows and 6 macOS rows execute ~5,500 tests with `--test-threads=1`, while `parallel-test-smoke` already runs the same default suite under the standard parallel runner on both OSes and is a required job. The crate ships a reader/writer process-env lock for exactly this (`src/tests/mod.rs:15-140`). Serial execution multiplies test wall time (not compile time) on every row: on an 8-vCPU Linux runner the suite's run phase is several times longer than parallel.
- WHERE: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:666-668` (`Test (...) on Linux`: `cargo test --locked ${{ matrix.features }} -- --test-threads=1 --skip ...`), `:673-676` (macOS row), `:811-876` (`parallel-test-smoke`, comment at 811-813 states serial rows exist so "only this job sees the load of the standard parallel runner").

Then the ubuntu entry of `parallel-test-smoke` is redundant with the default (`""`) Linux row: restrict its matrix to `macos-latest` (line 819-820, `os: ${{ fromJSON(needs.changes.outputs.test_os) }}` -> keep only macOS). If a specific row flakes in parallel, pin only that row with `--test-threads=1` rather than all 14. title: Gate the Bedrock and Vertex provider crates behind `bedrock`/`vertex` default features
description:
- Priority: P2
- Dimension: dependencies
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: the seven `aws-*` crates and `google-cloud-auth` (with google-cloud-gax/rpc/wkt, serde_with, jiff, time, ...) are unconditional dependencies although they serve exactly two provider back-ends. `cargo tree` shows 54 crates reachable only through them (aws-config, aws-credential-types, aws-runtime, aws-sdk-sso, aws-sdk-ssooidc, aws-sdk-sts, aws-sigv4, 10 aws-smithy-*, aws-types, google-cloud-auth/gax/rpc/wkt, base64 0.23, base64-simd, block-buffer 0.12, bytes-utils, chacha20, cmov, const-oid, cpufeatures 0.3, crypto-common 0.2, ctutils, deranged, digest 0.11, either, hex, hmac, hybrid-array, jiff, jiff-core, num-conv, pin-utils, powerfmt, rand 0.10, regex-lite, sha1, sha2 0.11, time, time-core, urlencoding, xmlparser). title: CI test-impact selection: skip jobs whose inputs did not change (test-only scope + per-job pass fingerprints)
description:
WHAT: CI re-runs the full ~80-job matrix (incl. Windows/macOS) for any non-docs change, even a one-line test fix whose production inputs are identical to an already-green commit (observed 2026-10-19: test-only fixes re-ran every Windows/macOS job). GitHub results are per-commit and the changes job only distinguishes docs-only vs code.

HOW:
1. Test-only scope in the changes job: classify the diff as docs | tests | code. 'tests' = every changed path is test-only by PATH (src/tests/**, any *_tests.rs, src/**/tests/**, tests/**, test fixtures) — production files with inline #[cfg(test)] modules count as code. For 'tests' scope run fmt/policy, Linux clippy and the Linux test rows (+ parallel-test-smoke ubuntu); skip macOS/Windows test rows, platform smokes, packaging/install, vscode and heavy gates — EXCEPT when a changed test path is platform-specific (path or name contains windows/macos/seatbelt/appcontainer/lpac/bwrap/linux, or the file is cfg(target_os)-gated as a whole), then also run that platform's rows. ci-success accepts skipped jobs only for this scope on push/PR.
2. Per-job pass fingerprints: each expensive job computes a fingerprint = SHA-256 over (its input class files from git ls-files — 'production' = all tracked files except docs/** not embedded or test-read, src/tests/**, *_tests.rs, tests/**; 'production+tests' for jobs that run tests — plus feature row, runner OS/ImageOS, toolchain, Cargo.lock, and the workflow file). After a successful job on a push to main, save a marker via actions/cache keyed ci-pass-<job-id>-<fingerprint>; at job start, lookup-only restore: on hit, skip the remaining steps and succeed with a notice naming the fingerprint. Never on tags/schedule/dispatch (always run). PR runs may READ main's markers but never write.
3. Fail open everywhere: unresolvable base, missing git history, or any classification doubt -> full matrix.

VERIFY: policy tests under scripts/tests for: scope classification (docs/tests/code, inline-test production file = code, platform-specific test path keeps its platform, mixed diff = code), ci_success acceptance per scope/event, fingerprint input sets (a docs-only change does not change 'production'; a test change changes only 'production+tests'; workflow change invalidates all), tags/schedule/dispatch never skip. Docs: CONTRIBUTING.md CI cost policy.
close_reason: Implemented on ci/test-impact (de8b7e0e, f801e060, e058fd26), merged to main: scripts/ci_scope.py test-only scope, scripts/ci_fingerprint.py + .github/actions/ci-fingerprint pass markers (main-push write only, never on tag/schedule/dispatch, containment gates never skipped); 339 policy tests OK.

title: No way to stop per-command approvals for read-only shell commands in standard mode
description:
Source: feedback B2. Verified on HEAD.

Facts: `(a)` grants only the exact command (suggest_pattern returns the input unchanged for bash, src/ui/utils.rs:337); `(w)`/`(f)` cover file edits/folders only (:288-292, :39). Built-in bash allow list (src/permission/mod.rs:740-748) is only pwd, git status, cargo check/build/test/fmt/clippy, pip list — ls/cat/grep/sed -n/git log all prompt. Options line (:36-44, :55) doesn't mention Shift+Tab/yolo. An Opus audit needed 26 approvals for read-only commands.

Fix: classify a conservative set of read-only commands as auto-allowed in standard mode (careful with sed -i, find -exec/-delete, redirections, pipes into writers — note whole script is the permission key), and/or add an "allow all non-destructive shell this session" option; mention Shift+Tab in the prompt.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only repository analysis (ls/cat/grep/rg/find/sed -n/head/tail/wc/git log|show|diff|status) runs without per-command approvals; destructive commands still ask; prompt help mentions Shift+Tab/yolo; tests in permission checker.
close_reason: [done] New src/permission/readonly_shell.rs: lexer + allowlist (ls cat head tail wc grep rg find sed -n git log/show/diff/status/blame/rev-parse/ls-files). Rejects > < $ backtick \ ( ) { } # @ single &, tee/xargs/anything else, env assignments, find -exec/-delete/-fprint*, sed -i/w/e, rg --pre/-z, tail -f, git -c/-C/--output/--ext-diff, paths outside workdir/~/.. . Hooked in PermissionChecker::check_inner: Standard mode, shell, no matched rule, would-ask -> Allow; git withheld when sandbox is DegradedUnavailable. Prompt options now end with Shift+Tab/yolo hint (appended last so (w) is not truncated). Docs in CONFIG.md. | Notes: Updated existing tests whose premise changed: checker_tests (ls -la / git status | cat / git status "--short" now allowed; git status --verbose replaced with git commit --verbose). Residual risk: path confinement is lexical (symlinks inside workspace pointing outside not resolved). @ rejected for PowerShell splatting. Did not add 'allow all non-destructive session' option. No subprocess/config-loading code touched, so inventory/config tests not run. FOLLOWUP bfbd7d93: paths resolved with checker resolver, must be in workspace and pass read deny/isolation; -R/-L/-H/--follow refused; recursive (grep -r, rg, find) only with Enforced sandbox. Symlink residual risk closed. | merged to main via fb/f1-git-permission (2026-10-19).

title: Permission prompt is written into the transcript and also pinned, so it shows twice and stays
description:
Source: feedback B1 (reporter-local bead mini-agent-tz86 partly, never pushed). Verified on HEAD.

Root cause: PermissionApproval::show (src/ui/permission_handler.rs:304-305) writes header+options via renderer.write_line, then sets renderer.permission_prompt (:306). finish() (:272) clears only the pinned panel, so the transcript copy remains; pressing `a` adds a third line "-> will allow: …" (:517). Long shell requests take most of the screen twice.

Fix: render pending requests only in the pinned panel; after the decision leave at most one compact line (e.g. `✓ allowed shell: <truncated>`).
acceptance_criteria: A pending request appears once (pinned panel only); after answering, the transcript holds at most one compact line for it.
close_reason: [done] show() no longer writes header/options to transcript (pinned panel only); '-> will allow' and per-grant 'allowed ... for this session' lines removed; one compact line '✓ allowed (this session) shell: <60 chars>' / '✗ denied ...' written after the decision (decision_line, tested). | Notes: Abort/stop paths leave no line. d10 nav keys and d7 timing code untouched; no renderer edits. | merged to main via fb/f4-ui-prompts (2026-10-19).

title: Build prerequisites and Git runtime bootstrap error don't name OS packages (curl-config / libcurl dev)
description:
Source: feedback A13. Verified on HEAD.

Symptom: `make install` failed after compiling everything: `Git build toolchain program is unavailable: curl-config` / `provision the documented native toolchain or supply MINI_AGENT_GIT_RUNTIME_BUNDLE`; fixed by `apt install libcurl4-openssl-dev`. Another team member hit an install error too.

Gaps: README.md:391-392 says only "native C, curl and zlib development toolchain"; docs/development/git-runtime-bootstrap.md has no package names; scripts/git_runtime_build.rs:132 (via build.rs:7) and scripts/build-git-runtime.py:269-272 name the program, not the package.

Fix: list packages per distro (Debian/Ubuntu: build-essential libcurl4-openssl-dev zlib1g-dev python3; plus Fedora/macOS equivalents) in README and in the error; optionally preflight before compiling the dependency graph.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh Ubuntu machine the first failure message names the exact package (libcurl4-openssl-dev etc.); README lists per-distro packages and notes prebuilt archives already contain the payload.
close_reason: [done] README table of per-distro packages, bootstrap doc, python toolchain_identity error and build-script errors name apt/dnf/xcode packages (curl-config -> libcurl4-openssl-dev). | Notes: scripts/git_runtime_build.rs strings only; reached by build.rs and compiled during every cargo test. | merged to main via fb/f3-config-startup (2026-10-19).

title: No token-based session budget for providers without prices
description:
Source: feedback A12. Verified on HEAD.

Facts: existing limits are turn_token_budget (per turn, src/config/keys.rs:125), max_budget_usd (USD, keys.rs:126) and subagent task_max_cost_units. Nothing bounds total session tokens, so unpriced providers (and /cron, which warns "scheduled turns are unbounded in spend") have no ceiling. The three audit runs used ~19.5M subagent input tokens.

Fix: add a session-level token budget (input and/or total) enforced like max_budget_usd, including subagents and cron fires.
acceptance_criteria: A token budget (e.g. max_session_input_tokens) stops a session/cron when no price is known; documented in CONFIG.md; tests.
close_reason: [done] Config max_session_input_tokens / max_session_total_tokens (global-only, stripped from project layers, editor refuses project writes); counted in spend::Account.observe, enforced in admit/admit_effect, shared by subagents and cron; cron warning and TUI/ACP cron gating treat them as a ceiling; resume adds ledger history; docs in CONFIG.md, COST_TRACKING.md, COMMANDS.md. | Notes: No new env var, no CLI flag. Not added to --print limits list or /cost output. Overshoot by an admitted request as with USD. | merged to main via fb/f3-config-startup (2026-10-19).

title: js read_file denial carries no reason; default config (no js-read-roots) denies every workspace read
description:
Source: feedback A11 (Observed). Logic verified on HEAD.

Root cause: js tool built with cfg.js_read_roots (src/agent/builder.rs:817-824), None by default (src/config/mod.rs:444). host.rs:398-402 returns Deny(NoConfiguredRoots) when no roots and not unrestricted, including workspace-relative paths (authorize_bound_read, host.rs:291, :3224-3228). broker.rs:832-837 collapses policy reasons into TargetDenied/PermissionDenied; the wire carries only EffectError{code} (:804, :809-813); worker.rs:847 throws `js/read_file: denied`. service_host_error (host.rs:1107-1135), which would add a reason, is test-only.

Fix: propagate a closed, non-sensitive denial reason code (e.g. no_configured_roots / outside_roots / permission) to the model, and/or document defaulting js-read-roots to the workspace. Check docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md invariants (closed diagnostics) before changing. The separate 'arrow-function syntax' report is unverified (no child tool logs).
acceptance_criteria: A js read_file on a workspace path either succeeds when configured, or the model-visible error names the missing grant (e.g. 'no js-read-roots configured'); Phase 6 invariants preserved; broker unit + contained-worker test for the denial message.
close_reason: [done] EffectError gains optional closed DenialReason (no_configured_roots/outside_roots/permission_denied), skip-serialized when absent; broker maps typed service errors; worker message 'js/read_file: denied (no js-read-roots configured)'. Spec Delivered corrections + 00-index updated. | Notes: Model sees message only if script catches e.message (tool output still hides exception text per invariant 6). Contained test uses permission denial reason; no-roots path covered at broker+worker level. | merged to main via fb/f6-hooks-js-trust (2026-10-19).

title: Project personas in an agents-only project are silently ignored (trust tied to missing config.toml)
description:
Source: feedback A9 (reporter-local bead mini-agent-0rzx, never pushed). Verified on HEAD.

Repro: create <tmp>/.mini-agent/agents/x.md with no config.toml, start mini-agent, type `@x` -> `no matches`; no trust prompt.

Root cause: src/context/agents.rs:758-763 project_definitions_trusted -> project_config_is_trusted_in_workspace (src/config/load.rs:2485-2494) returns false when .mini-agent/config.toml is absent; the loader then skips project layers silently (agents.rs:1174-1177, :1216).

Fix: content-bound interactive trust for persona files without config.toml, or at least a notice naming ignored personas and how to trust them.
acceptance_criteria: An agents-only project (.mini-agent/agents/*.md, no config.toml) can be trusted interactively and its personas then appear in @ and /agent; at minimum a one-line notice names ignored personas; headless/ACP stay inert; tests cover agents-only.
close_reason: [done] persona_bindings in the private trust store keyed on canonical project + digest of sorted (path, sha256) of persona files; startup y/N prompt (interactive only); trusted personas load, edit/add/remove voids; TUI dim notice and headless stderr notice. | Notes: prompt is the stdin y/N pattern used by config trust (pre-TUI); also prompts when a non-sensitive project config exists but personas untrusted. | merged to main via fb/f6-hooks-js-trust (2026-10-19).

title: Subagent tool results are never persisted and background tasks record no tool calls at all
description:
Source: feedback A7 — PARTIALLY confirmed on HEAD (report overstated).

Correction: foreground child tool calls ARE persisted as MessageRole::SubagentToolCall with name+args (src/session/mod.rs:1914-1925, from src/ui/event_handler.rs:286-292).
Confirmed gaps: (1) tool results/errors are never persisted — no result event reaches the parent (session/mod.rs:1909-1912); (2) background tasks set event_tx=None (task_tool.rs:936-940), so their tool calls are neither shown nor stored; (3) /tasks (src/ui/slash/tasks.rs) shows no tool log.

Fix: bounded per-child log (tool name, args, result size, error) stored with the task result and viewable via /tasks <id>.
acceptance_criteria: After a failed delegation (foreground or background) the user can list the child's tool calls with result sizes/errors via /tasks <id>; log is bounded.

title: Unknown hook event drops every hook in the settings file; PreCompact/Notification/PermissionRequest rejected
description:
Source: feedback A8 (reporter-local bead mini-agent-vni0, never pushed). Verified on HEAD.

Repro: start mini-agent in this repo -> WARN `unsupported hook event "PreCompact"`; the same file's SessionStart `bd prime` hook no longer runs.

title: No notice when a model falls back to the default 128k context window
description:
Source: feedback A6. Verified on HEAD (with one correction).

Facts: main context_window falls back to 128_000 (src/config/mod.rs:842); subagents to 131_072 (:1189-1192); mid_turn_compact_threshold is None by default (:296, :1075-1080). Opus session reached 149k/128k (116%) with 0 compactions. No notice is shown when a fallback applies (startup only silently re-derives on resume, src/startup.rs:1293-1297).

Correction to report: a quick-model `context_window` (src/config/types.rs:379) DOES already feed subagent resolution (mod.rs:1162-1172).

Fix: print a fallback notice at startup/model switch; warn when the gauge exceeds 100%; consider defaulting mid-turn compaction (~0.8) when the window is a fallback value.

title: Host-repaired subagent report discards raw child text with no user-visible copy
description:
Source: feedback A5 (by design, UX gap). Verified on HEAD.

Behaviour: task_tool.rs:2378-2391 `host_repaired_report` replaces the report with fixed text ("raw child text was omitted"); :2443-2466 never quotes malformed responses. `/tasks result <id>` (src/ui/slash/tasks.rs:42-45) shows only the repaired row.result. Raw text survives only for valid-but-oversized reports (:2397-2435).

Keep the fail-closed defence (raw text never reaches the parent model). Fix: persist the raw child response as a session artifact viewable only by the user, marked unverified.
acceptance_criteria: After a host repair the user can open the original child text (e.g. /tasks result <id> or a printed artifact path) clearly marked unverified; the parent model still receives only the fixed text.
close_reason: [done] Raw child text (6 KiB cap) kept in details.unverified after host repair; /tasks result <id> prints it marked UNVERIFIED, user-only; never in task_result output. | Notes: Follow-up: host_repaired_report no longer quotes raw child text; parent gets fixed text + pointer to /tasks result <id>. Tests inverted (report_contract* 19 passed with new tests). Oversized-valid partial_report path still quotes a prefix (unchanged). | merged to main via fb/f2-subagents (2026-10-19).

title: TUI navigation: page up/down and jump to session start/end via modifier chords, Shift+wheel paging, /top and /bottom
description:
WHAT: Transcript navigation depends on keys many setups do not deliver. Today (docs/agent/COMMANDS.md:797-799, src/ui/app.rs:854-870, src/ui/mod.rs:758): PageUp/PageDown scroll the viewport, the mouse wheel scrolls by line, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End jump to the top/bottom of the session, and plain Home/End do so only when the input is empty or a picker is open. macOS laptop keyboards have no PageUp/PageDown/Home/End keys (only fn+arrow chords, which several terminals remap), and Windows Terminal/WSL and VS Code's terminal intercept Shift+PageUp/PageDown and some Ctrl+Home/End combinations for their own scrollback, so users there cannot page or jump reliably. The mouse wheel only moves line by line, so long sessions are slow to traverse.

WHERE: src/ui/app.rs (TranscriptScroll, transcript_scroll_key, the key dispatch that maps PageUp/PageDown), src/ui/mod.rs:758-790 (mouse event mapping), src/ui/renderer.rs (scroll_to_top/scroll_to_bottom/page scroll), src/ui/permission_handler.rs:92-117 (PromptScroll mirrors the same keys while a permission prompt waits), the keybindings config (docs/agent/CONFIG.md keybindings section), docs/agent/COMMANDS.md:797-806.

HOW:
1. Page up/down alternatives with a modifier that work without PageUp/PageDown keys: Alt+Up / Alt+Down (Option+arrow on macOS) and Shift+Up / Shift+Down for one page; keep PageUp/PageDown. Do not take Ctrl+U/Ctrl+D (editor kill/exit semantics).
2. Jump to the beginning/end of the session without Home/End keys: Alt+Shift+Up / Alt+Shift+Down (or Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down) and the emacs-style Alt+< / Alt+>; keep Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End and the empty-input Home/End rule. Also add /top and /bottom slash commands as a key-independent fallback.
3. Mouse: Shift+wheel (or Ctrl+wheel) scrolls a page per notch; plain wheel keeps line scrolling with a configurable step (e.g. [ui] mouse_scroll_lines, default unchanged). Respect mouse_capture = false (nothing changes then).
4. All new bindings go through the existing keybindings layer so users can rebind or disable them; none may shadow an existing editor/vim binding (check src/ui/input/vim.rs and the input editor's Alt+arrow word motions first; if Alt+arrow is already word motion in the editor, apply the alternative only when the input is empty or prefer Shift+arrow for paging and document the choice).
5. Apply the same alternatives inside the permission prompt (PromptScroll) so behaviour is consistent while a request waits.

VERIFY: unit tests for the key mapping (each new chord -> the right scroll action, with input empty/non-empty and picker open/closed, and that existing Home/End/PageUp/PageDown/Ctrl+Home/End behaviour is unchanged); mouse mapping test for Shift+wheel; permission_handler prompt_scroll tests extended; COMMANDS.md table and CONFIG.md keybindings updated; manual check in a terminal without PageUp (macOS laptop) and in Windows Terminal/WSL.
close_reason: [done] Alt+Up/Down page; Alt+Shift+Up/Down and Alt+< / Alt+> jump to top/bottom (added as default chords of page_up/page_down/transcript_top/transcript_bottom in keybindings layer, rebindable); Shift/Ctrl+wheel pages via new UserEvent::ScrollPageUp/Down; new top-level config mouse_scroll_lines (1..=20, default 1); /top and /bottom slash commands (allowed while running); permission/question prompt_scroll now resolves via keybindings table. Docs: COMMANDS.md, CONFIG.md, GET_STARTED.md, input-keybindings.md, /help. | Notes: Config key is top-level like mouse_capture, not [ui]. Behaviour change: Alt+Up/Down no longer acts as plain Up/Down (history) in the editor; documented, rebind page_up/page_down to restore. Terminals may still swallow Shift+wheel. | merged to main via d10-ui-navigation (perf2 round, 2026-10-19).

title: task tool hides persona model/mode, so models conclude a child model cannot be chosen
description:
WHAT: The task tool's `agent_type` description lists specialists only as `name: description`. It never says that a persona can pin its own model (`model:` frontmatter: raw id or quick-model alias, src/context/agents.rs:470) or run in `mode: write`. Observed 2026-10-19 (user screenshot, drawio-mcp-server session under /goal): the model concluded "the subagent tool has no setting for the model, so I can't choose GLM", which is false, and parked the goal.

HOW: Render each specialist as `name [mode: write|read, model: <id/alias>]: description` (omit unset fields; never leak resolved secrets, only the frontmatter string). Extend the agent_type description with one sentence: "The child model and write mode come from the persona definition (frontmatter `model:` and `mode: write`); add or edit a persona to change them. Write personas also require the user to set [subagents] allow_write = true." Keep the schema and enum unchanged.

title: Parallel write subagents: opt-in git-worktree isolation instead of the single shared write lane
description:
WHAT: Write-capable subagents are serialized: `write_lane: Arc::new(tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(1))` (src/extras/subagents/background.rs:404, task_tool.rs:1430) because every write child shares the parent workspace. Implementation fan-out ("implement these N beads in parallel") is therefore impossible inside mini-agent; users must hand-orchestrate separate git worktrees and instances (observed 2026-10-19, drawio-mcp-server /goal session).

WHERE: src/extras/subagents/{background.rs,task_tool.rs,builder.rs} (write lane, WriteChildTools, child workspace binding); src/extras/git_worktree/ (create/merge, already used by /wt and /wt-merge); src/context/agents.rs (persona frontmatter).

HOW: Add opt-in worktree isolation for write children: persona frontmatter `isolation: worktree` (and/or a per-brief field). For such a child: create a fresh git worktree + branch from the parent HEAD via the existing git_worktree create path, bind the child's WorkspaceBinding, permissions and sandbox roots to that worktree (never the parent tree), skip the shared write lane (bounded by the normal child concurrency), and on completion return the branch name, commit list and a diff stat instead of applying anything. Merging stays an explicit parent/user action (/wt-merge or a new task_result action). Clean up worktrees with no commits. Non-isolated write children keep the current serialized lane. Requires git-worktree + subagents features and still [subagents] allow_write = true.

VERIFY: integration test: two isolated write children editing the same file concurrently each produce a branch with their own change and the parent tree is untouched; cancellation removes the worktree; sandbox/permission tests that an isolated child cannot write the parent workspace; docs/agent/SUBAGENTS.md updated. Security review of the worktree binding (no write authority over the parent tree, .git metadata protections unchanged).
close_reason: [done] Persona frontmatter `isolation: worktree` (mode: write only). Each isolated child gets a worktree+branch via git_worktree::create; authorization (workspace binding, rebound sandbox, derived PermissionChecker) bound to the worktree only; parent tree and any .git entry are a hard permission denial (no grant/yolo/approval lifts it); shell dropped if sandbox is off/host-wide/overlaps parent. Skips the shared write lane. Host commits child work and appends branch/commits/diff-stat; no-change or dropped (cancel/timeout) children are removed. Docs updated. | Notes: No end-to-end TaskTool.call test with a mock model (AnyClient is a closed enum); lane/limit decision is the unit-tested helper uses_shared_write_lane. Isolation refuses when permission checks are disabled (None checker). Worktrees live next to the repo or under wt_base_dir. Child commit needs a git identity; else worktree kept and reported. Follow-up commit closes mid-create cancellation (guard handed over a oneshot; test a_create_that_finishes_after_cancellation_is_discarded). | merged to main via d9-subagent-worktrees (perf2 round, 2026-10-19).

title: task tool bounces string list fields and per-brief agent_type, costing a model round trip each
description:
WHAT: The `task` tool rejects two unambiguous, common model mistakes at deserialization, and each rejection costs a full model round trip (seconds of latency plus re-sent context tokens) before any subagent starts. Observed live (2026-10-19 screenshot of a mini-agent session): one fan-out took three task calls — (1) `agent_type` placed inside each brief -> "failed to parse tool arguments: unknown field `agent_type`, expected one of `objective`, `files`, ..."; (2) `constraints` sent as a single string -> "invalid type: string \"READ-ONLY review, no edits. ...\", expected a sequence"; (3) success.

WHERE (main at b56d7a74): src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:58-68 (TaskBrief, deny_unknown_fields, Vec<String> list fields); src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:70-131 (TaskArgs custom Deserialize, RawTaskArgs); src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:700-751 (input schema); src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:39 (TASK_MISSING_HANDOFF_ERROR text).

HOT PATH: every model-initiated subagent fan-out (task tool call) -> rig tool-arg deserialization -> error string returned to the model -> model re-issues the whole call. Cost = one extra model turn per mistake; weaker/non-Claude models make these mistakes repeatedly.

EXTRACT:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct TaskBrief {
    pub objective: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub files: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub constraints: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub expected_sections: Vec<String>,
}
// RawTaskArgs (line 76-84): agent_type is only accepted at the top level.
```

HOW: Accept the unambiguous forms instead of bouncing them, keeping the schema advertised unchanged and every real ambiguity an error:
1. List fields (`files`, `constraints`, `expected_sections`, and top-level `prompts`): accept a single non-empty string as a one-element list (`deserialize_with` a string-or-seq helper). Empty/whitespace string = empty list.
2. `agent_type` inside a brief: accept it in the per-brief raw form; if every brief that carries one names the same type and the top-level value is absent or equal, hoist it to the top-level field. If briefs disagree with each other or with the top level, return a precise error: "task: agent_type is a top-level field shared by all briefs; briefs named X and Y — issue one task call per agent_type".
3. For any remaining unknown brief field, keep deny_unknown_fields but make the error say where the field belongs when it is a known top-level field (run_in_background, agent_type).
Do not loosen anything else (unknown fields stay errors; objective still required; maxItems limits still enforced after coercion).

VERIFY: unit tests in task_tool tests: string constraints -> vec of one; per-brief agent_type hoisted when consistent; conflicting per-brief agent_type -> the new error text; unknown field still rejected; existing TaskArgs deserialization tests unchanged and green. Filter: `cargo test --bin mini-agent -- extras::subagents::task_tool`.

Category: redundant-work (wasted model round trips) · Confidence: high · Source: user-reported screenshot 2026-10-19, verified against task_tool.rs. Related: mini-agent-27wjl, mini-agent-2fxau (same file).
close_reason: [done] StringList accepts bare strings for files/constraints/expected_sections/prompts (blank = empty); per-brief agent_type hoisted when consistent, conflicts give the specified error; run_in_background in a brief gets a precise error; other unknown fields still rejected; schema unchanged. | Notes: Added #[derive(Debug)] to TaskArgs. | commit 15955cc9 on perf/c13-lsp-hooks-git-extras, merged to main.

title: Hook launches run the full sandbox preparation (git metadata scan, profile build) inline on the async executor
description:
WHAT: cttyn.51 moved model-command wrapping onto the blocking pool because `wrap_command` canonicalizes, opens and scans `.git` metadata (sandbox-2) and builds the Seatbelt profile. The hook path still does all of that synchronously inside an `async fn`: PATH resolution via `which`, SHA-256 of every pinned hook file, `canonical_non_root`, `retain_canonical_git_write_roots`, `get_seatbelt_profile`/`bwrap_git_metadata_binds` and the spawn itself. With hooks on every tool call this stalls the executor worker for the same milliseconds-to-tens-of-milliseconds that sandbox-2 measures, and on the current-thread/UI flavour it stalls rendering.

WHERE (main at b56d7a74): src/extras/hooks/subprocess.rs:412; src/extras/hooks/subprocess.rs:447-460; src/extras/hooks/subprocess.rs:489-493; src/sandbox.rs:2989-3100; src/sandbox.rs:734-741

HOT PATH: extras/hooks dispatcher -> run_hook_with_policy_and_limits, per hook event (PreToolUse/PostToolUse per tool call, PermissionRequest per prompt, Notification, Stop), on whatever tokio worker the tool future runs on.

EXTRACT:
```rust
async fn run_hook_with_policy_and_limits(
    ...
    let program =
        match super::pins::resolve_hook_program(&program, search_path.as_deref(), project_dir) {   // which::which_in PATH walk
    ...
    if let Some(pins) = &policy.content_pins
        && let Err(message) = pins.verify_launch(project_dir, &program, &args)                      // SHA-256 of each pinned operand
    ...
    let mut cmd = match policy
        .sandbox
        .wrap_hook_command(&program, &args, project_dir, explicit_env)                            // retain roots + seatbelt profile (.git scan) / bwrap binds, synchronously
    {

/// What the output worker launches. A shell command is wrapped by the worker
/// itself, on the blocking pool, so the caller's task (an executor worker, or
/// the TUI task for `!`) never runs the sandbox preparation and Git metadata
/// pin scan.
enum PendingCommand {
    Built(ExecutionCommand),
    Shell { ... },
```

HOW: Wrap the program resolution, pin verification and `wrap_hook_command` in `crate::agent::runner::spawn_blocking_scoped` (as `run_built_output_command` does for `PendingCommand::Shell`), returning the built `Command` to the async hook runner; keep the ordering (validate, wrap, then spawn) unchanged.

VERIFY: Hook integration tests in src/extras/hooks (subprocess, pins) stay green; add a test asserting `wrap_hook_command` is not called on a current-thread runtime's main task (e.g. via `tokio::task::block_in_place` panic guard or a thread-name assertion in a test seam).

Category: blocking-io · Confidence: medium · Review id: sandbox-6 · Related prior beads: mini-agent-cttyn.51, mini-agent-cttyn.55
Source: performance review 2026-10-19 (epic perf-2026-10-19). Do not weaken the Phase 6 security invariants (docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md) or the sandbox/permission fail-closed checks; make them cheaper or move them off the hot task, never skip them.

Test launch_preparation_runs_off_the_calling_task_thread. | commit 2dcdedb3 on perf/c07-sandbox-unix, merged to main.

title: web_http::send_async builds a new reqwest Client (TLS connector, pool) per request and per redirect hop
description:
WHAT: reqwest is built with native-tls (Cargo.toml:127): every ClientBuilder::build() constructs a fresh native_tls TlsConnector (SecureTransport context on macOS, OpenSSL SSL_CTX with CA bundle load from /etc/ssl on Linux), a new hyper connection pool and a new resolver, typically several ms and allocations each. pool_max_idle_per_host(0) additionally forbids connection reuse, so a same-origin redirect chain re-does TCP+TLS handshakes per hop even though the pinned addresses are identical. The only reason for the per-call build is resolve_to_addrs, which needs the DNS answer first.

WHERE (main at b56d7a74): src/agent/tools/web_http.rs:703-744; src/agent/tools/web_http.rs:861-941; Cargo.toml:124-131

HOT PATH: web_fetch / web_search tool call -> NativeWebClient::execute -> send_async once per hop (up to FETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS+1 = 6 hops), each hop inside the 10 s total budget.

EXTRACT:
```rust
// web_http.rs:722-737 (called once per hop from NativeWebClient::execute)
    let host = url.host_str().ok_or(FetchError::MissingHost)?;
    let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
        .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
        .no_proxy()
        .no_gzip()
        .no_brotli()
        .no_zstd()
        .no_deflate()
        .pool_max_idle_per_host(0)
        .connect_timeout(limits.connect_timeout)
        .read_timeout(limits.read_timeout)
        .timeout(limits.total_timeout)
        .user_agent(concat!("mini-agent-web/", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
        .resolve_to_addrs(host, addresses)
        .build()
        .map_err(|e| FetchError::ClientBuild(e.to_string()))?;
// web_http.rs:870-919 loop over redirects, each iteration calls send_async(...)
            for redirects in 0..=FETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS {
                ...
                match send_async(send_url, request, &addresses)
```
