title: Configurable home dot files/folders mounted into (and masked from) the command sandbox
description:
WHAT: Let the user choose which dot files and dot folders under $HOME are mounted into the ordinary-command sandbox, instead of only the hard-coded behaviour. Today the `workspace` profile exposes nothing from home except explicit absolute `sandbox-read-roots`/`sandbox-write-roots` (max 32, src/sandbox/general_profile.rs roots()), while `host-read`/`host-full` expose all of home minus a hard-coded secret mask list in private_paths() (general_profile.rs:16-43: .ssh .aws .gnupg .kube .azure .config/gcloud .config/gh plus the private application dirs). Tools like git, cargo, npm and pip need ~/.gitconfig, ~/.cargo, ~/.npmrc, ~/.config/<tool> in the `workspace` profile, and users with other credential stores need to hide more in host profiles.

WHERE: src/sandbox/general_profile.rs (private_paths, roots, HostFilesystem::capture, Linux bwrap mounts and the shared Seatbelt renderer on macOS), src/sandbox.rs (Sandbox struct: read_roots/write_roots), src/config/keys.rs (next to sandbox-read-roots, ~:209) and src/config/mod.rs resolver; Windows AppContainer read roots (windows_appcontainer_read_roots, keys.rs ~:213) for parity or an explicit unsupported note; docs/agent/CONFIG.md sandbox profile paragraph (~:820-830).

HOW: Add two config keys, both string lists of HOME-RELATIVE paths:
  - `sandbox-home-mounts` (alias sandbox_home_mounts): dot paths to expose inside the sandbox, read-only by default; an entry suffixed `:rw` (or a parallel `sandbox-home-write-mounts`, pick one and document) is writable. Applies to the `workspace` profile; in host profiles it is a no-op for reads (already visible) but still grants writes where the profile would not.
  - `sandbox-home-masks` (alias sandbox_home_masks): extra dot paths hidden in every profile, ADDED to the built-in mask list; the built-in masks and private application dirs can never be removed or mounted (a mount entry that names or contains a masked path is a config error, not a silent drop).
  Validation (fail closed with a clear error at sandbox capture): entry must be relative, start with '.', contain no '..' or empty components, resolve (canonicalize) to a path still under HOME (no symlink escape), and count toward the existing 32-root cap. Missing paths are skipped with a debug log, not created. Project-local layers may only ADD masks; adding mounts from a project layer requires the existing sensitive-config/project-trust approval. Keep the JS worker launcher untouched (it does not use these grants; Phase 6 invariants unchanged). Restart-required like other startup keys.

VERIFY: unit tests for validation (absolute path, '..', non-dot, symlink escaping HOME, entry naming a built-in mask such as .ssh or .config/gh, cap overflow, missing path skipped); Linux bwrap and macOS Seatbelt profile tests in general_profile.rs proving a configured ~/.gitconfig is readable in `workspace`, an unconfigured dotfile is not, a `:rw` entry is writable, an extra mask hides a file in host-read; project-layer mount refused without trust; config_key_catalogue_* and config68_dedicated_cli_values_are_visible_without_becoming_saved_defaults; native containment tests for the sandbox rows CI runs. Docs: CONFIG.md keys and the profile paragraph.
close_reason: sandbox-home-mounts (read-only, :rw for directories) and additive sandbox-home-masks with fail-closed validation, project-trust for mounts, Windows AppContainer refusal; macOS Seatbelt native + 521 sandbox/config tests pass; Linux bwrap native test wired into CI. Merged to main.

title: /cron fire path: idle predicate, parked single fire, budget gate, scheduler origin, select! arm, interrupt/teardown semantics
description:
WHAT: Entries fire only when the TUI is truly idle: !run.is_running (a live goal keeps it true, so goals count as busy and are parked silently), permission_prompt and question_prompt None, MCP admin idle, chain.git.work None (start_main_run_prepared ensure!s this and would otherwise return Err and exit the TUI), pending_inputs empty (queued user text runs first). When a deadline passes while busy the entry is marked due and fires once at the next idle settle (no catch-up; at most one parked fire per entry). A fire calls ensure_agent(), then budget_admission_notice() (budget exhaustion suspends all entries with one notice and does not delete them), echoes a host marker line '⟳ cron c1 (every 5m): <prompt>' distinct from the user's '>' echo, and starts a normal turn in the same session. Fires carry a scheduler origin (QuestionOrigin::Scheduled or equivalent) so UserPromptSubmit hooks and prompts can tell scheduler from human, and are accounted as RequestKind::Scheduled. Ctrl-C interrupts the running fire's turn but keeps the schedule; Esc at an idle empty editor clears a parked due fire; /cron stop removes; Quit and teardown drop all entries. A fire whose turn opens a permission prompt parks the scheduler until answered (status shows 'waiting'); it is never auto-approved.
WHERE: src/ui/app.rs run_inner select! (:2418): one new arm 'sleep_until(next_fire), if next_fire.is_some()' patterned on forced_refresh (:2534-2538), next_fire computed before the select! from the store; arm body = crate::startup::heap_future(|| self.fire_due_cron()).await? (startup.rs:505, 1 MiB stack budget); fire path reuses budget_admission_notice (:5539), echo (:5654 echo_submission :63-70) and start_main_run (:5384) with the new origin; settle point for parked fires = the queue-replay block (:4542-4559) after pending_inputs is drained; Esc/Ctrl-C handling near :4722-4732 and the key arm; teardown :2660-2700; src/question.rs QuestionOrigin; src/spend.rs:177 RequestKind (check VersionedRow readers tolerate the new variant, spend.rs:189-191); hooks context for UserPromptSubmit (src/extras/hooks, provider.rs:4272) to expose the origin.
HOW: Decide the fire inside the small arm body only; all heavy work in the boxed fn. Update next_at before starting the turn so a long turn does not double-fire. Increment fires and remove the entry when it reaches cron_max_fires with a notice. Do not pre-empt a goal relaunch (finish_goal_round sets is_running before returning, event_handler.rs:1095-1176). Record each fired prompt as an ordinary persisted User message (it appears in rewind/history; the ⟳ marker is display-only — document).
VERIFY: App fixture tests: (1) idle entry fires at its deadline, echo marker present, session gains one user message, origin visible to a UserPromptSubmit hook fixture; (2) deadline during a run parks one fire that runs after settle and after queued user input; two missed deadlines fire once; (3) a pending git proposal or MCP admin op defers the fire and run_inner does not return Err; (4) budget-capped session suspends entries with one notice and keeps them; (5) Ctrl-C mid-fire keeps the schedule, Esc at idle clears a parked fire, Quit drops entries; (6) cron_max_fires reached removes the entry. Run cargo test --all-features --test headless_json -- startup_commands_run_with_the_windows_default_stack_budget after touching run_inner; spend tests for RequestKind round-trip; existing singleflight, loop_command_tests, goal round tests stay green.
close_reason: Fire path in src/ui/cron_app.rs: select! wakeup arm via heap_future, full idle predicate, parked single fire, budget suspend, QuestionOrigin::Scheduled, RequestKind::Scheduled, UserPromptSubmit origin, Ctrl-C/Esc/Quit/teardown semantics; 7 App fixture tests + 472 related + stack budget pass. Merged to main.

title: /cron command, CronStore and interval parsing (prompt payloads, constants, cron_max_fires)
description:
WHAT: A session-local recurring scheduler. /cron <interval> <prompt> arms an entry; /cron or /cron list shows id, interval, time until next fire (relative), fires/max and payload; /cron stop <id>|all removes; /cron run <id> fires at the next idle point. Interval grammar ^\d+(s|m|h)$; constants CRON_MIN_INTERVAL = 60 s (shorter rounds up with a notice), CRON_MAX_INTERVAL = 24 h, CRON_MAX_ENTRIES = 16; one live config key cron_max_fires (default 24) bounding fires per entry. Payloads are plain prompts only: text starting with / or ! is refused with a one-line reason (keeps Phase 6 and the slash whitelist untouched; prevents self-replicating /cron or /steer fires). Arming when max_budget_usd is unset prints a one-time warning that scheduled turns are unbounded. The existing /loop goal preset is untouched; a /loop whose first argument matches the interval grammar is refused with 'did you mean /cron <interval> ...?' (today /loop auto-starts round 1, app.rs:6805-6815, so a typo would immediately burn a goal round). Ungated (no new Cargo feature).
WHERE: new src/ui/slash/cron.rs (handler, modelled on src/ui/slash/features.rs:36-131 handle_loop and the /jobs stop <id> shape in src/ui/slash/jobs.rs) and new src/ui/cron.rs (CronStore, Entry{id, interval, next_at: tokio Instant, due: bool, fires, payload}, interval parser, next_deadline()); dispatch arm in src/ui/slash/mod.rs:864-1046 next to "/loop" (:985); /loop refusal in features.rs handle_loop (anchored on the whole first token so '5minute-plan' passes); whitelist: src/ui/mod.rs:870-886 allowed_while_running + a cron_control_while_running sibling of loop_control_while_running (:891) allowing every /cron verb (adding only schedules; the fire waits for idle); store ownership on App (reachable from SlashCtx; EventLoopState only reads next_deadline); picker catalogue src/ui/pickers/list.rs BASE_COMMANDS and /help in src/ui/slash/help.rs (help-sync test); config key in src/config/keys.rs (key("cron_max_fires").described(..).live().shaped(ConfigShape::Integer)) with field + resolve_cron_max_fires in src/config/mod.rs (pattern :1226-1228).
HOW: Ids c1, c2, ... monotonic per session. next_at = now + interval at arming and after each fire START (monotonic; document that suspend shifts deadlines and display is always relative, e.g. 'in 4m'). Keep the store free of tokio Notify: slash edits run inside handle_user_event_batch and the loop recomputes deadlines at the top of run_inner. Docs: docs/agent/COMMANDS.md new '## Cron' section (syntax, idle-only firing, no catch-up, one parked fire, session-local, budget warning) plus one disambiguation sentence in the Loop section (:373) and the table (:424-426); docs/agent/CONFIG.md cron_max_fires; docs/agent/ARCHITECTURE.md module list.
VERIFY: unit tests in src/ui/cron.rs (interval grammar incl. rejects 0, 59s rounds up, 25h refused, 17th entry refused, ids monotonic, next_deadline picks the earliest, stop/all); src/ui/slash tests for /cron list|stop|run output and the payload refusals (/x, !x); src/tests/singleflight_tests.rs: running_cron_controls_pass (/cron, /cron list, /cron stop c1, /cron 5m x while running -> Run) beside running_loop_controls_pass_but_new_starts_remain_blocked (:77); loop_command_tests: new loop_refuses_an_interval_first_argument_with_a_cron_hint, existing four stay green; config_key_catalogue_* tests; help-sync test; command_list_is_sorted_unique_and_includes_feature_commands.

title: TUI submit: resolve @agent mentions, fail closed on unknown names, route via a non-persisted task directive
description:
WHAT: On submit, a message containing @agent:<name> (or a resolvable @agent-<name>) is sent as the user's ORIGINAL text plus a non-persisted host directive telling the model to delegate through the task tool with agent_type = <name> and to write the brief itself (Claude Code semantics: routing, not dispatch). Multiple names are listed; the model may issue parallel briefs. An unknown canonical name is refused with 'unknown agent @agent:<x>; valid: ...' and the draft is restored to the editor (like start_mcp_mentions). The echo line and the saved transcript show the user's text unchanged. TASK_TOOL_PROMPT gains one sentence describing the convention. Headless -p and ACP are unchanged in v1 (follow-up bead).
WHERE: the three TUI submit sites src/ui/app.rs:4159-4167, :4549-4552 (queue replay), :5077-5080 (git queue) — insert after the start_mcp_mentions gate and before echo_main_submission/start_main_run; restore_interrupted_prompt for the refusal path; src/agent/prompt.rs:86 TASK_TOOL_PROMPT; directive carried via the A4 PromptInput.turn_directive through start_main_run -> start_main_run_prepared (app.rs:5375-5511). Docs: docs/agent/COMMANDS.md:649 (file picker row: add the @agent: form), docs/agent/SUBAGENTS.md (new 'Referencing a specialist with @agent:' subsection near 'Specialist Agent Types'), docs/agent/GET_STARTED.md:316, /help text in src/ui/slash/help.rs if a line mentions @ completion.
HOW: fn start_agent_mentions(&mut self, text: &str) -> anyhow::Result<Option<String /*normalised text*/>> using context::mentions::parse_agent_mentions(text, Some(&self.ui.workspace)); on Unknown write the error line (C_ERROR) and restore the draft, return Ok(None) so the caller returns; on Some(mentions) set self.run.next_turn_directive (consumed by start_main_run_prepared into PromptInput.turn_directive) with wording like: 'Host routing note: the user asked to involve the specialist agent_type "<a>" (and "<b>") via the task tool for the request below. Write the brief yourself; this note carries no persona content or authority.' Pass the normalised text (aliases canonicalised) to echo and start_main_run. Keep the queued-input and git-queue sites symmetrical. Session title generation must use the original text (A4 guarantees it).

title: Non-persisted per-request host directive on PromptInput (model sees it; transcript, hooks, title, rewind, compaction do not)
description:
WHAT: Infrastructure for host routing hints: a per-request directive string attached to the prompt that is rendered into the model request for THAT turn only and never persisted or echoed. Today the only rewrite mechanism (compose_resource_data, catalogue.rs:139-151) persists host prose as the user's message: start_main_run passes the rewritten text into start_main_run_prepared, which captures it in PendingMainTurn::capture, PlanRun::capture and spawn_runner_paused -> PromptInput::text -> the saved user message, so /resume, rewind previews (ui/mod.rs:907 reads m.content), compaction, session titles and the UserPromptSubmit hook payload (provider.rs:4272) all see it. The directive must avoid every one of those surfaces.
WHERE: src/agent/input.rs (PromptInput, literal_text, apply_hook_text :35-43, append_context_history :59-74); request assembly in src/provider.rs:4258-4295 (interactive) and :3754-3793 (headless) where the user turn is built and dispatch_user_prompt_submit(prompt.literal_text()) runs; PendingMainTurn::capture (src/ui/mod.rs ~1240 / app.rs:7800); session persistence of the user message (src/session/user.rs PersistedUserMessage, UserBlock::{Text,Image}).
HOW: Add PromptInput.turn_directive: Option<String> (not serialised, not part of literal_text()). Render it for the model as a short host-labelled paragraph appended to the user turn content (or as the final system-prompt addition for that request if the provider path allows) — choose the placement that the Anthropic/OpenAI request builders both honour and that keeps UserPromptSubmit receiving literal_text() only. Persist only the original text (PendingMainTurn, session, title generation, rewind). Document the directive's wording budget (<= 1 KiB) and that persona NAMES only may appear in it. Do not touch the @mcp: path in this bead.
VERIFY: tests: a prompt with turn_directive produces a provider request whose last user content contains the directive (wire-level test harness as in provider tests) while session.messages last user content equals the original text; UserPromptSubmit hook fixture receives the original text; rewind picker/title fixtures unaffected; --continue replay of a saved session has no directive text. cargo test --bin mini-agent -- agent::input provider::effort_tests turn_persistence_tests session:: hooks.
close_reason: PromptInput.turn_directive (<=1KiB, last user text block for one request; excluded from literal_text, persistence, hooks, title, rewind, compaction); run.next_turn_directive consumed by start_main_run_prepared; wire + App tests pass. Documented exception: Anthropic native thinking-replay frames keep the exact sent request (byte-exact replay requirement), see TOOL_RUNTIME.md. Merged to main.

title: Agent-mention parser: canonical @agent:<name>, @agent-<name> alias, trust-gated resolution
description:
WHAT: A shared, pure parser for agent mentions in submitted text. An unknown canonical name is an error naming the valid personas (same wording family as task_tool.rs:447 'unknown agent_type ... valid types'). title: @agent mentions and /cron recurring scheduler (Claude Code parity, 2026-10-18 design)
description:
Design (2026-10-18) for two Claude Code parity features, adapted to mini-agent after a sourced research pass, a code-indexer trace of the relevant plumbing, and a devil's-advocate review that overturned several first-draft decisions. Children are labelled feature-2026-10-18 (sub-labels mentions, cron) and each has WHAT / WHERE (file:line at da6e6433) / HOW / VERIFY.

FEATURE A — @agent mentions. Claude Code: typing @ lists subagents labelled 'name (agent)', inserts @"name (agent)", manual form @agent-<name>; the mention is a ROUTING DIRECTIVE, not a dispatch (a system reminder tells the model to invoke that agent; the model writes the subagent prompt). mini-agent today: @ opens the file picker, Tab consumes the @ and inserts a bare path; only @mcp:<server>:<uri> tokens are parsed at submit (start_mcp_mentions); personas are trust-gated files whose names form the task tool's agent_type enum; there is no system-reminder API and no tool_choice plumbing. Decisions: canonical token @agent:<name> (namespaced like @mcp:), alias @agent-<name> accepted and normalised only when it resolves (unresolvable alias stays plain text, since it is a legal filename shape); picker shows virtual @agent:<name> rows PREPENDED to file rows, no description column in v1; submit-time parsing TUI-only in v1 (headless -p and ACP parse no @ at all today, incl. @mcp:) with fail-closed draft restore on an unknown canonical name and trailing-punctuation trimming; the model-visible routing directive is a NON-PERSISTED per-request addition (echo, saved transcript, rewind, compaction, session title and UserPromptSubmit payload all see the user's original text) — the devil's advocate showed the @mcp: rewrite pattern persists host prose as the user's message, which we will not repeat; mention list and task enum share one trusted source; hard dispatch (host calls the task tool itself) rejected because check_perm runs inside the tool, briefs need the main model's context, and results need a main turn anyway; tool_choice forcing deferred as a later opt-in.

FEATURE B — /cron (name fixed by the user; the existing /loop is a goal preset that auto-starts round 1 and must stay untouched). Claude Code /loop: [interval] [prompt|/cmd], min 1 min, same conversation, fires only when idle, no catch-up (a missed interval fires once when idle), session-scoped, dynamic self-paced mode via a ScheduleWakeup tool. Decisions for v1: /cron <interval> <prompt> (prompt payloads only; slash and ! payloads refused — keeps Phase 6 untouched and avoids self-replicating /cron or /steer fires), /cron [list], /cron stop <id>|all, /cron run <id>; interval ^\d+(s|m|h)$ with constants 60 s min / 24 h max / 16 entries (not config); one live key cron_max_fires (default 24, bounded by compaction churn); fire only under a strict idle predicate (no run, no permission/question prompt, MCP admin idle, chain.git.work none — start_main_run_prepared ensure!s this and would exit the TUI — and pending_inputs empty so queued user text wins), ensure_agent() first, budget gate per fire; at most one parked 'due' fire per entry; a live goal counts as busy (park silently, one status indicator); monotonic deadlines (tokio Instant does not advance across macOS/Linux suspend; display relative 'in 4m', never clock time), no Notify (slash edits return to the loop top), one sleep_until select! arm with the body boxed via startup::heap_future; store on App/SlashState (EventLoopState only reads next_deadline); RequestKind::Scheduled and a scheduler origin visible to hooks; Ctrl-C keeps the schedule, Esc at an idle empty editor clears a parked fire, /cron stop removes, teardown drops; session-local, not persisted; warn once when max_budget_usd is unset; ungated (no new Cargo feature: no deps, no platform surface, and a feature would need CI rows and cfg pairs); /loop refuses an interval-first argument with a /cron hint (a typo would otherwise burn a goal round immediately). Follow-ups filed: picker description column, -p/ACP mention parity, tool_choice opt-in, dynamic self-paced /cron via a typed tool, persist-disarmed + /cron resume, ACP /cron with an Idle lease, slash-payload allowlist.
close_reason: All 10 children closed; @agent mentions and /cron delivered with docs.

title: Exit path serializes bounded and unbounded waits: early quit waits on the JS probe and prebuild, stuck MCP servers wait forever
description:
WHAT: teardown_owners runs sequentially retire_mcp_work, retire_session_title (5 s each), run.retire(5 s), prebuild.retire(5 s) (joins the prebuild rather than cancelling it, so an in-flight MCP connect/agent build is awaited then discarded), close_background_tasks (wait_idle per job, no timeout), mgr.shutdown() (serial per server, no timeout), then finish_session_end (SessionEnd hooks, 60 s default), persist_background_state (sync save + fsyncs); dispatch then awaits probe.retire() (unbounded join of the JS preflight) and JsWorkerSupervisor::shutdown_shared. Quitting in the first seconds waits on the probe/prebuild; quitting with a stuck MCP server waits indefinitely.

title: OSC-11 background query blocks the runtime thread up to 150 ms before the first frame
description:

title: Per-child subagent construction repeats invariant work for every child in a fan-out
description:

title: Turn end and exit wait unbounded on child blocking work; the 5 s settle/retire budgets stack
description:
WHAT: A cancelled or dropped child leaves an armed AgentRunCleanupGuard whose Drop spawns a waiter on scope.wait_idle() while holding semaphore permits and the parent's work registration; the parent turn's cleanup.settle() has no timeout, so Done (and the final paint, which runs after settle) is delayed until the child's spawn_blocking work (tool-result spill write, grep/find, ledger read) returns. At exit run.settle(5 s) and run.retire(5 s) can each time out and close_background_tasks -> pool.close() then waits with no timeout at all.
WHERE: src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs:1260-1283, 1719; src/agent/runner.rs:921-933 (auxiliary_child registers in the parent scope), 954-968 (Drop waiter), 3949 (parent settle), 118-128 (spill hook); src/ui/state.rs:595-606; src/ui/app.rs:2185-2199 (TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT); src/session/mod.rs:893-897 (close_background_tasks); src/extras/subagents/background.rs:674-696.
HOW: Wrap close_background_tasks in the same TEARDOWN_TIMEOUT (warn and continue; the OS reaps blocking threads); make child blocking tools observe AgentWorkScope::cancelled() (background jobs already select! on it at background.rs:777-781; foreground children rely only on future drop); consider spawn_blocking for the spill write only above a larger threshold; paint the final response before awaiting settle (see the final-parse bead).
VERIFY: background.rs background56_cancel_does_not_publish_terminal_until_blocking_child_retires, background56_closed_owner_refuses_reserved_but_not_registered_work; task_tool.rs background56_cancelled_child_keeps_both_lanes_until_actual_effect_retirement, task124_live_budget_cancels_owned_siblings_and_preserves_known_units; app.rs teardown tests.

title: Foreground subagent fan-out is throttled by the session-wide pool semaphore and the deadline includes queue time
description:
WHAT: Every foreground child acquires pool.concurrency (sized by task_max_concurrency, clamp 1..32, shared with background jobs) after the scheduler already counted it as started and after its wall-clock deadline began. title: within_budget scans the whole agent block 2-6 times per repaint, before the layout cache is consulted

title: Reasoning and plain streaming blocks re-wrap their whole text on every repaint (quadratic over a stream)

title: Final response parse re-renders the whole block and waits on settle before painting
description:
WHAT: When a response segment finishes (every ToolCall and the final Done), finalize_block clears md_cache and render_cache, so the complete response is re-parsed as markdown and re-highlighted from byte 0 synchronously on the UI task, even though the streaming path already maintains stable segments up to the last stable boundary. title: First frame after /resume lays out the whole feed: lazy bottom-up layout
description:
WHAT: render_session pushes every stored message as feed blocks, and the first refresh() calls Feed::lines(width) which runs compute_lines over all blocks: every assistant message is parsed as markdown and syntax highlighted before a single row is painted, although only the last ~40 rows are visible. For a long session (the feed keeps up to 4096 blocks / 16 MiB) this is a multi-second synchronous stall in the debug build at exactly the moment the user expects the prompt. The same full pass runs after /clear-and-replay paths and after any width change (resize).
WHERE: src/ui/feed.rs:806-823 (lines), 845-863 (compute_lines iterates all blocks), 1049-1073 (block_segments per block); src/ui/events.rs:28-90 (render_session), 191-240 (push_session_records); src/ui/renderer.rs:1455-1470 (render_viewport needs total and the visible window only).
HOW: Lay out lazily from the tail: compute segments for blocks from the end until visible rows are satisfied, keep a prefix-sum index that is extended on demand when scrolling up or when a selection/click needs earlier rows; alternatively precompute the remaining blocks in an idle tick (budgeted, e.g. 5 ms per tick). Keep FeedLines semantics (len() may need the total: cache per-block row counts separately from rendered rows, which is cheaper than parsing because it can be computed from a plain wrap for non-agent blocks and from the markdown pass only when needed).
VERIFY: Feed test: a feed with 2000 agent blocks and width 80; assert block_renders() after the first lines() call is bounded by the blocks needed for 50 rows; scrolling to the top renders the rest; existing feed layout tests stay green.

title: Statusline git polling spawns git status every second and reads .git on the UI task
description:
WHAT: Every event-loop iteration checks last_branch_check and, once per second, runs Session::refresh_git_branch (synchronous fs reads of .git and .git/HEAD on the UI task) and request_git_status_refresh, which spawns git status --porcelain=v2 --branch through the guarded GitRunner. With a git statusline item enabled this is a git subprocess every second for the lifetime of the TUI, even when idle, which costs CPU on large repositories and steals the UI task briefly on every spawn/receive.
WHERE: src/ui/app.rs:2023-2027 (1 s branch check), 1903-1920 (request_git_status_refresh), 2041-2047 (git_status_rx arm); src/session/mod.rs:1182-1218 (detect_git_branch), 1223-1245 (detect_git_status); src/ui/statusline.rs:118-120 (needs_git_status).
HOW: Poll on an adaptive schedule: refresh immediately after events that can change status (tool results that mutated files, bash/! commands, turn end, resume from suspend, /git commands) and otherwise every 10-15 s; before spawning git, compare mtimes of .git/HEAD, .git/index and the packed-refs/refs directory and skip the spawn when nothing changed; run detect_git_branch inside the same spawned task instead of on the UI task.
VERIFY: App fixture test with a fake GitStatusRefresh channel asserting at most one spawn per interval and one immediately after a ToolResult; existing statusline git tests stay green.

title: User events are painted one at a time: coalesce queued keys, wheel and drag events before painting
description:
WHAT: run_inner handles one UserEvent per select! arm and every arm ends in refresh() (full chat + bottom draw). Mouse wheel notches arrive as 3+ ScrollUp events, a drag produces one MouseDrag per pointer motion (each changing the selection snapshot and repainting all rows), and fast typing or a held key produces one frame per keystroke. The channel holds up to 64 events (app.rs:1740), so under load frames are painted for states the user never sees.
WHERE: src/ui/app.rs:2047-2052 (user_rx arm), 2715-2805 (ScrollUp/ScrollDown/MouseDrag arms), 2904-2906 (refresh after each event); src/ui/mod.rs:588-712 (event thread sends every crossterm event individually).
HOW: After receiving one event, drain user_rx.try_recv() into a small batch; merge consecutive ScrollUp/ScrollDown into a count, keep only the last MouseDrag, apply Key/Paste events in order without painting, then paint once. Keep modal and Quit semantics by stopping the drain at any event that changes mode (permission/picker/Quit).
VERIFY: App fixture test: push 10 ScrollUp events and 20 Key events into user_tx before running one loop iteration; assert one render_viewport/draw_bottom (counter) and the final state is identical to sequential handling; existing input/picker tests stay green.

title: Renderer::write_line repaints the viewport on every call: batch paints within one event
description:
WHAT: write_line, write_line_anchored and write_line_after each push a block and immediately call render_viewport when not scrolled. app.rs alone has 167 write_line call sites and several loops (steering replay app.rs:1662, 3882, 4906, 4959, 5053-5069; /tasks slash/tasks.rs:15,46; /jobs slash/jobs.rs:27; /context slash/context.rs:465; diagnostics app.rs:2039,2152; /help prints ~60 lines). title: Streaming repaint throttle is bypassed for reasoning deltas and newline-terminated tokens
description:
WHAT: stream_repaint_due(segment_len, completes_line, since_last_paint) returns true whenever completes_line or segment_len < 200. For AgentEvent::Reasoning the segment is the delta itself (almost always < 200 bytes), so every reasoning delta triggers an immediate full render_viewport with no time throttle at all. For AgentEvent::Token every delta containing a newline repaints immediately, so code-heavy answers repaint at token rate rather than at STREAM_REPAINT_INTERVAL (40 ms). Combined with per-row flushing this is the dominant cost while the model is streaming. The 100 ms running tick that is meant to paint the tail (paint_pending_chat) is a fresh sleep future created on every select! loop iteration, so during a burst of events closer than 100 ms apart it never fires.
WHERE: src/ui/event_handler.rs:69-85 (STREAM_REPAINT_INTERVAL, stream_repaint_due), 159-166 (Reasoning), 195-213 (Token); src/ui/app.rs:2089-2097 (sleep(100ms) tick branch inside tokio::select!).
HOW: Make the throttle purely time based (paint when since_last_paint >= interval, plus a first-paint exception) for both Reasoning and Token; store a tokio::time::Interval (or a deadline Instant) in App so the tail paint fires reliably at the interval while is_running; lower the tail interval to the repaint interval (40 ms) while a stream is active and keep 100 ms for the spinner. Keep the existing test long_streamed_paragraphs_keep_repainting_without_newlines meaningful by asserting a bounded time-to-paint instead of immediate paint.
VERIFY: src/ui/event_handler.rs tests for stream_repaint_due updated; an App fixture test streams 500 one-line tokens 1 ms apart and asserts render_viewport count <= elapsed/interval + 2 (count via a test counter on Renderer); feed tests markdown_bytes_parsed/block_renders stay green.

title: Sandbox profile ladder (workspace | host-read | host-full): let bwrap grant the maximum filesystem access it can, chosen explicitly like yolo, with permissions staying orthogonal
description:
WHAT: The sandbox has only on/off while permissions have a ladder up to `yolo` ("allow everything; ask for destructive shell commands", src/permission/mod.rs:457-478). On Linux the bwrap profile is an empty root plus `/usr /bin /sbin /lib /lib32 /lib64 /nix` read-only, `/etc/localtime` and `/etc/ld.so.cache`, fresh `/proc` and `/dev`, a tmpfs `/tmp`, the workspace and the sandbox cache read-write (src/sandbox.rs:2650-2676; the hook profile at :2240-2262 and the loop validator use the same set). Everything else is invisible: `~/.cargo`, `~/.rustup`, `~/.npm`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.config/`, `/opt`, `/snap`, `/var/lib`, `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/resolv.conf`, other projects under `$HOME`. So `cargo test` fails whenever rustup lives in `$HOME` (the normal install), `node`/`python` tools under `~/.local` or `/opt` are "not found", and the model concludes the host is broken. The only escape is `--no-sandbox`, which drops all containment at once. macOS is already far more permissive for the same permission mode: the Seatbelt profile grants `(allow file-read*)` over the whole host minus the private denies with writes limited to workspace, cache and /dev/null (src/sandbox.rs:4401-4409). Windows has `windows-appcontainer-read-roots` / `write-roots` keys (CONFIG.md:651-652) but Linux and macOS have no equivalent. Codex offers `--sandbox read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access`; Claude Code's Linux sandbox binds the full host read-only with workspace write. The request: a sandbox ladder up to the maximum filesystem access bubblewrap can grant, chosen explicitly like `yolo`, with the permission mode staying orthogonal (profile = what the OS lets a command touch; mode = when the user is asked). WHERE: src/sandbox.rs build_bwrap_base_command (:2650) and the hook/validator builders; the Seatbelt profile builder (:4396-4410) for the macOS analogue (write scope); src/config/keys.rs + src/config/mod.rs (new keys), src/cli.rs (`--sandbox-profile`), src/ui/slash/settings.rs (`/sandbox`), src/ui/statusline.rs (segment), docs/agent/CONFIG.md, GET_STARTED.md "Feature contract", TOOL_RUNTIME.md. The JS worker profile (src/sandbox/worker/linux.rs, Phase 6) is out of scope and must stay broker-only. HOW: 1. Config `sandbox-profile = "workspace" | "host-read" | "host-full"` (default `workspace`, today's behaviour), plus `sandbox-read-roots` / `sandbox-write-roots` arrays as the Linux/macOS analogue of the Windows root keys; CLI `--sandbox-profile

`; `/sandbox` prints the active profile with a one-line description per level and switches it for the session (same shape as `/mode`); `--print-config` shows it. 2. `host-read` (bwrap): `--ro-bind / /` first, then the read-write binds (workspace at its real path per mini-agent-i7ro6.99, cache, configured write roots), fresh `--proc /proc`, `--dev /dev`, `--tmpfs /tmp`, then the read-only Git metadata binds on top, then the private denies: mini-agent's config, credentials, state and data directories and the usual secret directories (reuse the exact list the Seatbelt `private_read_denies` uses so both platforms agree) masked with `--tmpfs` or `--ro-bind-try /dev/null`. Namespaces, `--new-session`, `--die-with-parent`, no-new-privs and seccomp unchanged. 3. `host-full`: the maximum bubblewrap allows: `--bind / /` read-write with the same private denies, Git metadata protections and namespaces; still never `--share-net` by itself: network stays governed by the existing `deny_network` decision (src/sandbox.rs:1887-1924, :2461), optionally exposed as a separate `sandbox-network = deny | allow` key since bwrap can only share or unshare the stack. Explicit opt-in only (config key or flag; never selected by a prompt or project config without the trust binding), a red `sandbox:host-full` status segment, and the startup notice names it, mirroring the `yolo` and `sandbox:off` treatment. 4. macOS: `host-read` is already the Seatbelt default; `host-full` widens `(allow file-write*)` to the host minus the private and Git denies; `workspace` tightens reads to the workspace, cache and system paths. Keep profiles symmetric in meaning across platforms and document where a platform cannot honour a level (Windows: map to the existing root keys). 5. The built-in auto-allows for workspace toolchain commands (`cargo test` etc.) stay as they are; `host-full` does not change permission mode. VERIFY: src/sandbox.rs bind-argument tests per profile (root bind first, private denies present, Git metadata binds after the workspace bind, workspace bound read-write, `--unshare-net` still follows deny_network); src/tests/sandbox_platform_tests.rs on Linux: under `host-read` `cat ~/.bashrc` works, `touch ~/x` fails, `ls ` and `ls ~/.ssh` are empty or denied, workspace writes work, `cargo --version` from a rustup in `$HOME` works; under `host-full` `touch ~/x` works and the config dir is still unreadable; under `workspace` behaviour is byte-identical to today; config tests for the keys, the explicit-opt-in rule and project-config trust; statusline test for the segment; `--print-config` shows the profile; docs updated; `cargo test` and strict Clippy green on Linux and macOS.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux: (a) sandbox-profile defaults to workspace and produces today's bwrap argument list byte for byte; (b) host-read exposes the whole host read-only, workspace/cache/configured write roots read-write, fresh /proc /dev /tmp, Git metadata read-only, and masks mini-agent's config/credentials/state dirs and the secret directories the macOS private deny list names; (c) host-full is read-write everywhere except those masks and Git metadata, requires explicit opt-in, shows a red status segment and a startup notice, and never changes the permission mode or shares the network on its own; (d) cargo test with rustup in $HOME passes under host-read; (e) /sandbox shows and switches the profile; (f) macOS honours the same three names with documented semantics; (g) the JS worker profile is untouched (Phase 6 checklist re-read, no change).

title: Linux sandbox shows the workspace as /workspace while the prompt and file tools use the real path: bind the workspace at its real path (decision locked), /workspace only as an announced fallback
description:
WHAT: On Linux with the bwrap sandbox the model is told "Current working directory: /home/<user>/projekte/testprojekt" (src/agent/builder.rs:358-360 appends the real `cwd` to the preamble), but every shell command runs with that directory bound at `/workspace`: `Sandbox::sandbox_cwd` (src/sandbox.rs:2678-2684) returns `/workspace` whenever a workspace binding exists on unix, and the launcher does `--dir /workspace` + `--bind <cwd> /workspace` (src/sandbox.rs:2666-2671; the same remap is applied at :2587 and :2632). So `pwd` prints `/workspace`, `ls /home/<user>/projekte/testprojekt` fails inside the sandbox, while `read`/`edit`/`grep` use the real path. Nothing tells the model about the alias: grep "/workspace" over src/agent, data/prompts and docs/agent finds only an unrelated SKILLS.md line. Observed result in a real session: the model concluded the shell and the file tools "see different filesystems" and stopped trusting its own edits.

WHERE: src/agent/builder.rs preamble "Current working directory" (:358, and the second builder at :1259); the shell tool description in src/agent/tools/bash.rs (schema text) and src/agent/prompt.rs shell guidance; the sandbox knows whether the remap is active (`Sandbox::sandbox_cwd(cwd) != cwd`); docs/agent/TOOL_RUNTIME.md and GET_STARTED.md "Feature contract" (Linux section) never mention `/workspace`.

DECISION (2026-10-13, after an advocate / devil's-advocate pass): remove the second view instead of translating it. The bwrap bind source is the pinned workspace authority descriptor (`/proc/self/fd/197`, src/sandbox.rs:1359), not the pathname, so the destination is a free choice; `/workspace` is only a convention introduced in 3099d5c3 with no stated reason. Bind the workspace at its real canonical path. Rejected: bidirectional textual mapping (rewrite real path -> /workspace in scripts, /workspace -> real path in output, alias in file tools) because it would make the executed script differ from the script the user approved in the permission prompt, corrupt legitimate output that contains the string, add an alias into permission-sensitive path resolution, and still leave sandbox-produced artifacts (cargo dep-info and incremental caches, compile_commands.json, LSP paths) keyed by /workspace so the host rebuilds everything. Rejected as the final state: a prompt line alone, which teaches the model to live with the defect.

HOW:
  1. `Sandbox::sandbox_cwd` (src/sandbox.rs:2678-2684) returns the real canonical workspace path (WorkspaceBinding.root, src/paths.rs:68-76) on Linux instead of `/workspace`; `build_bwrap_base_command` (:2650-2676) binds fd 197 at that path (bwrap creates the destination directories inside the empty root) and the three launch sites (:2587, :2632, :2666) plus `append_bwrap_isolation --chdir` follow automatically. Order the workspace bind after the `/usr`.. ro-binds and the `/tmp` tmpfs so a workspace under them mounts on top. Keep the read-only Git metadata binds derived from sandbox_cwd (git_metadata.apply) and the alternate/linked-worktree gitdir binds at their real paths, which they already are.
  2. If the spelled workspace path differs from the canonical one (a symlinked `/home`), bind at the canonical path and add `--symlink <canonical> <spelled>` for each differing ancestor so both spellings work; the prompt keeps stating the spelled path.
  3. Fallback: if the real path cannot be a bind destination (it is `/`, or under `/proc`, `/dev`, `/sys`, or the sandbox control directories), keep the `/workspace` bind and, only then, append the explanatory line after "Current working directory:" in src/agent/builder.rs:358 and in the shell tool description, sourced from a new `Sandbox::shell_cwd_alias() -> Option<PathBuf>` so the string is not hard-coded and the preamble stays byte-identical on hosts without the fallback (macOS Seatbelt and Windows never remap).
  4. Update the tests that pin `/workspace` (src/sandbox.rs ~5780-6124) to the real path, keep one fallback test, and document in docs/agent/TOOL_RUNTIME.md and the Linux section of GET_STARTED.md that sandboxed commands see the workspace at its real path (fallback: /workspace, announced in the prompt).

VERIFY: Linux: `mini-agent -p "run pwd and then read ./README.md; do the two tools see the same directory?"` prints the real path from pwd and answers yes; `cargo test` run inside the sandbox then `cargo test` on the host does not rebuild the crate (dep-info paths match); src/sandbox.rs bind tests assert the real destination, the symlinked-ancestor case, and the `/workspace` fallback with the prompt line; builder test beside `prompt_cache_prefix_is_byte_stable_across_consecutive_turns` asserts no alias line when no fallback is active; the existing Git metadata and fd-197 closing tests (:5846-5882, :6110) still pass; macOS/Windows suites unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux with bwrap: (a) pwd inside a sandboxed shell prints the real canonical workspace path and shell commands naming that path succeed; (b) no textual rewriting of scripts or output exists anywhere; (c) sandbox-produced cargo artifacts are reused by a host cargo run without rebuilding; (d) a symlinked ancestor spelling also resolves inside the sandbox; (e) when the real path cannot be a bind destination the /workspace fallback is used and the preamble plus shell tool description state it, sourced from Sandbox, and are byte-identical to today otherwise; (f) Git metadata read-only binds, alternate gitdir binds and the fd-197 close still hold; (g) manual -p check answers that both tools see the same directory without hedging.

title: /mcp add|remove, project .mcp.json support and an allow_local option for loopback HTTP servers
description:
WHAT: `handle_mcp` (src/ui/slash/settings.rs:464-640) has only list/login/logout; servers are configured by editing TOML (CONFIG.md:1780-2006). `.mcp.json` (Claude Code's project format, also read by opencode/Codex-compatible tools) is not read; project servers only via .zerostack/config.toml (CONFIG.md:1860). `parse_mcp_server_url` rejects localhost (src/extras/mcp/client.rs:867) and `is_restricted_ipv4` rejects 127/10/192.168 (client.rs:933) with "use a stdio server", but `http://localhost:3000/mcp` dev servers are the common case in Claude Code and opencode.

WHERE: src/ui/slash/settings.rs; config writer used by `/models-add` (src/ui/slash/providers.rs); src/extras/mcp/config.rs (new `.mcp.json` loader, trust-gated like project config, env var substitution `${VAR}`); src/extras/mcp/client.rs per-server `allow_local = true` that skips egress pinning only for loopback addresses and still forbids redirects elsewhere.

HOW: `/mcp add <name> <command|url> [args…]` writes the server to the global or project config (`--project`), reconnects (`reconnect_in_binding`); `/mcp remove <name>`; `.mcp.json` servers listed with their origin in `/mcp`; `allow_local` documented with the DNS-rebinding rationale kept for non-loopback.

VERIFY: slash tests for add/remove round trip on a temp config; mcp config test for .mcp.json parsing and trust; client test that loopback is accepted only with allow_local; `cargo test mcp`.
design:
Read-only design against f4b49dd3; relevant MCP/config/settings/providers/paths code is identical to the owned79756 index. No new worktree/source/Cargo until parent stable batch authorization.

1. Operator surface: /mcp add <name> <command|url> [literal args...] [--project] [--allow-local]; /mcp remove <name> [--project]. Consume raw command via a bounded literal argv parser (quotes/empty strings/Unicode preserved; no shell/env expansion here, flags only explicit syntax, -- separator). Reject duplicate names rather than replace invisibly. URL form forbids trailing argv; --allow-local applies only URL. Built-in registrations remain opaque and cannot be forged/removed as user entries; explain their dedicated enable settings. Listing must work even manager=None, showing every selected/inactive per-server origin and connection state without contacting untrusted definitions.

2. Structural persistence: use existing private structural Config delta for global TOML/JSON preserving unavailable keys, nested unknown fields and unchanged project values; never serialize effective Config wholesale. Project writes target captured workspace .mcp.json with a retained no-follow regular snapshot/identity+content CAS and private atomic publication, including new-file create-only. Existing JSON fields outside mcpServers and unknown server fields survive. Project TOML servers remain supported; removal targets the declared owning source, not an unrelated inherited record. Failure leaves memory/catalogue/connection unchanged. Confirm exact write destination and reject an origin mismatch rather than silently deleting a shadowed lower-layer definition.

description:
WHAT: Cargo.toml default features omit `lsp`, `hooks` and `multimodal`, so release binaries cannot show diagnostics after an edit, run lifecycle hooks, or attach an image, although all three are table stakes in Claude Code and opencode (opencode auto-loads LSPs; Claude Code has hooks and reads images by default). Post-edit diagnostics are already implemented (src/agent/tools/edit.rs:1125+, write.rs:247) but gated by the feature AND `[lsp] enabled = true` (src/config/mod.rs:798). The extra dependencies are small: `process-wrap` and `which` are already in the default build via `mcp`; lsp adds `lsp-types` + `url`; hooks adds nothing; multimodal adds `rig/image`. Built-in LSP servers only spawn when the binary is on PATH (src/extras/lsp/registry.rs).

WHERE: Cargo.toml [features] default; src/config/mod.rs lsp enabled default (auto when a built-in server is on PATH); docs README feature table, GET_STARTED "Feature contract", CONFIG.md; CI feature matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml rows that build the non-default combinations); the LSP registry ordering bug should land first.

HOW: add the three features to default; make `[lsp].enabled` default to "auto" (on when a registry server is found); keep the hooks dispatcher inert without config; update docs and CHANGELOG; keep the `-lite` archive unchanged.

VERIFY: `cargo test` default build includes the lsp/hooks/multimodal test modules; release workflow builds succeed; `/toggle` lists lsp/hooks availability; manual: edit a .rs file with rust-analyzer installed shows diagnostics.

title: Configurable shell foreground deadline and job_status wait/list actions so long commands stop costing a turn per poll
description:
WHAT: src/agent/tools/bash.rs:131-135 clamps `timeout` to DEFAULT_COMMAND_LIMITS.timeout (30 s, src/sandbox.rs:362); `JobStatusTool::call` (bash.rs:184-191) only polls a snapshot or stops; docs/agent/TOOL_RUNTIME.md documents this as deliberate. Consequence: `cargo test` must go to the background and the model spends one turn (and max_agent_turns budget) per immediate poll; job ids are lost after compaction with no `list`. Claude Code's default foreground limit is 2 min (configurable to 10), Codex has no fixed 30 s cap.

WHERE: src/agent/tools/bash.rs BashArgs/JobStatusArgs (src/agent/tools/mod.rs:342); src/sandbox.rs DEFAULT_COMMAND_LIMITS; config key `shell_timeout_secs` (default e.g. 120, hard max e.g. 600) in src/config; docs TOOL_RUNTIME.md and CONFIG.md.

HOW: make the foreground deadline configurable with a hard ceiling; `job_status` gains `action: "wait"` with `timeout_ms` (blocks up to the limit, returns when the job ends or the wait expires, with new output) and `action: "list"`; the schema text says the effective cap.

VERIFY: tests beside `background_job_timeout_is_terminal_and_has_no_exit_code` (bash.rs:764) for wait returning early on completion and on timeout, and list after compaction; config test for the ceiling; `cargo test bash`.

title: web_fetch and web_search model tools (outside the JS runtime)
description:
WHAT: Claude Code (WebFetch/WebSearch), Codex (web search) and opencode (webfetch) give the model direct web access with domain permissions. Here fetch exists only inside the JS runtime (`fetch` effect, src/extras/js/worker.rs:500, FetchPolicy src/extras/js/host.rs:145, `js-fetch-origins`), and search only through the built-in Exa MCP server (src/extras/mcp/config.rs TrustedMcpServer::Exa, needs EXA_API_KEY); grep web_fetch|web_search in src: none. title: --allow / --deny CLI rules to seed session permissions in headless runs (allowedTools equivalent)
description:
WHAT: Claude Code's `--allowedTools "Bash(git *)" --disallowedTools …` and Codex's approval/sandbox flags let a CI job grant exactly what the task needs. Here `--tools/--no-tools` select tools (src/cli.rs:593-601), modes (`--read-only/--guarded/--accept-all/--yolo`) are coarse, and per-session allow patterns exist only in `Session.permission_allowlist` + `permission::add_session_allowlist` (used by ACP AllowAlways, src/extras/acp/mod.rs:1808); nothing seeds them from the CLI, so headless either asks (and fails closed) or runs yolo.

WHERE: src/cli.rs; src/startup.rs Startup::init after session resolution (~760); src/permission/checker.rs (session allow/deny lists; the Bash prefix form from the "Bash allow rules" bead).

HOW: repeatable `--allow <tool>:<pattern>` and `--deny <tool>:<pattern>` (same syntax as permission-allow keys, e.g. `--allow "bash:cargo test" --allow "write:src/**" --deny "write:**/*.env"`), applied as session rules after config rules with deny winning; `--print-config` shows the effective rules; document in GET_STARTED CLI flags and CONFIG.md rule precedence.

VERIFY: src/tests/checker_tests.rs for precedence; tests/headless_json.rs run with `--allow write:tmp/**` writes without an ask channel and `--deny` blocks; `cargo test`.

title: Headless scripting ergonomics: session_id in --output json, stdin as prompt context, tool progress on stderr in text mode
description:
WHAT (three small gaps that every CI/script user hits):
  1. `HeadlessJsonOutput` (src/print.rs:384) has result, files_changed, tool_calls, usage, cost, stop_reason, goal but no `session_id`/`session_name`, so a script cannot `--session <id>` on the next call.
  2. `cat file | mini-agent -p "summarize"` ignores stdin: src/main.rs:219 uses `is_terminal()` only to choose the TUI; startup stdin reads are interactive prompts; tests/headless_json.rs:512 asserts loop mode never reads stdin. Claude Code and Codex append piped stdin to the prompt.
  3. In text mode tool calls are shown only with `--pure-stdout`, and then on stdout mixed with the answer (src/agent/runner.rs:3666-3669); reasoning already goes to stderr (:3634). Scripts want a clean stdout answer and progress on stderr.

WHERE: src/print.rs HeadlessJsonOutput; src/startup.rs dispatch_print (~1365); src/agent/runner.rs text-mode printing; docs GET_STARTED.md CLI flags and the `--output json` example (:284).

HOW: add session_id/session_name to the JSON object; when stdin is not a terminal and not empty, read it (bounded, e.g. 1 MiB) and append it as a fenced block after the prompt (never when the prompt is empty: see the empty-prompt bug); print `◈ tool args` and one-line result summaries to stderr by default in text mode (`--quiet` to silence), keep stdout for the answer.

VERIFY: tests/headless_json.rs: JSON contains session_id matching the saved session; piped stdin appears in the persisted user message; stderr contains the tool line and stdout only the answer; `cargo test headless_json`.

title: Esc-Esc opens /rewind, and rewind can restore the files the agent changed (per-turn checkpoints)
description:
WHAT: Claude Code checkpoints every file before an edit and `/rewind` (or Esc Esc) restores code, conversation or both; opencode has undo/redo of file changes. Here `rewind_targets` (src/ui/mod.rs:697) rewinds messages only, `/undo stash` is a plain git stash, the picker is reachable only via `/rewind` (code comments mention double-Esc at src/ui/pickers/rewind.rs:23 and input/mod.rs:533 but no handler exists), and "checkpoint" hits in src are JS/fs internals.

WHERE: src/agent/tools/edit.rs and write.rs (before the atomic write; `pending.record_tool_output` hook in src/ui/event_handler.rs:210 already sees touched paths); src/session (per-message checkpoint map); src/ui/pickers/rewind.rs confirm stage; src/ui/app.rs handle_key_event for the Esc timer; session storage `tool_outputs` dir for blobs.

HOW: (1) Esc on an empty idle input twice within 500 ms opens the rewind picker (S). (2) Before each write/edit, store the prior content (content-addressed under the session dir, bounded total size, skip files > N MiB) keyed by message index; the rewind confirm offers "conversation only / files only / both" and restores by rewriting the files (refuse if the file changed since the checkpoint unless forced). Document the storage and bounds.

VERIFY: tests in src/ui/app.rs for the Esc-Esc timing; session tests for checkpoint recording and restore (TempDir); manual: edit a file, `/rewind` -> both -> file content restored.

title: Add /diff, /commit and /pr commands over the structured git tool
description:
WHAT: src/git/tool.rs:760 exposes status, diff, log, show, stage, unstage, commit (no remotes/network) but there is no user-facing `/diff`, `/commit` or `/pr` (grep over src/ui/slash: none). Codex has /diff, Claude Code users rely on `/commit`-style commands and PR creation; opencode has /share-able sessions. `pending.record_tool_output(path)` (src/ui/event_handler.rs:210) already tracks files touched this turn and `print::files_changed_since` + `WorkspaceChangeBaseline` (src/print.rs:645) exist for headless.

WHERE: src/ui/slash/mod.rs dispatch (:733-822) + new src/ui/slash/git.rs; src/git/tool.rs; src/ui/slash/review.rs as the one-shot prompt pattern.

HOW: `/diff [path|turn]` runs the git tool's diff (working tree, or only this turn's touched files) and renders it with the diff block styles from the inline-diff bead; `/commit [msg]` is a one-shot prompt like `/review` that stages the turn's files and commits through the git tool (message generated when absent, user confirms in the chain prompt); `/pr` runs `gh pr create` via the shell tool under normal permission with a generated title/body and prints the URL. Headless: `--commit` flag optional later.

VERIFY: tests in src/ui/slash for dispatch and for the git tool calls (TempRepo helper in src/tests/worktree_tests.rs); manual: edit, `/diff`, `/commit`, `git log -1`.
design: Implement user-facing commands in new bounded src/ui/slash/git.rs. /diff uses the existing captured GitTool through an owned SDK-free native actor with AgentWorkScope/AgentRunCleanupGuard and normal Ask channel, so UI cancellation and permission replies remain live; no ambient git subprocess API or policy bypass. Reuse parent-owned semantic diff colors, sanitize/cap rows, feature-off diagnostics. Turn selection derives bounded literal native edit/write request paths from the latest visible turn, labels it accurately; captured workspace strips only inside-root absolute paths, no shell/MCP text guessing. /commit freezes selected paths; supplied message skips model generation, absent message uses existing one-shot read-only review run and bounded exact JSON decode. Show paths/message then explicit chain Y/N/B. After approval, native actor checks git/status, refuses unrelated existing staged paths, stages only frozen operands and commits captured literal message via the structured GitTool. No LLM receives write tools for actual commit execution. /pr uses read-only preparation for bounded generated title/body, previews before confirmation, then invokes fixed gh pr create through the normal ShellTool with dialect-appropriate literal quoting and normal permissions. Keep proposal tied to session/workspace identity, discard on failure/interruption/session switch; do not fabricate effects or usage, do not treat imported history requests as effect proof. Tests: actual dispatcher/native actor controls, decline/cancel/stale identity, exact selected paths/literal message, prior staged unrelated guard, real offline native smoke. No unrelated full local Rust suite; current pushed cef CI remains independent.

description:

title: A message starting with "." is swallowed as a prompt switch (".gitignore is wrong" -> unknown prompt), and one-shot .prompt messages echo twice
description:
WHAT: `handle_dot_command` (src/ui/app.rs:2285-2355) treats any text starting with `.` as a prompt command: `.gitignore is wrong` and `...continue` print "error: unknown prompt 'gitignore'" (app.rs:2328/2352) and the message is dropped after being echoed. Idle checks use `text.starts_with('.')` / `'/'` without trimming (app.rs ~2289, ~1715) so `" .foo"` reaches the model, but while running `classify_submission` (src/ui/mod.rs:720-724) trims and returns RejectWhileRunning, so the leading-space escape only works when idle. Separately, a one-shot `.plan what changed?` is echoed as `> .plan what changed?` (app.rs:2294-2298) and again as `> what changed?` by the caller (app.rs:1720-1724).

WHERE: src/ui/app.rs handle_dot_command and the submit path ~1715-1725; src/ui/mod.rs classify_submission.

HOW: treat `.name` as a command only when `name` is a known prompt (or the bare `.`), otherwise fall through to a normal message; make the leading-whitespace rule identical in the idle and running paths; echo the one-shot message once (drop the first echo or make the caller skip it when the dot handler already echoed).

VERIFY: tests on `classify_submission` in src/ui/mod.rs and a new test on `handle_dot_command` with `.gitignore is wrong` (sent as prompt), `.plan foo` (one-shot, echoed once), `.unknownprompt` alone (error); `cargo test ui`.
design: Reconcile HOW literal unknown dot+message with VERIFY bare-identifier diagnostic: unknown names with message and punctuation/ellipsis are ordinary model text; unknown bare identifier errors. Shared DotSubmission parser uses current known prompt map for idle handler and running gate. Dot leading whitespace ignored consistently; slash/bang whitespace unchanged. Known prompt with whitespace-only tail switches, never sends empty message. title: Ctrl-C during a run destroys the typed draft (no kill ring) and silently discards queued messages
description:
WHAT: `abort_main_run` (src/ui/app.rs ~2113 and ~2147-2149): `self.run.pending_inputs.clear();` with no transcript notice, and `if !self.input.buffer.is_empty() { self.input.clear_buffer(); }`. `clear_buffer` (src/ui/input/mod.rs:391) just clears; the idle Ctrl-C path uses `discard_draft()` (input/mod.rs:401, app.rs ~1439) which pushes to the kill ring so Ctrl+Y restores. `fail_pending_main_turn` (app.rs ~2075) also clears pending_inputs silently. Repro: start a turn, type a long follow-up, press Ctrl-C: the text is gone and Ctrl+Y does nothing; with two queued messages, Ctrl-C then `/queue` prints "queue is empty". COMMANDS.md documents only the idle behaviour ("Ctrl+Y brings it back") and `/queue` never says interrupts drop the queue. Claude Code keeps the draft on interrupt.

WHERE: src/ui/app.rs abort_main_run, fail_pending_main_turn; src/ui/input/mod.rs clear_buffer/discard_draft; docs/agent/COMMANDS.md Ctrl+C row and /queue rows.

HOW: in both abort paths call `discard_draft()` instead of `clear_buffer()` (or do not touch the buffer at all unless a failed prompt is being reloaded, and then push the current draft to the kill ring first); keep queued inputs and print "N queued inputs kept; /queue clear to drop them" (or drop them with a visible "dropped N queued inputs" line). Update the two doc rows.

VERIFY: tests beside `cancelled_turn_restores_the_prompt_and_pre_turn_transcript` (src/ui/app.rs ~3762): after abort with a non-empty draft, Ctrl+Y yields the draft; after abort with two pending inputs, the transcript contains the notice and `/queue` lists or reports them; `cargo test ui`.

Progress-preserving interrupts leave draft in editor. Queued inputs still drop to prevent automatic post-interrupt restart, with visible dropped N queued inputs notice (best-effort presentation in exception-safe failure cleanup; warns if renderer fails). title: /wt-merge cleanup is refused whenever the worktree holds any ignored file (target/, node_modules/), leaving the branch and worktree behind with no documented reason
description:

For a Rust or JS repo the agent has run `cargo test`/`npm test` in the worktree, so every `/wt-merge` ends this way. The test `ignored_source_files_refuse_cleanup_and_survive_a_successful_merge` (src/tests/worktree_tests.rs:3089) pins this as intended (an ignored `.env` must not be deleted by `worktree remove --force`), but docs/agent/COMMANDS.md Worktree section and CONFIG.md never mention it (grep "ignored" finds nothing relevant).

title: Bash allow rules are exact-string only, so permission-allow globs like "git status*" are silent no-ops; warn at load and add an opt-in prefix form
description:
WHAT: src/permission/checker.rs ~790: `let matches = if tool == "shell" && *action == Action::Allow { pattern.original == policy_input } else { pattern.matches(policy_input) };` ("Model B: allow only the exact, complete script"). `permission-allow = { bash = ["git status*", "cargo test*"] }` therefore never allows anything, while `permission-ask`/`permission-deny` for the same tool are pattern-based. CONFIG.md:1575-1582 explains Model B, but the key table at CONFIG.md:1744-1757 describes all three maps as "a list of glob patterns" without the exception, and Claude Code users expect `Bash(git *)`-style rules. Fail-closed, so not a security bug, but a trap that makes the permission system feel broken. Related inconsistency: src/permission/pattern.rs ~300 `glob_to_regex` maps `*` to `[^/]*` but `?` to `.` (matches `/`), undocumented.

WHERE: src/permission/checker.rs compile_config (~163) and the shell allow branch (~790); src/permission/pattern.rs glob_to_regex; docs/agent/CONFIG.md:1744-1757.

HOW: (1) At config load, warn once for every `bash` allow entry containing `*`, `?`, `[` or `**` ("bash allow rules match the exact script; use a prefix rule"), and say so in the key table. (2) Add an opt-in prefix form, e.g. `bash = { "git status" = "allow-prefix" }` or `permission-allow-prefix`, that parses the first simple command's argv (no `;`, `&&`, `|`, backticks, `$(`) and matches argv prefix, keeping Model B as the default. (3) Make `?` not match `/` and document glob semantics in one place.

VERIFY: extend src/tests/checker_tests.rs (`standard_allows_configured_bash_commands`, `bash_compound_command_permission_requires_exact_complete_script`) with: glob allow entry emits the load warning and still denies; prefix rule allows `git status --short` but not `git status; rm -rf /`; `?` no longer matches a separator; `cargo test checker`.

title: Completion retry never retries HTTP 408 (and ignores Retry-After) because the provider-status branch returns early
description:
WHAT: src/retry.rs:127-135: `if let Some(provider_status) = provider_response_status(error) { let code = …; return code == 429 || code == 500 || code == 502 || code == 503 || code == 504 || code == 529; }`. Retry-After headers are never consulted (the backoff is purely computed). Claude Code and Codex retry 408/409/425 and honour Retry-After for 429/529.

WHERE: src/retry.rs is_retryable, message_has_retryable_status, backoff computation; tests at retry.rs ~361 (`test_is_retryable_anthropic_529_from_provider_status`).

HOW: add 408 (and 409, 425) to both lists; when the provider error carries headers, parse Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date) and use max(backoff, retry_after) capped by the configured ceiling.

title: find_files tries the pattern as a regex before a glob, so common globs like src/*.rs and test_*.rs silently match nothing
description:
WHAT: `FindFilesPattern::compile` (src/agent/tools/find_files.rs:1111-1123) does `match Regex::new(pattern) { Ok(regex) => FileNameRegex(regex), Err(_) => GlobBuilder… }` and `is_match` applies a regex to the bare file name. `**/*.rs`, `*.rs` and `docs/**` fail regex compilation and become globs (tested at ~1818), but `src/*.rs`, `test_*.rs`, `foo*.ts` are valid regexes (`src/*.rs` means "src", zero or more "/", any char, "rs" tested against a file name) and return "No files found matching the pattern." with no hint. The system prompt tells the model the opposite: src/agent/prompt.rs:79 "**find_files** finds paths by glob". Verified with Python's re: src/*.rs and test_*.rs compile, **/*.rs, *.rs and docs/** do not.

WHERE: src/agent/tools/find_files.rs FindFilesPattern::compile / is_match; schema description in src/agent/tools/mod.rs FindFilesArgs; prompt.rs:79.

HOW: decide glob-first: if the pattern contains any of `* ? [ { /` treat it as a relative-path glob (literal_separator true, and prepend `**/` when it has no `/` so `*.rs` still matches at any depth); fall back to regex only when glob compilation fails or an explicit `mode: "regex"` argument is given. When zero results, append a one-line hint ("interpreted as <glob|regex>; try …"). Update the schema description with both examples.

VERIFY: new tests beside `path_glob_matches_nested_and_root_files` asserting `src/*.rs`, `test_*.rs` and `*.rs` each find `src/test_a.rs`, and `^test_.*\.rs$` still works in regex mode; `cargo test find_files`.

title: /undo cannot remove a turn that used tools: it strips only the final assistant text and then reports nothing to undo
description:
WHAT: `undo_last` (src/ui/slash/mod.rs:351-375) inspects only the last one or two messages: Assistant preceded by User removes 2, Assistant preceded by anything else removes 1, User removes 1, anything else removes 0. A turn with tool use is persisted as User, ToolCall, ToolResult, ..., Assistant (TUI: src/ui/event_handler.rs ~175/211/444; headless: src/print.rs:746-835), so the first `/undo` removes only the assistant text, the second `/undo` sees a ToolResult last and returns 0 ("nothing to undo"), and `/redo` restores only the text. docs/agent/COMMANDS.md promises "Remove the last exchange (user message + assistant response)". No test covers a tool-bearing turn (grep undo_last src/tests: none). Claude Code's /undo and /rewind remove the whole exchange.

WHERE: src/ui/slash/mod.rs undo_last; src/ui/slash/session.rs handle_undo / undo_session_mutation (:547, :649); tests at src/ui/slash/session.rs:1305-1360 (session_with_turn helper at ~1123).

title: Fix gitlink probe pathspec under literal-path policy
description: The hardened internal Git environment sets GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, but populated_gitlinks invokes git ls-files --stage -z -- :(top). Under literal paths, :(top) is interpreted as a literal filename, so even a populated index yields empty output and nested gitlinks are never enumerated. Read-only repro on clean linked fixture: with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, git -C <repo> ls-files --stage -z -- :(top) prints no bytes; without it, tracked entries print. Review nested-repository scan policy as separate security work; user asked to skip cyber fixes for current task.
acceptance_criteria: Nested gitlinks are enumerated under the hardened policy and tests cover literal pathspec handling; preserve canonical containment invariants.
close_reason: False positive. populated_gitlinks explicitly overrides GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=0 after build_internal_command; on Git 2.50.1 the exact ls-files --stage -z -- :(top) probe lists tracked entries with =0 and returns empty only with =1. Earlier read-only reproduction omitted this probe-specific override. No source fix needed.

title: grep/find_files/list_dir return content and names from files the user denied to `read`; per-file deny rules are not honoured
description:
src/agent/tools/grep.rs:424-476 authorises only the search root (check_perm_bound_path for `.`) then
search_bound_directory returns matching lines from every file beneath with no per-file check; deny rules
are keyed per tool and `read` aliases only to js/read_file and lsp_diagnostics
(src/permission/checker.rs:1395-1403). `permission.read = { "config/secrets/**" = "deny" }` blocks `read`
but `grep {pattern: ".", path: "."}` returns the file's contents (unless gitignored); find_files leaks
names. docs/agent/CONFIG.md:1579-1586 implies path denies cover every spelling. FIX: while walking, check
each candidate file's workspace-relative path against the read and grep deny rules
(matches_path_for_deny) and skip denied files/directories via a new non-prompting
PermissionChecker::is_path_denied(tool, relative) (no doom-loop tracking); apply the same filter to
find_files and list_dir. Document in CONFIG.md. TESTS: grep_skips_files_matching_read_deny_rules,
grep_skips_directories_matching_grep_deny_rules, find_files_omits_denied_paths, list_dir equivalent.
close_reason: Merged: PathDenyProbe (deny-only, non-prompting) filters grep/find_files/list_dir walks for read and tool deny rules incl. external_directory denies; tests added. Follow-up suggestion: apply the same filter to JS host directory discovery.

title: LSP and stdio MCP executables resolve through relative/empty PATH entries and can run workspace-planted binaries (hooks already defend)
description:
src/extras/lsp/client.rs:1233-1252 uses which::which(cfg.command); src/extras/mcp/client.rs:683-687 uses
rmcp::transport::which_command (which::which). which 8.0.6 resolves relative PATH entries against the
process cwd (the workspace) and keeps empty entries on Unix (finder.rs:175-181). Built-in LSP servers
have sandbox: None (src/extras/lsp/registry.rs:11-23). Hooks strip such entries deliberately
(src/extras/hooks/pins.rs:205-219 absolute_search_path). A repo shipping an executable rust-analyzer/
gopls at a matching relative location runs unsandboxed when PATH has `.`/relative/empty entries. FIX:
share absolute_search_path (move to a common module) and resolve LSP and MCP stdio commands with
which::which_in(cmd, Some(absolute_path), <non-workspace cwd>); reject relative commands containing a
separator unless the config explicitly anchors them. Update docs/specs/subprocess-trust.md launch
fields for TC-LSP/TC-MCP. TESTS: with PATH="<tmp>/bin::", cwd = temp workspace, fake rust-analyzer in
both, assert lsp_command and stdio_command pick <tmp>/bin; with only the workspace copy, "not found".
close_reason: Merged a58c4d7: shared executable_search resolves LSP/stdio MCP commands only through absolute PATH entries from a non-workspace cwd; relative paths with a directory need an anchoring cwd; mcp feature uses dep:which; tests and spec rows updated.

title: Untrusted project config can set unbounded [retry] values (benign key): clamp RetryConfig at load
description:
src/config/load.rs:22-58 BENIGN_PROJECT_CONFIG_KEYS contains "retry" (merged without a trust prompt,
also headless). src/retry.rs:7-23 RetryConfig has no validation; retry.rs:209-245 never clamps the
initial backoff by max_backoff and sleeps `delay`. A cloned repo's .zerostack/config.toml with
`[retry] max_attempts = 4000000000, initial_backoff_ms = 0, max_backoff_ms = 0` turns every 429/5xx into
a zero-delay loop (also mid-stream via CompletionRetryState::retry_delay src/agent/runner.rs:1151-1183);
`initial_backoff_ms = 9000000000000000` hangs `-p` in CI (tokio saturates). CONFIG.md:50-56 calls retry
"bounded". FIX: validate RetryConfig at load: clamp max_attempts to 1..=10, both backoffs to <= 60_000 ms,
initial <= max; warn when clamped. Consider removing `retry` (and review `model`) from the benign list
or accepting project values only when tighter than the global config. Update CONFIG.md and
docs/specs/platform-paths.md:107-115 wording. TESTS: config-load test that extreme project [retry] is
clamped in headless mode; retry unit test that the first delay never exceeds max_backoff_ms.
close_reason: Merged: RetryConfig clamped at load (attempts 1..=10, backoffs <= 60 s, initial <= max) and at every retry site; project config may only tighten the global policy; clamped fields warn on stderr; tests added; docs updated.

title: A custom provider named after a built-in alias (custom, google, openai...) inherits the vendor key and sends it to its third-party base_url
description:
src/auth.rs:15-24 maps "openai" | "custom" to ProviderKind::OpenAI; custom_provider() (auth.rs:73-82)
returns None whenever the name is a built-in alias, so auth.rs:104-137 falls back to the vendor env var
(OPENAI_API_KEY) and api_keys.openai for `custom_providers.custom = { base_url = "https://gw.example" }`.
The in-code comment promises the opposite. Same for entries named google/anthropic. Existing tests
cover only local-vllm. FIX: treat any name present in custom_providers (whose base_url differs from the
built-in endpoint) as custom for credential purposes: only its own api_key_env and api_keys[<name>]
apply. If shadowing a built-in to reuse its key is a supported proxy feature, require an explicit
`inherit_builtin_key = true`. Document in CONFIG.md. TESTS: AuthResolver/create_client test with
custom_providers.custom (provider_type openai, base_url gw.example) and OPENAI_API_KEY set asserting a
"No API key found for custom provider" error; same for google.
close_reason: Merged: custom_providers entries named after built-ins are credential-isolated unless on the vendor's own origin or inherit_builtin_key = true; error names the fix; tests and CONFIG.md updated.
