or JS spawn denies anything. FIX: add a macOS CI step running these three tests with --exact --nocapture
and failing on any 'skipping' output (or make them panic when MINI_AGENT_REQUIRE_REAL_SANDBOX=1 / CI is
set). TESTS: extend scripts/tests/test_phase6_ci_workflow.py to require the guard step.
close_reason: Merged: skip_unusable_real_sandbox_test panics under MINI_AGENT_REQUIRE_REAL_SANDBOX=1; macos-worker-containment-gate runs the three real Seatbelt general-sandbox tests with it set and fails on skip; policy test added; phase-2 spec documents the guard.

title: No cross-process guard on session files: two processes resuming the same session silently lose each other's turns
description:
src/session/storage.rs:83-100 save_session() is a whole-snapshot atomic overwrite with no lock and no
version check; nothing in src/session, startup.rs or ui/app.rs locks (memory does: Mem::lock_store,
memory/mod.rs:415-428). Two `mini-agent --continue` in one repo (find_recent_sessions_for_workspace picks
the same id) or TUI + scripted `-p --continue` last-writer-wins: turns, tool records, cost and goal
progress vanish silently; with /goal a lost round repeats side effects. FIX: advisory lock (File::lock,
as memory does) on <id>.lock held while a process owns a session; refuse or fork to a new id (with a
notice) on --continue/--session when held; or optimistic concurrency (record updated_at/content hash at
load, refuse to overwrite a changed file). Cover ACP sessions too. TESTS: storage test opening the
session twice, saving A then B, asserting the second save fails or the second open is refused while the
first holds the lock; a --continue test that forks instead of clobbering.
close_reason: Merged 248e3ab: advisory <id>.lock per session (std File::try_lock), save refuses when held elsewhere, --continue/--session and /sessions fork with a notice; tests and docs (CONFIG, GET_STARTED, COMMANDS, platform-paths).

title: Streamable-HTTP MCP responses are unbounded (only stdio has the 16 MiB cap); non-2xx bodies are copied verbatim into errors
description:
src/extras/mcp/client.rs:445-504, 517-528 sets only a connect timeout for the HTTP client; rmcp 2.2.0
streamable_http_client.rs:202-206 puts the whole non-2xx body into the error string, :226 SSE has no
per-event cap, :233 response.json buffers the whole body. MCP_STDIO_MAX_LINE_BYTES (client.rs:51-55) has
no HTTP counterpart, so a misbehaving/compromised remote server can OOM the agent during startup tool
collection or any call, and oversized error text floods notices/model context. FIX: bound response
bodies (custom StreamableHttpClient impl or reqwest wrapper using bytes_stream() with a running cap equal
to MCP_STDIO_MAX_LINE_BYTES that fails the request once exceeded, incl. SSE events); truncate HTTP error
bodies to a few KiB before they enter an error. Reuse existing dependencies; do not add a second
reqwest. TESTS: loopback HTTP fixture returning a JSON body and an SSE event larger than the cap;
assert list_all_tools_bounded / call_tool_bounded fail with a bounded error and the error string
length is capped.
close_reason: Merged 368c73c: BoundedHttpClient implements rmcp StreamableHttpClient over the existing reqwest client with a 16 MiB body/SSE-event cap and 4 KiB non-2xx error excerpt; used for the plain and OAuth transports; loopback tests. OAuth manager's own token/metadata traffic remains rmcp-internal (noted).

title: Config: unknown/misspelled keys are silently ignored (incl. security keys), kebab/snake spellings are not aliased, TOML errors hide position
description:
Config is #[serde(default)] without unknown-key diagnostics (src/config/mod.rs:35-37, 188-204, 267-268;
`#[serde(flatten)] preserved` at mod.rs:384-389). Security keys are kebab-case (permission-deny,
permission-allow, sandbox-backend, permission-modes, js-fetch-origins) while neighbours are snake_case
(default_permission_mode, accept_all, max_tokens). Verified with --print-config: `sandbox_backend =
"bogus"`, `defualt_permission_mode = "readonly"` and `permission_deny = [...]` are silently dropped =>
fail-open misconfiguration of exactly the restricting keys. src/config/load.rs:283-294 maps TOML errors
to "config is not valid TOML" with no line/column. FIX: add #[serde(alias)] for the snake_case spelling
of every kebab key (and the reverse where sensible); collect unknown top-level keys (serde_ignored or
inspect `preserved` against a static list of feature-gated keys so builds don't warn about each other's
keys) and print a startup warning naming each unknown key with its nearest match; surface warnings in
--print-config; print the TOML error line:column (no source snippet). Update CONFIG.md:530-547.
TESTS: config-load test that sandbox_backend, permission_deny, permission_modes, js_fetch_origins
deserialize identically to their kebab forms; unknown key `sandbx = true` yields a warning containing
the key, none for a feature-gated key like mcp_servers in a no-mcp build; parse error includes line.
close_reason: Merged: config key catalogue with feature ownership and aliases (22 kebab keys accept snake_case; default-permission-mode and allow-all-mcp-calls kebab aliases), unknown top-level keys warn with nearest-key suggestion (feature-gated keys silent), both spellings of one key is an error, TOML/YAML errors report line:column without echoing values, warnings shown by --print-config; docs updated.

title: Compaction usage is never charged: session cost, headless JSON cost and goal token bounds omit up to 16 full-context summarizer requests
description:
src/provider.rs:434-480 compress_messages() -> summarize_with_model(...).map(|(summary, _usage)| summary)
(line 473) drops usage; MAX_COMPACTION_REQUESTS = 16 (provider.rs:35). Callers (src/startup.rs:424,
src/ui/slash/mod.rs:449, src/extras/acp/mod.rs:2371) cannot charge it. The judge was fixed (kfsup,
Session::charge_judge_call); the title exclusion is documented (CONFIG.md:492); compaction's is not.
FIX: sum Usage across rolling requests in compress_messages_with/summarize_conversation_bounded and
return it; callers normalize_usage + charge_usage_delta at the session model's prices and goal drivers
add it to the goal token count; document in CONFIG.md (cost section). Also charge or document
src/session/title.rs:121. TESTS: compress_messages_with test with a fake summarizer returning usage
over 3 rolling requests asserting the summed usage; headless test that total_cost increases after
auto-compaction.
close_reason: Merged 208f745: compress_messages returns CompactionOutput with summed usage; headless, TUI /compress and auto-compaction charge it at the session model's prices and add it to goal token counts; ACP adds it to outcome usage; docs updated. Failed compactions are not charged (documented).

title: GPL Corresponding Source tarball omits the npm dependencies bundled into the VSIX dist/extension.js
description:

step, so the VSIX cannot be rebuilt offline the way editors/vscode/SOURCE.md and SOURCE.md claim for the
Rust binary. FIX: include the extension's locked npm dependency sources in the Corresponding Source
archive (e.g. `npm ci --ignore-scripts` + `npm pack` tarballs of every package in package-lock.json, or
a vendored node_modules tarball with integrity hashes) and document the offline rebuild steps in
editors/vscode/SOURCE.md. Keep the archive reproducible and covered by
scripts/tests/test_package_corresponding_source.py (add an assertion that the npm sources are present
and match package-lock.json).
close_reason: Merged a0148d2: Corresponding Source vendors every locked npm tarball (integrity-verified), proves an offline rebuild, deterministic tar; Node pinned in the release corresponding-source job and the CI fmt job; tests added. Note: archive grows to ~342 MB and the fmt job by ~7 min.

title: cancellation_reaps_production_bash_process_tree_before_responding flakes under the parallel runner on macOS (1 in 4); no macOS parallel-test-smoke
description:
src/extras/acp/mod.rs:4643-4760 exercise_cancellation_process_tree waits a fixed 15 s for the spawned
shell's pid file (tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(15) ...) at ~4743); under ~885% CPU from the
parallel suite the mock-model -> agent -> BashTool -> sh chain exceeds it ("production BashTool should
publish its process tree: Elapsed"). Observed 1 failure in 4 `cargo test --locked` runs on macOS 26.4.1;
passes 3/3 in isolation. ci.yml parallel-test-smoke (lines 493-502) is ubuntu-only and every macOS row
uses --test-threads=1, so CI cannot see it, but CLAUDE.md's mandated `cargo test` hits it locally. FIX:
separate "spawn happened" from "pid published" as done for mini-agent-s2nl0 (signal readiness from the
agent's tool-start event before starting the timer, or bound each stage separately and report which
stalled); add a macOS row to parallel-test-smoke (with TMPDIR=/private/tmp). Verify with a stress loop
(5x under --test-threads=16) before closing. TESTS: the hardened test itself; policy test update if the
matrix shape is asserted anywhere in scripts/tests.

title: Installer and recipe-digest refresh trust the release origin only: verify SLSA attestations and SHA256SUMS
description:
install.sh:196-205, 318-360 downloads the archive and SHA256SUMS from the same origin; release.yml:748-752
produces actions/attest provenance but neither install.sh nor README mentions `gh attestation verify`
(only PUBLISHING_RELEASES.md:179-195). scripts/update-release-checksums.sh:24-36, 76-80 (just
post-release) pins Homebrew/AUR/conda digests from a fresh curl without comparing to SHA256SUMS or the
attestation. README.md:264-275 never shows `--release <version>`. FIX: in install.sh, when `gh` is on
PATH run `gh attestation verify "$ARCHIVE" --repo sebahrens/mini-agent` (opt-out env var, e.g.
MINI_AGENT_SKIP_ATTESTATION=1), otherwise print how to verify manually; in update-release-checksums.sh
download SHA256SUMS and fail if any computed digest differs, and run gh attestation verify when
available; README: show `bash -s -- --release X.Y.Z` and the verification command; soften the
"checksum-verified" wording to what it guarantees. TESTS: extend scripts/test-install-checksums.sh and
scripts/tests/test_install_script.py with a stubbed `gh attestation verify` failure case; add a test
that update-release-checksums.sh rejects a digest disagreeing with the manifest.
close_reason: Merged: install.sh runs gh attestation verify --repo when an authenticated gh is present (abort on failure; warning + manual command otherwise; MINI_AGENT_SKIP_ATTESTATION=1 opt-out); update-release-checksums.sh verifies every asset against SHA256SUMS and attestation before writing recipes; README/GET_STARTED show pinned install and verification; new test module and installer cases.

title: JS spawn results over the 8 MiB frame cap turn an executed command into a 'protocol violation' (invites replay of a mutating command)
description:
src/extras/js/host.rs:2764-2766 caps SPAWN_STDOUT/STDERR at 1 MiB each and combined 1.5 MiB in RAW bytes;
serde_json escapes control bytes to 6-byte \u00XX so 1.5 MiB can encode to ~9 MiB > MAX_FRAME_BYTES
(8 MiB, src/extras/js/protocol.rs:1005-1031). The parent builds EffectResponse after the effect executed
and was audited (supervisor.rs:2025-2046) and write_parent fails with FrameTooLarge ->
WorkerError::Protocol (supervisor.rs:2447-2456): the model sees "JavaScript worker violated its
protocol" and the worker recycles. Probe confirmed: 1 MiB NUL stdout + 512 KiB NUL stderr ->
FrameTooLarge{8388609}. Discovery (discovery_json_string_upper_bound host.rs:3479) and read_files budget
for escaping; spawn does not. FIX: bound spawn output by encoded JSON size (escape-aware truncation in
decode_spawn_stream with *_truncated = true), or derive raw caps so 6x combined + envelope <
MAX_FRAME_BYTES; as a backstop check encoded size before write_parent and return
EffectErrorCode::TooLarge (OutcomeUnknown when mutating) instead of a protocol fault. Preserve the
Phase 6 invariants checklist. TESTS: unit test that worst case (all-NUL at caps) encodes below
MAX_FRAME_BYTES; bwrap-gated host test running `spawn('sh',['-c','head -c 1048576 /dev/zero; head -c
600000 /dev/zero >&2'])` gets a truncated Spawn result, not WorkerError::Protocol.
close_reason: Merged 1b6cfbf: spawn streams bounded by encoded JSON size (3 MiB each) with truncation flags; supervisor backstop turns an oversized effect response into TooLarge (read-only) or OutcomeUnknown (mutating) instead of a protocol fault; tests incl. real-worker e2e and a bwrap-gated linux_spawn test (CI count guard 3->4).

title: A caller-supplied out-of-scope target passed into an active skill quarantines the revision immediately (contradicts Phase 5 fault-only rule)
description:
src/extras/js/broker.rs:2004-2016 records any CapabilityDenied | ManifestDenied against the skill
invocation; telemetry.rs:1256-1284 maps SkillEventKind::CapabilityDenied to
QuarantineReason::CapabilityPolicyFault; quarantine.rs:29-33,130-140 treats that as immediate (no
threshold). ManifestDenied from enforce_manifest_scope (broker.rs:1594-1656) fires when MODEL CODE passes
an out-of-scope argument (e.g. summarize("README.md") with scope read_file: ["docs"]) => one call from a
prompt-injected model permanently quarantines every effectful learned skill. Phase 5 spec 12a.1 says an
uncorroborated exception caused by caller input is telemetry, not evidence. FIX: split target-derived
scope misses (argument outside declared prefixes/origins/programs) from genuine capability-policy
faults (operation outside the declared capability set, or a CapabilityDenied for a missing grant);
record only the latter as CapabilityDenied; treat target misses as threw-class telemetry behind the
behavioural threshold. Update docs/specs/phase-5-evidence-learning.md wording if needed. TESTS: e2e test
that out-of-scope path into an active read-scoped skill leaves the revision active and records a
non-severe event; a skill calling an undeclared capability still quarantines.
close_reason: Merged: manifest denials classified as ScopeMiss (caller-derived target outside a declared capability's scope) vs PolicyFault (undeclared capability, missing manifest, spawn identity drift, missing grant capability); only faults quarantine immediately, scope misses are threw-class telemetry; e2e and broker tests; Phase 5/6 specs updated.

title: File tools treat `$HOME/...` as workspace-relative but report the expanded home path (silent misplacement, false success)
description:
src/fs.rs:2536-2553 expand_tilde expands both `~/` and `$HOME/`, so resolve_tool_path reports
/Users/x/.zshrc, but every tool gates the workspace capability with `!is_absolute() &&
!starts_with('~')` (write.rs:190-247 esp. 205-209; read.rs:193-204; edit.rs:936-944; list_dir.rs:96;
grep.rs:428; find_files.rs:1169; agent/tools/mod.rs:60-69). WorkspaceBinding::normalize_relative accepts
`$HOME` as a Normal component and open_directory_path(create_missing=true) (paths.rs:411-414) creates it:
`write {"path":"$HOME/.config/tool/config.toml"}` creates ./$HOME/.config/... inside the repo and reports
"Written N bytes to /Users/<u>/.config/tool/config.toml"; the permission check names <ws>/$HOME/...;
read/edit of $HOME/... fail with a bare not-found naming the home path. FIX: decide bound vs ambient from
the EXPANDED path (compute expanded once; Path::new(&expanded).is_absolute() gates, or treat a
`$`-prefixed first component as ambient) in all tools sharing the pattern; report the path actually
written (workspace.logical_relative_path). TESTS: for write/read/edit/list_dir/grep/find_files with a
bound workspace and HOME=temp dir, `$HOME/x` resolves through the ambient permission path (or is
rejected); assert no `$HOME` directory is created in the workspace and the reported path equals the
on-disk path.
close_reason: Merged 00556d0: resolve_tool_target decides bound vs ambient from the expanded path in read/write/edit/list_dir/grep/find_files and reports the on-disk path; tests added. JS host equivalent filed as mini-agent-c1o7m.

title: task tool schema: move prompts/briefs exclusivity out of top-level oneOf into descriptions + actionable error
description:
## Problem
Top-level `oneOf` in the task tool schema (task_tool.rs:597-601) is ignored by non-strict OpenAI/LiteLLM gateways, not allowed by Anthropic tool input_schema, and would be rewritten to anyOf + all-required by rig's strict sanitize_schema (rig-core openai/mod.rs:39-117), guaranteeing rejection if strict mode is ever enabled. Error text also doesn't tell the model how to recover.

## Fix
- Drop the top-level oneOf; state the rule in the tool description and both property descriptions ("omit this field or pass [] when using briefs").
- Error: "send only one of prompts/briefs; to use briefs omit prompts entirely".
- If strict tools are ever enabled: make prompts/briefs/agent_type nullable.

## Acceptance
Schema test at task_tool.rs:1564 updated; schema validated against Anthropic + OpenAI tool schema rules.
close_reason: Top-level oneOf + minItems removed; exclusivity stated in tool/property descriptions; actionable error text; schema tests. Verified: targeted tests, 10-row CI clippy matrix + all-features clippy, full default cargo test (2493 passed).

Proposed: when the input buffer is non-empty (or cursor not already at the edge), Home/End move the cursor (to line start/end in multi-line input); transcript scroll moves to Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End (or only when input empty). Update docs/agent/COMMANDS.md:474, GET_STARTED.md:173, src/ui/slash/help.rs:290. Keep picker contract tests (picker_tests::slash_picker_contract) green. Add app-level test, not just input-level (input_tests.rs:202 passes today because it bypasses app).
close_reason: Home/End move cursor to line edges when input non-empty; scroll when empty/picker open; Ctrl+Home/End always scroll; docs/help updated; home_end_tests. Verified: targeted tests, 10-row CI clippy matrix + all-features clippy, full default cargo test (2493 passed).

Any click (e.g. on history) copies and prints noise. Docs describe drag-to-copy (COMMANDS.md:477, help.rs). Only copy when the selection spans a drag (start != end or moved); do not print a message for plain clicks.

While the agent is streaming, opening the slash picker paints the list once and the next token erases it, although the picker stays logically active: further letters go into the query and Enter still inserts the hidden highlight. From the user's side the completion "does not work while the agent is running".

Root cause: `refresh_display` in src/ui/mod.rs draws the picker after the viewport and bottom, then calls `renderer.invalidate()` so the overlay is repainted next frame. But the main loop's agent-event arm in src/ui/app.rs (`self.handle_agent_event(event).await?` inside `tokio::select!`) does not call `self.refresh()`, and the streaming arm in src/ui/event_handler.rs (`AgentEvent` text delta, and `finalize_response_segment`) calls `renderer.render_viewport()` directly. With `chat_dirty` already set by `invalidate()`, that paint covers the picker rows and nothing redraws the picker until the next user key. `handle_agent_event` in app.rs only refreshes on the compaction/pressure branches. The permission prompt path (src/ui/permission_handler.rs) paints viewport and bottom directly as well.

Fix: every paint path that repaints the chat region while a picker is active must redraw the picker (route the streaming repaint through `refresh_display`, or have `render_viewport` callers finish with the picker overlay). Add a renderer-level test with a fake terminal size asserting the picker rows survive a viewport repaint, or an event-handler test that a text delta with an active picker leaves the picker drawn.
close_reason: Main loop's agent-event arm calls refresh() when a picker is active, so streaming repaints redraw the overlay and restore the caret. Code-verified plus full suite and clippy; not reproduced live because that needs a paid model stream.

title: /goal is dispatched and documented but missing from the slash picker list
description:
`/goal` (feature `goal`, in the default feature set) is dispatched by src/ui/slash/mod.rs and documented in docs/agent/COMMANDS.md, but `available_commands()` in src/ui/pickers/list.rs never pushes it, so the slash picker cannot complete it. Verified 2026-09-14 by diffing the dispatcher's string literals against the picker's list: the only dispatcher command missing from the picker is `/goal`. (`/btw` and `/queue` are in the picker and handled in src/ui/app.rs, so they are fine.)

Root cause: the list is hand-maintained ("Keep this in sync with the dispatcher in crate::ui::slash") and the goal feature (commits 931d272 onward) added the dispatcher arm and docs without touching the picker; no test enforces the sync.

Fix: add `#[cfg(feature = "goal")] cmds.push("/goal");` in the alphabetical feature block, and add a test that derives the dispatcher's command set (or the `/help` table) and asserts every entry is offered by the picker, so the next feature cannot regress this.
close_reason: /goal added under cfg(feature=goal); /memory moved to the always-on list to match dispatcher and help. New ui::slash::help test asserts every command /help names is offered by the picker, passing on default and no-default-features builds.

title: Flaky: several process- and socket-heavy tests fail under parallel load, on every CI row
description:
WHERE: src/tests/hooks/dispatcher_tests.rs async_hook_cancellation_fixture_settles_readiness_failures.

SYMPTOM: fails roughly one run in two under `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 cargo test --no-default-features --features hooks,js,subagents,skills,sandbox` (a CI matrix row) and under `cargo test --features hooks`. Passes in isolation every time. Other hook tests (tests::worktree_tests::tests::worktree_rebind_updates_production_hook_child_envelope_and_project_dir) fail on the same rows on other runs, which points at shared process state or a timing assumption rather than one bad assertion.

NOT A REGRESSION: measured on 2026-09-12 at the same rate with the goal-review changes stashed (1 of 2 runs failed before, 1 of 2 after), so this predates epic mini-agent-c75u1.

WHY IT MATTERS: a CI row that fails half the time is a CI row nobody trusts, and it will mask a real failure.

DO: run the test under `--test-threads=1` to confirm cross-test interference, then either isolate the shared state (the hook dispatcher's globals are the first suspects) or make the readiness wait deterministic. Separately, `cargo test --features hooks` overflows the default 2 MiB test stack without RUST_MIN_STACK; that combination is not a CI row, so decide whether to support it or document that the hooks rows need the larger stack.
notes:
Also seen on the default row: tests::worktree_tests::tests::timed_out_post_checkout_hook_restores_branch_before_stash_pop failed once in a full-suite run on 2026-09-12 and passed in isolation and on the next full run. Same shape as the hooks-row flakes: timing or shared process state, not an assertion that is wrong.

MEASURED 2026-09-12, more carefully. It is not one test. Across six full runs of `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 cargo test --no-default-features --features hooks,js,subagents,skills,sandbox`, two failed, each a different process-heavy test:
- tests::hooks::dispatcher_tests::async_hook_cancellation_fixture_settles_readiness_failures
- tests::shell_mode_tests::lazygit_style_caller_drop_audits_cleanup_and_allows_the_next_launch
and on the non-CI `--features hooks` row, tests::worktree_tests::tests::worktree_rebind_updates_production_hook_child_envelope_and_project_dir.

Each passes in isolation every time: async_hook_cancellation passed 8 of 8 runs alone. So the trigger is parallel load on a row that compiles the sandbox, the JS worker and hooks together, and the suspects are shared process bookkeeping or the audit sink rather than any one assertion.

Rate is roughly one failure per three full runs, and identical with the goal-review changes stashed, so it predates epic mini-agent-c75u1.

NEXT STEP: run this row with `--test-threads=1` to confirm it is contention rather than timing, then bisect the shared resource. Retitle once the actual cause is known — the current title names only the first symptom seen.

WIDER THAN THE HOOKS ROWS. The plain `--no-default-features` row is flaky too: startup::tests::pricing_server_drop_closes_idle_partial_and_active_connections failed 2 of 3 full runs on the pre-review commit 919185f and passed 4 of 4 in isolation on both trees. So this is not about hooks, not about the goal work, and not about any single test — it is load-dependent failure in tests that own sockets or child processes, reproducible on a commit that predates epic mini-agent-c75u1 entirely.

Known members so far: pricing_server_drop_closes_idle_partial_and_active_connections (--no-default-features, acp, mcp rows), async_hook_cancellation_fixture_settles_readiness_failures and lazygit_style_caller_drop_audits_cleanup_and_allows_the_next_launch (hooks,js,subagents,skills,sandbox row), worktree_rebind_updates_production_hook_child_envelope_and_project_dir (--features hooks).

Each binds a port or spawns a process tree and waits on it with a fixed guard. The most likely cause is that those guards are short relative to a loaded machine rather than any shared corruption; confirm by running one row with --test-threads=1 and, if that is clean, by raising the guards rather than hunting for a shared resource.

RESOLVED IN THREE PARTS, 2026-09-12. The single symptom was three unrelated causes.

1. REAL DEFECT, hooks process-group drain. src/extras/hooks/subprocess.rs had its own copy of terminate_and_reap that never received the fix commit 8251082 made in src/sandbox.rs: it signalled the group and returned, so a hook reported settlement while a descendant was still runnable. Found by cancelling_owning_work_scope_terminates_async_hook_descendants failing with the descendant Live, running and reparented to init — and that test accepts a zombie, so a running process two seconds after a group SIGKILL was not a sampling artifact. Both hook paths now share the sandbox's await_drained_process_group. subprocess-trust.md's TC-PROJECT-AUTOMATION row updated to state the drain, matching TC-MODEL-ACTION.

2. UNSOUND ASSERTION, pricing fixture. pricing_server_drop_closes_idle_partial_and_active_connections probed whether anything answered on the address it had just released. A freed port is recycled immediately and machine-wide, so under a parallel suite the probe observed another test's listener. Removed: the fixture's listener is moved into its worker thread and Drop joins it, so teardown is what guarantees the property, and the effect on an existing connection is still checked.

3. LOST, NOT LATE, lazygit audit. lazygit_style_caller_drop asserted the cancelled utility's audit line after the tracing subscriber's scope had closed, while the worker that writes it is a separate task that disarms its process-group guard before emitting. A line written a moment later could never be captured. The test now waits for the record inside the runtime and inside the scope; a record that never arrives still fails, with the buffer.

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, full runs:
- --no-default-features: 2 of 3 failed before, 0 of 8 after.
- hooks,js,subagents,skills,sandbox: about 1 in 3 before, 0 of 6 after all three (1 of 18 after the first two, which was cause 3).
Single-threaded runs were clean throughout, which is what pointed at contention rather than a wrong assertion.

Everything here predates epic mini-agent-c75u1 and was reproduced with those changes stashed.
close_reason: Three causes, all addressed: a real drain gap in the hooks subprocess path, an unsound port probe, and an audit assertion made outside its subscriber's scope. Heavy row went from roughly 1 in 3 runs failing to 0 of 6; the plain row from 2 of 3 to 0 of 8.

title: Docs drift: goals.md 'Not reachable' paragraph is stale, GOALS.md overclaims loop early-finish, and user docs omit the goal surfaces
description:
1. docs/specs/goals.md:218-223 "Not reachable: recording goal verdicts as Phase 5 task-outcome rows ... (mini-agent-a1qwa.20)" is stale: a1qwa.20 closed in f1a04bd; driver::set_outcome_recorder is installed from src/ui/event_handler.rs:697 and src/startup.rs:1544 behind the skills feature. Replace with "Reachable with the skills feature: verdicts are recorded as TaskOutcomeSource::Goal rows from TUI and headless; not in the default build; promotion reachability unchanged" and move it into the reachable list. 00-index.md inherits this via "see its shipped-binary status".
2. docs/agent/GOALS.md:163-165 "Nothing weaker ends it: a claim no command proved never shortens a loop" is false without --loop-run: preset.rs sets no judge guard and gate_post stops Met with VerdictSource::ModelReport when no checks exist (an Auto judge agreeing, or an outage under the ladder). COMMANDS.md:239-240 states it correctly. Reword, or make the preset refuse self-report-only completion (coordinate with the loop-preset judge decision in the config bead).
3. docs/specs/goals.md:58 says "four unrelated conditions" but lists five and PauseReason has five variants.
4. Gaps: CONFIG.md statusline segment list (~L1148, ~L1200) omits the goal segment (src/ui/statusline.rs ~L355); GET_STARTED.md flag table (~L204) omits --goal*; ARCHITECTURE.md directory layout (~L145-151) omits src/extras/goal/ although CLAUDE.md requires docs for new modules; ACP _meta.goal is documented only in the spec; the Stop-envelope goal fields (envelope.rs ~L29-33, ~L101-103) are not listed in any user doc.
5. src/extras/goal/gate.rs:152-156: #[allow(dead_code)] on JudgeOutcome with a comment citing a1qwa.9/.10 as future work; judge.rs constructs both variants now. Remove.
6. --loop-max 0: headless returns before creating a goal (loop/headless.rs ~L55-58) while the preset maps 0 to max_rounds 1 (preset.rs ~L130-135) and TUI /loop uses 100. Pick one and document it.
close_reason: Landed in f3b17f1.

title: Goal test coverage gaps against the spec's Required tests list
description:
Concrete missing scenarios found while mapping the spec's Required tests to the suite (things that exist are listed in the parent epic's review notes):
- Gate: no test for exhausted bound + judge NotYet / Impossible-with-proof / Unavailable (see the bound-escape bead); the combinatorial sweep (gate.rs ~L1551-1614) asserts only no-panic, verdict present and rounds+1, not "correct counters" (no assertions on consecutive_*, wrap_up_issued, judge_failures); no ordering-collision tests for bound+needs_user, bound+blocked-streak, bound+impossible, failed-round-while-wrap_up_issued; no verify_passed Some(true)/Some(false) tests; no apply_config clamp or flag-vs-config test.
- Driver/headless: no binary test runs with --goal at all (grep -- --goal tests/ is empty); no per-outcome JSON+exit-code test; no test of both history modes at the surface; no interrupt-during-verification test asserting the goal is uncounted; no persisted-prompt/no-duplicate-persistence test; no headless --loop first-round-prompt test; no Stop-hook loop-field test.
- Judge/checks/tool: no cross-provider request test; no test that drift-check outages leave judge_failures unchanged; no fence-escape test; no >24KiB tail test; no headless current-round-in-transcript test; no checks test for cancellation, output-limit breach or launch failure (spec lists all three as failures); no end-to-end check_every_round feed-forward test; no two-goal_report-calls-in-one-round test; no goal_report-while-paused test; no test of the transcript write path (write failure non-fatal, path layout) - render() bypasses save_round.
- Surfaces: no test drives handle_goal (replace refused, reopen only from impossible, clear, pause/resume, check, bounds re-arming); no CLI parsing test for any --goal* flag; session_restore_tests has no goal case; no TUI round-loop test for relaunch history, persistence between rounds or a parked-goal turn; hooks envelope tests use hand-supplied fields, nothing checks current_hook_info after set/clear; ACP tests cover JSON reading and compaction only; no export test writes or imports the goal record.
Split into per-area tasks as the fixes land; each fix bead above should add its own regression, and this bead tracks the remainder.
close_reason: Landed in f87c1c7.

title: Add the spec-required authority test: security mode unchanged across a goal lifecycle
description:
WHERE: docs/specs/goals.md Authority: "a test asserts the security mode is unchanged across a goal lifecycle" and Required tests: "Authority: security mode unchanged across a goal lifecycle". grep -rn -i "security\|permission" src/extras/goal/*.rs hits only checks.rs ~L171 (authority resolution), src/tests/ has no goal test file, and no test exercises a goal lifecycle against the security mode or permission allowlist. Only the benign-config half exists (config/load.rs ~L1524-1575, which also does not assert [goal].judge - see the config authority bead).

FIX: add a test that creates a goal, runs rounds through settle_round with checks and a report, pauses/resumes/clears it, and asserts the security mode, permission allowlist and sandbox policy objects are unchanged (and that the goal module has no handle to them); update the spec if the wording changes.
close_reason: Landed in ce403be.

title: Blocked streak: gate_pre and apply disagree on a blocked round that made edits
description:
WHERE: src/extras/goal/gate.rs gate_pre (~L389-393) computes streak = 1 when mutating_tool_calls > 0 and labels the instruction "attempt 1 of N"; apply (~L767-771) resets consecutive_blocked to 0 in that case. The next edit-free blocked round is therefore also "attempt 1 of N" and with blocked_rounds=3 the stop arrives on the 4th consecutive blocked round. Test progress_resets_the_blocked_streak_even_when_the_blocker_is_reworded asserts the 0 and pins the inconsistency.

FIX: make apply set consecutive_blocked = 1 for blocked-with-edits (or gate_pre use 0+1); assert the attempt labels are monotone.
close_reason: Landed in a79d0df.

title: Skip the judge when checks already rejected the claim; record goal outcomes once per goal, not per round
description:
WHERE: src/startup.rs ~L2032-2062 and src/ui/event_handler.rs ~L603-617 run checks then unconditionally ask the judge when request.run_judge, but gate_post returns on !outcome.all_passed before reading the judge, so the call is pure cost and a transport failure there still advances judge_failures. src/extras/goal/driver.rs apply_decision (~L748) calls record_outcome on every decision including Continue (last_verdict outcome NotYet) so a 20-round goal writes 19 passed=false task-outcome rows plus one success for the same goal id; record_outcome also re-records the previous verdict on a Cancelled round (apply leaves last_verdict untouched); the TUI re-resolves skill services and reinstalls the recorder every round (event_handler.rs ~L697).

FIX: skip the judge when checks.is_some_and(|c| !c.all_passed); record only on GateDecision::Stop (or when a claim was adjudicated) and skip Cancelled; install the recorder once. Tests.
close_reason: Landed in 3d66197.

title: Goal CLI flags are silently ignored without --goal; the --no-tools refusal misses a resumed live goal
description:
WHERE: src/startup.rs apply_goal_flags (~L1848-1856) returns Ok(()) when --goal is absent or blank, so --goal-done, --goal-check, --goal-max-rounds, --goal-continuation and --goal-replace vanish without a message (while cli.rs ~L989 configured_validation_needs_shell still makes the sandbox eligible for the dropped check). The --no-tools refusal (~L1863) sits inside that early-return, so --continue --no-tools on a session holding a live goal is accepted and stalls into paused{no_progress}. No CLI parsing test covers any --goal* flag.

FIX: clap requires = "goal" on the dependent flags; after session load check goal_store.is_live() && no_tools; add CLI parsing tests (spec Required tests: "CLI parsing").
close_reason: Landed in 65e41a2.

title: ACP: unverified met is not labelled, the judge request is silently dropped, and _meta.goal is not a closed schema
description:
WHERE: src/extras/acp/mod.rs settle_acp_goal_round (~L1572-1575) returns (checks, None) for every VerifyRequest; met_claim_request sets run_judge for JudgePolicy::Auto, and gate_post treats None as "no judge" so judge_failures never moves and the ladder cannot engage. The report is decision_line ("goal: met after N round(s) - reason", driver.rs ~L301-317) and _meta.goal (~L1494-1502) carries id/status/round/max_rounds/reason only. apply_meta_goal (~L1006-1050) reads clear/objective/criteria/replace and ignores unknown keys (checks, judge, bounds), drops non-string criteria via filter_map, and clear:true wins over a supplied objective.

SPEC (Shipped-binary status): "the judge tier is not wired for ACP yet, and a completion no command proved is labelled as such" - the label only exists in the TUI /goal status.

FIX: add "verified"/"evidence" to _meta.goal and append "(not proved by any command)" to the met thought when unverified; set judge = Off for ACP goals or return JudgeOutcome::Unavailable; reject unknown _meta.goal keys with -32602. Wire tests for apply_meta_goal, settle_acp_goal_round and the report (goal_acp_tests today cover only JSON reading, store.set and compaction).
close_reason: Landed in 7a205c3.

title: /goal subcommand parsing hijacks objectives, turns prose into a shell check, and pause/clear are unreachable while rounds chain
description:
WHERE: src/ui/slash/goal.rs: only "status" is guarded by parts.len() <= 2 (~L183); pause|resume|reopen|clear|bounds|check match with trailing words, so "/goal pause the deploy" pauses, "/goal clear the cache" deletes the goal, and "/goal check the login flow works" registers that prose as a COMMAND the validation runner executes on the next claim (~L256-270). "/goal bounds a=1 b=2" cannot work because handle_slash tokenizes with splitn(3, ' ') (slash/mod.rs ~L592) while the loop at goal.rs ~L225 expects one assignment per element. USAGE (~L8-9) omits check while help lists it; "/goal pause" on a met goal fails set_status but prints write_ok "goal met" (~L195-200). Rounds relaunch back-to-back inside handle_agent_done so is_running never drops and slash commands are RejectWhileRunning (ui/mod.rs ~L506; only /queue and /btw allowed), so the only intervention is Ctrl-C (see the TUI interrupt bead); queued messages drain only in finalize_turn, so the guide's "Typing a message is a normal turn" is not true while rounds chain.

FIX: guard the no-argument verbs with parts.len() <= 2; require an explicit form for check (e.g. "check -- <cmd>"); split_whitespace the bounds body; fix USAGE and the pause-on-met message; allow /goal pause|status in allowed_while_running with pause meaning "stop after this round". Tests driving handle_goal for each subcommand (none exist today; only parse_objective/parse_bound/render_status are tested).
close_reason: Landed in 8be4f99.

title: Headless --loop parity gaps after the fold onto the goal driver
description:
Gaps found comparing the pre-ed420cb LoopState behaviour with the preset:
1. First round never shows the plan or loop instructions: src/extras/loop/headless.rs ~L76-84 passes the raw prompt and run_headless_goal_rounds runs run_print(message) (startup.rs ~L1961); only next_round (rounds >= 2) calls push_context_file/round_header. With --loop-max 1 the plan is never seen. The TUI /loop uses driver::first_round_prompt (app.rs ~L2494).
2. Agent is built before the goal exists (dispatch_loop startup.rs ~L1699 then headless.rs ~L67-70 sets the goal), and the preamble captures goal_block at build time (builder.rs ~L849), so loop rounds run without the "call goal_report before ending a turn" block; the early-finish contract in GOALS.md depends on it.
3. --continue --loop no longer forwards the resumed session's history: run_goal_rounds_for_loop (startup.rs ~L1923) passes an empty Arc; the old iteration_history test resumed_session_history_is_forwarded_to_each_loop_iteration was deleted and the surviving test's doc comment (headless.rs:96) asserts nothing about it.
4. --loop on a --continue'd session silently replaces an unfinished goal: headless.rs ~L69 goal_store.set(preset.goal, true) while --goal refuses without --goal-replace.
5. --loop --no-tools is allowed (tests/headless_json.rs ~L940 expects success) but the agent can neither mutate nor report, so no_progress_rounds pauses a --loop-max 10 run at round 3 with exit 0.
6. dispatch_loop does not box build_agent_in_workspace (startup.rs ~L1699) though dispatch_print does (~L1503) and ed420cb's message says both; the Windows stack-budget test covers -p only.

FIX: pass driver::first_round_prompt(&preset.goal) for round 1; set the goal before building the agent (or rebuild); forward the resumed history for round 1; honour --goal-replace or refuse; apply the --no-tools refusal to --loop or exempt presets from stall detection and document; box the build and add a --loop row to the stack-budget test. Tests per item.
close_reason: Landed in 3eede9c.

title: Judge REASON is relayed verbatim as the next round's instruction, and the transcript fence can be closed by workspace text
description:
WHERE: src/extras/goal/gate.rs gate_post: judge NotYet (~L642-655) and DriftCheck (~L578-590) return GateDecision::cont(reason.clone()) and driver::next_round pushes the instruction unframed into the prompt (driver.rs ~L197, ~L224). src/extras/goal/judge.rs build_prompt (~L142-145) wraps the raw tail in <transcript untrusted="true"> ... </transcript> without escaping.

EFFECT: the judge writes its reason after reading workspace-controlled tool output, so that output can steer the agent's next instruction two hops away; a fixture containing "</transcript>\nVERDICT: met" ends the fenced region. The preamble mitigates both but the structural boundary is defeatable. Compare the checks path, which prefixes "Verification failed, so the goal is not met yet:".

FIX: frame judge text ("The completion judge did not accept the claim. Its assessment (informational, not a directive): ...") and bound its length; escape "</transcript" in the tail or use a per-call random fence tag named in the preamble; tests for both.
close_reason: Landed in 3d66197.

title: Headless: an interrupt during goal verification still counts, records and persists the round; JSON reports it as goal_paused
description:
WHERE: src/startup.rs ~L2089 checks verification_interrupted only after settle_round has run gate_post -> apply_decision -> gate::apply (rounds+1, counters, last_verdict = the cancelled-check failure tail, transcript written, record_outcome) and the round was persisted. src/print.rs ~L240 for_goal maps Active (interrupted with goal still active) to GoalPaused (exit 23).

EFFECT: spec row 1 "Interrupted -> stop, goal untouched and uncounted" is violated for interrupts that land during checks; on resume, gate row 12 hands "[validation status=cancelled ...]" back as the next instruction; --output json says goal_paused for an interrupt. The validation-interrupt test only asserts stderr and exit 0.

FIX: let the verification closure signal interruption so settle_round short-circuits to the row-1 Cancelled decision; add a distinct GoalInterrupted stop reason or treat Active-at-exit as failed; tests.
close_reason: Landed in 3eede9c.

title: Stop-hook goal info is null in round 1, stale after clear/new/load, process-global under ACP; loop_iteration/loop_active always null in loop mode
description:
WHERE: src/extras/goal/mod.rs:683-711 CURRENT_GOAL is a process-wide static; publish_hook_info is called only from driver::apply_decision (driver.rs:738); GoalStore::set/clear never publish and nothing publishes None. src/startup.rs run_headless_goal_rounds passes None for LoopInfo on both run_print calls (~L1968, ~L2112) whereas the old loop passed Some(LoopInfo{iteration, active}); envelope.rs ~L99-100 still emits the fields and headless.rs:13 hook_loop_active is now test-only.

EFFECT: /goal X then a prompt -> the round-1 Stop envelope has goal_id null despite an active goal (spec: "carries the goal id, status, and round; null without a goal"); after /goal clear, /loop stop, /new or /sessions load hooks keep seeing the old goal until another gate runs; under ACP the envelope can carry another session's goal. Loop hook consumers now get null iteration fields with no doc note.

FIX: publish from GoalStore::set/clear/with_mut (or read a session-scoped handle); derive LoopInfo{iteration: rounds+1, active} for loop presets or document the removal and delete hook_loop_active; tests for the round-1 envelope and for clear.
close_reason: Landed in 4f6332d.

title: Parked goals keep collecting rounds on ordinary chat turns; goal_report is accepted while parked; reports reuse the round number after an interrupt
description:
WHERE: src/ui/event_handler.rs:73 collects when goal_store.is_live() (paused/blocked/budget_limited/awaiting_user included) and run_goal_round (~L529) filters only terminal; src/extras/acp/mod.rs ~L1547 same. gate::apply increments rounds/tokens/active_secs unconditionally and set_status from Paused allows any transition. src/agent/builder.rs:701 registers goal_report when is_live() and report_tool.rs ~L200-208 refuses only terminal goals; resume() (mod.rs ~L614) clears streaks but not reports; goal_report stamps round = rounds+1 and apply() does not advance rounds on Cancelled, so a report filed just before an interrupt carries the same round number as the next attempt and RoundCollector::finish (driver.rs ~L104-108) lets it speak for the resumed round.

EFFECT: after /goal pause every chat turn burns budget and prints "goal: not yet (round N)"; a budget_limited goal prints its line every turn; a met filed during ordinary chat while paused becomes the first resumed round's claim; a pre-interrupt met/needs_user/blocked can decide a round that filed nothing.

FIX: collect/gate only when is_active() (or treat a user turn on a parked goal as resume); refuse goal_report unless status.is_running(); on Cancelled drop reports with round == rounds+1 (or stamp reports with an attempt id). Tests for each.
close_reason: Landed in 8be4f99.

title: [goal] max_rounds in config silently overrides --goal-max-rounds; apply_config clamps wrap-up to >= 1
description:
WHERE: src/startup.rs:1869-1880 sets goal.bounds.max_rounds from the flag, then goal.bounds.apply_config(cfg) overwrites it when [goal].max_rounds is set. src/extras/goal/mod.rs apply_config clamps wrap_up_max_agent_turns to 1..=100, so if the loop preset (wrap_up 0 for exactness) is ever wired through apply_config a [goal] entry silently re-enables the wind-down round.

FIX: apply config first, then flags; make the clamp allow 0 (or have the preset apply config before zeroing); tests for flag-vs-config precedence and for the loop preset keeping wrap_up 0 under a [goal] table.
close_reason: Landed in 65e41a2.

title: Gate never reads verify_passed: an in-round verify_command result earns no evidence and a failed one is not rejected
description:
WHERE: RoundSummary.verify_passed (src/extras/goal/gate.rs:64) is set by RoundCollector (driver.rs ~L64-67) but never consulted in gate_pre/gate_post (only in a test at ~L1273). met_claim_request sets run_verify_command = verify_configured && !verify_ran, and evidence comes only from checks.verified (~L638).

EFFECT: a round where the runner's verify_command ran and PASSED yields Met with evidence [SelfReport] -> met_unverified() true, the UI labels a command-proven completion "unverified" and skill evidence loses it. A round where it ran and FAILED is only safe because the runner escalates to AgentEvent::Error after max_attempts; the gate itself would accept verify_ran && verify_passed==Some(false) as met.

title: A completion claim made in the wrap-up round is discarded as budget_limited
description:

WRAP_UP_INSTRUCTION tells the model to summarize and finish; if it finishes and reports met with passing checks in that round the verified claim is lost. Test budget_exhaustion_issues_one_wrap_up_round_then_stops pins this.

SPEC: prose says "The claim is still verified on the way out, in a wrap-up round" while table row 5 says wrap-up already ran -> budget_limited. The code chose the less useful reading and the spec is internally inconsistent.

FIX: mirror the exhausted-branch exception: if wrap_up_issued { if met && open_todos==0 -> Verify(met_claim_request) else BudgetLimited } and in gate_post convert any resulting Continue into BudgetLimited when wrap_up_issued; reconcile the spec sentence.

title: Judge failure ladder: drift-check and impossibility outages are counted, resume never resets it, and the ladder is unreachable without checks
description:
WHERE: src/extras/goal/gate.rs apply (~L758-765) increments judge_failures on any JudgeOutcome::Unavailable regardless of VerifyCause; the comment above it and the spec say only completion claims count. src/extras/goal/mod.rs resume() (~L614-623) and reopen() (~L626-632) reset other streaks but not judge_failures (reopen resets none). gate_post MetClaim (~L689-699) parks only when !externally_proven && judge_failures+1 >= 3, otherwise `Some(Unavailable)|None => {}` falls through to Stop{Met} on self-report alone (terminal).

REPRO (throwaway test during review): judge_every=1, two drift-check outages then one met-claim outage -> paused{judge_unavailable}. Conversely with no checks configured a single outage on a met claim completes the goal as Met (unverified), so three consecutive claim outages can never accumulate in production; the test repeated_judge_failures_park_the_goal_but_a_single_one_does_not has to force status back to Active between iterations.

SPEC: "One unreachable judge costs nothing: the claim is evaluated as if none were configured" vs "Three consecutive failures on completion claims park the goal" - contradictory when the judge is the only verifier. Decide in the spec.

FIX: pass VerifyCause into apply (or only pass judge for MetClaim); reset judge_failures in resume(); decide what reopen() resets; if the ladder is meant to protect self-report-only completions, treat Unavailable on an unproven met claim as Continue and park at 3. Tests for each.
close_reason: Landed in a79d0df.

title: Per-round goal checks, so a loop validator's contract can be expressed
description:
CONTEXT: a1qwa.16 found that --loop cannot fold onto goals faithfully. A loop validator (--loop-run) executes after every iteration and its output feeds the next prompt as feedback; a goal check runs only on a completion claim and gates it. Converting one into the other would change behaviour for existing --loop-run users.

DO: let a goal run checks every round, not only on a completion claim. Add a per-goal option (e.g. GoalBounds::check_every_round, config [goal].check_every_round, /goal bounds check_every_round=true). When set, the gate requests checks on an otherwise-Continue round via a new VerifyCause (RoundFeedback); the rendered output becomes part of the next round's instruction; a failure is feedback and does NOT by itself stop the goal, but a completion claim is still gated by the same checks. Document the two modes in docs/specs/goals.md (Verification tiers) and docs/agent/GOALS.md.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING BEYOND THE FOLD: continuous verification is useful in its own right — an agent that learns its tests fail at the end of every round corrects sooner than one told only when it claims completion.

VERIFY: gate tests for the new cause and for a failing per-round check not stopping the goal; a driver test proving the output reaches the next instruction; the existing completion-gating tests unchanged. Real-binary: a goal with check_every_round and a failing check shows the failure in each round's feedback and still never reaches Met.

DONE WHEN: a loop validator's contract is expressible as a goal, unblocking a1qwa.17.
close_reason:
Landed in 747a22d. GoalBounds::check_every_round (config [goal].check_every_round, /goal bounds check_every_round=true, default false). New VerifyCause::RoundFeedback: on an otherwise-Continue round with checks configured, the gate runs them and feeds a failure into the next instruction without stopping the goal. A completion claim still takes the MetClaim path and is gated by the same checks, asserted by a test. /goal status says which mode is active. 3 new gate tests plus slash and status tests; docs updated in goals.md, GOALS.md and CONFIG.md. Unblocks a1qwa.17.

[REAL-BINARY EVIDENCE]
Interface: headless
Commands: cargo install --path . --debug; project .zerostack/config.toml with [goal] check_every_round = true; mini-agent -p --no-session --yolo --goal 'Create fb.txt containing FB' --goal-check 'false' --goal-max-rounds 3 'Begin.'
Expected: a failing check is reported as feedback at the end of every round and never lets the goal complete.
Observed: 'goal: not yet (round 1) — Verification failed, so the goal is not met yet:', the same at round 2, then 'budget reached at round 3 — wrapping up' and 'budget limited'. The goal never reached met despite the agent repeatedly claiming the file was correct.
Result: PASS

title: Judge wiring: met/impossible adjudication, cadence drift check, fail-open
description:
CONTEXT: spec §4.4 rows 9 and 15, §4.5 (cadence drift check), §4.9 (fail-open). Depends on a1qwa.9.

DO:
1. Wire judge.rs into the driver's tier-3 hook: on Step::VerifyMet after checks passed → call the judge; map NotYet → Continue(reason); Impossible → NotYet when the round's checks or verify passed, else Stop(Impossible); Met → gate_post finishes with Stop(Met) and evidence += Judge. On Step::AdjudicateImpossible (model reported impossible): judge Impossible → Stop(Impossible) with evidence [SelfReport, Judge]; anything else → Continue(judge reason or "keep working"). With judge Off: impossible report → Stop(Impossible) tagged SelfReport.
2. Cadence drift check: every goal.bounds.judge_every rounds (default 5) when no met/impossible report occurred, call the judge with a cheaper "is the agent still on the objective?" prompt whose only allowed outputs are not_yet + guidance (any other verdict is coerced to NotYet); the guidance becomes the next instruction.
3. Fail-open policy: provider error or Unparseable → Continue with reason "judge verdict unavailable; keep working" and increment a per-goal judge_failures counter; after 2 consecutive failures on met claims evaluate the claim as if judge=Off and tag the verdict judge_unavailable; after 3 consecutive failed met claims → Stop(Paused{JudgeUnavailable}). Any success resets the counter. A judge outage never produces Met on its own and never terminates a goal.

title: Process-tree reaping assertions use kill -0, which cannot tell a zombie from a live descendant
description:
Run 34455186103 (07ba72d2), test (ubuntu-latest), failed:

  extras::acp::protocol_tests::cancellation_reaps_production_bash_process_tree_before_responding
  src/extras/acp/mod.rs:3365 -- 'Cancelled was returned before the Bash descendant exited'

First observed occurrence: the ubuntu default row passed on b082b62c, baf4427d, bf1efe9c and 609109e5. The shell assertion immediately above it passed, so the shell was reaped and only the descendant was still visible.

The problem is that the check cannot support the conclusion either way. process_exists (src/extras/acp/mod.rs:2580) shells out to "kill -0 <pid>" and treats success as existence. kill -0 succeeds for a ZOMBIE. A descendant already SIGKILLed but not yet reaped by its parent -- or not yet reaped by init after reparenting, since the shell it was a child of was killed first -- still answers kill -0. So the failure has two possible meanings with opposite severity:

- the descendant is a zombie: containment held, the process is dead, and the assertion is simply imprecise;
- the descendant is alive: cancellation returned Cancelled while a live process survived, a real containment gap in the ACP cancellation contract.

Nothing in the failure output distinguishes them. Unlike the other recent flakes this assertion has no wall-clock budget to blame -- it is an immediate check right after the response -- so this is NOT an instance of mini-agent-emfnr.

Fix the precision so the next occurrence is interpretable:
1. Check process STATE rather than existence. On Linux read /proc/<pid>/stat and treat state Z as exited; portably run "ps -o state= -p <pid>" and treat Z as exited.
2. Or wait for the pid to disappear with a bounded retry, which converts a zombie window into a pass while a live survivor still fails. Note this reintroduces a time bound, so prefer option 1.

This matters beyond one test. It is the third assertion in three days that cannot distinguish a security property being violated from benign housekeeping timing: mini-agent-l07k (containment gates failing at cleanup, never at containment) and mini-agent-i74o (a bound authority denial failing on a starved runner) are the others. Each ambiguous one teaches readers to treat a red security gate as noise.
notes:
Scope reconciliation with concurrently filed P1uyi0q: this bead owns precise process-state/identity observation and regression controls that distinguish a live descendant from an exited zombie without weakening the immediate cancellation boundary. uyi0q owns native reproduction and diagnosis of the observed failure, including any required production fix, using these diagnostics. A bounded wait that lets a live survivor exit after Cancelled would weaken the assertion and is not equivalent evidence. Historical correction: i74o native failures were traced to production-only helper markers being passed to libtest and missing directory-list access on retained authority handles (usb3/bhug), not attributed to a starved runner. Preserve the separate delivered defects rather than classifying authority failures as timing noise.
Implemented test-only Linux/macOS state helper with pre-cancellation identity capture, distinct Live/Exited/Gone/Replaced, Linux /proc state/start ticks and macOS libproc plus system-ps zombie fallback. Actual macOS C probe shows proc_pidinfo returns ESRCH for a held zombie even while kill0 succeeds; new native control requires Exited before wait and Gone after wait. ACP retains strict direct-child reap and immediate descendant exit snapshot; FIFO and work-scope cleanup occur afterward, including injected readiness panic. Linux real ACP false failure reproduced as Z, and direct-child-only termination mutant is rejected as Live(S); same live-survivor mutant fails on macOS. Identity-ignored and zombie-as-gone mutants also fail normally. Final gates underway; no production cancellation change.
Validation complete: full macOS ACP suites21/20/23 across default, ACP-only and rich hooks/ACP/skills; process-state controls pass in all three rows, final inventory27, all9strict Clippy and skills-enabled debug install. Final platform cfg narrowing rechecked with ACP20 and strict ACP Clippy. Native Linux unprivileged ACP20 and state2 plus strict ACP Clippy pass; final owned-pipe control rechecked natively. Direct-child-only kill mutations fail with a live descendant on Linux and macOS; identity-ignored and zombie-as-gone controls fail normally on macOS. Fixture catches readiness panic, releases owned FIFO, settles prompt/scope, and propagates failure after cleanup. No production cancellation or deadline change. Evidence /tmp/mini-agent-process-state-gates.json, negative.json, reviews.json and /tmp/mini-agent-acp-linux-owned-pipe-gates.json. Task-owned Docker container and volumes removed after validation.

title: Cancel ACP permission requests when their caller abandons the reply

Configured verification therefore fails with configured shell unavailable and can incorrectly exhaust repair attempts. Cover configured CLI validation and interactive validation with shell excluded; audit completion verify_command for the same coupling. New caller tests exposed this on macOS.

title: Prevent status socket notifications from blocking turn lifecycle
description: StatusSignals synchronously connects a UnixStream and calls write_all with no deadline or nonblocking mode. send_start/send_stop run inline in TUI and headless turn lifecycle, including interruption and shutdown. A listening status socket whose accept queue is full can therefore stall the UI before agent work or retirement. Preserve existing newline-delimited stream messages, keep sends best-effort and bounded without unbounded background threads/tasks, and verify a saturated listener plus healthy delivery and endpoint failure.
notes: Implemented a shared socket2 sender with nonblocking mode set before connect and write, preserving newline stream payloads and best-effort semantics without background tasks. socket2 was already resolved; only direct Unix dependency added. Default/minimal native macOS status suites pass; UI95, inventory27, default/minimal/adapters Clippy and debug install pass. KEEP IN PROGRESS pending native Linux full_status_listener_queue_cannot_stall_turn_lifecycle CI evidence: native macOS returns ECONNREFUSED when full, so the old blocking implementation passes that host. Linux unix_stream_connect in https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/net/unix/af_unix.c (lines1572 and1613-1625 at inspection) explicitly waits for peer unless O_NONBLOCK selects EAGAIN. Local evidence /tmp/mini-agent-status-review.json. Follow current pushed commit CI; do not claim Linux reproduction from macOS results.
close_reason: Previously delivered in ce5e67a; native Linux evidence now verified on descendant6138328. description: The Error arm in src/ui/event_handler.rs ignores AgentEvent::Error.interactions, although the runner attaches the canonical transcript for completed work. The Done path adopts provider call/item IDs and reasoning into the live tool records; failed TUI turns preserve only display-event lifecycle IDs and omit that provenance. This is also why Error.interactions is reported as unread in minimal production builds. Exercise successful and failed terminal events through the real handler with differing lifecycle/provider IDs and reasoning, verify replay and no duplicated tools, then adopt error metadata before fallible presentation/settlement. Preserve zero-progress rollback and existing interruption accounting.

Replaced the narrow success-only helper test with a real handler matrix covering success/failure and native/fallback identifiers. title: Reject replaced editor directories before readback and cleanup
description: EditorTemp retains only an ambient directory/path pair. If the editor moves that directory aside and creates a new directory at the original path, read_contents accepts the replacement message.md and Drop deletes it. Bind the temporary directory to a retained handle/identity, reject replacement before reading, and keep cleanup confined to the owned directory. Verify both a replacement directory and symlink leave foreign contents untouched and preserve the original input.
close_reason: EditorTemp now retains an opened directory capability and CheckedMetadata identity, validates original path identity before/after readback and cleanup, and uses relative draft opens/unlinks. Directory and symlink replacements reject readback and preserve foreign plus renamed owned files. Initial old-implementation regression failed; disabling identity validation is detected. Native tmux directory/symlink replacement cases preserve original input, report changed directory, reopen editor, and reap fixture MCP processes. title: Redraw unchanged input after external-editor terminal restoration
description: Native tmux readback-error fixture on c4ef3eb and the current fix restores the terminal and prints the editor diagnostic, but the unchanged original input is absent from the screen. The editor buffer remains correct in unit tests; terminal resumption clears the screen while renderer input caches still consider it unchanged. Force input/status invalidation after terminal handoff and verify unchanged or rejected drafts are visibly restored, including repeated Ctrl-G. Evidence /private/tmp/mini-agent-readback-native-0ac35d6d/editor-delete/handoff-screen.txt.

Native pre-fix screenshot retained a read-error diagnostic but no draft at /private/tmp/mini-agent-readback-native-0ac35d6d/editor-delete; same fixture now visibly restores original draft for deletion, FIFO, invalid UTF-8, oversized output, and symlink cases at /private/tmp/mini-agent-readback-native-0fae733d. title: Bound external-editor readback and report missing or unreadable drafts
description: InputEditor::edit_buffer reads the edited temporary path with unbounded std::fs::read_to_string and silently ignores errors. An editor deleting the file, replacing it with a FIFO, or producing an oversized file can silently lose edits or block/exhaust the TUI on return. Use bounded regular-file readback with no special-file following; preserve original input and report failures. Cover deletion, invalid UTF-8, oversized output, and FIFO replacement.

Readback rejects symlinks/special files, uses Unix no-follow/nonblocking open plus descriptor checks, and caps bytes consumed even after file growth. UTF-8/read failures preserve original input and are reported with any simultaneous exit error; atomic replacement saves remain supported. Extended existing real-shell result matrix and added one independent byte-consumption/input-bound test; all three negative controls detect removed safeguards. Default UI 93, minimal UI 72, input 16, inventory 27 tests pass; default/minimal Clippy and debug install pass.
