title: Unblock saturated terminal input when handing off to lazygit
description: App::run_lazygit directly clears running and joins event_handle while the terminal thread may be blocked sending to a full user event queue. Unlike pause_event_thread, this direct path never releases that sender, so Ctrl-H can hang before lazygit starts. Route lazygit through the shared cancellable reader lifecycle and cover full-queue shutdown.
close_reason: Lazygit now uses the shared pause/join path, releasing saturated terminal sends while preserving queued events. Controlled native full-queue Ctrl-H fixture stalls before lazygit on the prior 592df58 binary and reaches the interactive fixture with the fix; exact input delivered and clean exit/MCP teardown verified. Negative /private/tmp/mini-agent-editor-native-def2bcab; positive /private/tmp/mini-agent-editor-native-955f41b6. Existing native normal/error/full-queue exit and init handoff matrix also passes at /private/tmp/mini-agent-tui-settlement-native-6676d219.

title: Preserve background completion events across TUI input-reader rebinds
description: rebind_event_thread replaces both user_tx and user_rx, but background work retains clones of the previous sender. For example handle_agent_done starts loop validation and captures validation_tx; opening an editor or another terminal handoff before it finishes replaces that channel. The completion is then lost and active_validation can remain set indefinitely. Preserve the shared UI event channel while restarting only the terminal reader, and make reader cancellation unblock a saturated send without dropping completion events. Cover a validator completing after a rebind.
close_reason: Rebinding now restarts only the terminal reader and preserves the shared completion channel. Joining drains queued events into the deferred FIFO to release saturated sends without closing the receiver. Permanent matrix covers two handoffs, preserved ordering, retained background senders, and real loop-validator completion clearing active state. Restoring receiver closure makes the regression fail. Default UI 92 and minimal UI 71 tests pass; strict default and minimal Clippy pass.

title: Keep the event reader paused for the full external-editor handoff
description: The Ctrl-G branch in App::handle_key_event calls rebind_event_thread immediately before InputEditor::open_in_editor. Rebinding stops the old reader but starts a new one, so crossterm remains a live stdin consumer while the external editor inherits the same terminal. Use pause before entering the editor and rebind after it returns, including failure paths. Verify editor input reaches the editor without being consumed as TUI events.
close_reason: Ctrl-G pauses before entering the editor and rebinds after return, including editor errors. Native tmux fixture directly observes terminal kqueue polling: prior 592df58 binary polls during editor ownership; fixed binary does not. Success and failure cases receive exact typed input, return edited drafts, support a second Ctrl-G, and reap MCP fixtures. Evidence /private/tmp/mini-agent-editor-native-955f41b6; negative /private/tmp/mini-agent-editor-native-6827cdac. Initial typing-only negative passed on old code and is not treated as proof.

title: Unblock queued input before pausing the TUI event thread for terminal handoff
description: App::pause_event_thread sets the running flag and joins the event thread without closing user_rx. Like the already-fixed teardown path, a full bounded input queue leaves that thread stuck in blocking_send, so editor/pager/setup handoff never completes. rebind_event_thread replaces the receiver afterward, so close the old receiver before joining during pause and share that stop path with teardown. Verify a saturated input queue cannot prevent terminal handoff.
close_reason: Terminal pause and teardown share a stop path that closes the input receiver before joining the reader. Corrected tmux fixture selects /init before explicit submission, blocks UI output while filling the channel, and confirms final binary reaches the stdin prompt and exits 0 with MCP reaped. Previous b5eb2a8 binary stalls before handoff under that same fixture. Earlier fixture attempts stopped at command selection and are not counted as evidence.

title: Prevent unclaimed startup prebuilds from overriding later model or context changes
description: App::run_slash_command can rebuild run.agent via /model, /provider or context commands while the independent startup prebuild still owns an unclaimed result. resolve_prebuild skips that result whenever run.agent is already Some, leaving the older receiver live. A later interruption/retirement clears run.agent, allowing the event loop to adopt the old prebuild and restore obsolete model/context or omit newly configured services. Invalidate or reconcile prebuild ownership on explicit rebuilds while preserving configured MCP availability; cover changing model before prebuild completion followed by interruption and another turn.
notes: Further source audit: handle_dot_command applies prompt mode/model and then deliberately clears run.agent before start_main_run; the startup prebuild can therefore override the first dot-prompt turn without any intermediate cached agent surviving to the event loop. A fix based only on noticing agent.is_some at loop boundaries is insufficient. run_chain_transition has the same clear-after-prompt shape. Preserve current prompt/model state and MCP availability when consuming delayed startup results, including dot prompts.
close_reason: Foreground AgentBuildCtx builds now invalidate the shared startup snapshot; dot prompts and chain transitions explicitly invalidate when clearing the cache without building. All adoption paths share reconciliation, consume pending services even with a cached agent, rebuild from current model/prompt/session, retain newer MCP managers, and close duplicate startup services. One isolated production-entry matrix verifies unchanged/model/prompt/newer-manager cases through actual local provider requests, MCP tool availability, interruption, next-turn reuse, and reaping. Shared isolation helper replaces duplicate setup. Native model/dot/help checks pass at /private/tmp/mini-agent-prebuild-native-2c30c50c; old binary starts model-changed turn before MCP readiness and sends stale dot prompt. Restoring cached-agent shortcut or ignoring invalidation fails the regression. Default UI 93, MCP 19, minimal MCP prebuild 5, minimal UI 72, skills prebuild 5, inventory 27 pass; all nine Clippy rows and debug install pass. No live MCP fixture processes remain.

title: Settle the runner lifecycle before discarding terminal event channels
description: src/ui/event_handler.rs drops run.agent_rx while handling both AgentEvent::Error and Done, and Done can start loop validation or the next iteration before the runner lifecycle channel has closed. AgentRunCleanupGuard in runner.rs settles owned child work after terminal events are sent. Consequently an ordinary terminal event can discard the completion barrier before subsequent TUI retirement sees it. Preserve terminal response/progress while waiting for cooperative runner settlement before advancing; do not simply abort Done and lose post-response bookkeeping. Cover a terminal payload delivered while owned child work remains live.
close_reason: Done commits its response and then waits for the lifecycle channel before presentation/post-processing; Error waits before advancing. AgentRunState::settle preserves cached agents and retains receiver/abort ownership on timeout; error teardown can still retire them. Actual Done/Error handler regression checks post-response bookkeeping, controlled child settlement, and timeout retention. Removing either handler settlement call independently fails the regression.

title: Join discarded queued prebuild services before rebuilding after a memory refresh
description: start_main_run invalidates stale prebuild state by assigning prebuild_rx=None when memory changes. If a completed (agent, MCP manager) payload is already queued, dropping the receiver only starts asynchronous manager cleanup, so the fresh agent can be built before old services settle. AgentPrebuild now closes rejected late sends and explicitly drains queued results on shutdown, but memory refresh must route its queued-result invalidation through the same owner retirement instead of dropping the receiver alone. Add a deterministic already-queued payload regression.
close_reason: AgentPrebuild now owns its result receiver; memory refresh retires the whole stale owner before any replacement turn can start, and cleanup errors propagate without starting a new turn. Added an isolated production start_main_run regression with a queued MCP manager and held scoped child; default and minimal memory+mcp builds pass. Removing memory retirement makes that regression fail.

title: Unblock the TUI input thread before joining it at shutdown
description: spawn_event_thread uses blocking_send into the bounded user event channel. App teardown sets the running flag and joins the input thread while retaining an open receiver that it no longer drains. If the event channel is full, blocking_send never observes the flag and join deadlocks. Close user_rx before joining so a blocked sender returns; verify the full-channel shutdown case without requiring keyboard timing.
close_reason: Teardown closes user_rx before joining the input thread. Native full-queue smoke exits 1 cleanly after injected rendering failure. Separate mutant binary with receiver.close removed hangs past the 10-second observation bound under the same fixture; harness terminates the owned mutant session.

title: Await main-run work on TUI interruption and nonterminal presentation failure
description: Direct teardown does not cancel or settle the main runner. In addition, fail_pending_main_turn and abort_main_run already abort the runner but drop agent_rx immediately, discarding the AgentRunCleanupGuard lifecycle barrier before scoped children finish. Centralize bounded main-run retirement in AgentRunState, await it before clearing either failure/interrupt state, and also invoke it during teardown and worktree cleanup. Preserve partial progress and the original event-loop error; prove the event channel remains the completion barrier after runner abort.
notes: Implemented bounded AgentRunState retirement used by teardown, worktree cleanup, Ctrl-C, and fail_pending_main_turn. Separate terminal-event handler drops were identified during review and filed independently; this bead does not claim terminal Done/Error payload settlement is solved.
close_reason: AgentRunState retirement aborts the runner and awaits its lifecycle event channel. Teardown, worktree cleanup, Ctrl-C and fail_pending_main_turn use it before clearing state. Default/minimal controlled-child regression verifies runner abort completes while retirement still waits for the owned blocking child. Ordinary terminal-event channel disposal is tracked separately as mini-agent-ejgl.

title: Always run TUI teardown after an event-loop error
description: run_interactive currently uses app.run().await? before app.teardown().await. Any event-loop I/O or settlement error skips explicit task and manager cleanup entirely. Preserve the original run result, always await teardown after successful App construction, then return that original result. Verify normal and failing UI shutdown paths as feasible without provider calls.
close_reason: run_interactive retains App.run result, always awaits teardown, and returns the original result. Final installed binary under an injected stdout EIO exits 1 with the pending MCP process reaped; normal exit remains 0.

title: Wait for owned side-question work during TUI teardown
description: App.teardown aborts each btw task and signals its AgentWorkScope but waits only for the JoinHandle. spawn_blocking_scoped children can remain live after that handle settles. Use existing retire_scoped_task, which also waits for scope.wait_idle with a bound, before manager shutdown; keep timeout reporting explicit. Move the actual blocking-child retirement regression out of the git-worktree-only suite and remove overlapping Tokio-only abort tests.
close_reason: Normal teardown now uses retire_scoped_task and reports retirement errors. Consolidated the prior worktree blocking-child test and two weaker Tokio-only tests into one actual owned-child regression, available and passing without git-worktree as well as in the default build.

title: Retire unfinished agent prebuild work during normal TUI teardown
description: App retains prebuild_task and prebuild_scope, but normal teardown never consumes them; they are used only by git-worktree cleanup. Quitting while prebuild/MCP startup is pending drops the JoinHandle and detaches its work. Route normal shutdown through bounded scope cancellation, task abort/join and wait_idle; drop the prebuild result receiver before retirement. Keep task and scope ownership paired so minimal builds retain real cleanup rather than gating away the unused fields.
close_reason: Added AgentPrebuild ownership with cooperative scope cancellation, explicit shutdown of queued/rejected MCP managers, owned-child settlement, and bounded timeout reporting. Native MCP matrix verifies ready plus initializing and queued servers, queued payloads, and rejected sends; final tmux normal/error exits both reap the pending server.

title: Reject unrepresentable Gym deadlines before launching subprocesses
description: run_bounded launches Popen before calculating its deadline and before entering the cleanup try/finally. task.json positive_int accepts arbitrarily large integers; timeout_secs=10**400 raises OverflowError after launch and leaves the direct process and its pipes alive. Reproduced with a real child, explicitly killed/reaped afterward. Validate timeout numeric representability before effects, reject invalid task timeouts before episode setup, and keep large finite deadlines from overflowing the selector wait. Add meaningful boundary/no-launch regression coverage; full descendant ownership remains separately open as m7bs.
close_reason: Reproduced timeout=10**400 launching a real child and raising OverflowError before cleanup, leaving it alive; probe child explicitly killed/reaped. Added shared positive/finite integer validation before Popen and task setup, computed deadline before launch, and capped individual selector waits while preserving the original overall deadline. Tests reject invalid defaults/task overrides/CLI timeouts before episode directories and agent launch, assert Popen is never called for invalid direct deadlines, and execute large finite deadlines with open/closed pipes. Removing the selector cap fails both large-finite cases natively. Full Gym plus harness CI policy suite: 60 passed (28.532s); cargo fmt and diff checks passed. Full descendant ownership remains open separately in m7bs.

title: Resolve Gym library package paths before neutral-directory imports
description: Task library paths are forwarded verbatim while imports run from a newly created neutral AppPaths directory. A real CLI probe with a valid package path relative to the invocation directory passed the none arm but failed the library arm with missing bundle. Normalize non-seed library paths against the invocation directory when loading tasks, preserving seeds and absolute paths. Exercise actual import argument file access and paired rows from a distinct working directory; document resolution semantics.
close_reason: Implemented with reproduced CLI failures and a six-case negative control for phase attribution. Final 49 Gym tests plus 10 harness-policy tests pass (59 total). Consolidated two timing tests into one matrix and removed their unused sleeping shell fixture. Updated operator docs; formatting and diff checks pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Relative package file and directory imports failed from the neutral cwd before the fix. A CLI test now launches from a directory distinct from both task file and checkout, verifies actual package-content reads by the importer, checks absolute import arguments, and completes all six paired rows including an existing absolute package path. Canonicalized the test scratch root to avoid the macOS /var -> /private/var alias mismatch.

title: Record Gym library database failures without aborting later episodes
description: A stub import that exits successfully but leaves an invalid skills.db makes train.query raise sqlite3.DatabaseError past run_episode and main. Reproduced on two tasks: process exits 1 with traceback after only the first none row, dropping the failed library row and all later episodes. Treat database read failures in library setup as library_install_failed, retain a bounded diagnostic, and prove continuation and cleanup with actual corrupt/incompatible SQLite files by extending the existing library-install failure test.
close_reason: Implemented with reproduced CLI failures and a six-case negative control for phase attribution. Final 49 Gym tests plus 10 harness-policy tests pass (59 total). Consolidated two timing tests into one matrix and removed their unused sleeping shell fixture. Updated operator docs; formatting and diff checks pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Real CLI baseline with corrupt SQLite or an empty incompatible schema exited 1 with traceback after only the first none row. Extended the existing install-failure matrix to command failure, corrupt DB, incompatible schema, missing DB, and no active roots, each across two tasks. SQLite failures now become bounded library_install_failed records; both none arms succeed and cleanup completes.

title: Close Gym SQLite readers deterministically after each query
description: The sqlite3 connection context manager commits or rolls back but does not close the connection. A real connection retained by a test probe remained usable after train.query returned. Repeated library activation queries therefore leave readers and descriptors to cyclic garbage collection, including exceptional query paths. Explicitly close readers on success and failure; extend the database query contract matrix to prove returned readers are unusable after each call.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewed with reproduced pre-fix failures. All 49 Gym tests passed, plus 10 harness-policy tests; final oracle matrix rerun includes link cycles and missing roots. Updated operator documentation. cargo fmt and git diff --check pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: A retained real connection stayed usable after query returned; the regression failed all four path cases before explicit contextlib.closing. Shared query matrix now retains actual connections and proves they reject SELECT after successful and failed queries, while finally closing fixture readers even if assertions fail. Full 49 Gym tests passed.

title: Encode Gym SQLite database paths before constructing read-only URIs
description: train.query interpolates a filesystem path into file:{database}?mode=ro without URI escaping. A real database named skills#probe.db caused the query to open a different file named skills, discard mode=ro as a URI fragment, create that unintended database, and fail with no such table. Encode the absolute path using Path.as_uri before adding mode=ro. Verify reserved URI characters, literal percent escapes, missing-file refusal, read-only enforcement, and the library-arm operator path.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewed with reproduced pre-fix failures. All 49 Gym tests passed, plus 10 harness-policy tests; final oracle matrix rerun includes link cycles and missing roots. Updated operator documentation. cargo fmt and git diff --check pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Baseline failed three literal URI-character paths and the existing full successful-run scenario moved under a root containing #?%23 and spaces. Encoded absolute file URI now preserves the intended database and mode=ro. Shared query matrix proves writes are refused, missing readers create no files, expected records survive, and the library arm still installs/activates its roots. Full 49 Gym tests passed.

title: Keep Gym file-oracle reads inside the bound workspace
description: The expected_files oracle opens workspace / relative directly and follows final and ancestor symlinks. A real probe with workspace/answer pointing to an external file containing the expected text returned success (0, empty detail), so benchmark success can depend on output outside the task workspace. Bind the workspace root, walk directories without following symlinks, and read only a regular final entry through the bound parent while retaining bounded reads and FIFO refusal. Cover external final/ancestor/root links and deterministic path replacement races without duplicating the existing content boundary matrix.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewed with reproduced pre-fix failures. All 49 Gym tests passed, plus 10 harness-policy tests; final oracle matrix rerun includes link cycles and missing roots. Updated operator documentation. cargo fmt and git diff --check pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Reproduced six false-success cases before the fix: external final/ancestor/root links and replacement of final/parent/root paths at the actual open. Added one matrix preserving three forms of internal symlink, rejecting a replacement before parent acquisition and a link cycle/missing root. Reopen resolved internal paths through bound descriptors with no-follow final regular-file validation. Existing exact-content, memory-bound, and independent FIFO deadline tests retained. Full 49-test Gym suite passed; final oracle and harness-policy subset also checked.

title: Classify the learned-skill status macro in the subprocess inventory
description: CI run 34396521636 at db3b8b7 fails the Windows-capable production process-terminal inventory across Linux and macOS rows. The new matches!(status.as_str(), verified | awaiting_approval) expression in skills/store.rs is conservatively recognized as a status terminal inside an opaque macro, requiring an exact content-addressed non-process classification. Audit that macro and add its precise exemption without weakening discovery or bypassing the checker; run the complete inventory suite. Logs: /tmp/mini-agent-ci-db3b8b7-{no-features,linux-policy,macos-default}.log.
close_reason: Audited the database status matches macro and registered its exact non-process source fingerprint and full macro-context digest without weakening discovery. All 27 inventory tests pass, including mutation and nested-context rejection. Fixes the shared failure verified in 17 CI jobs; three Clippy rows pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Confirmed the same inventory test is the sole failing test in all 17 inspected failed CI jobs (three full logs plus fourteen failure summaries). Local reproduction: /tmp/mini-agent-status-macro-before.log. Audited status as a SQLite String and the standard matches! expression as a data-only branch. Added its exact NON-PROCESS source fingerprint and SHA-256 macro-context identity, occurrence count 1; no scanner or discovery logic changed. The full 27-test subprocess inventory suite passes, including macro substitution/nesting/token-identity fail-closed regressions.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Full CI run 34399989186 at 6f3c08b is now completed SUCCESS, independently confirming the inventory classification repair across the full feature/platform matrix.

title: Reset spent claim budgets when reopening proposals waiting for a held-out suite
description: A proposal can use its final claim to reach verified plus held_out_suite_required, for example after earlier expired leases. request_blocked_reevaluation accepts it but only resets exhausted deferred or awaiting_approval budgets, so it returns an unclaimable pending row. The next evaluator sweeps it back to deferred instead of evaluating the newly imported baseline. Reset any spent budget on an otherwise eligible authenticated reopen, retaining report history and numbering. Extend the existing missing-suite recovery test with a final-claim scenario using real lease transitions.
close_reason: Reset spent claim budgets for every eligible authenticated reopen, including verified proposals awaiting a held-out suite. Regression covers first and final claims through real expired leases, one-request recovery, and preserved monotonic report history. 32 admission and 35 operator tests pass; three Clippy rows and debug installation pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Reproduced with seven expired leases followed by a real eighth evaluation that parks verified for a missing suite. After importing the suite, the baseline accepted reevaluation but evaluate_next returned None instead of evaluating it: /tmp/mini-agent-final-claim-suite-before.log. The existing missing-suite recovery test now covers both a first-claim and final-claim decision, one-request recovery, correct budget reset and retention of the blocked report with monotonic report numbering.

title: Keep evaluation report numbering unique when resetting an exhausted claim budget
description: Reports are unique by (proposal_id, attempt), but ProposalLease.attempt is derived directly from the resettable attempt_count claim budget. If a proposal has an earlier successful report, later budget exhaustion and authenticated reopening resets attempt_count to zero and the next report collides with historical attempt 1. Separate report sequence allocation from the bounded claim counter inside the claim transaction, retain historical reports, and allow an explicit refresh at the claim cap to restart its budget. Extend exhaustion and stale-review tests across prior reports and more than eight refreshes.
close_reason: Authenticated reevaluation now refreshes unapproved awaiting_approval reports while preserving history and refusing approved/rejected states. Report numbering is allocated from durable history separately from the bounded claim counter, fixing the reproduced UNIQUE collision after budget reset. Existing exhaustion test covers prior history; operator test covers verifier/corpus changes, authorization/version guards and ten reports across the eight-claim cap. 32 admission +35 operator tests pass. Eight installed-binary checks include a real version-5 to version-6 report upgrade and approval with history preserved. All Clippy rows and debug install pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Reproduced a UNIQUE constraint failure on evaluation_reports.proposal_id/evaluation_reports.attempt after exhausting and reopening a proposal with a prior report: /tmp/mini-agent-report-sequence-before.log. Report numbers now allocate above historical MAX(attempt) under the existing immediate claim transaction; the resettable claim budget remains bounded. Existing exhaustion coverage now includes both empty and populated report histories; the operator refresh test runs through ten reports across the eight-claim budget.

title: Allow operators to refresh stale evaluations awaiting approval
description: Approval rejects an awaiting_approval report when verifier/fakes versions or selected suite hashes change, but authenticated reevaluation only accepts parked verified/deferred proposals. Reimport is idempotent for awaiting_approval, leaving an immutable candidate permanently stuck after a verifier upgrade or trusted-corpus change. Extend explicit local-owner reevaluation to unapproved awaiting_approval rows with atomic row-version guards, preserve report history and attempts, invalidate the old binding, and prove refresh plus subsequent approval through operator tests.
close_reason: Authenticated reevaluation now refreshes unapproved awaiting_approval reports while preserving history and refusing approved/rejected states. Report numbering is allocated from durable history separately from the bounded claim counter, fixing the reproduced UNIQUE collision after budget reset. Existing exhaustion test covers prior history; operator test covers verifier/corpus changes, authorization/version guards and ten reports across the eight-claim cap. 32 admission +35 operator tests pass. Eight installed-binary checks include a real version-5 to version-6 report upgrade and approval with history preserved. All Clippy rows and debug install pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: The corrected regression fixture preserves evaluation-report identity while modeling the previous verifier version. Baseline /tmp/mini-agent-stale-review-before.log shows reevaluation failing on awaiting_approval. The final operator test covers verifier and corpus changes, unauthorized/stale requests, historical report preservation, fresh evaluation and approval, and refusal to reopen an approved canary.

title: Reject special files and symlink swaps when reading learned-skill packages
description: operations::read_package uses blocking File::open after import_path metadata or directory entry checks. Replacing a checked regular file with a FIFO can block forever; a symlink replacement can be followed despite the explicit import symlink rejection. Open with no-follow/nonblocking flags on Unix, verify descriptor and observed identity using existing file helpers, retain bounded reads, and add deterministic read-path tests.
close_reason: Package reads now use checked metadata, no-follow/nonblocking Unix opens (reparse-point opens on Windows), descriptor type/identity verification and the existing 256 KiB bound. Deterministic regular-file/symlink/FIFO replacement tests pass. Directory collection rejects the 33rd matching file before sorting/parsing; existing directory prevalidation test covers capacity and no mutation. 35 operator tests, all three Clippy rows and debug install pass.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: After correcting an initial fixture setup error, the old File::open reader reproducibly accepted a symlink: /tmp/mini-agent-package-reader-before.log. The final test checks exact and oversized byte limits, directories and symlinks, then deterministically replaces an already-checked regular file with a new regular file, symlink or FIFO before open. All are refused without waiting for a FIFO writer. No production test hook or test-only fixture API is compiled outside cfg(test).

title: Compare held-out integer expectations across JavaScript numeric representations
description: verification_expected_matches accepts Integer(i64) only through QuickJS as_int(), which represents i32 values. Correct integer results outside i32 are floating-point Numbers and fail evaluation, permanently rejecting valid candidates. Conversely suite validation accepts i64 expectations not exactly representable as a JavaScript Number. Compare numeric values exactly without narrowing or rounding, reject unrepresentable trusted expectations on import, and cover boundaries plus type/fraction mismatches through the real worker verification path.
close_reason: Fixed exact integer comparison across QuickJS numeric representations and rejected unrepresentable expected integers before suite import. Verifier version is now 6. Boundary/type/rounding regression passes in the 13-test held-out suite; 42 verifier tests pass; installed native contained worker accepts 4294967296 and invalid 9007199254740993 expectation is refused. Three Clippy configurations and debug install pass. Docs updated.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Reproduced with the production worker verification adapter: an exactly representable integer fixture failed HeldOutError::CaseFailed before the change. /tmp/mini-agent-numeric-import-before.log records the failure. The regression covers both QuickJS numeric representations, i32 boundaries, exact integers beyond 2^53, i64::MIN, fraction/type/non-finite mismatches, rounded neighbors, and rejected unrepresentable imports.

title: Reject generic lifecycle transitions into canary without Phase 4 approval
description: The crate-private transition_in_tx rejects Active and active-to-superseded transitions, but permits verified-to-canary using only a policy/evidence snapshot. This bypasses the sole Phase 4 authenticated canary transaction and leaves proposal, approval and lineage state inconsistent. No shipped caller currently requests this edge; quarantine is the production caller. Prove the bypass with the existing lifecycle transaction test, reject Canary as privileged, and preserve legitimate verification/quarantine transitions.
close_reason: Delivered the generic canary guard, removed the misleading source-text test and unused coordinated wrapper, and gated the standalone test adapter. Regression reproduced unauthorized canary creation before the fix. Validation: 6 lifecycle + 32 admission + 6 quarantine + 33 operator tests pass; rich/default/no-JS all-target Clippy rows pass; debug cargo install passes; fmt and diff check pass. Phase 4/5 docs updated. Review artifacts and logs: /tmp/mini-agent-lifecycle-guard-*.

comments.author: platon2001
comments.text: Reproduced against 94e9d3d: the existing lifecycle transaction fixture accepted verified-to-canary with no Phase 4 proposal or authorization, returned transition_id 2, row_version 3 and desired_generation 2. Regression output: /tmp/mini-agent-lifecycle-guard-before.log. The generic primitive now rejects Canary alongside Active before any database mutation. Production callers were audited: quarantine is the only generic transaction caller and requests Quarantined.

title: Reject command must not replay approval for already approved proposals
description: The CLI routes --reject-learned-skill through review_and_admit. That method returns ReviewOutcome::Canary for an already Approved proposal before consulting the reviewer, so a rejection request reports command=approve and republishes an index generation instead of rejecting the ineligible request. Restrict the local-owner reject operation to AwaitingApproval, return an error for approved/canary/active or other ineligible states, and prove state and generation remain unchanged. Keep idempotent approval replay for explicit approval requests.
notes: Baseline lifecycle test reproduced --reject behavior returning success for an already approved proposal. Local-owner rejection now requires AwaitingApproval through a separate admission action; LocalOwnerReviewer is approval-only and obsolete operator denial-result handling was removed. Existing real lifecycle test checks rejection failure for canary and active revisions with proposal/revision/generation unchanged, and explicit approval replay still succeeds. Installed binary rejects an Approved proposal with no mutation or approval output even when embedding config is unavailable. Final 33 operator + 33 admission tests, three all-target Clippy rows, debug install, fmt/diff check and six native CLI checks passed. Evidence /tmp/mini-agent-offline-admin-before.log, /tmp/mini-agent-offline-admin-cli-smoke.json, /tmp/mini-agent-offline-admin-review.json.
close_reason: Reject requests cannot enter approval replay; ineligible approved states fail without mutation and explicit approval replay remains intact.

title: Allow local-owner proposal rejection when embedding initialization is unavailable
description: operations::review_proposal initializes the configured embedding backend even for --reject-learned-skill. Missing external credentials or an unavailable local embedding backend prevent a database-only human denial. Provide a local-owner rejection path through the admission service with existing optimistic status/version checks and no embedding or worker dependency. Verify rejection persists with unusable embedding configuration while approval still requires its real configured backend.
notes: Baseline queue/operator test failed on missing embedding API key before denial. Added authenticated admission::reject_proposal over the existing optimistic denial transaction and routed local-owner rejection through it before backend construction. Generic human-review denial remains tested; added unauthenticated rejection refusal to that existing test. Existing operator test now proves approval still requires the configured unavailable backend while rejection succeeds and remains queryable as terminal. Native CLI smoke with missing API key confirms command=reject and rejected state. All 66 targeted tests, three Clippy rows and debug install passed.
close_reason: Local-owner rejection no longer depends on embedding credentials or verification infrastructure; authenticated state/version checks remain enforced.

title: Requeue parked skill proposals without initializing an embedding backend
description: operations::reevaluate_skill constructs Embedder::from_config and AdmissionEvaluator before calling the store-only request_reevaluation transition. An external backend with an unavailable API key, or a local backend unsupported by this build, therefore blocks --reevaluate-learned-skill although requeueing needs no embeddings or verification. Use the authenticated optimistic store transition directly; preserve the exact parked-state and row-version guards. Extend the existing operator reevaluation test with an unusable embedding configuration. Authority: Phase 4 Stable rejection and retry codes and shipped --reevaluate-learned-skill contract.
notes: Baseline operator test failed because reevaluation tried to initialize an external embedder with missing credentials. reevaluate_skill now invokes request_blocked_reevaluation on the already-open store, binding the observed row version and authenticated local owner. Existing test passes with unusable embedding config, clears the exhausted budget, and proves a second request cannot reopen an already pending row. Installed-binary smoke with missing embedding API key also requeues successfully. Shared final validation: 33 operator tests, 33 admission tests, three all-target Clippy configurations, debug install and six installed-binary checks passed.
close_reason: Authenticated reevaluation is database-only and preserves parking/version guards without requiring an embedding backend.

title: Expose local-owner held-out suite listing and disabling for corpus repair
description: Corpus capacity/corruption failures are recoverable in admission, but shipped operator commands cannot list or disable individual trusted held-out suites. Existing recovery tests disable rows through SQL. Add source-free suite listing and authenticated local-owner disable by canonical suite ID, CLI conflict/dispatch coverage and JSON operator reports; preserve approval revalidation and no model/proposal access. Explicit validated reimport should re-enable a disabled suite. Prove correction of an oversized or obsolete corpus through operator surfaces followed by --reevaluate-learned-skill. Document the explicit operator contract in Phase 4 before implementation.
notes: Added --list-learned-skill-suites and --disable-learned-skill-suite with mutually exclusive operator dispatch and JSON reports. Listing loads only suite IDs and enabled state; authenticated disable is transactional, preserves immutable payload/history, and is idempotent. Existing operator lifecycle test now parks a real oversized corpus, lists/disables through LibraryOperation, reevaluates, imports, approves and activates; schema test covers authentication, unknown IDs, immutable payload and row-version preservation, and reimport re-enabling. Existing CLI matrix covers parsing/conflicts. Seven installed-binary checks in isolated ZS_* roots passed, including empty/populated/disabled JSON listings, repeat disable, unknown ID and conflicts; hidden sentinel stayed out of output and persisted bytes were retained. Evidence /tmp/mini-agent-suite-cli-smoke.json. Final three Clippy rows and debug install passed. No additional Rust test functions.
close_reason: Corpus listing, disabling and recovery are reachable through tested local-owner CLI commands without exposing hidden fixtures.

title: Repair damaged held-out suite records on authenticated reimport
description: SkillStore::import_held_out_suite treats a primary-key conflict as idempotent when stored content_hash matches, without comparing canonical_payload, selector_json, cases_json or enabled. Reimporting a valid package therefore cannot repair corrupted suite projections/payload; a damaged content_hash instead returns UNIQUE. Add atomic authenticated restoration from the validated draft, re-enable an explicitly reimported suite, preserve true no-op imports and identity, and prove successful evaluation after repair through ordinary import. Authority: docs/specs/phase-4-auto-admission.md Independent held-out suites and immutable content-addressed human-approved import.
notes: Reproduced before the fix: authenticated reimport returned success while subsequent selection still returned TamperedSuite. Replaced the uniqueness-error shortcut with atomic UPSERT restoration of canonical payload, projections, hash and enabled state; repairs refresh approval metadata and row version, intact enabled reimports remain no-ops. Existing reproducibility test covers damaged selector/cases/payload/hash and disabled state, successful evaluation after every repair, and repeat idempotence. title: Keep malformed trusted held-out suites from permanently rejecting candidate identities
description: AdmissionEvaluator maps HeldOutError::Json, TamperedSuite, InvalidSuite and UnsupportedVersion to deterministic held_out_failed. These errors originate in trusted stored corpus decoding before candidate held-out execution, so corrupted or incompatible suite state permanently rejects otherwise valid proposal identities and prevents reevaluation after repair. Separate trusted corpus availability from actual CaseFailed/TranscriptMismatch. Reproduce through durable admission state, preserve bounded retry/defer and corrected-corpus recovery, and retain tamper rejection at suite decoding and fail-closed approval. Authority: docs/specs/phase-4-auto-admission.md Stable rejection and retry codes and Independent held-out suites.
notes: Before-fix durable admission reproduction returned rejected/held_out_failed for a tampered trusted suite. Json/TamperedSuite/InvalidSuite/UnsupportedVersion now use bounded infrastructure retry/defer; approval reports infrastructure unavailability and preserves the proposal. Fixed diagnostic text prevents hidden parser values from leaking. Expanded existing retry and approval matrices with all four stored-corpus fault classes, repair, same-identity resubmission and successful review; expanded candidate failure matrix with real held-out value/transcript mismatch, permanent rejection and refusal to reopen. Final 33 admission tests, 12 held-out tests, two bundled-seed tests, three all-target Clippy rows, debug install, fmt and diff check passed. Raw baseline logs /tmp/mini-agent-held-out-corruption-before.log; final admission log /tmp/mini-agent-held-out-integrity-admission-final.log. Historical rejected rows are not automatically reclassified.
close_reason: Trusted corpus defects no longer permanently reject valid identities; bounded recovery, approval recovery and hidden-data secrecy are verified.

title: Reject duplicate held-out spawn and fetch fixture keys before import
description: HeldOutSuiteDraft::validate bounds fake_spawns/fake_fetches but accepts duplicate request keys. FakeHostGlobals::seed_spawn and seed_fetch reject duplicate keys during worker initialization, so an imported trusted suite cannot execute even when the candidate and held-out expression are valid. Reject repeated (program,args) and (url,method) keys at draft validation/import and decode; distinct argument vectors or methods and the same fixture in different cases remain valid. Authority: docs/specs/phase-4-auto-admission.md Independent held-out suites; import validates trusted fixture contracts.
notes: Before-fix import regression accepted duplicate spawn fixture keys and persisted the suite. Added per-case request-key uniqueness validation for spawn (program,args) and fetch (url,method), used by import and stored-suite decoding. Matrix covers identical/conflicting duplicate responses for both effect types, rejects without persistence, and accepts distinct args/methods plus key reuse across cases. Phase 4 spec documents contract. Final 12 held-out tests, 33 admission tests, two bundled-seed tests, all three all-target Clippy rows, debug install, fmt and diff check passed. Review: /tmp/mini-agent-held-out-integrity-review.json.
close_reason: Duplicate effect fixture keys are rejected before import; distinct request keys and independent case fixtures remain valid.

title: Keep oversized trusted held-out corpora from permanently rejecting valid skill identities
description: Source-traced follow-up to 9x8q and u0cn: held_out::evaluate returns InvalidSuite when the trusted corpus exceeds the case or suite cap. AdmissionEvaluator::evaluate_lease maps InvalidSuite to deterministic held_out_failed; evaluate_next permanently rejects the proposal and revision. SkillStore::request_blocked_reevaluation permits only missing-suite verified rows and two deferred infrastructure states, so correcting the trusted corpus cannot recover the same candidate identity. The candidate has not failed a regression. Reproduce through the admission API, classify corpus-capacity failure as recoverable without weakening actual failed-case rejection, and prove reevaluation succeeds after the corpus is corrected. Authority: docs/specs/phase-4-auto-admission.md, Stable rejection and retry codes and Independent held-out suites; document the recoverable policy in the owning spec before implementation.
notes: Reproduced through evaluate_next before the fix: valid candidate plus 33 trusted suites returned a permanent rejected/held_out_failed report. Added typed CorpusCapacity for suite/case overflow; evaluation uses existing bounded infrastructure retry/defer, approval reports Infrastructure without consuming the reviewed proposal. Expanded the existing scheduler retry test into cancellation/suite-cap/case-cap cases with real imports, bounded parking, corpus correction, unchanged-identity resubmission, and successful evaluation. Expanded existing review-staleness test with overflow during human review and successful admission after correcting corpus. No additional Rust test functions. Final validation: 33 admission tests, 11 held-out tests, rich/default/no-JS all-target Clippy, debug cargo install, cargo fmt and diff check passed. Owning Phase 4 spec documents policy. Historical rejected reports are not automatically migrated because the old unsupported-suite summary did not identify the capacity cause.
close_reason: Corpus capacity failures remain recoverable during evaluation and human approval; bounded retry and corrected-corpus recovery verified.

title: Cap Gym miner metadata output without accepting truncated records
description: At a7b47d6 all Git and bd metadata output is captured completely. A real 4 MiB flood on each stream retained both entire streams and allocated much more than diagnostic-tail capture. Tests lower cap to64KiB, flood real streams, accept complete exact-cap JSON, reject valid prefixes with overflowing whitespace, preserve existing task artifacts, and prove peak allocation below1MiB. description: Reproduced a post-checkout hook locking its temporary worktree and failing. Both trainer and miner invoke git worktree remove with only one --force; Git refuses locked registrations, filesystem cleanup deletes the directory, and prune preserves the locked entry. description: train.prepare_workspace/remove_workspace and mine_tasks.oracle_at invoke git worktree add/remove/prune with subprocess.run(capture_output=True) and no timeout. description: episode_env interpolates --provider and --model directly inside TOML quotes. description: Reproduced a post-checkout hook that writes a file then fails: prepare_workspace(..., allow_empty=True) keeps .git, tracked base files, and hook output instead of creating an empty fallback. As a deleted_files entry this recursively removes the entire worktree; as an initial or expected file it targets a directory instead of a file. Reject empty component sequences during task loading and verify no episodes launch for those entries.

Unchecked candidates are therefore presented as measured evidence. Retains prompt and loader compatibility assertions. Baseline failed both provenance cases; final Gym/harness suite49 passed.

title: windows-general-sandbox-policy flakes on probe readiness, and one authority denial fails with it
description:
windows-general-sandbox-policy gates ordinary pushes (it ran on the push runs b5327ff4 and 71dfe5cd), and it is intermittent: failed on b5327ff4 (push) and 0e39cd0b (workflow_dispatch), passed on 71dfe5cd (push) and 0f1f261d (dispatch).

Run 34372655666 (0e39cd0b) failed three tests at once:

  sandbox::windows::tests::next_process_recovers_a_preserved_profile_job_acls_and_root
    src\sandbox\windows.rs:6153 -- restart-recovery helper must become ready:
    'timed out waiting for probe readiness: ...mini-agent-preflight-reco...'

  sandbox::windows::tests::timed_out_general_preflight_reaps_tree_and_removes_recovery_state
    src\sandbox\windows.rs:6465 -- descendant must become ready:
    'timed out waiting for probe readiness: ...mini-agent-general-timeout-test-parent...'

  sandbox::windows::tests::control_root_authority_denies_root_swap_after_attestation
    src\sandbox\windows.rs:5814 (helper thread) -- 'bound control authority must deny directory replacement: ()'
    src\sandbox\windows.rs:5817 -- 'control-root mutator must not panic: Any { .. }'

The first two are plainly load-sensitive: both are explicit readiness waits that timed out, the same family as mini-agent-ualx (wall-clock p99 gate), mini-agent-02cp (wall-clock drain bound) and mini-agent-l07k (cleanup racing process teardown). Raising or removing those fixed bounds is the same remedy.

The third deserves separate attention and should not be assumed to be the same flake. It is an assertion that a bound control authority DENIES a directory replacement, and it failed in a helper thread, which then surfaced as 'control-root mutator must not panic'. A denial assertion that fails intermittently is either (a) test setup racing the authority binding, so the mutator runs before the authority is in force, or (b) a real window in which the authority does not yet deny. Those have opposite consequences and the logs cannot distinguish them, because all three tests failed in the same run on what looks like a starved runner.

Suggested order of work: fix the two readiness waits first so the noise is gone, then re-run the authority test in isolation under load to see whether it still fails. If it does, it is a real attestation-ordering gap in the general Windows sandbox, not a test race.
notes:
Current evidence separates these paths. The earlier passing Windows jobs ran the installed runtime probe plus (in0f1f261) one cache test; they did NOT execute the other32 general-sandbox unit tests. Commit0e39cd0 enabled the full33-test module for the first time (510g), exposing30 passes/3 failures. The two readiness fixtures re-execute the libtest binary for production helper markers; libtest replaces main and cannot dispatch those markers (usb3). The direct root-rename assertion failed despite an established authority, whose handle had only metadata/security access (bhug). Fixes in748969d use the installed production binary for fixture helpers and add directory-list access to new/recovered root handles. Native validation run34373678292 is live. Original cached production-preflight failure atb5327ff remains separate underqi5r. There is no evidence here justifying raising or removing the bounded production deadlines.
Native run34373678292 job102540950052 at748969d succeeded: all33 general-sandbox unit tests plus the full installed-binary probe. Root replacement is fixed under bhug by directory-list access on retained new/recovered root handles; readiness fixtures are fixed under usb3 by invoking the installed production helper instead of libtest. No deadline increases. Original intermittent cached production preflight failure remains separately unresolved under qi5r; this passing run does not establish its cause.
close_reason: All three named failures are fixed under bhug and usb3 (748969d): retained directory-list handles deny root replacement and recovery fixtures invoke the installed production helper. Independently reconfirmed at 6f3c08b in native Windows job 102629383660: all 33 general-sandbox tests pass, including both readiness cases and direct root-swap denial, followed by the full installed WINDOWS_GENERAL_SANDBOX_PASS probe. Original intermittent production preflight failure remains separately open as qi5r; no timeout increases or inference about that cause.

title: Keep advisor context current and isolated within each request
description: AdvisorTool reads a process-global transcript populated at session boundaries. No setter receives tool results or assistant output produced during the active request, so an advisor asked about a just-completed tool result cannot see it. ACP does not seed this global transcript, and concurrent requests can read another session snapshot. Replace the snapshot with request-owned context populated from the runner completion/tool events, including bounded model-visible tool results. Verify a multi-turn tool-to-advisor sequence, request isolation and retry refresh without duplicate history.
close_reason: Delivered request-owned advisor transcripts populated by CompletionCall, ModelTurnFinished and post-rewrite ToolResult hooks. Removed global transcript publication from startup/UI; only agents with the advisor tool collect context. Three distinct tests cover live same-batch results and refresh without duplicates, forced concurrent isolation, and text-only media/reasoning projection. Process-global negative control fails isolation test. Passed 3003 unit +13 integration, isolated skills 21+1, minimal advisor16, three Clippy rows and debug install.

title: Resolve advisor runtime model choices with the startup provider rules
description: /advisor model writes the supplied token directly into advisor_model and reuses the previous client. Startup resolves quick-model aliases into provider plus actual model ID and can construct a separate client. Use one resolver for startup and runtime selection, publish the model/client pair only after successful resolution, and verify aliases, bare IDs and failed provider construction without changing the previous selection.
close_reason: Delivered shared startup/runtime advisor model resolution and provider-identity-aware client refresh. Regression tests verify concrete custom gateway endpoints, aliases, bare model IDs, same-provider refresh, and unchanged selection on failure. title: Preserve the selected advisor provider across main-agent rebuilds
description: Advisor startup can select a different provider via a quick-model alias, but SlashCtx::rebuild_agent and main provider/session switches unconditionally replace its client with the main client while retaining the advisor model ID. Even a prompt or advisor settings rebuild can route that model to the wrong service. Store the configured advisor provider identity and refresh its client only when that exact provider changes; distinguish custom gateways that use the same protocol. title: Terminal-frame drain is wall-clock bounded, so a starved runner still discards the frame
description:
The enx3 regression test failed on run 34347345285 (4d043c84), macos --features skills:

  extras::js::supervisor::worker_exit_tests::exit_poll_drains_the_pending_read_with_cancellation_and_a_bound
  JS_TEST_WORKER_EXIT class=success
  exit poll discarded the pending frame: Err(Transport)

enx3 is closed and its fix is correct in mechanism, but the drain it added is bounded by wall-clock time:

  src/extras/js/supervisor.rs:2086
  let drain_deadline = deadline.min(Instant::now() + PROCESS_EXIT_RECONCILIATION_TIMEOUT);  // 100ms
  match await_controlled(&mut task, cancellation, drain_deadline).await {
      Ok(tagged) => break tagged.map_err(|_| WorkerError::Transport)?,
      Err(WorkerError::TimedOut) if Instant::now() < deadline => {
          return Err(classify_worker_exit(exit_status));
      }

The failure log proves which branch ran: JS_TEST_WORKER_EXIT is printed only from classify_worker_exit, so the 100ms drain expired and the pending frame was discarded, returning Transport for a worker that had exited cleanly. That is precisely the outcome enx3 set out to eliminate, reached through a narrower window.

The bound is deliberate -- the comment says it stops an inherited or still-open pipe from making a dead worker's caller wait. But it cannot distinguish that case from the reader task simply not being scheduled within 100ms, which is ordinary on a contended CI runner. The same job has previously run 30 percent over baseline (see the load evidence recorded on enx3).

This is the same failure class as mini-agent-ualx: a fixed wall-clock bound asserted on a shared runner. Options, in rough order of preference:
1. Bound on reader progress rather than elapsed time -- the process has already exited, so a genuinely empty pipe returns EOF immediately and only a foreign holder keeps it open.
2. Distinguish 'reader not yet scheduled' from 'pipe held elsewhere', e.g. by confirming the read task has been polled at least once before starting the clock.
3. If a wall-clock bound is kept, raise it well above scheduling jitter: the caller's worker is already dead, so the only cost of waiting is latency on an error path.

Note the test is a deterministic regression for both orderings, so a flake here is not cosmetic: it means the race can still resolve the wrong way in production under load.
notes: Native Windows containment job 102480663350 in run 34354906277 at fb3157f passed with the new controlled pipe reader. It exercises the production worker protocol path; original c9500c0 cleanup sharing failure was unrelated and is tracked separately in x7ts.

Buffered terminal frames survive delayed reader scheduling; empty or partial frames terminate even while a foreign writer remains open. Cancellation, invocation deadlines, abnormal-exit handling, protocol validation, and generation retirement remain enforced. Old-supervisor negative control fails with queued reader lost its buffered terminal: Err(Transport); final worker-exit suite passes on rich and skills-only feature rows. Validation: 2976 broad unit tests plus 13 integration tests, isolated skill bindings and library test, three all-target Clippy rows, debug install, and native macOS production containment matrix passed. title: Handle SIGTERM during headless loop validation
description: extras/loop/headless.rs awaits validation with tokio::signal::ctrl_c only. title: Phase 6 containment gates flake at cleanup on both macOS and Windows
description: CI run 34323063453 at cb6f7e4 failed the production macOS containment matrix with MACOS_PARENT_DEATH_FAILED=workspace_cleanup. The stage checks deletion of a probe sentinel, not removal of a directory. Parent death closes protocol stdin and heartbeat; worker EOF can finish worker.wait and let run_guardian exit while its detached heartbeat monitor is still cleaning the sentinel. Injecting a 300 ms monitor delay reproduces the exact matrix failure. Join the monitor before guardian exit, with a private worker-reaped notification and parent acknowledgement to avoid circular normal-shutdown waiting. Preserve whole-group parent-death termination, mandatory sentinel cleanup, exact guardian reap before publication retirement, and fail-closed availability. Replace the weaker heartbeat-only regression with lifecycle coverage and verify the same delayed production matrix passes.
notes:
Confirmed the race using the non-libtest production binary: injecting a 300 ms pause in the parent-death monitor after heartbeat EOF and before sentinel cleanup deterministically produces MACOS_PARENT_DEATH_FAILED=workspace_cleanup (matrix exit 1). Source restored afterward. Logs: /tmp/mini-agent-guardian-race-before-{install,matrix}.log. Fix: guardian joins its monitor before exit; trusted guardian reports worker reap on its private duplex heartbeat, and parent try_wait acknowledges normal release before waiting for guardian reap. Publication retirement still follows exact guardian reap. Keep sentinel cleanup gating.
Same failure on Windows, so this is not macOS-specific. Run 34352141510 (c9500c0d), windows-worker-containment-gate:

  test extras::js::tests::worker_containment::windows_js_worker_containment ... FAILED
  Windows JS worker containment and install-location probes must pass:
    Custom { kind: Other, error: "remove disposable LPAC executable: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process" }
  Windows containment probe failed with exit code 101

phase6-cross-platform-gate failed alongside it, as it did for the macOS occurrence, because it consumes the probe outputs.

Flake, not regression: the Windows gate passed on the five runs before (4d043c84, 7f56e221, 94ba9e61, fdb97017, 7c3c8a41) and on the run after (fb3157f3, where all three containment gates were green). The candidate commits in between were clipboard helper work, which does not touch the LPAC executable lifecycle.

The two platforms fail the same way, and that is the point: both gates fail at their CLEANUP step, never at a containment assertion.
- macOS: MACOS_PARENT_DEATH_FAILED=workspace_cleanup -- the workspace directory cannot be removed after the parent dies.
- Windows: 'remove disposable LPAC executable ... being used by another process' -- the disposable worker executable cannot be unlinked.

Both are one bug wearing two OS error messages: cleanup runs before the contained process tree is fully reaped, so something still holds the file or directory. Unix lets you unlink an open file, which is why macOS surfaces it as a directory-removal failure while Windows surfaces it as a sharing violation on the executable itself.

Fix once, in the shared teardown: wait for the reaped process tree before cleanup, or report cleanup failure as a distinct non-gating diagnostic. The security-relevant part of both gates -- that containment held -- passed in every one of these failures. Keeping cleanup as a gating assertion is what turns a housekeeping race into a red Phase 6 security gate, and that is what trains readers to dismiss a real breach as noise.
Follow-up audit: the macOS guardian race has a deterministic parent-death monitor negative control and a delivered join/handshake fix. The Windows sharing failure is tracked atomically as x7ts (plus partial-progress flza); its probe already waits for the root and uses a single-process Job. Matching cleanup-stage symptoms do not establish a shared root cause or justify making cleanup failures non-gating. Preserve the canonical fail-closed cleanup contracts. Native sharing-holder execution was missing from CI and is now tracked as mhf8.
close_reason: Confirmed and fixed guardian main exiting before its detached parent-death monitor. Added private worker-reaped/normal-release handshake and monitor join; publication retirement still follows exact guardian reap. Replaced heartbeat-only test with lifecycle regression plus nonblocking/invalid/closed-peer cases. Negative control removing join fails. Original production matrix fails with 300 ms monitor delay; fixed matrix passes 3/3 with delay and final ordinary native matrix passes. title: Bound task-miner Git blob reads before materialization

close_reason: Git blob reader now checks object size before content capture and independently caps complete stdout at MAX_BLOB_BYTES+1 with a 30-second read deadline. Oversize, failed, or timed-out required blobs skip the complete file; adds/deletes distinguish absent sides from empty blobs. Existing byte/CRLF behavior remains intact. Real commit matrix covers exact limit, one byte over on either side, large added/modified/deleted blobs, empty files, and newline filenames. Baseline peak 13,629,676 traced bytes failed the four-MiB bound; fixed matrix passes. A real Git ref switched after the size query is rejected with peak below one MiB, proving the stream cap. All 256 Python regressions passed; diagnostic capture tests remain green. Logs /tmp/mini-agent-gym-blob-*.log.

title: Terminate Gym subprocess descendants on timeout
description: scripts/gym/train.py run delegates to subprocess.run(capture_output=True, timeout=...). Python kills only the immediate process at timeout, leaving agent/oracle descendants alive across workspace cleanup and subsequent arms. Existing timeout fixtures spawn sleep 30 but assert only the row and worktree cleanup. notes:
The shared scripts/gym/process_capture.py now bounds output but still only kills the immediate child. Verified with real Python subprocesses at timeout=1: both an ordinary child and a child launched with start_new_session=True survived and wrote a delayed marker afterward; all probe descendants were explicitly killed. Evidence /tmp/mini-agent-gym-descendant-probe.json. Production workers and sandbox commands create separate groups/sessions on Linux/macOS, so killpg on a Gym root alone is insufficient. macOS JS guardian has its own parent-death monitor (race separately tracked as l07k); general commands and arbitrary oracle descendants still require complete ownership. Keep this issue open until independently grouped children are reached with actual regressions.
2026-09-09 native investigation: Darwin select exposes KQ_NOTE_TRACK, but registering NOTE_FORK|NOTE_TRACK|NOTE_EXIT for an owned live child returns errno 45 (ENOTSUP). Confirmed in current Apple XNU kern_event.c filt_procattach: NOTE_TRACK/NOTE_TRACKERR/NOTE_CHILD are rejected. Source https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/kern_event.c . Both temporary probe children were explicitly killed/reaped. Existing macOS worker cleanup scans one process group and does not provide general ownership across setsid. Linux PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER is a potential isolated-supervisor building block, not an implemented fix. Full descendant ownership remains open. Separately reproduced direct-child deadline-overflow leak is tracked in 5kbz; fixing it does not close this issue.
Linux portion is now closed in bskq7, with sf4pd/8rttu startup and interrupted-cleanup corrections. Native unprivileged Linux: all 57 Gym tests pass, including 15 ordinary/setsid/double-fork exit/timeout/overflow cases and caller death. Original capture passes prior three tests but fails every new descendant case. macOS complete descendant ownership remains unresolved; process-group-only cleanup cannot cover setsid descendants. Do not close this parent on Linux evidence alone.
2026-09-10 further platform investigation: current Apple XNU bsd/kern/sys_coalition.c coalition() requires task_is_in_privileged_coalition and returns EPERM otherwise (lines208-236); coalition termination only arms empty notification and does not kill existing members (lines88-94). This private API is not a general unprivileged Gym ownership replacement. Current kern_prot.c setsid_internal/setsid and setpgid directly enter groups without a MAC-policy hook, so a presumed Seatbelt deny-setsid rule is not supported by that source. Sources https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/xnu/blob/main/bsd/kern/sys_coalition.c and /bsd/kern/kern_prot.c . No platform support narrowed, no process-group-only fix substituted, and complete macOS ownership remains unresolved.
close_reason: Native macOS now runs each Gym tree in a disposable launchd resource coalition, enumerates descendants across setsid/double-fork, signals kernel-checked identities and acknowledges complete cleanup before workspace deletion; caller death retains the owner through settlement. Native 15-case matrix plus caller-death test and all 64 existing Gym tests pass (8 Linux-specific skips); unrelated live process is preserved. Linux delivered ownership remains unchanged.

description: scripts/gym/train.py run_oracle uses target.open followed by unbounded handle.read for expected_files. Fixed test passes that ceiling. All 251 scripts/tests Python regressions pass. Logs /tmp/mini-agent-gym-file-oracle-*.log. title: Enforce media attachment byte limit while reading
description: load_attachment checks metadata(path).len against MAX_MEDIA_BYTES and then calls unbounded std::fs::read(path). A file that grows or is replaced after metadata can bypass the 20 MiB memory limit; a non-regular file may also block despite a small reported size. Open and validate the actual file, bound the read to the limit plus one byte, reject oversized results, and add a deterministic regression for growth/replacement without duplicating signature tests.
notes: Implemented a single opened handle for metadata/content, regular-file checks, O_NONBLOCK on Unix to cover FIFO replacement, and a MAX_MEDIA_BYTES+1 bounded read with oversize rejection. Two regressions: six-case boundary/change/compatibility matrix and two FIFO cases. Baseline accepted the oversized grown file; disabling O_NONBLOCK failed the FIFO test at its 5-second watchdog. Restored suite: 12 attachment tests pass; full extras 1651 unit +1 integration pass. Final lint/install checks ongoing.
close_reason: Attachment reads now validate the opened regular file and read through that handle with a 20 MiB+1 byte cap, rejecting oversize data even after growth. Unix O_NONBLOCK prevents FIFO replacement from blocking open; symlinks to regular files remain supported. Six-case boundary/change/compatibility matrix plus two FIFO cases pass. Baseline reproduced acceptance of a grown oversized file. Removing O_NONBLOCK made the FIFO watchdog fail in 5.02s; restored attachment suite passed 12 tests. Full extras: 1651 unit +1 integration passed. Rich/default/extras all-target Clippy and debug cargo install with skills,lsp,pdf passed. Logs: /tmp/mini-agent-media-bounds-*.log. Documented the regular-file and live read-limit contract.
