title: Isolate unreadable Agent Skill packages during catalog signature refresh
description: catalog_signature propagates per-package read_dir/metadata/ACTIVE-read errors before refresh reaches its scan_record error isolation. One unreadable ACTIVE or package directory therefore makes all installed Agent Skills unavailable. Record unavailable package paths in the signature, omit only those packages, and detect recovery on the next refresh. Extend the existing corrupt-sibling regression with real read failure and repair; preserve errors reading the catalog root itself.
close_reason: Package-local signature collection failures now record unavailable paths instead of aborting the entire catalog. Refresh omits those packages while retaining valid siblings; signature retry observes pointer repair and stable failures avoid repeated embedding/rebuilds. Root collection errors still propagate. Existing corruption regression now covers refresh, fresh startup, stable failure and repair, including a real unreadable ACTIVE that failed before the fix with PermissionDenied. All 63 targeted tests, three Clippy rows and debug install pass.

title: Test runtime capability revocation through the shipped lifecycle boundary
description: The cancellation_and_worker_recycle test calls WorkerCapabilityLifecycle::cancel, which is cfg(test), and is the sole consumer of InvocationCapabilityRuntime::cancel. Production revokes the complete worker runtime through lifecycle Drop/recycle and parent cancellation, so the selective-cancel fixture falsely represents a shipped path. Remove both unused cancel adapters and revise the existing regression to verify production lifecycle Drop invalidates active, queued and bound authority, with a positive fresh-runtime dispatch control. Preserve independent parent-broker cancellation and effect-budget tests.
close_reason: Removed the fixture-only WorkerCapabilityLifecycle::cancel adapter and its unused runtime cancel implementation. Replaced the old selective-cancel/recycle test with production lifecycle Drop coverage for active, queued and bound authority, stale tokens/guards, and positive dispatch before teardown and after a fresh lifecycle. Negative control retaining prepared authority failed at old-handle binding as expected; exact implementation restored and regression passed. Related 21 binding, 13 attribution, 13 parent effect cancellation tests pass; three Clippy rows, debug install and native macOS containment pass.

title: Replace test-only worker waits with bounded production teardown
description: WorkerProcess::wait and all three platform wait methods have only test callers. The Linux wait_worker_bounded timeout branch invokes this unbounded wait after termination, so its advertised bound can be lost. Migrate explicit termination tests to terminate_and_reap, retain natural-exit observation for the protocol-fault probe, bound its timeout cleanup, and delete the unused unbounded worker facade and platform methods. Preserve ordinary Child cleanup and cached-root termination-error coverage.
notes: Full caller audit and compilation also found two runtime transcript fixture calls outside the launcher module: five-second exit-wait timeout cleanup and failed-startup retry cleanup. Both now use bounded production teardown; retry requires cleanup success. The initial targeted compilation exposed these remaining references before verification.
close_reason: Removed WorkerProcess::wait and all three platform wait wrappers. Launcher explicit teardown, Linux termination probe, and runtime timeout/retry fixtures now use bounded production terminate_and_reap. Natural protocol-fault exits are still observed before timeout cleanup. Launcher tests assert failed exit, cached reap and observer release; cached-root tree-error regression retained. Passed 7 launcher, 63 runtime/supervisor (1 intentionally ignored), and 27 inventory tests, all three required Clippy rows, debug install, and the installed native macOS containment matrix. Linux/Windows native execution remains CI-owned.

title: Retry interrupted reads in the worker stderr drain
description: start_stderr_drain stops its while-let loop on every read error, including ErrorKind::Interrupted. Rust Read documents Interrupted as non-fatal and retryable (https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Read.html#errors). If the drain exits after a signal interrupts a pipe read, the still-live worker can fill stderr and block before producing its protocol result. Preserve fixed-size discard storage, retry only Interrupted, stop on EOF or other errors, and prove retry/terminal behavior with injected reader events plus the real-worker backpressure regression.
close_reason: Reproduced premature exit with an injected Interrupted read: the old loop left later stderr events unread. The shared fixed-buffer drain now retries Interrupted and stops on EOF or other errors. The regression covers interruptions before and between successful reads and both terminal paths; the real 256 KiB worker backpressure test also passes. Three Clippy rows, debug install, and native macOS containment matrix pass.

title: Remove synthetic stderr memory assertions and production test counters
description: The worker stderr regression asserts StderrStats.retained_bytes == 0, but the accessor supplies a hard-coded zero. Its capped observation counters are used only by that test yet allocate Arc atomics and execute on every production stderr read. Remove the synthetic metric and counters, preserve the fixed 4096-byte discard buffer and continuous draining, and retain the actual 256 KiB worker-output backpressure regression without claiming a measured retention bound.
close_reason: Removed hard-coded retained_bytes assertions and the capped Arc/atomic counters that existed solely for them. Production continuously discards stderr in a fixed 4096-byte buffer. The real-worker 256 KiB backpressure test remains, with a five-second watchdog and explicit shutdown; disabling the actual drain causes its expected timeout. Supervisor, tool, binding, lifecycle, and inventory checks pass.

title: Exercise production proposal cancellation and remove duplicate execution wrappers
description: ProposalEffectService::execute has only test callers, and its test-only execute_cancellable duplicates the real execute_prepared_cancellable cancellation path. The cancellation test therefore cannot catch regressions in the production entry point and races 10 ms/50 ms sleeps. Migrate cancellation coverage to the actual prepared dispatch path with deterministic queue receipt/reply coordination, retain cancellation-before-dispatch and subsequent-call recovery assertions, remove both duplicate wrappers, and keep one production-path malformed-proposal budget test.
close_reason: Removed the unused synchronous execute wrapper and duplicate test-only cancellation API. Cancellation now exercises execute_prepared_cancellable with queue receipt/reply barriers, asserts no pre-cancel enqueue, exact OutcomeUnknown after receipt, retained late-response waiter, and successful next call. Folded missing-tests budget coverage into the contained JsTool regression; removed the overlapping direct-wrapper test. All 21 proposal tests and the durable session test pass; a negative control changing the production result to Cancelled failed the expected assertion. Three Clippy rows and debug install pass.

title: Classify telemetry dispatcher test calls in the subprocess inventory
description: The subprocess inventory gate flags two TelemetryDispatcher::spawn calls added to the operations tests by the durable evidence fixes as unrecognized unguarded spawn terminals. They create the in-process telemetry worker, not OS subprocesses. Add exact test-only inventory entries for both call sites and rerun the inventory suite.
close_reason: Added exact TEST-ONLY ownership entries for the two TelemetryDispatcher test calls in both inventory tables. All 27 subprocess inventory tests pass; all three Clippy feature rows pass.

title: Preserve maximum turn latency independently of worst invocation outcome
description: qualify collapses a turn to one InvocationEvidence reference, preferring outcome severity over latency. A fast failure can therefore hide a much slower successful invocation in that same turn, despite the stated worst-outcome/highest-latency contract. Accumulate outcome severity and maximum latency independently and test reversed input order, duplicated evidence, exact p95, and resulting latency gates.
close_reason: Accumulate worst direct outcome and maximum invocation latency independently per turn. Regression catches p95 dropping from 1000us to 100us when a fast failure hides a slow success; asserts both latency gates and order/duplicate invariance. Relevant tests, three Clippy feature rows, and debug install pass.

title: Apply configured secret replacement after credential shape detection
description: Redactor currently substitutes exact secrets before matching credential shapes. A configured substring inside a label or inside an unquoted value can hide the label or insert a bracket delimiter, leaving an unconfigured credential suffix intact (for example exact SPLIT with password=beforeSPLITafter). Move exact replacement after shape detection and cover labels, value interiors, and private-key markers. This is a latent API defect: the current production feedback caller passes an empty exact-secret list.
close_reason: Moved configured exact-secret replacement after PEM, labeled, bearer, and vendor shape detection. Regression reproduced a leaked suffix for password=beforeSPLITafter; matrix covers label/value/vendor/PEM interference and standalone configured secrets. All 20 feedback/repair tests and required lint/build gates passed. Phase 5 contract updated.

title: Include combined fake-transcript exhaustion and OOM in native worker CI suites
description: The exact mtg1 crash regression allocation_failure_remains_terminal_after_fake_transcript_exhaustion lives in skill_verification_semantics, which is not selected by the dedicated Windows/macOS/Linux native Phase 6 suite filters. General skill matrix runs it on Linux/macOS, while native gates currently prove resolver cleanup through a timeout scenario. Preserved the verifier ResourceLimit assertion and removed the old copy. title: Bound concurrent query embedding work before entering the blocking pool
description: Phase 3 specifies a bounded blocking embedding worker, but Embedder::embed_query_cached starts a spawn_blocking_scoped task for every cache miss. That wrapper only tracks lifecycle ownership and forwards to Tokio; neither embedder nor wrapper bounds admitted jobs or queued query copies. WorkerSaturated is never constructed. Add an explicit per-service inference admission bound, keep the permit owned by the blocking job through cancellation, and exercise saturation plus capacity recovery with a gated backend. Preserve cache hits and agent work ownership.
close_reason: Added four per-Embedder query slots acquired before copying or queueing a cache miss. Blocking jobs own permits through caller cancellation, failure, and panic; cache hits bypass admission. title: Report verifier heap and stack exhaustion as resource limits instead of timeouts
description: skills/verify.rs::test_result maps every DiagnosticClass::ResourceLimit to TestResult::Timeout, even though the closed worker diagnostic also covers memory and stack exhaustion. TestResult::OutOfMemory is never constructed. This produces misleading operator-facing errors for non-timeout failures. Reproduce through verify_skill with real bounded heap/stack exhaustion, use an honest ResourceLimit outcome for the shared diagnostic, remove the unreachable OutOfMemory outcome, and preserve the stable verification_resource_limit admission code and source-free rendering.
notes: Implemented ResourceLimit for the shared closed resource diagnostic, including OOM during promise-job draining (which previously looked like JobLimitExceeded). Retained/local heap and stack regressions pass; source-free forged OOM text remains an ordinary exception. Related sticky-allocation evidence is implemented under mini-agent-mdrs, with verifier version 5. Final transcript-limit interaction regression and feature gates are being completed.

title: Signal closed LSP fixture stdin only after closing the native handle
description: The close-stdin fixture writes LSP_FIXTURE_STDIN_CLOSED_FILE inside its initialized handler, then breaks, drops the reader, and closes stdin. A parent that observes the marker can still write before the handle closes, making the broken-stdin lifecycle assertion race scheduling. title: Release blocking test gates when an assertion unwinds
description: AgentWorkScope::new_with_blocking_test_gate returns BlockingTestRelease without Drop. If a cancellation test panics after its worker enters the gate but before release(), Tokio runtime shutdown waits forever on the blocked native thread, hiding the regression as a hung test job. Make the release handle unblock on drop and verify worker completion when the handle is dropped during unwinding.
notes: Added cfg(test) Drop for BlockingTestRelease. Regression catches an intentional panic after the worker enters, verifies unwind alone releases it, and includes an explicit rescue so the old implementation fails without hanging runtime shutdown. Removing release-on-drop produced the expected assertion failure. Log: /tmp/mini-agent-lsp-gate-control.log. Rich gate exercises existing grep, OAuth, worktree, runner, and skill-rebuild callers.
close_reason: BlockingTestRelease now releases on Drop, including unwinding. A deterministic native-worker regression with bounded rescue fails without this Drop. Its final lint-compatible setup passes directly; rich and LSP-only suites cover existing grep, OAuth, runner, worktree, and skill rebuild gates. Default/minimal/rich Clippy and debug install passed.

title: Drain LSP diagnostic publication workers before service shutdown completes
description: The LSP reader awaits raw spawn_blocking(store_diagnostics). supervise_child times out its reader drain and aborts the reader, then marks the client stopped. Give publication work service-owned lifetime tracking and test a paused publication across shutdown/replacement; keep it independent of per-turn AgentWorkScope ownership.

title: Set the current user as owner when creating Windows OAuth storage
description: Windows CI 34292067446 job 102280633231 fails OAuth setup at mcp_http_tests.rs:85 with credential prepare PermissionDenied. Set explicit creation owner, preserve foreign-owner rejection, retain native private-storage and real HTTP tests as validation; native CI required.

title: Track asynchronous MCP credential I/O through cancellation
description: FileCredentialStore load/save/clear use raw spawn_blocking. Dropping an OAuth initialization or other scoped credential future can therefore leave disk reads, migration, writes, or clears running after the agent reports cancellation. Register these operations through the existing agent work scope and verify that cancelled, dropped futures keep the scope non-idle until the native operation finishes. Exercise the real credential store for all three operations.

The test pauses each native operation, cancels and drops its caller, proves wait_idle is still pending, then releases the disk work and checks the exact retained credential state. No process-wide credential paths or user credentials are used by this test.

title: Finish MCP teardown before ACP terminal responses and session unlock
description: run_prompt owns a per-prompt MCP manager, but cancellation branches after build_agent_in_workspace or spawn_runner_paused_in_scope return without awaiting manager.shutdown. The running-turn path awaits manager.shutdown only after relay_paused_runner has sent its terminal response and released the owned history guard. MCP server processes can therefore outlive the reported completed/cancelled turn and overlap the next prompt. Move manager teardown into the terminal lifecycle before response and session unlock, preserving cleanup of tool peers and tracking cancellation races after successful MCP startup.
notes: Implemented one outer prompt completion boundary: MCP manager survives preparation and event relay, shuts down before generation settlement/history commit/terminal response/history unlock, and cancellation during cleanup preserves completed progress. Real stdio EOF-gated protocol matrix covers done, partial error, closed channel, preparation error/cancel, defensive compaction, and late cancellation. Moving shutdown after response fails with response preceded server exit. Full default/rich, ACP-only, native MCP feature tests, four Clippy rows and debug install passed locally; native CI confirmation remains pending.
close_reason: Verified native stdio step passed on Linux job 102280633118, macOS 102280633148, and Windows 102280633231 in CI 34292067446 at 5d51c41. This includes canonical cwd and MCP teardown before terminal response/session settlement. Windows HTTP OAuth setup failure is tracked separately as ropf.

title: Make the MCP OAuth timeout regression reach the network
description: The existing mcp_http_oauth_connect_to_silent_server_times_out only asserted the server name in the returned error. With no stored token it passed immediately on no OAuth token stored, never reaching the silent server or exercising the initialization timeout. The consolidated test exposed this false positive. Seed isolated fake stored credentials through the real credential store and assert an observed network request plus timeout/cancellation, without reading or modifying user credentials.
notes: The stronger test reproduced the old false positive: OAuth returned no OAuth token stored without reaching the listener. It now uses temporary process roots, verifies the credential/data roots stay inside that fixture, and seeds fake credentials through FileCredentialStore. Both OAuth cases prove actual received bytes; one requires the configured timeout and the other cancels only after a request reaches the server.
close_reason: Verified on the final source: full default suite 2214 unit plus 9 integration tests; rich suite 2999 unit plus 9 integration tests with the 22 usual isolated-test exclusions; 91 MCP tests in the native CI feature configuration; four Clippy rows and debug install passed. title: Honor ACP cancellation during MCP connection startup
description: In run_prompt, startup::connect_headless_mcp is awaited directly after history compaction and before run_owned_pre_run. TurnControl cancellation only signals the sandbox and attached runner; MCP connection startup has neither an attached runner nor a cancellation select. A cancelled or closed ACP prompt can therefore remain alive through MCP connection/initialization timeouts. Verify cancellation-safe teardown of partially connected handles and active subprocess handshakes, then make this pre-run stage observe TurnControl. Preserve process reaping before the session lock is released.
design: Use the existing AgentWorkScope cancellation signal during MCP connection startup, and await pending initialization teardown plus explicit shutdown of already-connected handles before returning Cancelled. The stdio adapter must expose completion of kill/reap after a dropped initialization future; generic future cancellation alone is insufficient because RMCP ChildWithCleanup currently starts an untracked Tokio task. Preserve graceful shutdown on successful connections and use forced cleanup for interrupted initialization.
notes: CI 34292067446 at 5d51c41: startup cancellation test passed on all three native stdio jobs, including Windows 102280633231. Linux/macOS HTTP matrix passed; Windows HTTP matrix could not prepare OAuth storage due to owner descriptor omission tracked by ropf. Keep final native HTTP confirmation pending that fix.
close_reason: CI 34293121475 at a196c6b passed all native MCP stdio and HTTP/OAuth lifecycle jobs: Windows 102285658343, Linux 102285658383, macOS 102285658449. Startup cancellation, owned child cleanup, and real OAuth/plain HTTP deadline-cancellation tests all passed; prerequisite Windows owner issue ropf is closed.

title: Finish ACP history compaction after a partial successful summary
description: SessionHistory::compact_with accepts a summary of only a complete oldest prefix, removes that prefix, and returns without checking the history bounds again. provider::compress_messages_with explicitly may return only a prefix after its multi-request budget. A partial success can therefore leave ACP history over 128 turns or 2 MiB, and run_prompt passes that oversized snapshot directly to the next model. Continue compaction while making verified whole-turn progress, carry the prior summary forward, and retain emergency handling for failed or zero-progress summaries. Extend existing compaction tests with partial progress and exact retained history.
notes: Reproduced a successful one-turn summary returning while needs_compaction remained true. compact_with now repeats only after verified whole-turn progress, carrying the bounded prior recap forward; failed or zero-progress summaries still use emergency eviction. One parameterized regression checks count and byte limits, every prior-summary handoff, and exact retained transcript. The normal whole-slice and failed/incomplete-summary tests remain for their distinct selection and fallback contracts.
close_reason: Delivered cancellable repeated history compaction and consolidated capability coverage. ACP tests passed in default (43), rich hooks/skills/LSP (47), and ACP-only (40) configurations; all four Clippy rows and debug cargo install passed. Both original compaction failures were reproduced before the fix; the retained wire test rejected a deliberately missing close advertisement.

title: Honor ACP cancellation while history summarization is pending
description: run_prompt awaits SessionHistory::compact_with directly before creating its AgentWorkScope or registering runner cancellation. Session cancel and close only signal TurnControl, so a hung summarizer can hold the session history lock until the provider compaction timeout (300 seconds), delaying cancellation and queued turns. Race compaction with the existing cancellation signal and preserve history if the pending summarizer is dropped; test a pending summarizer, cancellation completion, and subsequent history access.
notes: Reproduced pending-summary cancellation timing out at the regression outer deadline. compact_with now observes TurnControl directly, drops the pending provider future, and returns a cancellation outcome consumed as StopReason::Cancelled by run_prompt. Regression covers cancellation before any committed pass, after one successful pass, an already-cancelled retry, exact retained history, released history mutex, and successful later compaction.
close_reason: Delivered cancellable repeated history compaction and consolidated capability coverage. ACP tests passed in default (43), rich hooks/skills/LSP (47), and ACP-only (40) configurations; all four Clippy rows and debug cargo install passed. Both original compaction failures were reproduced before the fix; the retained wire test rejected a deliberately missing close advertisement.

title: Isolate embedding backend construction assertions from concurrent tests
description: Full concurrent skills suite at bbdf448 plus diagnostic changes failed a_proposal_enabled_bundle_initializes_one_embedding_backend while 2769 tests passed. The test subtracts two reads of a process-global BACKEND_CONSTRUCTIONS AtomicUsize, which also counts backends built by unrelated concurrent tests. Replace global counter-delta evidence with session-scoped factory/identity evidence that proves retrieval, telemetry and admission share one backend, and verify it rejects a real duplicate while tolerating unrelated construction. Log: /tmp/mini-agent-worker-reasons-full.log.
design: Count constructors per thread in test builds. start_components runs synchronously on one blocking worker, so the counter sees every actual constructor in startup while excluding unrelated test threads. The existing startup test now deliberately constructs an unrelated backend on another thread within the measured interval. A temporary second actual constructor in start_components must still fail the test.
notes: Reproduced deterministically: the old global counter reported 2 versus 1 when an unrelated thread constructed a backend. The thread-local counter passes that case. Negative control adding a second real Embedder::from_config to synchronous startup still failed 2 versus 1; the temporary mutation was removed. Full parallel skills suite passed 2770 unit and 9 integration tests, and the two CI-isolated groups passed another 22 unit tests. Thirteen intentional ignores remain.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: 2792 unit tests plus 9 integration tests passed, 13 intentional ignores; all four Clippy feature rows passed and debug cargo install succeeded. Closed-reason mapping and durable admission coverage retained; backend counter rejects actual duplicate startup while tolerating unrelated concurrent construction.

title: Preserve closed worker error classes in verification infrastructure failures
description: skills::verify::worker_error collapses ten distinct fieldless WorkerError variants into InfrastructureUnavailable("worker unavailable"), hiding containment, launch, transport, protocol, build, prompt timeout, unknown effect outcome, generation, identity-space and blocking-runtime causes. Native CI failures in mini-agent-enx3 therefore cannot be classified. Preserve each existing source-free WorkerError display reason while retaining infrastructure attribution and deferred admission. Extend the existing mapping test to distinguish the closed causes; do not expose exception or OS error data.
notes: The old mapping failed the new consolidated matrix at ContainmentUnavailable (observed worker unavailable, expected closed containment reason). The ten formerly collapsed variants now reuse fieldless WorkerError static Display messages; source attribution, queue handling, watchdog and cumulative CPU classification are unchanged. The matrix checks all ten reasons plus watchdog/native CPU. Three shallow mapper tests became one matrix; durable admission tests remain. Final targeted validation: 43 verification-semantics tests and 45 admission tests passed, 88 unique.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: 2792 unit tests plus 9 integration tests passed, 13 intentional ignores; all four Clippy feature rows passed and debug cargo install succeeded. Closed-reason mapping and durable admission coverage retained; backend counter rejects actual duplicate startup while tolerating unrelated concurrent construction.

title: Align LSP real-tool regression with Windows bound-edit refusal
description: lsp_process_diagnostics_reach_real_write_edit_and_query_tools requires every relative EditTool call to succeed on Windows. WorkspaceBinding::exchange_relative deliberately returns Unsupported on Windows to preserve the atomic expected-identity replacement contract; its native race test verifies refusal without mutation. Update the existing real-tool matrix to assert this exact refusal, unchanged file/diagnostic version, and successful later query, while retaining successful absolute edit coverage. Document the existing platform limitation instead of weakening compare-and-replace guarantees.
notes: Updated the existing real write/edit/query test: Windows relative edit must report the precise Unsupported compare-and-replace error, leave bytes as before and retain diagnostic version 1; a later query synchronizes version 2. Absolute edits and Linux/macOS relative edits retain their successful version 2 edit / version 3 query expectations. Operation and relative-path context now appear in assertion errors. CONFIG.md already documents the Windows bound-replacement refusal at the permission contract. Native Windows validation pending; all 21 local lifecycle tests passed.
close_reason: Verified natively on Windows CI run 34281928468 at bbdf448, job 102251552745: all 22 atomic-write tests and all 19 LSP lifecycle tests passed. This includes live-reader old/new content, delete-sharing locks, cancellation and parent-race checks, valid directory-bound creation, and the real write/edit/query matrix with exact Windows relative-edit refusal.

title: Fix Windows atomic edit publication failing in LSP tool regression
description: Native Windows CI run 34279862429 at 0788937, job 102243088739, now passes all fixture cleanup but lsp_process_diagnostics_reach_real_write_edit_and_query_tools fails after cleanup: ATOMIC_WRITE_FAILED=platform_publication and file tool must succeed: Msg("Access is denied. (os error 5)"). Eighteen other lifecycle tests pass. Diagnose the real WriteTool/EditTool publication path and retained file handles; preserve content identity/digest and atomic rollback contracts. Existing real-tool regression covers absolute and relative writes/edits and must pass natively. Log: /tmp/mini-agent-lsp-fixture-windows-verification.log.
notes: Code trace: LSP retains read-capable CheckedMetadata handles, and absolute EditTool also keeps its reader alive through publication. Windows FileRenameInformation rejects an open replacement target even with delete sharing. Microsoft FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION documentation specifies FileRenameInformationEx plus FILE_RENAME_REPLACE_IF_EXISTS|FILE_RENAME_POSIX_SEMANTICS to retain existing readers. Implemented that class/flags for replacement only; create-only retains FileRenameInformation. Preserved directory-relative publication, cancellation, bounded lock retry and all identity/content checks. Extended the existing Windows metadata test with a live reader that must keep old bytes while new opens see the replacement. Removed overlapping source-string assertions; added full atomic_write_tests to the native Windows LSP CI job. Native confirmation pending. Local 20 atomic tests, 21 lifecycle tests, 29 workflow tests, four Clippy rows passed.
close_reason: Verified natively on Windows CI run 34281928468 at bbdf448, job 102251552745: all 22 atomic-write tests and all 19 LSP lifecycle tests passed. This includes live-reader old/new content, delete-sharing locks, cancellation and parent-race checks, valid directory-bound creation, and the real write/edit/query matrix with exact Windows relative-edit refusal.

title: Skip disabled retrieval channels before index work
description: ImmutableSkillIndex::dense_candidates still calls HNSW when dense_candidate_limit is zero, because candidate_count has ANN_MIN_CANDIDATES as a floor and truncation to zero happens only after search. The default nonsemantic backend disables dense retrieval by setting this limit to zero, so ANN-sized libraries still perform unnecessary dense search. lexical_candidates likewise locks SQLite and derives FTS terms before executing LIMIT 0. Return before channel work when its budget is zero and prove disabled channels do no index work using behavior/operation evidence rather than timing.
notes: Reproduced in the existing 2,000-revision smoke audit: with both channels disabled, exact snapshot still entered SQLite once; ANN snapshot entered SQLite and HNSW once. Added early exits before ANN/SQLite access. Test-only counters are scoped to each immutable snapshot and its clones, recording actual ANN calls, exact rows evaluated, and lexical entry. Existing audit covers both-disabled exact/ANN snapshots, lexical-only, and dense-only paths without new corpus fixtures. Red log: /tmp/mini-agent-retrieval-work-red.log; green and final retrieval suite passed.
close_reason: Delivered disabled-channel early exits and deterministic smoke operation checks, retaining dedicated full performance gates. Existing benchmark reproduced disabled work before the fix; full-scan negative control fails and inflated-timing control passes with an honest informational verdict. Final 21 index/retrieval tests, four Clippy configurations, cargo fmt and debug install passed.

title: Release LSP fixture workspace bindings before Windows cleanup
description: CI run 34272157777 failed six Windows LSP lifecycle tests with sharing violation 32 during FixtureBuild::cleanup. Several tests still hold LspClient objects whose WorkspaceBinding deliberately denies directory deletion after process shutdown. The cancelled-initialization test has no client owner, but synchronous cleanup sleeps on its current-thread Tokio runtime, preventing asynchronous supervisor/reader cleanup from releasing the binding. Drop retained clients/managers before cleanup and make bounded cleanup retries yield to async teardown. Preserve workspace pinning and process-reap assertions; verify through the existing lifecycle suite.
notes: Implemented: all fixture removals are async; bounded Windows sharing-violation retries yield to supervisor/reader teardown. Direct clients and file-tool/manager owners are dropped before cleanup. Extended the existing cancelled-initialization test on Windows with a binding released by a queued task, proving cleanup must yield without adding a duplicate process fixture. Existing process-reap assertions remain. Local validation: 21 lifecycle tests passed with no-default-features,lsp and normal parallelism; 27 inventory tests; four Clippy configurations. Native Windows confirmation pending CI. Additional pre-fix run 34276575396 at 7706ca8 failed seven Windows lifecycle tests, all at the same cleanup sharing violation; logs saved at /tmp/mini-agent-lsp-windows-current-ci.log.
close_reason: Native Windows CI run 34279862429 / job 102243088739 confirms all fixture cleanup succeeds, including cancelled initialization and queued binding release; 18 lifecycle tests pass. The sole remaining real-tool test now reaches its later result assertion and exposes a separate atomic-publication access-denied failure, filed independently. Local lifecycle/inventory tests and four Clippy rows passed; debug install passed.

title: Latch LSP transport failure before queued writers can resume
description: TransportWriteGuard signals asynchronous shutdown, while LspClient::is_stopped becomes true only after process termination and protocol-task drain. When a write fails, times out or is cancelled, releasing stdin can wake another queued writer before shutdown is observed; that writer can advance document state or attempt another frame on an already-invalid transport. Introduce a shared terminal/closing latch at the writer boundary and test queued callers against cancellation/failure before cleanup finishes. Preserve stopped as the completed-reap signal if needed.
notes: Expanded the existing cancellation regression with a pause before reaping. The old transport allowed a queued document to advance while the failed server was still alive. TransportWriteGuard now owns stdin and latches a shared terminal flag in Drop before releasing it; queued document writes, requests and server replies all consult that flag. Reader/protocol/explicit shutdown paths mark the same state, while stopped remains the completed-reap signal. The manager refuses closing clients and awaits cleanup before its existing failure cooldown. The real-process regression also verifies no post-failure request is sent, pending requests are cleared, and manager acquisition waits for cleanup.
close_reason: Delivered LSP closing latch before writer unlock, manager cleanup-before-reuse, and per-client test deadlines. Regression tests reproduced both prior failures; final validation passed 70 LSP tests, 27 subprocess inventory tests, four Clippy feature configurations, cargo fmt, and debug cargo install with skills,lsp.

title: Serialize LSP document versions with transport publication
description: LspClient::sync_document advances the per-document version and releases the open-map mutex before JSON serialization and acquisition of the separate stdin mutex. Concurrent callers on different executor threads can therefore assign didOpen version 1 and didChange version 2 in that order but write didChange before didOpen, especially while the first caller serializes a large document. The parent then tracks a newer version than the server accepted. Bind version advancement and notification order to one serialization boundary; reproduce the interleaving with the real process fixture rather than adding retries or widening timeouts.
notes: The deterministic real-process regression reproduced didChange version 2 arriving before didOpen version 1. A per-client test probe pauses after version advancement, allowing a second caller to overtake the old implementation without timing assumptions. Synchronization now acquires stdin before content revalidation and state advancement, retains it through encoding and frame write, and applies one deadline to queue plus publication. The matrix also rewrites queued content and proves rejection consumes no version and preserves subsequent sync. A cancellation regression proves abandoning advanced-but-unpublished state reaps the server before reuse. All 69 LSP tests pass, including existing full-pipe and queued-writer deadline coverage.
close_reason: Serialized queued content validation, document version advancement and frame publication under the stdin lock and one deadline. The real-process regression reproduced didChange 2 before didOpen 1 on the old code, then passed with ordered frames and stale-queued-content rejection without version loss. Cancellation reaps the server before reuse. Validation: 69 LSP tests, 27 inventory checks, four Clippy configurations, and debug install passed.

title: Retire the unused LSP aggregate formatter and test the real query path
description: LspManager::all_diagnostics_block and all_diagnostics_block_inner have no production callers; LspTool aggregates through candidate binding, permission checks, snapshot_bound_diagnostics and all_diagnostics_block_for_snapshots. Several tests still exercise the unused formatter, including a fabricated /tmp/x.rs entry with no real file identity. Migrate those assertions to actual LspTool project queries with real temporary files, then remove the duplicate formatter instead of keeping a test-only implementation.
notes: Removed all_diagnostics_block and its duplicate all_diagnostics_block_inner formatter. Versionless publication/clear assertions now call the real LspTool project-query path. The clean-project test now uses a real temporary file, validated publication and the production query instead of a fabricated /tmp/x.rs cache fixture. The affected LSP suite passes after this migration.
close_reason: Implemented digest-based LSP content freshness, cursor-independent and strictly bounded digest reads, and migration of duplicate aggregate tests to real project queries. Regression tests reproduced stale delayed/cached results and both digest bugs; the concurrent snapshot guard also has a failing negative control. Validation totals 2279 unit tests and 9 integration tests across the full run and focused reruns, plus four Clippy configurations and debug install. Native Windows helper execution remains for CI.

title: Preserve shared file cursors when validating content digests
description: ContentDigest::matches_file documents that it leaves the caller cursor unchanged, but it clones a File and seeks/reads the clone. Duplicated file handles share the underlying offset, so the caller cursor moves and concurrent digest checks can interfere. Use positional reads and verify both a nonzero caller offset and concurrent checks on cloned handles.
notes: Regression reproduced the caller offset changing from 7 to 131072 after a digest check. Unix validation now uses positional read_at; Windows uses ReOpenFile on the retained object because std FileExt::seek_read also changes the shared cursor. The same regression includes four concurrent readers and verifies the caller cursor remains unchanged. Windows API behavior was checked against local Rust source and Microsoft documentation; native Windows execution awaits CI.
close_reason: Implemented digest-based LSP content freshness, cursor-independent and strictly bounded digest reads, and migration of duplicate aggregate tests to real project queries. Regression tests reproduced stale delayed/cached results and both digest bugs; the concurrent snapshot guard also has a failing negative control. Validation totals 2279 unit tests and 9 integration tests across the full run and focused reruns, plus four Clippy configurations and debug install. Native Windows helper execution remains for CI.

title: Invalidate LSP diagnostics after in-place source rewrites
description: The LSP synchronized and cached file checks compare stable file identity only. An external writer can truncate and rewrite the same inode after synchronization; a delayed matching-version reply and existing cached diagnostics still pass identity validation despite referring to different text. Extend freshness attribution to synchronized content or an appropriate change fingerprint, test same-inode rewrites through the real delayed process fixture, and account for the cost of validating content.
notes: Expanded the existing delayed-publication and real-tool process tests to rewrite files without changing inode, length or mtime. Both delayed insertion and cached single-file output failed on the old code. Documents now carry SHA-256 digests from the exact authorized read; sync, incoming publications and explicit/aggregate cached reads validate bounded content on blocking workers without holding document/cache mutexes. Project content reads follow per-file authorization. Version checks are repeated before commit/snapshot after I/O. Added one deterministic queued-worker regression proving a concurrent publication invalidates the old bound snapshot; removing that recheck fails the new test. Shared digest fixes are tracked separately in a4ge and ueia.
close_reason: Implemented digest-based LSP content freshness, cursor-independent and strictly bounded digest reads, and migration of duplicate aggregate tests to real project queries. Regression tests reproduced stale delayed/cached results and both digest bugs; the concurrent snapshot guard also has a failing negative control. Validation totals 2279 unit tests and 9 integration tests across the full run and focused reruns, plus four Clippy configurations and debug install. Native Windows helper execution remains for CI.

title: skill_retrieval_benchmark_smoke wall-clock p99 gate flakes on loaded CI runners
description:
extras::js::tests::skill_retrieval_benchmark::skill_retrieval_benchmark_smoke asserts a wall-clock p99 bound of 50ms. On run 34266586217 (1a43f128), macos --features skills, it measured p50 55183us / p95 64230us / p99 64230us and failed with 'smoke retrieval p99 regressed above 50ms: 64230.0us'.

The same job took 316.73s against roughly 242s for that row when green, and a second test in the same job failed with a macOS worker launch error (mini-agent-enx3), so the runner was starved rather than the retrieval path regressing.

A hard wall-clock bound on a shared CI runner will keep flaking regardless of code quality. The same problem was hit on 2026-09-08 in the skill statistics work: a wall-clock scaling assertion failed on macOS at 9.7x against an 8x bound and was replaced with a deterministic EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN assertion that checks no CORRELATED node has a SCAN child. That is the pattern to follow -- assert the algorithmic property that the benchmark is really defending (index use, absence of a full scan, bounded comparisons) rather than elapsed microseconds. Keep the timing measurement as reported output for the benchmark record, just do not gate CI on it.
notes: Replaced smoke p99 and build/rebuild elapsed-time assertions with operation checks in the existing benchmark; retained dedicated 100k performance gates, recall, deterministic ordering, visibility and zero-result checks. Removed duplicate rebuild-recall assertion. JSON now reports search_work and gate.enforced so an informational failed timing verdict is not disguised. Negative control replacing ANN with exact full scan fails hybrid-path assertion. A separate temporary control adding 1s to measured searches and 60s to builds passes smoke with gate.passed=false and gate.enforced=false. All mutations restored. Final validation: 18 index tests plus 3 retrieval tests (1 dedicated full audit ignored); four Clippy feature configurations passed.
close_reason: Delivered disabled-channel early exits and deterministic smoke operation checks, retaining dedicated full performance gates. Existing benchmark reproduced disabled work before the fix; full-scan negative control fails and inflated-timing control passes with an honest informational verdict. Final 21 index/retrieval tests, four Clippy configurations, cargo fmt and debug install passed.

title: Bound LSP synchronized document state and retained file handles
description: LspClient.open grows for every distinct synchronized URI with no ceiling or eviction. Retaining authorized source identities for mini-agent-ymdj would additionally keep one file handle per entry. Bound synchronized document state consistently with the existing 128-file diagnostic cache contract, keep updates to already-tracked documents working at capacity, and verify the boundary through the process fixture.
notes: Bound synchronized documents to the existing per-server 128-file ceiling; already-tracked documents can still advance and replace their retained identity at capacity. The real process regression synchronizes 129 distinct files, verifies exactly 128 didOpen frames, then replaces and resynchronizes the first file with didChange version 2. Removing the cap makes the new-document rejection assertion fail. CONFIG.md documents the ceiling and restart behavior.
close_reason: Implemented authorized read-handle identity attribution through synchronization and diagnostic storage, plus a 128-document per-server ceiling that preserves tracked-file updates. Extended the existing rejected-document test and added real delayed-publication and capacity regressions. All 66 LSP tests, four Clippy feature configurations, and debug install passed; negative controls failed as expected.

title: Bind delayed LSP publications to the file identity synchronized with the server
description: SyncedDocument retains a version but no source file identity. store_diagnostics captures checked metadata from the current pathname when a message arrives. If an external writer atomically replaces a file after didOpen/didChange but before the server publishes that version, the old-text diagnostics are tagged with the replacement inode and survive diagnostic_identity_is_current. Retain the authorized synchronized file identity and reject publication for a changed file; reproduce through a delayed publish in the real process fixture, not only pre-injected cache entries.
notes: Reproduced the race through delayed stdio publishDiagnostics: the old code attached a version-1 reply to the replacement inode and created a cache entry. Reads now construct a Document containing bounded text and CheckedMetadata from the same authorized handle; sync validates that identity before advancing state, and publication validates against it before committing a shared identity into the cache. The real-process matrix covers absolute/relative sync, delayed didOpen/didChange, a protocol barrier proving the stale reply was processed, and successful resync of the replacement. Extended the existing rejected-document process test to cover replacement between read and sync; removing that guard makes the regression fail. All 66 LSP tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented authorized read-handle identity attribution through synchronization and diagnostic storage, plus a 128-document per-server ceiling that preserves tracked-file updates. Extended the existing rejected-document test and added real delayed-publication and capacity regressions. All 66 LSP tests, four Clippy feature configurations, and debug install passed; negative controls failed as expected.

title: Bound LSP document reads before allocating the full file
description: LspManager::notify_changed and notify_changed_relative read_to_string the entire authorized file before LspClient::sync_text applies its 4 MiB MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES limit. An explicit LSP query on a very large file can therefore allocate unbounded parent memory even though synchronization is eventually rejected; read_stable_text/sync_file has the same shape. Read through a limit+1 bound on the already-authorized handle and retain no-sync/no-version-change behavior for oversized inputs. Extend the existing oversized-document coverage to verify the read boundary.
notes: All LSP file readers now use one asynchronous limit+1 reader on the authorized handle. Boundary matrix covers limit-1, limit, limit+1, 2x limit and exact-limit UTF-8. Negative control removing the cap consumed 8388608 bytes rather than at most 4194305 and failed the regression. Existing process test still verifies oversized input does not advance sync state.
close_reason: Implemented LSP publication baseline propagation, retained-workspace URI translation, bounded asynchronous document reads, real process/tool regression coverage, and corrected cache-limit documentation. Full tests, targeted regression, required Clippy configurations, and debug install passed.

title: Verify LSP diagnostics end to end through the process fixture
description: The LSP process fixture verifies initialization and synchronization but never sends publishDiagnostics. Diagnostic tests inject directly into the parent cache, so they do not exercise wire-root/parent-path translation or real document-version attribution. Extend the existing fixture to publish versioned diagnostics for didOpen/didChange and use it to cover absolute and workspace-relative queries/edits, early publication and stale/outside-workspace rejection without duplicating cache-only formatting tests.
notes: The real stdio fixture now sends outside-workspace, stale-version, and matching-version publications. The four-case absolute/relative and descriptor/canonical matrix proves only the expected URI reaches the cache and early replies complete immediately. Real write/edit/query tools and URI/read boundary tests also pass. Validation: 2274 unit tests and 9 integration tests passed, 8 ignored; final outside-publication regression passed after extension. Debug install succeeded; four Clippy feature configurations passed before final test extension, with affected configurations rerun before commit.
close_reason: Implemented LSP publication baseline propagation, retained-workspace URI translation, bounded asynchronous document reads, real process/tool regression coverage, and corrected cache-limit documentation. Full tests, targeted regression, required Clippy configurations, and debug install passed.

title: Capture LSP diagnostic baseline before synchronizing edits and explicit queries
description: EditTool, WriteTool and explicit LspTool synchronize a document before diagnostics_block snapshots its publish counter. A fast server can publish during synchronization, then the waiter treats that fresh publication as its baseline and waits the full 1s edit/2s query timeout for an unnecessary second publication. Capture the baseline before synchronization and preserve the bounded wait plus file-identity and version checks across ambient and workspace-bound paths.
notes: The baseline is captured inside LspClient while advancing the synchronized document version, under the same open-then-diags lock order as the reader, and propagated through edit/write/query waits. Sampling before the whole sync would risk accepting a prior-version publication. Negative control ignoring the captured baseline fails the real-publication regression with Elapsed even though the cache already contains the answer.
close_reason: Implemented LSP publication baseline propagation, retained-workspace URI translation, bounded asynchronous document reads, real process/tool regression coverage, and corrected cache-limit documentation. Full tests, targeted regression, required Clippy configurations, and debug install passed.

title: Assert real PlanWrite permission decisions after failed workspace rebind
description: The failed worktree rebind regression uses plan_write_authorization, a wrapper with no production callers, to assert the original workspace remains authorized and the replacement is not. Exercise the actual permission-checking entry point for both paths and delete the unused wrapper so rollback coverage follows the policy used by tools.
close_reason: The failed workspace-rebind regression now asserts Allowed for the original PLAN.md and Denied for the replacement workspace through PermissionChecker::check_path. Removed the unused plan_write_authorization wrapper. Passed 300 related tests, 27 subprocess inventory checks, default/LSP/minimal Clippy rows and debug install.

title: Exercise active edit publication in the LSP replacement-identity regression
description: The LSP atomic-edit regression calls atomic_write_resolved_checked and claims it is EditTool’s primitive, but production edits now require expected ContentDigest via atomic_write_resolved_expecting. The old unchecked-content wrapper has no production callers. Move this regression to the current publication path (prefer the real EditTool flow where practical) and remove the obsolete wrapper while preserving replacement-identity diagnostic coverage.
close_reason: The LSP replacement-identity regression now performs an actual EditTool SEARCH/REPLACE edit and verifies the written content before checking stale/fresh diagnostics. Removed atomic_write_resolved_checked, whose only caller was that test. Passed 300 LSP/edit/atomic-write/permission/worktree tests, 27 inventory tests, three Clippy configurations and skills debug install.

title: Repair subprocess inventory drift from subagent output-budget test changes
description: The full default+skills suite fails both subprocess inventory gates on unchanged task_tool.rs test fixtures. The line inventory counts a sixth output: Ok("must not start".into()) field; macro-context classification has stale or missing vec! fingerprints after output-budget test edits. Determine whether the scanner can exclude test fixture field false positives safely; preserve detection of genuine process calls and update the reviewed inventory and its coverage.
notes: The scanner deliberately treats terminal-like identifiers in opaque macro bodies conservatively; excluding output fields globally would weaken macro coverage. Reviewed all three changed vec! fixtures, added their exact NON-PROCESS field and content-addressed macro entries, and updated the must-not-start occurrence count from 5 to 6. All 27 subprocess-inventory tests now pass; no scanner logic was relaxed.
close_reason: Reviewed and classified the three new FakeStep vec! contexts and their response fields, and corrected the sixth must-not-start field occurrence. Preserved conservative macro scanning and content-addressed exemptions. All 27 inventory checks pass, including both failures from the full suite; four Clippy configurations also pass.

title: Exercise telemetry contention and shutdown with production timeout behavior
description: Current telemetry shutdown tests replace production busy_timeout with 1ms, masking long blocking attempts and queued-tail delays. The test named telemetry_shutdown_still_flushes_a_transiently_busy_batch never holds a writer lock. Replace the timeout shortcut with production configuration, use bounded watchdog/release logic for failure cases, and consolidate shared fixture setup while retaining distinct retry, permanent-lock, and transient-shutdown assertions.
notes: Replaced three contention/shutdown tests with production-configuration matrices for both command types, a 64-command locked queue tail, and real transient shutdown contention plus uncontended drain. Reused the existing skill fixture and removed the timeout-override constructor. Test count unchanged; current test diff removes duplicated setup. Full suite validation underway.
close_reason: Replaced three weak contention/shutdown tests with production-configuration matrices covering both command types, real writer contention during shutdown, and a 64-command queue tail. Removed the busy-timeout override constructor and duplicated fixture setup; retained FIFO attribution and ordinary-store WAL/timeout assertions. Same test count, 29 fewer test-source lines. Both bug regressions failed before the fix and pass afterward.

title: Bound telemetry queue shutdown independently of SQLite busy_timeout
description: The production telemetry connection inherits the store five-second busy_timeout. ingest_retrying_busy checks shutdown only after a failed SQLite attempt; queued commands each attempt ingestion again after the shared 1.5-second flush deadline. A locked database can therefore delay teardown by five seconds per queued item. Use application-owned busy retries on the worker connection and check the shared deadline before starting each attempt; count discarded evidence.
notes: Regression reproduced: dropping a dispatcher with 64 mixed queued commands failed the two-second watchdog while the writer remained locked, despite a 200ms shutdown budget. Worker connection now uses busy_timeout=0 and application retries check one shared deadline before every attempt. Revised test verifies completion while still locked, all 64 losses counted and no persisted rows.
close_reason: Disabled native SQLite busy waiting only on the telemetry worker connection and check one shared shutdown deadline before every ingestion attempt. A locked 64-command mixed queue now exits within the watchdog while the writer remains locked, records all 64 losses, and persists no rows. Transient contention still drains successfully. Full/isolated coverage, four Clippy rows and debug install passed.

title: Retry task-outcome telemetry on transient SQLite writer contention
description: TelemetryDispatcher retries busy SQLite failures for EventBatch, but TaskOutcome commands call ingest_task_outcome once and discard the evidence on any error. A short-lived competing writer therefore loses verification/oracle outcomes despite queue admission. Route both command types through the bounded-on-shutdown busy retry policy and preserve FIFO attribution.
notes: Regression reproduced with the production dispatcher configuration: a held SQLite writer caused task_outcome=true to increment observability_lost to 1 and discard the admitted outcome. Both command types now use the same FIFO busy-retry helper; targeted telemetry/retention suite passes.
close_reason: Task outcomes now share event ingestion’s capped busy retry policy and FIFO worker ordering. Production-configuration regression reproduced the previous lost outcome, then passed with the fix. Completed unit coverage across full, isolated and corrected-inventory runs (2795 passing, 13 ignored), 9 integration tests, four Clippy configurations and debug install.

title: Drain TUI MCP notices after every prebuild and rebuild path
description: Only UiApp::take_prebuild(notify=true) drains MCP notices. resolve_prebuild used by early prompt submission, reconnect/model/config rebuilds, and fallback prebuild adoption bypass it. Move notice draining to a common event-loop point so startup timing does not hide catalog failures and accumulated notices do not remain until a later unrelated rebuild.
close_reason: TUI notice draining now runs at the common event-loop entry instead of one notify=true prebuild branch. Removed the obsolete notify flag and infallible adoption Result. Installed-binary tmux smoke with delayed MCP tools/list verifies early prompt submission receives the notice and /toggle todo rebuilding emits a new notice without replaying old ones. Passed 91 MCP tests, 12 UI tests, three Clippy configurations and debug install.

title: Emit headless MCP catalog notices after agent construction
description: connect_headless_mcp prints only initial manager.notices before tools/list runs. dispatch_print and dispatch_loop never drain the tool notice queue after building the agent, so list failures, alias changes and reserved-name omissions are hidden. Emit and drain notices after construction on stderr, preserve stdout output formats, and test late notices and one-time delivery.
close_reason: Headless connection notices are drained immediately, and dispatch_print/dispatch_loop drain new catalog notices after agent construction through a sanitized stderr sink. Regression verifies late notices and one-time delivery. Installed-binary smoke confirms valid JSON-only stdout plus exactly one stderr omission notice, and loop-max=0 confirms loop delivery without a model turn.

title: Make MCP name-allocation tests prove normalization and original wire identity
description: The provider-limit test only exercises duplicate names and misses the unique-name fast path. The determinism test compares allocate(entries) to itself without an expected mapping. The stdio fixture answers tools/call regardless of the requested name, so routing tests cannot detect accidentally sending a normalized alias instead of the original wire name. Strengthen the existing tests and fixture rather than adding overlapping helper-only coverage.
close_reason: Replaced the self-comparison allocation test with an exact collision mapping, expanded the provider-limit matrix, and upgraded the existing stdio test to assert original permission identity plus the actual tools/call request for valid, dotted, Unicode, quoted and long names. Negative control sending registered aliases failed on the wire-name assertion. Test count unchanged. Passed 90 MCP tests, 12 minimal-feature manager tests, three Clippy rows and debug install.

title: Expose omitted MCP built-in name collisions in operator notices
description: Agent builder skips MCP tools whose registered name is reserved by a built-in, but reports this only through tracing::warn with no tool/server identity. McpClientManager already accumulates operator notices for catalog failures and renames; the omission should be surfaced there so users can identify why a connected server tool is missing without reading tracing logs.
close_reason: The production builder now collects MCP tools through a shared filtering path that records each reserved-name omission with tool and server identity. Regression exercises real stdio catalogs and confirms only the non-reserved tool is retained.

title: Normalize unique MCP tool names before provider registration
description: allocate_registered_tool_names reserves every unique bare name unchanged, bypassing the sanitizer used for generated collision names. A unique empty, non-ASCII, punctuation-containing, or over-64-byte tool name can invalidate the provider tool schema. Preserve valid unique names first, normalize all other aliases against the same used-name set, keep original wire and permission identity, and report renames accurately.
close_reason: Unique bare names now stay unchanged only when they satisfy the provider identifier rules. All other aliases use the existing collision-safe sanitizer after valid names are reserved; notices describe normalization as well as collisions. Expanded provider-limit tests reproduced failures for unique overlong and punctuation names before the fix.

title: Replace obsolete compaction-gate tests with active pruning-aware boundary coverage
description: Session::needs_compaction and needs_compaction_with_pending have no production callers; active TUI/headless paths use pruning-aware gates. title: Keep multiline subagent prompts inside one result heading
description: TaskReport renders the first 60 prompt characters directly in Markdown task headings. title: Count subagent report framing and quoting before scheduling more work
description: execute_tasks charges raw success response length plus section_overhead_bytes, but TaskReport::render_with_notice adds per-line quotation prefixes and begin/end markers. A newline-heavy response can exhaust the rendered aggregate budget while scheduler accounting still permits queued children to start; final truncation then hides their work. Reproduce through execute_tasks and enforce the bound using the rendered representation, preserving cancellation and cost accounting.
close_reason: Reproduced with a 320-byte newline-heavy response exceeding a 512-byte rendered budget while a queued child still started. Scheduler now shares outcome/heading rendering with TaskReport and charges the specialist notice before admission. Added exact-boundary and notice-exhaustion coverage; preserved cancellation and usage accounting.

title: Publish skill-service retry metadata before making initialization visible
description: WorkspaceServiceCache publishes its OnceCell result before it updates failure/backoff metadata. A concurrent caller can observe a newly degraded result with no backoff and immediately start another initialization, bypassing throttling. Compute and commit matching-cell metadata inside the initializer before OnceCell wakes its waiters.
acceptance_criteria: A second caller joins a paused initial degraded completion instead of starting a replacement before backoff is published. Use a deterministic scheduling regression; existing concurrent callers still share one initializer.
notes:
Deterministic regression pauses the first degradation callback and polls a second resolve exactly once. Original code returned a replacement before the first callback could publish backoff; fixed code keeps the second caller pending and shares the first result. Metadata is committed inside get_or_init before the cached result is published. Fixture runs its paused initializer on Tokio blocking pool so optional multithread-runtime support is not required.
Final verification passed: affected hooks/js/subagents/skills/sandbox row 2576 unit tests plus 8 integrations, all 21 runtime-binding tests in fresh invocations, isolated library-axis harness, all nine Clippy feature rows, cargo fmt, diff check and debug installation. Initial focused suite had exactly the three new regression failures; the fixed suite passed 19/19. The concurrency fixture was adapted to the blocking pool after a no-default feature check exposed that multithread Tokio is optional.
close_reason: Fixed with deterministic regressions; full affected row, isolated tests, all Clippy rows and debug installation passed.

title: Count each completed skill-service initialization exactly once
description: WorkspaceServiceCache increments attempts before retrying a degraded bundle and again when that retry fails, but does not count the initial degraded result. Permanent degraded startup therefore allows five calls with a four-attempt budget, and mixed results produce inconsistent diagnostics and backoff. Existing degraded test only asserts an upper bound of budget plus one.
acceptance_criteria: Outright failure, degraded success and mixed sequences have exactly one charge per completed initialization, stop at the four-attempt budget, and report accurate attempt counts. Consolidate the two overlapping permanent-budget tests into one outcome matrix.
notes:
Consolidated the two permanent-budget tests into one matrix: all failures, all degraded successes, and both mixed orderings. Every completed call must equal the reported count, and exactly SERVICE_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS calls are allowed. The old code failed on its initial degraded result (reported 0 for one completed call). All completion types now increment once inside the initializer.
Final verification passed: affected hooks/js/subagents/skills/sandbox row 2576 unit tests plus 8 integrations, all 21 runtime-binding tests in fresh invocations, isolated library-axis harness, all nine Clippy feature rows, cargo fmt, diff check and debug installation. title: Ignore stale skill-service initialization results after workspace rebinding
description: WorkspaceServiceCache::resolve updates attempts, backoff and failure after initialization using only root equality. If initialization for A is still pending while the owner switches A to B to A, the old result overwrites the new A slot: a stale failure marks healthy services degraded, and stale success clears a current failure.
acceptance_criteria: Delayed error, degraded success and healthy success from a superseded A initialization do not alter the new A slot after an A-B-A switch. Completion bookkeeping is tied to the exact initialization cell.
notes:
Deterministic regression holds an old A initialization with a oneshot, resolves B and a replacement A, then releases the old result. Error, degraded-success and healthy-success cases originally changed the replacement failure record. Completion now checks both the root and Arc identity of the exact OnceCell before updating bookkeeping.

title: Preserve exact database paths in shared coordinator cache keys
description: shared_coordinator formats learned_skills_db().display() into a String key. On Unix, distinct paths with non-UTF-8 bytes can have the same lossy display text, including a valid replacement-character path. With a live coordinator at the first path, lookup of the second path returns the first database coordinator before attempting to open the requested database. Use an exact PathBuf plus structured embedding metadata key.
acceptance_criteria: A regression holds a coordinator for a valid replacement-character path and requests a byte-distinct path with identical display text; lookup must open its own coordinator or return that path open error, never reuse the first. Cache key equality preserves path bytes and separate metadata fields.
notes:
Reproduced on macOS with a valid data-U+FFFD directory and a byte-distinct data-0xFF path whose display text matches: old lookup returned the exact same coordinator before opening the requested path. Replaced delimiter-joined display strings with (PathBuf, ModelMetadata) keys and derived Hash for immutable model metadata. Regression passes after the fix; it covers Unix bytes and a Windows unpaired-surrogate fixture, accepting only a distinct coordinator or a filesystem/SQLite rejection of the invalid path.
Final validation passed: full hooks/js/subagents/skills/sandbox row 2575 unit tests plus 8 integrations (CI exclusions retained); all 21 runtime-binding tests in fresh invocations; isolated library-axis harness; all nine Clippy feature rows; cargo fmt; git diff --check; debug installation with default+skills. close_reason: Fixed and regression-verified; complete feature-row tests, isolated skill tests, all Clippy rows and debug installation pass.

title: Release learned-skill coordinators when their session owners disappear
description: The process-wide COORDINATORS registry in skills/turn.rs stores strong Arc values and never evicts them. Each IndexCoordinator owns an open SkillStore connection, embedder and published index, so every workspace/backend visited remains alive after all session services are dropped. This defeats session teardown and accumulates database handles and index memory.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent/live owners of one database/backend share a coordinator; dropping the last owner releases it. Reopening creates a fresh coordinator and reports initialization required. Registry entries use weak ownership and expired keys are pruned. A regression fails with the original strong registry.
notes:
Reproduced with a real coordinator/store: after both owner Arcs were dropped, the old global strong registry still kept the Weak lifetime probe upgradeable. Converted registry values to Weak, pruned expired entries on lookup, preserved sharing for live owners and fresh initialization after teardown. The regression also verifies expired entries from a different workspace are removed. Owning Phase 3 spec documents lifetime behavior.
Final validation passed: full hooks/js/subagents/skills/sandbox row 2575 unit tests plus 8 integrations (CI exclusions retained); all 21 runtime-binding tests in fresh invocations; isolated library-axis harness; all nine Clippy feature rows; cargo fmt; git diff --check; debug installation with default+skills. title: Avoid blocking headless loop startup on nonterminal stdin
