title: Overlap the macOS one-time image byte proof with worker process start
description:
Follow-up to mini-agent-wldr.19. The sealed one-time image's SHA-256 proof runs serially before the worker is spawned and costs ~365 ms of a ~835 ms cold start on macOS 26 (docs/benchmarks/2026-09-08-macos-worker-cold-start.md).

Overlap it with process start: seal and exec first, then complete the byte proof before Ready is authenticated, so no work is ever dispatched to an unverified image. This must preserve one-time executable identity, every containment check, parent-death cleanup, zero idle runtimes and one live worker, and must kill the child on a mismatch before any effect can run.

Requires matched-host before/after measurements on a supported macOS runner and a re-run of the macOS production-binary denial/guardian/one-time-image matrices.
close_reason: Implemented sealed-image proof/startup overlap with a pending guardian guard; proof completes before protocol pipes reach the supervisor. Fault-stage ordering, real-child digest mismatch cleanup, spawn failure, and missing-pipe cleanup are covered. Passed 240 worker unit tests, 7 bootstrap integration tests, 27 inventory tests, three Clippy rows, both debug installs, and the exact final production-binary macOS containment matrix. Matched-host 10-warmup/100-sample reports committed under docs/benchmarks: cold Ready p95 1073.517 to 1061.325 ms; recovery 1057.204 to 1055.913 ms. Both 1000 ms targets remain unmet; the small observed change is below the 15% repeat-run tolerance. Corrected the earlier 365 ms projection because Ready-time rehash remains serialized.

title: Skill statistics repeatedly scan task baselines and approach cubic work as history grows
description:
## Problem

For every retained revision, load_skill_stats separately counts baseline tasks and baseline passes by scanning all task outcomes and running another correlated observed-skill/source match for each baseline. A hermetic probe extracts the exact production SQL and uses a reduced SQLite schema with the relevant production indexes. With one observed task and one no-library baseline per revision under a shared oracle, 20/40/80 revisions executed approximately 177,700 / 1,215,400 / 8,942,800 VM steps: doubling data multiplied work 6.84x then 7.36x. EXPLAIN shows a baseline scan inside a correlated subquery and a further source-index search inside it. This measurement used local SQLite 3.53.2 rather than the Rust-bundled build; measured times were 3/21/174 ms and are illustrative only. An initial larger run was explicitly interrupted and is not used as completed evidence.

## Where

src/extras/js/skills/operations.rs:268-344 (load_skill_stats baseline subqueries); src/extras/js/skills/store.rs:3707-3710 (task-outcome indexes)

## Required change

Compute qualified outcome groups, per-skill observed source scopes and comparable baseline counts in set-based grouped queries or bounded pre-aggregations, then join the results once per revision. Avoid rescanning every baseline and every observed task for every skill. Preserve exact source-kind/source-id and production matching, distinct-turn semantics, absent-baseline n/a behavior, and exclusion of incomplete evidence required by .22.

## Reproduction and verification

Run python3 docs/reviews/2026-09-08-stats-scaling.py from the repository root; its recorded query plan and VM-step counts are in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-stats-scaling.json. Add a regression on the actual Rust-bundled SQLite/schema through load_skill_stats at increasing revision/outcome counts, verify exact utility results, and demonstrate that doubling both sets no longer multiplies query work approximately 8x. Include repeated oracle IDs, many source scopes, production/gym traffic, multiple attempts and missing baselines; report bounded latency at the documented retained-corpus scale.
acceptance_criteria: Run python3 docs/reviews/2026-09-08-stats-scaling.py from the repository root; its recorded query plan and VM-step counts are in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-stats-scaling.json. Add a regression on the actual Rust-bundled SQLite/schema through load_skill_stats at increasing revision/outcome counts, verify exact utility results, and demonstrate that doubling both sets no longer multiplies query work approximately 8x. Include repeated oracle IDs, many source scopes, production/gym traffic, multiple attempts and missing baselines; report bounded latency at the documented retained-corpus scale.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lost invocation telemetry is counted as a successful no-skill baseline
description:
## Problem

When invocation events are rejected or dropped, ingest_task_outcome silently removes the unmatched skill IDs and still persists the successful task outcome. load_skill_stats interprets absence of outcome links as a no-skill baseline and does not exclude observability-lost turns. A dispatcher probe recorded one healthy linked task plus a turn with an explicit ObservabilityLost event, then successful outcomes for both. The production stats loader counted the lost-evidence turn as one baseline task instead of excluding it. A session counter/log saying positive evidence was excluded does not enforce that exclusion in durable outcomes.

## Where

src/extras/js/skills/telemetry.rs:795-858,977-985; src/extras/js/skills/operations.rs:292-328; src/extras/js/tool.rs:1407-1432

## Required change

Persist a parent-authoritative per-turn evidence-completeness/attribution state and distinguish verified no-invocation turns from unknown/lost evidence. Exclude incomplete turns from positive utility and baseline comparisons even when no invocation row survived. Preserve real selected-but-unused/no-library baselines and make queue saturation or rejected worker telemetry update completeness without relying on the same saturated queue.

## Reproduction and verification

Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_observability_loss_is_not_a_no_skill_baseline -- --nocapture. It currently reports baseline_tasks=1 instead of0. Add rejected-worker-batch, saturated/disconnected queue, delayed persistence and clean selected-but-unused cases; verify restart persistence and production/gym separation. Assert incomplete evidence changes neither positive skill outcomes nor no-library baseline pass rates.
acceptance_criteria: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_observability_loss_is_not_a_no_skill_baseline -- --nocapture. It currently reports baseline_tasks=1 instead of0. Add rejected-worker-batch, saturated/disconnected queue, delayed persistence and clean selected-but-unused cases; verify restart persistence and production/gym separation. Assert incomplete evidence changes neither positive skill outcomes nor no-library baseline pass rates.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mid-turn skills_search removes task-outcome credit for skills invoked before the search
description:
## Problem

TaskOutcomeRecorder snapshots only the final selected skill bundle. ingest_task_outcome checks durable invocations only for IDs present in that snapshot. A real SkillRuntime probe selected and invoked a skill, re-froze the same turn with an unrelated search, and recorded a successful oracle through TaskOutcomeRecorder. The outcome persisted but had zero links to the previously invoked skill. Preserving turn_id across searches does not preserve the union of invoked skills. Utility statistics and lifecycle task evidence omit that actual invocation; an empty final bundle can also create a false no-library baseline.

## Where

src/agent/runner.rs:386-410 (TaskOutcomeRecorder::record); src/extras/js/skills/turn.rs:343-362; src/extras/js/skills/telemetry.rs:810-826

## Required change

Attribute task outcomes to the complete set of qualified durable invocations for the parent-owned turn, independent of the latest retrieval bundle. Alternatively retain a parent-authoritative per-turn invocation set across every search. Preserve selected-but-unused exclusion, production/gym isolation, bounded cardinality, idempotency and stale/purged-revision handling.

## Reproduction and verification

Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_search_keeps_outcomes_linked_to_earlier_invocations -- --nocapture. It currently persists zero links instead of one. Cover A invoked then search B, A and B both invoked, an empty final bundle, multiple completion-verification attempts and selected-but-unused candidates. Assert task evidence and displayed utility count all actual invoked revisions once per turn.
acceptance_criteria: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-telemetry.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_search_keeps_outcomes_linked_to_earlier_invocations -- --nocapture. It currently persists zero links instead of one. Cover A invoked then search B, A and B both invoked, an empty final bundle, multiple completion-verification attempts and selected-but-unused candidates. Assert task evidence and displayed utility count all actual invoked revisions once per turn.

title: macOS 26 CI evidence incorrectly reports that no production worker is available
description:
## Problem

The macOS evidence writer hard-codes assurance=deprecated-best-effort-fail-closed and native_resource_gate=unavailable-no-production-worker for both macos-15 and macos-26. In baseline CI 34190987872, the macos-26 artifact simultaneously says production_binary_matrix=passed, resource_measurement=recorded and no production worker; its actual resource artifact records a running seatbelt worker with deprecated-best-effort assurance. The summary therefore cannot distinguish supported-but-weaker macOS 26 containment from macOS 15 fail-closed unavailability and misreports the platform's release evidence.

## Where

.github/workflows/ci.yml:735-763 (macOS source-free Phase 6 evidence writer)

## Required change

Generate availability, assurance and native resource evidence from the actual validated probe result, distinguishing unsupported hosts, available deprecated-best-effort containment, failed probes and not-run steps. Do not infer success solely from the matrix label or emit completed native checks after an earlier failure. Preserve source-free output and validate consistency between gate and resource artifacts.

## Reproduction and verification

Add behavior-level tests for evidence generation covering successful macOS 26, unsupported macOS 15, preflight refusal and a skipped/failed native probe. Assert that measured production-worker resources cannot coexist with unavailable-no-production-worker and that assurance matches the runtime's typed status. Run both macOS CI rows and inspect the generated JSON. Contradictory baseline artifacts are preserved in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-platform-evidence.json.
acceptance_criteria: Add behavior-level tests for evidence generation covering successful macOS 26, unsupported macOS 15, preflight refusal and a skipped/failed native probe. Assert that measured production-worker resources cannot coexist with unavailable-no-production-worker and that assurance matches the runtime's typed status. Run both macOS CI rows and inspect the generated JSON. Contradictory baseline artifacts are preserved in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-platform-evidence.json.
close_reason: Closed

title: macOS worker cold startup and cancellation recovery exceed the recorded latency targets
description:
## Problem

The actual v1.8.0 debug resource artifact from baseline CI 34190987872 contains two matched-runner samples on macOS 26 / virtual Apple M1, each with 10 warmups and 100 measured iterations. Cold Ready p95 was 2678.268 ms then 1879.391 ms against the 300 ms target; cancel-and-recover p95 was 2172.205 ms then 1900.945 ms against 1000 ms. Warm pure calls remained 0.839/1.232 ms. The cost is concentrated in obtaining a fresh contained worker, not normal warm execution. The launcher performs publication sweep, immutable image preparation, guardian launch and authenticated Ready; which phase dominates still requires profiling. Timing targets are explicitly informational, so this is a measured performance finding rather than a failed security gate or a proven regression against another build.

## Where

src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs:477-589,2548-2701; src/extras/js/supervisor.rs:1605-1707; src/extras/js/tests/worker_resource_benchmark.rs:1088-1167; docs/benchmarks/results/js-worker-baseline.json

## Required change

Profile source-free elapsed times for publication sweep, image snapshot/sealing, guardian launch and Ready authentication on the same supported macOS runner. Optimize the dominant fresh-worker costs to meet the stated cold/recovery budgets while preserving one-time executable identity, all containment checks, parent-death cleanup, zero idle runtimes and one live worker. Record matched-host before/after measurements; if the target cannot be met without weakening containment, obtain an explicit documented release performance decision instead of silently treating green CI as meeting the target.

## Reproduction and verification

Use the installed debug production binary and js_worker_resource_benchmark on supported macOS 26, retaining 10 warmups/100 samples and matched-runner repeats. Require cold Ready p95 <=300 ms and cancel-and-recover p95 <=1000 ms, or a specifically reviewed target exception backed by measurements. Re-run macOS production-binary denial/guardian/one-time-image matrices and ensure warm-call latency, memory and process/runtime counts do not regress. Existing evidence is preserved in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-platform-evidence.json with source CI/artifact IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Use the installed debug production binary and js_worker_resource_benchmark on supported macOS 26, retaining 10 warmups/100 samples and matched-runner repeats. Require cold Ready p95 <=300 ms and cancel-and-recover p95 <=1000 ms, or a specifically reviewed target exception backed by measurements. Re-run macOS production-binary denial/guardian/one-time-image matrices and ensure warm-call latency, memory and process/runtime counts do not regress. Existing evidence is preserved in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-platform-evidence.json with source CI/artifact IDs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Proposal-enabled learned-skill sessions load the local embedding model three times
description:
## Problem

With skills-embed and backend=local, SkillRuntime construction, observation startup and admission startup each call Embedder::from_config, and every call invokes FastembedBackend::new -> TextEmbedding::try_new. Observation initializes a complete model before shared_coordinator discovers that the runtime already registered that coordinator, so this second model is immediately discarded. Runtime and admission retain separate model instances, and new sessions construct another set even when the shared coordinator exists. The three-initialization/two-retained-model result is code-confirmed; no ONNX memory or timing measurement is claimed.

## Where

src/extras/js/skills/turn.rs:199-212,877-901; src/extras/js/skills/session.rs:858-895; src/extras/js/skills/embed.rs:567-587,856-879

## Required change

Share an initialized embedding backend across runtime retrieval, coordinator/telemetry and admission for one compatible embedding configuration. Avoid constructing a backend merely to look up an existing coordinator. Preserve model metadata/cache invalidation and serialize inference as required by the backend; do not share incompatible provider/configuration identities. Give shared models a bounded lifetime.

## Reproduction and verification

Add a counting backend factory or equivalent construction seam and open a production-shaped service bundle with proposals enabled: assert exactly one expensive backend initialization and reuse by retrieval and admission. With skills-embed and a cached local model, measure startup and resident memory before/after, verify identical embeddings/retrieval, concurrent inference and release on session teardown. Cover changes in model/revision/dimensions/provider configuration so sharing cannot reuse the wrong backend.
acceptance_criteria: Add a counting backend factory or equivalent construction seam and open a production-shaped service bundle with proposals enabled: assert exactly one expensive backend initialization and reuse by retrieval and admission. With skills-embed and a cached local model, measure startup and resident memory before/after, verify identical embeddings/retrieval, concurrent inference and release on session teardown. Cover changes in model/revision/dimensions/provider configuration so sharing cannot reuse the wrong backend.
close_reason: Closed

title: Skill observation and proposal startup block the async executor on SQLite and model initialization
description:
## Problem

open_with_paths offloads only SkillRuntime construction. It then synchronously starts telemetry and proposal services inside the async future, opening three SQLite connections and constructing embedders. Store opens run an FTS schema-write probe with a five-second busy timeout; the local backend also synchronously initializes/downloads an ONNX model. A real SQLite writer held for 400 ms delayed a 20 ms current-thread Tokio timer by 416 ms when the actual observation-startup helper ran in the same call shape as production. Main runtime startup being offloaded does not protect this tail.

## Where

src/extras/js/skills/session.rs:828-897; src/extras/js/skills/telemetry.rs:652-658; src/extras/js/skills/store.rs:374-409; src/extras/js/skills/embed.rs:578-583,856-879

## Required change

Move all blocking observation/proposal initialization to a tracked blocking worker with cancellation-safe ownership and bounded waiting. Keep async timers, UI and cancellation responsive while SQLite is busy or model construction is slow. Preserve session-lifetime workers and clean up any late initialization result after cancellation; do not merely shorten the SQLite timeout or reduce test parallelism.

## Reproduction and verification

Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-skill-startup.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_observation_startup_keeps_executor_responsive -- --nocapture. Currently the timer runs after 416 ms instead of near its 20 ms deadline. The probe targets the synchronous helper called directly by open_with_paths; add an end-to-end current-thread open_with_paths test with a deterministic handoff into the observation/proposal phase, real SQLite contention and a slow model initializer. Assert timely timer/cancellation progress and eventual cleanup of initialized workers.
acceptance_criteria: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-skill-startup.patch and run cargo test --features skills release_review_probe_observation_startup_keeps_executor_responsive -- --nocapture. Currently the timer runs after 416 ms instead of near its 20 ms deadline. The probe targets the synchronous helper called directly by open_with_paths; add an end-to-end current-thread open_with_paths test with a deterministic handoff into the observation/proposal phase, real SQLite contention and a slow model initializer. Assert timely timer/cancellation progress and eventual cleanup of initialized workers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Post-tool hooks receive original arguments after a pre-hook input rewrite
description:
## Problem

PreToolUse updated_input is serialized and passed to the inner tool, but both PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure receive the original parsed tool_input. A real hook subprocess rewriting path from original-target to actual-target made the tool return actual-target while the post-hook JSON still reported original-target. Post hooks that audit or validate the affected file/command therefore inspect a different operation from the one executed.

## Where

src/extras/hooks/decorator.rs:72-73,123-138,148-163

## Required change

Retain the effective serialized/parsed arguments actually passed to the inner tool and send those to both success and failure post hooks. If original input is needed for provenance, expose it separately with documented semantics. Keep chained pre-hook rewrites and non-rewritten calls consistent.

## Reproduction and verification

Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-hooks.patch and run cargo test --features hooks,skills release_review_probe_post_hook_observes_executed_rewritten_input -- --nocapture. Currently the post envelope contains original-target. Require actual-target and add failure-path and multiple-rewrite tests that compare the captured inner-tool arguments with post-hook input; verify unchanged input when no rewrite occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Apply docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-hooks.patch and run cargo test --features hooks,skills release_review_probe_post_hook_observes_executed_rewritten_input -- --nocapture. Currently the post envelope contains original-target. Require actual-target and add failure-path and multiple-rewrite tests that compare the captured inner-tool arguments with post-hook input; verify unchanged input when no rewrite occurs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Streaming Markdown mistakes a shorter code fence for a closing delimiter
description:
Reviewed baseline: 6021ba1 (2026-09-08).

Where: src/ui/feed.rs:716-748 (find_stable_boundary fence tracking)

Failure: The boundary scanner tracks only fence character, not opening delimiter length or closing-line validity. After a four-backtick opening, an embedded triple-backtick code line is treated as a close. A following blank line caches an unsafe stable boundary, so '# literal header' is rendered as a heading while streaming even though it remains literal code; finalization visibly changes the content.

Required change: Match the actual Markdown fence rules: retain opening character/length and indentation, require a valid closing line of sufficient length and no non-whitespace suffix, and keep invalid shorter delimiters inside the fence. Share parser state where possible instead of duplicating an incomplete grammar.
acceptance_criteria: release_review_probe_long_fence_delimiter_streaming_matches_final_render in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch proves streamed rows lose the literal '#' while finalized rows retain it. Add chunk-boundary tests for 3/4/5 delimiters, tildes, trailing text, indentation and embedded blank lines; compare rendered text and style before/after finalization.
close_reason: Closed

title: Streaming a code fence repeatedly reparses the whole fence quadratically
description:
Reviewed baseline: 6021ba1 (2026-09-08).

Where: src/ui/feed.rs:694-707,857-940 (find_stable_boundary and agent_completed_lines)

Failure: Every newly completed code line scans and reparses from the fence start because no stable boundary is published inside a fence. A deterministic 1,000-line, 19,008-byte fenced response sends 9,517,500 bytes through the markdown parser (~501x source size). Long generated code, logs, lists and paragraphs stall the UI as the response grows; the mixed-paragraph benchmark does not cover this path.

Required change: Maintain incremental fence/list rendering state or render bounded live tails with completed rows retained until finalization. Avoid cloning the full stable row prefix on every chunk as part of the performance fix. Preserve exact finalized Markdown behavior and width-change invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: release_review_probe_long_fence_parsing_is_linear in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch measures parser work, not noisy wall time; fails at 9,517,500 parsed bytes for 19,008 source bytes. Add 1k/2k/4k-line scaling tests for fenced code and long lists/paragraphs, and measure total layout work/allocation as well as parser bytes; require near-linear work and equivalent final output.
close_reason: Closed

title: MCP structured-only tool results are silently returned as empty output
description:
Reviewed baseline: 6021ba1 (2026-09-08).

Where: src/extras/mcp/tool.rs:263-285 (successful content rendering)

Failure: The success path iterates result.content and ignores result.structured_content entirely. A successful result with content:[] and structuredContent:{answer:42} becomes only empty MCP delimiters. The model loses the result and may repeat a side-effecting call or invent an answer.

Required change: Preserve structuredContent in model-visible output with the existing size/spill limits and untrusted-content delimiters. Define deterministic behavior when both text content and structuredContent exist so data is available without unbounded duplication. Also make unsupported content kinds explicit instead of presenting an unexplained empty success.
acceptance_criteria: release_review_probe_mcp_preserves_structured_only_result in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-integrations.patch calls a real fixture returning answer:42; current output is '[mcp output begins]\n> \n[mcp output ends]'. Add structured-only, mixed, large structured result and isError tests through McpTool::call; no repeated execution should be needed to obtain the value.
close_reason: Closed

title: One unsafe saved-session entry prevents lookup of unrelated healthy sessions
description:
Reviewed baseline: 6021ba1 (2026-09-08).

Where: src/session/storage.rs:166-184,239-251,283-288 (find_sessions_by_prefix/find_session_by_name/find_recent_sessions)

Failure: Directory enumeration propagates read_private_string errors with ?. A single broken symlink, unsafe file, or entry disappearing during iteration aborts the whole search, even when the requested valid session was loaded. Session selection/resume can become unavailable until the user manually repairs an unrelated entry.

Required change: Keep exact-ID loading fail-closed, but isolate per-entry errors in multi-session discovery: skip unsafe/unreadable/raced-away entries with a bounded diagnostic and continue collecting healthy matches. Apply the requested limit to successfully decoded sessions rather than candidates so bad recent files cannot hide older valid sessions.
acceptance_criteria: release_review_probe_one_bad_session_does_not_hide_healthy_sessions saves one valid session and unrelated broken.json symlink; exact-prefix discovery returns Err. Add tests for prefix/name/recent/workspace queries with bad entry before/after healthy ones, invalid JSON and concurrent deletion; never follow or mutate the unsafe entry.
close_reason: Closed

title: Distilling to a user-selected file changes its existing parent directory permissions
description:
Reviewed baseline: 6021ba1 (2026-09-08).

Where: src/extras/js/skills/distill.rs:911-925; src/fs/private.rs:42-78,177-184

Failure: --distill-learned-skill-out /shared/project/draft.json calls ensure_private_directory on the existing destination parent, then private_atomic_create_sync repeats it. On Unix this unconditionally chmods /shared/project to 0700, removing group/other access. It happens even if the destination already exists and export fails.

Required change: Separate private application-state directory creation from user-selected export destinations. Preserve permissions/ACLs of existing output parents, keep the new draft file private and create-only, and preserve no-follow/atomic guarantees. Audit analogous explicit export-path callers without weakening app-private storage defaults.
acceptance_criteria: release_review_probe_distill_preserves_destination_directory_mode in docs/reviews/2026-09-08-probes-core.patch fails: expected 0755, observed 0700. Test 0755 and 0770 existing parents on successful export and AlreadyExists, default private output directory, symlink rejection and file 0600. Run cargo test --features skills distill.
close_reason: Closed

title: Unfixtured spawn and fetch fabricate success during verification, weakening admission evidence
description: Parent epic: mini-agent-q4xh. Source: 2026-09-07 review, documentation sweep; verified against code at a65f618. Documenting what the verification sandbox exposes (bead mini-agent-ii57) turned up an inconsistency the review had recorded imprecisely. An unconfigured effect does NOT uniformly fail: read_file without a fixture fails with 'File not found:', but spawn without a fixture returns a synthetic 'simulated <program> completed' with exit code 0, and fetch without a fixture returns a synthetic HTTP 200 JSON body (src/extras/js/skills/fakes.rs). Consequence: a proposed skill that shells out to a real executable, or that depends on a real HTTP response, passes its embedded tests and its held-out suite on fabricated success and is admitted on evidence that proves nothing about its behaviour. This is the mechanism behind the operator's original observation that a skill can report 100% success while returning semantically wrong data. Options: fail an unfixtured spawn/fetch the way read_file does (strictest, may break existing seeds and suites, so check them first); or require a declared fixture whenever a capability grant includes spawn or fetch; or keep the fake but mark the resulting report so the outcome cannot satisfy the held-out gate. Decide deliberately and record the choice in docs/specs/phase-3-skill-library.md, which currently documents the fakes without flagging that two of them fabricate success.
close_reason: Option one implemented in f03e5d3; CI green (run 34189429653, 77/77 jobs, 0 failures). An unfixtured spawn or fetch now fails and names the missing fixture, matching read_file. FAKES_VERSION bumped 3->4 so admission refuses reports produced against the fabricated responses. Two existing tests were passing only because of the fabrication and were corrected: skill_held_out_evaluator's probe asserted stdout.startsWith('simulated '), and skill_store_schema's sideeffecting fixture spawned printf from an embedded test. Embedded cases have no fixture channel, so effect behaviour can now only be proved in a held-out suite. Recorded in docs/specs/phase-3-skill-library.md and docs/agent/SKILLS.md.

title: parseToml seed resolves sections through inherited properties and can write onto Object.prototype methods
description: Parent epic: mini-agent-q4xh. Source: 2026-09-07 adversarial round 2 (unwired-code sweep, readiness trace, refutation pass, skipped-module review, Gym Rust/CI verification); verified against code at HEAD d1bf068. assets/learned-skills/toml-parse.json source: `section = out[name] || (out[name] = {})` with `out` a plain {}; a section named toString, valueOf or hasOwnProperty resolves to the intrinsic function and subsequent `section[key] = value` writes properties onto the shared Object.prototype method (the realm freezes prototypes but not their methods); `[__proto__]` throws TypeError on the frozen prototype; a scalar key followed by `[samekey]` selects a string primitive and throws in strict mode. Its embedded tests and held-out cases do not cover these inputs. Fix: Object.create(null) for out and sections plus an own-property check, add held-out cases for those section names, re-import as a replacement (which currently cannot be activated, mini-agent-83k9). The csv/json/table/diff seeds were verified correct.
close_reason: Implemented in 547dfaf; CI green on that commit.

title: harness_eval library arm ignores library:'seeds' and bypasses admission with a hand-inserted artifact
description: Parent epic: mini-agent-q4xh. Source: 2026-09-07 adversarial round 2 (unwired-code sweep, readiness trace, refutation pass, skipped-module review, Gym Rust/CI verification); verified against code at HEAD d1bf068. harness_eval_tests.rs:513 asserts `specification.defaults.library == "seeds"` as a constant and :530-548 inserts a hand-built gymNormalize artifact via SkillStore::insert_verified; the bundled seeds, --install-learned-skill-seeds/--import-learned-skill, admission and the contained held-out verifier are never exercised, so the arm measures a library that does not exist for operators. title: Gym ops: scripts/gym/train.sh runs a training session over mined tasks with library arms, records task-outcome evidence, and reports library-level deltas
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-nyqb. Source: 2026-09-06 skill-gym decision (mini-agent-b3dl); training material = this repo's beads + fix commits.

Build scripts/gym/train.sh (bash driver, ~200 lines) plus a small Python reporter that:
1. Reads gym.toml and the task manifest; selects tasks by tier (full/stripped prompt), area, post-cutoff flag, and a --limit/--seed; supports --dry-run.
2. For each task and each library arm (none | seeds | current): check out a fresh detached worktree at base_commit (from the pool), run mini-agent -p --output json headless with the isolated gym AppPaths, the stripped or full prompt, the configured live model, budgets (max turns/tool calls/tokens/wall clock), verify_command = 'cargo test --locked <fail_to_pass filters> && <pass_to_pass sample>' executed through the background-job path so the 30 s foreground cap does not apply, and enable_skill_proposals per arm.
3. Records one JSON line per episode: task id, arm, success (verify passed), turns, tool calls, js calls, effects, tokens (input/cached/output), wall clock, cost, skills retrieved/invoked, proposals emitted; the task-outcome evidence kind (gym step 2) is written into the gym store with production=false.
4. Never stores the fix diff or close reason in any prompt or log; isolates worktrees per episode and removes them on exit (trap), kills background jobs, and is resumable (skips episodes already recorded for the same run id).
5. After the run: harvests successful js steps for the optional distiller (follow-up bead), then prints a report: per-arm success rate with N and a Wilson interval, token and round-trip deltas, per-skill invocations vs task outcome, proposals -> verified -> awaiting-approval funnel. Explicitly non-gating; the report says so.
6. Cost guard: --max-cost-usd aborts the run when the summed provider cost exceeds the cap.
Acceptance: a --dry-run lists the episode matrix without calling a provider; a smoke run with --limit 2 --arm none against a scripted or cheap model produces valid JSONL and a report; a test proves an episode's prompt never contains close_reason text.
Depends on setup.sh, gym step 2 (task-outcome evidence, mini-agent-lkff) and gym step 3 (task.json + library axis, mini-agent-32hz).
close_reason: Added paired-arm train.sh/train.py runner with isolated worktrees/state, library installation, MINI_AGENT_GYM non-production evidence context, oracle execution, and JSONL GYM_OUTCOME reporting; script policy tests pass.

title: Gym data: scripts/gym/mine_tasks.py pairs closed beads with fix commits and validates fail-to-pass oracles into task.json candidates
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-nyqb. Source: 2026-09-06 skill-gym decision (mini-agent-b3dl); training material = this repo's beads + fix commits.

Why: 975 commits, 381 fix/feat commits since 2026-08-01 of which 229 touch test files; 698 beads, 610 with close reasons, 329 with file:line evidence, but only 21 commits name a bead id. The tests added or changed by a fix commit are a SWE-bench-style oracle (fail at parent, pass at fix); the bead description is the problem statement; close reasons are hidden grading notes only.

Build (~250 LOC Python in scripts/gym/mine_tasks.py, tests in scripts/tests/test_mine_tasks.py):
1. Pair beads to commits: explicit id in message first; otherwise closed_at within a window of the commit time and overlap between file:line paths in the description and files touched by the commit; emit a confidence score.
2. For each pair extract: parent sha, fix sha, test files added/modified (paths + test names via grep of #[test]/fn names), non-test files touched (for the hidden hint tier only).
3. Validate mechanically (cached in scripts/gym/cache/<fix_sha>.json): in a detached worktree at parent sha apply ONLY the test files from the fix commit, run cargo test --locked <filters> and require failure; at fix sha require pass. Reject pairs that do not flip. Record durations.
4. Emit tests/harness_eval/tasks/<bead-id>/task.json in the gym step 3 format: prompt (two tiers: full description, and a stripped tier with 'Fix shape' paragraphs and file:line removed), base_commit, test_patch (paths), fail_to_pass test names, pass_to_pass sample (N tests from the same crate module), budgets, tags (area:*, priority, commit date, post-cutoff flag), and NEVER the close reason or the fix diff.
5. Print a manifest: candidates found, validated, rejected by reason, per-area counts, split by commit date.
Acceptance: run on this repo yields >= 50 validated tasks; a unit test proves a task.json never contains close_reason or non-test diff text; re-running is idempotent via the cache.
close_reason: Added mine_tasks.py to pair closed beads with grep-matched fix commits, extract bounded UTF-8 deltas, validate explicit oracles fail on parent/pass on fix in detached worktrees, and emit bounded task.json candidates; unit test proves fail-to-pass validation.

title: Gym ops: scripts/gym/setup.sh prepares a host for a training session (toolchain, sandbox preflight, warm build cache, seed library, worktree pool, mined tasks)
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-nyqb. Source: 2026-09-06 skill-gym decision (mini-agent-b3dl); training material = this repo's beads + fix commits.

Build scripts/gym/setup.sh (bash, idempotent, exits non-zero with a named failing step; ~150 lines) that:
1. Verifies prerequisites: rustup toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml, cargo, git >= 2.40, python3, jq; on Linux verifies bwrap can actually unshare (real probe, since the sandbox capability check only tests binary existence); refuses to run if the workspace lives under /private/tmp (Seatbelt test caveat).
2. Builds and installs the debug binary (cargo install --path . --debug; never cargo build) and warms a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR (scripts/gym/target) with cargo test --no-run so per-task worktrees compile incrementally.
3. Creates the gym data root ($GYM_ROOT, default $XDG_STATE_HOME/mini-agent-gym): isolated AppPaths (config/data/local/state/cache) so training never touches the operator's real skills.db, memory, sessions, or audit; writes gym.toml with verify_command, enable_skill_proposals, embedding backend, task budgets, and the library arms.
4. Installs the seed library into the gym store (mini-agent --install-learned-skill-seeds) and imports any --import-learned-skill bundles listed in gym.toml.
5. Runs scripts/gym/mine_tasks.py (or reuses its cache) and materializes the task manifest; optionally prepares a pool of N detached worktrees (git worktree add --detach) so episodes start without a clone.
6. Checks provider credentials for the live model without printing them, records the model id and cutoff date into the run metadata, and prints a summary: tasks available (by tier/area/post-cutoff), library arms, estimated cost per episode from the harness eval budgets.
Acceptance: setup.sh on a clean macOS or Linux host completes in one invocation; running it twice is a no-op; a bats/shell test covers the failure-step reporting and the isolated-paths guarantee (real ~/.local/share/mini-agent untouched, asserted by mtime).

title: Detect and break tool-call loops (identical call+args repeated, alternating edit/undo) with a corrective message
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Why: Terminal-Bench failure taxonomy lists step repetition; Cursor's error taxonomy and Aider's max_reflections bound repeated failures. mini-agent has read-dedupe only (tools/mod.rs:125-138) and empty_response_count (runner.rs); no general detector for a model re-issuing the same failing shell/edit/js call.
Design: hash (tool, args) per turn; on the 3rd identical failing call return a synthetic result 'this exact call has failed 3 times; change approach or ask' and count toward a turn cap; emit an AgentEvent for the TUI.
close_reason: Implemented run-scoped exact-call and alternating-edit loop detection with corrective synthetic results, TUI/ACP events, docs, and regression coverage. Verified cargo fmt, diff check, strict clippy (default/no-default), full cargo test (1991 passed), reduced-feature tests, debug install, live JSON smoke, and TUI launch.

title: Prune old tool results from the live context before summarizing (context-editing style tool-result clearing)
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Why: Anthropic context editing clears old tool results first (keep last N tool uses) and only then summarizes; SWE-Pruner reports 23-54% token cuts on SWE-bench Verified with improved success; OpenCode prunes outputs older than the last 40k tokens. mini-agent compacts by summarizing whole prefixes only (src/session/mod.rs select_compaction_cut) and re-sends every historical tool output until then.
Design: at each turn start, replace tool results older than K tool uses (or beyond a token distance) with '[result cleared: <name> <summary line>; re-run or read spill file <path>]' while keeping the call; make K configurable; never clear the last M; keep spilled files.
close_reason: Implemented configurable request-time tool-result pruning across TUI, headless, loop, BTW, compaction, and ACP; preserved structured calls, durable results and spill paths; corrected provider-calibration projection tracking; documented behavior. Verified cargo fmt, focused pruning/compaction/ACP/accounting tests, strict Clippy default and reduced-feature matrices, full cargo test (1999 unit + 1 headless + 7 worker; 0 failures), cargo install --path . --debug, and installed OpenRouter JSON smoke.

title: MCP results larger than 1 MiB are discarded entirely while smaller ones reach the model uncapped

Fix: head/tail truncate with a spill file (same format as session tool-result spill) instead of erroring; align with the tool-result bound issue.
close_reason: Replaced the 1 MiB discard path with the shared 12,000-character tool-result policy: oversized MCP success and error payloads are privately spilled and returned as a 2k head/path/8k tail view; storage failures keep a bounded recoverable head/tail response. Added exact-threshold, >1 MiB full-spill, and spill-failure regressions; documented behavior. Verified MCP-only tests and strict Clippy, default strict Clippy, full cargo test (2001 + 1 + 7 passed), cargo fmt, diff check, and cargo install --path . --debug.

title: prepare_turn does synchronous SQLite under a std::Mutex that the background rebuild holds across embedding I/O, on the async executor
description:

Evidence: src/extras/js/skills/turn.rs:224-228 calls coordinator.routing_key()/replacement_candidate() outside spawn_blocking; coordinator.rs:318-355 holds the store lock while embedding every missing document (external HTTP backend, 30 s timeout per batch). needs_refresh short-circuits on rebuild_in_flight but these two calls do not, so a turn can block a tokio worker for the rebuild duration; plus 1 + 3-4 queries per selected skill per turn.

title: Trusted skill context is spliced into the user message text: spoofable by an unescaped prompt and persisted into history every turn (up to 64 KiB)

title: Add a typed structured-result channel (final_answer/return value as JSON) and a parent-side scratch store for cross-step values
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Why: today the only channel back is console text + the last expression stringified (64 KiB). Research (Anthropic programmatic tool calling, smolagents final_answer with host validators, Cloudflare Dynamic Workers env stubs) converges on: (1) documented return schemas so the model composes results in code instead of printing blobs; (2) an explicit terminal call the parent can validate/reject without a model round trip; (3) a size-capped parent-owned scratch_put(key, json)/scratch_get(key) so fresh-runtime invariants hold while large intermediates are not re-fetched every step.
Design constraints: all three are typed effects or worker-side pure helpers; no persistence of JS heap; scratch is JSON-only, per-session, size-capped, audited like write_file. Also consider pure worker helpers (path/glob-match/diff/table) so data is filtered in-sandbox.
notes: Implemented protocol v9 model-only typed result/scratch effects; parent JSON/key/shape/byte validation; per-session/workspace bounded process-local scratch surviving agent rebuilds but excluded from persistence; durable audit intent/completion with keyed target redaction; broker-terminal first result; worker interruption; parent receipt rejects forged structured outcomes; user/canonical docs and regression coverage. Verified cargo fmt, full unsandboxed cargo test (2114 passed, 8 ignored plus integration tests), no-default compile, JS-only compile, worker broker/audit suites, stored-skill isolation, persistence exclusion, legacy/result caps, and process inventory.
close_reason: Typed result and bounded parent scratch channel implemented, documented, adversarially validated, and fully tested.

title: js tool description and prompt state no limits, no examples, no sync/async or no-state guidance

Nothing says 'use js to read N files and aggregate in one call'.

title: Effects are strictly sequential: each is one IPC round trip, two spawn_blocking hops and two fsync'd audit records; add batched read_files/multi-effect requests
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: worker WorkerTransport::round_trip blocks the JS thread (src/extras/js/worker.rs:1370-1404); parent handles one EffectRequest at a time (supervisor.rs:1567-1690) with write_parent/read_worker on spawn_blocking (:1732-1760,:1775-1832); broker appends intent + completion, each sync_all()'d (audit.rs:845-880, sync_file :1488; F_FULLFSYNC on macOS). 256 reads => 512 fsyncs => seconds of the 30 s budget.
Fix: a read_files([...]) effect (one intent/completion pair, one frame, every path individually narrowed) and/or group-commit of audit records within a step; measure with the js-worker benchmark.
close_reason: Implemented protocol-v8 read_files batching with one IPC request and one durable audit intent/completion pair; every path is normalized, manifest/session-permission authorized before reads, results are ordered and bounded (256 paths, 1 MiB path text, 6 MiB JSON). Added worker, protocol, broker, audit/privacy, denial, and integration regressions plus updated Phase 6/tool documentation. Verified strict js+skills clippy, default unit suite (2099 pass; bootstrap fixture corrected for v8), no-default js suite (1649 pass), and debug install.

title: Add read-only list_dir/glob/grep effects to the JS realm; on macOS spawn is never granted so multi-file programs cannot discover files
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: install_model_effect_globals (src/extras/js/worker.rs:246-328) exposes only read_file/write_file/spawn/fetch; Spawn authority requires owns_complete_process_tree() (src/sandbox.rs:1096-1104: Linux bwrap or Windows appcontainer only), so on macOS the model must call native find_files/list_dir/grep first and paste paths into JS - one round trip per stage, exactly what code-as-tool should remove.
Design: route new read-only effects through the same FileEffectService policy (workspace-bound, prefix-narrowed, permission-checked, audited); additive under Phase 6 invariant 5. This is the single biggest lever for the README's 'read many files and aggregate in one program' claim.
close_reason: Implemented protocol-v7 brokered list_dir/glob/grep globals with workspace-bound read authorization, prefix narrowing, permission/audit reuse, descriptor-bound traversal, ignore/symlink safety, and strict result/visit/byte limits. Added worker/protocol/broker/security regressions and docs. Verified: focused discovery tests 19/19; full js+skills 2505 passed and no-default 1316 passed; strict clippy; fmt/diff checks; debug install.

title: Effect error reasons collapse (NotFound, IsADirectory, InvalidInput, TargetDenied all become invalid_target) and are thrown as rquickjs FromJs TypeErrors
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/extras/js/host.rs:1983-1994 maps NotFound|InvalidInput|NotADirectory|IsADirectory -> EffectServiceError::InvalidTarget; broker.rs:747 InvalidTarget|TargetDenied -> EffectErrorCode::InvalidTarget; worker.rs:497-513 surfaces it as "Error converting from js 'parent effect' into type 'read_file': invalid_target".
A mistyped path and a policy fence look identical to the model. NotFound/TargetDenied/InvalidBody are closed classes, not secrets.
Fix: add NotFound/IsDirectory/Denied/TooLarge codes; throw a plain Error('read_file: not_found') with a .code property.
close_reason: Implemented protocol v6 closed effect errors: not_found, is_directory, denied, invalid_target, and too_large. Parent services preserve actionable file/policy/size distinctions; worker globals throw plain bounded Error objects with an own stable .code property and no target text. Updated tool guidance and canonical docs. Added protocol, broker, filesystem, local validation, prototype-poisoning, and QuickJS teardown tests. Full JS+skills/no-default suites, strict Clippy, fmt, and diff checks pass.

title: Permission-prompt wait is charged to the 30 s step budget and reported to the model as 'execution timed out'
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/extras/js/tool.rs:657 PermissionBridgeOwner::new(.., STEP_TIMEOUT); tool.rs:824-826 single call_deadline; supervisor.rs:1585-1600 selects on that deadline while the parent services the effect; broker.rs:794 knows HostEffectError::AskTimedOut but the model sees 'JS error: execution timed out (30s limit exceeded)' (tool.rs:974) with no stage/diagnostic, concludes its code is slow, retries and re-prompts the user.
Fix: keep the deadline semantics but render a distinct closed message ('permission prompt not answered within budget') and consider pausing the compute clock while an Ask is pending (spec change).
close_reason: Implemented invocation-scoped permission-prompt deadline attribution with a distinct non-retry model message; preserved the single 30s absolute deadline, cancellation precedence, target redaction, and worker recovery. Added prompt/noninteractive/race/recovery tests and updated the canonical Phase 6 spec. Full JS+skills tests, no-default tests, strict Clippy, fmt, and diff checks pass.

title: console.log(obj) prints [object Object]; add a bounded JSON/inspect fallback
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: CONSOLE_WRAPPER_SOURCE (src/extras/js/worker.rs:579) uses String(value) per part. The most common debugging move costs a second round trip. Byte budgeting already exists (take()/byteLength()); a JSON.stringify fallback for non-primitives adds no authority.
close_reason: Console object and array arguments now use a captured JSON.stringify fallback while retaining safe string fallbacks for circular and non-JSON objects; existing per-record and per-step byte caps still apply. Added contained-worker regression tests for nested JSON, monkey-patching resistance, circular values, Map fallback, and truncation. Both strict clippy profiles pass.

title: Object results with undefined/NaN/Date/Map/Set/class instances are rejected as 'invalid result' where JSON.stringify would succeed
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: STRICT_CLONE_SOURCE (src/extras/js/worker.rs:673-748) throws on any undefined property value, NaN/Infinity, non-Object.prototype protos, holes. ({a:1, b:undefined}) -> 'JS error: invalid result (stage: result_conversion; script: model)'. Description says only 'Returns the last expression value as a string' (tool.rs:802).
Fix: apply JSON.stringify semantics (drop undefined, toJSON for Date) before the strict clone, or tell the model to return a string/plain JSON and JSON.stringify anything else; make the error say so.
close_reason: Preserved the accessor-free strict result boundary and implemented the bead's safe explicit-stringification path: tool/prompt/docs now name unsupported object shapes and instruct JSON.stringify, while invalid-result diagnostics return the same actionable fixed hint. Added end-to-end coverage for undefined, NaN, Date, Map, Set, and class instances; both strict clippy profiles pass.

title: grep ergonomics: include matches basename only (**/*.rs silently fails), invalid glob becomes match-all, case-insensitivity undocumented, inconsistent context format
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/grep.rs:170-175 include matches file_name only, so '**/*.rs' or 'src/*.rs' return 'No matches found'; :153 invalid glob -> match-all; description (:74-100) does not mention (?i), max_results=150, or the 10 MiB skip; context-mode lines use 'path-N:' (:245-251) vs 'path:N:' (:215) and separators count against max_results. No files-only/count/head-limit modes.
Fix: path-aware include globs with an explicit error on invalid glob; add case_insensitive, files_only, count flags; unify output format.
close_reason: Make include globs relative-path aware with optional-root **/, segment-safe wildcards, and explicit malformed-brace errors; add case_insensitive, files_only, and count schema controls; normalize context output to path:line markers and count only emitted source/file results rather than group separators. Added path-glob, invalid-glob, case-folding, compact-mode, and context-format regressions; grep suites and strict default/no-default clippy pass.

title: Directory walkers descend into .git/ (grep reads loose objects; list_dir shows .git)
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/mod.rs:226-228 is_skip_dir matches only node_modules|target; .gitignore never lists .git, and no other skip exists (no '.git' literal in find_files.rs outside info/exclude). grep.rs:184-189 reads files before the binary check, so `grep TODO` opens every loose object and returns hits from .git/hooks/*.sample, COMMIT_EDITMSG, logs/HEAD.
Fix: skip .git (and common VCS dirs) unless explicitly requested.
close_reason: Skip .git/.hg/.svn/.bzr entries in bound directory listings and recursive walkers before opening them, while preserving explicit-root inspection. Added list/grep/find regressions, including metadata files, plus tool-schema guidance; focused test, default/no-default strict clippy, formatting, and diff check pass.

title: read's 1 MiB cap ignores offset/limit and non-UTF-8 files surface a raw io error
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/read.rs:172-184 rejects a 1.2 MB file even for limit: 50 with no next-step hint; the description (:83-94) never states the cap; read_to_string (:186) surfaces 'stream did not contain valid UTF-8' while edit.rs:717-721 has a good actionable message for the same case.
Fix: stream by lines to serve offset/limit on large files; return an actionable message for non-UTF-8 (suggest shell head/strings); document the cap.
close_reason: Stream UTF-8 files line-by-line and retain only the selected excerpt. Oversized files now accept explicit offset/limit windows, stop after one lookahead in similarity mode, retain whole-file CRC correctness in hashedit mode, and cap selected raw text bytes. Non-UTF-8 errors recommend strings/xxd; descriptions and CONFIG document the semantics. Added large-window, unbounded guidance, invalid UTF-8, description, and incremental CRC regressions; read/tool/CRC suites and strict default/no-default clippy pass.

title: todo_write persists nothing and has no todo_read; the list evaporates at compaction
description:

close_reason: Added session-persisted shared TodoStore, todo_read, agent/ACP rebuild wiring, and open-todo preservation in compaction summaries and mid-turn recaps; documented and tested JSON round-trip, read/write sharing, and compaction retention.

title: Edit result gives no resulting snippet and there is no replace_all mode
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/edit.rs:792-795 reports 'Applied N edit(s)' only; the model must re-read to verify (which the read-dedupe then allows only because the version changed). EditArgs (tools/mod.rs:244-252) has no replace_all, so a rename needs N unique blocks.
Fix: echo the replaced region with a few context lines; add replace_all: bool (Claude Code parity).
close_reason: Implemented opt-in exact replace_all for SEARCH/REPLACE edits and bounded post-edit excerpts with context; added regression coverage and passed edit suite plus no-default strict clippy.

title: grep emits unbounded matched-line lengths (minified bundles, lockfiles, SVGs blow the context)
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/grep.rs:215 and :245-251 push the entire matched line; the only binary guard is a NUL scan (:62-64); up to max_results=150 lines go straight to context.
Fix: truncate matched lines to ~N chars around the match with an ellipsis marker (Claude Code behaviour); document max_results and the 10 MiB skip (:177-179).
close_reason: Bound every grep-displayed source line to a 500-character Unicode-safe window, centered on a regex match when present and marked with ellipses when clipped; context lines are bounded too. Tool description now documents max_results, the per-line cap, and the 10 MiB/binary skip. Added long Unicode match, context-line, and description regressions; full grep module and default/no-default strict clippy pass.

title: SEARCH/REPLACE parser cannot express '=======' or '<<<<<<< SEARCH' as content
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/edit.rs:76-91 matches markers on line.trim(); '=======' flips phase 1->2 whenever it appears inside SEARCH text (a Markdown setext underline), so the search shrinks and the rest becomes the replacement; '<<<<<<< SEARCH' inside a block is a hard 'Nested SEARCH' error. Editing docs/tests that describe this tool is impossible.
Fix: require markers at column 0 and add an escape (e.g. a longer marker or a raw-block flag); or offer a JSON {old,new} edit form.
close_reason: Make SEARCH/REPLACE markers column-0 exact and add an 11-character literal-safe block syntax whose active delimiters allow all standard marker lines as ordinary search/replacement content. Updated tool description/schema and added end-to-end delimiter-content and indented-marker regressions. All 37 edit tests and strict default/no-default clippy pass.

title: Shell tool has a hard, non-raisable 30 s deadline, so cargo test / cargo install / npm install cannot be run by the model
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/sandbox.rs:315-320 DEFAULT_COMMAND_LIMITS timeout 30 s, not overridden by any config key; src/agent/tools/bash.rs:86-93 'The optional timeout can only lower the deadline'. The git tool already allows 60 s for mutations (git/runner.rs:28-33), so the ceiling is policy, not a sandbox limit. This repo's own mandated gate (cargo test) exceeds 30 s; the model gets [status: timed_out] and cannot verify its work (the single largest harness win per Terminal-Bench/LangChain ablations).
Fix: config key for the default/max command deadline (Claude Code: 2 min default, 10 min max), per-call raise up to the max with permission, and/or a background-run mode with a poll tool.
close_reason: Satisfied by the session-scoped background shell path already present in the current implementation: shell(background=true) runs builds/tests/install commands under the same sandbox and permission policy with a bounded 24-hour maximum, returns a job id, and the jointly registered job_status tool polls bounded output or stops/reaps the process tree. Foreground remains a short 30-second operation. Verified all 9 background-job lifecycle/status tests plus joint shell/job_status registration; git diff --check clean.

title: read returns no line numbers in Similarity edit mode, while grep/edit/offset all speak in line numbers
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/read.rs:216-224 emits raw lines in EditSystem::Similarity; grep (grep.rs:215) and edit errors (edit.rs:314,349) report line numbers; read's offset is a line index. The model must count lines by hand to turn a grep hit into an offset. Claude Code uses cat -n format.
Fix: prefix lines with right-aligned numbers (and report total line count) in both modes.
close_reason: Similarity read excerpts now prefix every returned line with a right-aligned absolute N| marker; widths expand beyond three digits, hashedit shares the same width calculation, and both headers continue reporting total or lower-bound line counts. Updated tool guidance and added numbering/width regressions; read suite and strict default/no-default clippy pass.

title: OpenRouter Claude route caches only the system block; conversation history is re-billed every turn
description:

Evidence: src/provider.rs:253 .with_prompt_caching() on the OpenRouter model; rig openrouter/completion.rs:1262-1300 marks only the first system message, whereas the native Anthropic adapter (anthropic/completion.rs:2138-2160) marks tools + system + last message.
Fix: add a message-level cache_control breakpoint on the last user/tool message via extra_body or manual message blocks for the OpenRouter Anthropic route; document the gap otherwise.
close_reason: Enabled OpenRouter's native top-level automatic cache_control for anthropic/* routes so the cache boundary advances with the conversation while retaining direct Anthropic routing. Added an HTTP request-capture regression proving cache_control/provider params reach the wire, plus routing/merge assertions and provider docs. Verified: default 2089+1+7 tests; no-default 1317+1; strict clippy both matrices; fmt/diff checks; debug install.

Added catalog/default/pricing invariants and made the context-window precedence test robust to catalog refreshes. Full default and no-default test matrices and strict Clippy passed.

title: Bare-digit and 'connection' substring matching retries context-length and auth errors before showing the hint
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/retry.rs:40-52 matches '500' etc. anywhere; src/agent/runner.rs:1448 checks is_retryable before with_context_length_hint (:1467). 'prompt is too long: 213500 tokens > 200000 maximum' contains '500' and is retried max_attempts times with backoff; an MCP 'connection refused' auth failure is likewise retried.
Fix: short-circuit is_context_length_error_message before retry; classify by status code.
close_reason: Context-window errors now short-circuit retry classification across the error chain before provider status or message fallbacks. Status-message fallback accepts only explicit HTTP/status syntax instead of bare digits, generic 'connection' text no longer retries application/auth errors, and specific connection-reset transport failures remain retryable. Added classifier regressions and interactive/headless tests proving exactly one provider request and immediate compaction guidance. Updated retry docs. Verified cargo fmt, focused tests, full cargo test (2009 passed, 7 ignored plus integration suites), strict default/no-default Clippy, required debug install, and git diff --check.

title: Persistent memory block is a startup snapshot, not refreshed every turn as documented
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/context/mod.rs:244 reads Mem::open().context_block() once at load; src/ui/state.rs:123-145 rebuild_agent reuses self.context; run.agent is reset only on model/prompt/worktree switches (src/ui/app.rs:1466,1509,1529,2675). Docs promise otherwise: src/extras/memory/mod.rs:614 ('injected into the system prompt every turn') and the memory_write tool description (:1063 'open ones are auto-injected').
Scenario: model writes '- [ ] fix X' to the scratchpad in turn 2; the prompt carries the turn-0 snapshot for the rest of the session.
Fix: refresh the block at turn boundaries only when the memory file hash changed (keeps the cache-stable prefix otherwise), and fix the docs.
close_reason: Refresh persistent-memory context asynchronously at UI and ACP user-turn boundaries, invalidate stale prebuilt agents only when rendered memory bytes changed, preserve cache-stable preambles otherwise, and document/test the boundary semantics.

title: System prompt lacks verification-before-completion, planning, js-vs-shell-vs-grep guidance, delegation thresholds and headless stopping criteria
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/prompt.rs:1-16 is ~12 lines (conciseness, style, 'Ask the user when you have doubts'). Missing vs modern harness prompts: (a) run build/tests after edits and show evidence (only 'verify changed areas after editing' in READ_TOOL_PROMPT:26); (b) planning (TODO_TOOL_PROMPT:38 is one clause); (c) when to use js vs shell vs read/grep (JS_TOOL_PROMPT:18-21 only contrasts js with Python; shell guidance comes separately from sandbox.shell_capability().model_guidance()); (d) delegation thresholds beyond TASK_TOOL_PROMPT:39; (e) stopping criteria for -p/--loop: 'Ask the user' makes headless turns end with an unanswered question; (f) 'Keep responses under 4 lines... One-word answers are best' suppresses the final report a headless caller needs; (g) tell the model compaction exists so it does not wrap up early.
Research: LangChain pre-completion checklist +13.7 on Terminal-Bench 2; Anthropic context-engineering guidance on 'right altitude' sections.
Fix: restructure into sections (operating model, tool selection incl. js/skills, planning, verification, batching, stopping) with a headless variant.
close_reason: Expanded interactive and headless system prompts with explicit planning, tool-selection, delegation, verification, compaction, and stopping guidance; added prompt contract tests; both strict clippy profiles and focused tests pass.

title: TUI empty-response check uses aggregate res.output while headless uses the streamed buffer; can inject 'Please continue' despite streamed text
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/runner.rs:1656-1722 uses response_text = res.output for the empty check and increments empty_response_count even when text was streamed (reconcile_terminal_response and the test at :4357 exist because some adapters deliver an empty aggregate with streamed text); headless path :2134 compares full_response.len() against response_len_at_stream_start.
Scenario: on such an adapter the TUI injects 'Please continue.' up to 3 times then fails the turn -> rollback.
Fix: use the same streamed-length test in both paths.
close_reason: Fixed interactive completion to treat streamed terminal text as a non-empty response even when the provider's aggregate FinalResponse output is empty, preventing an erroneous Please continue retry. Added a regression test proving one request and a Done event with the streamed answer. Focused tests and strict clippy default/no-default passed; git diff --check clean.

title: Compact at the next tool-result boundary instead of aborting the in-flight tool for mid-turn compaction
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/ui/mod.rs:709-716 aborts run.main_abort (own comment: a just-returned tool may be interrupted after partially applying changes), then continues from a recap built from run.turn_trace (TURN_TRACE_MAX=64, src/ui/app.rs:49) which holds one-line format_tool_call_summary entries; MID_TURN_CONTINUE_PROMPT tells the model not to redo completed work per that summary.
Fix shape: set a 'compact requested' flag and perform compaction in the runner between rig StepEvent::ToolResult and the next completion call; build the recap from structured interactions.
close_reason: Mid-turn compaction now uses an explicit UI/runner handshake, lets the full tool batch finish, emits exact structured interactions before stopping, never starts the next provider call, and leaves text-only/final-only completions intact. Added regression tests and updated docs; strict clippy, full default tests, JS+skills tests, and debug install pass.

title: Bound in-turn tool results against the context window before they reach the model (spill applies only when persisting)
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/session/mod.rs:474-483 spills outputs >TOOL_RESULT_SAVE_THRESHOLD (12k chars) to a file with a head/tail marker only when the UI records the result - after the model already received it whole. Live bounds: shell lines only (DEFAULT_MAX_BASH_OUTPUT_LINES=2000, src/config/mod.rs:33) with byte caps 1 MiB/1 MiB/1.5 MiB (src/sandbox.rs:317-319); MCP results up to 1 MiB uncapped (src/extras/mcp/tool.rs:63-72); grep lines unbounded.
Scenario: `shell cat package-lock.json` (few lines, ~1 MB) injects ~300k tokens -> context-length error -> turn rollback (see retry issue).
Fix shape: apply the existing head+tail+path spill at tool-result time (Claude Code caps tool results at ~25k tokens), uniformly for shell/js/MCP/grep.
close_reason: Implemented uniform pre-model tool-result spilling through a Rig ToolResult hook for main, /btw, ACP, and subagent agents; persisted full output out-of-band with exact correlation fallback; bounded persistence-failure results; added scoped cancellation-safe artifact cleanup, regression tests, and documentation. Verified cargo fmt, git diff --check, cargo test --locked (2092+1+7 passed), strict clippy, and cargo install --path . --debug.

title: Reset or scope the repeated-read block on compaction, turn rollback and /undo; its hint points at a result no longer in context
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: src/agent/tools/mod.rs:125-138 blocks a read of the same (path,offset,limit,version) with 'Use the previous result'. src/ui/slash/mod.rs:465-469 rebuild_agent after compaction passes the same read_tracker; only replace_session reinitialises it (:131). PendingMainTurn::rollback (src/ui/state.rs:266-276) restores messages but not the tracker; rewind_to/redo never touch it. src/session/mod.rs:657-723 compaction paths never clear it.
Scenario: model reads src/big.rs, auto-compaction summarises it away, model re-reads -> blocked; escape is guessing a different offset/limit or `shell cat`.
Fix shape: drop tracker entries whose tool result was drained by compaction/rollback/undo (or key entries by message index and prune with the cut).
close_reason: Reset session-scoped repeated-read tracking whenever compaction, truncate/rewind/undo, redo, clear, or failed-turn rollback changes visible history; made blocked-read guidance conditional and added mutation/rollback regressions.

title: Execute independent tool calls from one assistant message concurrently (rig tool_concurrency is left at 1)
description:
Parent epic: mini-agent-5ana. Source: 2026-09-05 harness design review; finding verified against code by the orchestrator.

Evidence: no call to tool_concurrency anywhere in src/ (grep empty); rig-core 0.40 runner.rs:321 default concurrency: 1. Meanwhile src/agent/prompt.rs:9 tells the model 'Batch independent operations in a single message', so batching buys no latency.
rig commits results in call order at concurrency>1 (rig runner.rs:382), so raising it for read-only tools (read/grep/find_files/list_dir/task/js without write grants) is safe; write/edit/shell should stay serialized or be ordered by path.
Fix shape: set tool_concurrency(N) on the agent builder and gate mutating tools with a per-path or global write lock; document in TOOL_RUNTIME.md.
close_reason: Enabled Rig tool concurrency (4) across interactive, headless, /btw, continuation, and subagent streaming paths. Added a shared read/exclusive-write ToolDyn lane to every agent tool set: explicitly read-only tools overlap, while mutations, MCP, and unknown extensions serialize and exclude reads; results retain provider call order. Added focused lane and production-runner concurrency tests and documented the contract. Adversarial/reliability review found no remaining blocker. Verified cargo fmt, diff check, strict clippy, default tests (2095+1+7), no-default tests (1323+1), and debug install.

title: CI: hook abort lifecycle test must not depend on host sandbox availability
description: The hooks-only Ubuntu matrix intermittently waits 30 seconds for abort_handle_reaps_configured_async_hook_before_channel_close because the lifecycle test inherits HookTrust::Sandboxed and therefore depends on the hosted runner's bwrap launch path. acceptance_criteria: Make the lifecycle test select an explicit trusted direct-exec hook policy, retain its process-reaping assertions, and verify the hooks-only/full test matrix passes without relying on a host sandbox backend.
close_reason: Fixed by b9277b3: the abort lifecycle test explicitly uses trusted direct execution, preserving scoped child cancellation/reaping assertions without depending on hosted bwrap. Verified in CI run 33881326043, Ubuntu hooks/advisor/lsp/multimodal/pdf job 101050828910.

title: subagents: add a broad Rust lifecycle maintainer persona
description:
## Outcome
Add a broad `rust-maintainer` specialist that covers the end-to-end Rust SDLC while using the existing `rust-async-concurrency`, `rust-security-review`, and `rust-unsafe-code-audit` personas as deeper focused reviews.

## Scope
The persona should discover workspace/crate topology, MSRV/toolchain/targets/features, public API and semver boundaries, ownership/lifetime/error/resource design, dependency/features/build scripts/proc macros, tests/doctests/benchmarks/fuzzing, formatting/lint/docs, CI target/feature matrices, packaging/publishing, migration/deprecation, performance evidence, deployment/operations, and safe-code security.

## Boundary
The child remains read-only and cannot compile or run checks. It must derive commands from repository policy (including prohibitions such as this repository's no-`cargo check` rule), state unverified checks explicitly, and delegate deep Tokio cancel-safety, unsafe/FFI soundness, and adversarial security to existing specialists instead of pretending one broad pass replaces them.
design: Create `data/agents/rust-maintainer.md` with established frontmatter and caveats-first report ordering. Define a lifecycle method that starts with repository/toolchain guidance discovery, then architecture/API/feature analysis, implementation correctness, test and feature/target matrices, performance/benchmark evidence, dependency/supply-chain review, docs/semver/release, and operational lifecycle. Include explicit escalation triggers to the three existing Rust specialists. Update task tool guidance/docs and add registration and boundary tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- `agent_type: rust-maintainer` resolves from compiled defaults and appears in task tool guidance/documentation.
- The prompt obeys repository-specific command policies, remains read-only/evidence-first, and never claims checks were executed.
- It covers broad Rust SDLC concerns without duplicating or weakening the async, unsafe, and security specialist contracts; escalation triggers are explicit.
- Fixtures cover workspace/single crate, libraries/binaries, feature matrices, build scripts/proc macros, MSRV/cross-target, and release/semver cues.
- `cargo test` passes.
