title: Produce signed Windows NSIS installers with a bounded WebView2 policy
description:
## Why
Tauri's setup executable uses NSIS and is the practical Windows MVP. The installer must choose an explicit WebView2 strategy, sign both app and installer, and preserve mini-agent's Windows sandbox and Unicode behavior.
design: Build on windows-latest for every approved target. Use the downloaded WebView2 bootstrapper unless the ADR requires offline installation; document the size/availability tradeoff. Bundle and sign the ACP-enabled mini-agent.exe, then sign the installer. Define per-user/per-machine mode explicitly and avoid PATH or shell discovery.
acceptance_criteria: On clean Windows 10 and 11 VMs, a standard user installs, launches, completes ACP and cancellation smokes from a Unicode path, upgrades without losing config, and uninstalls application files without deleting user data. Authenticode verifies app, sidecar, and installer; persistent WebView2/network failure is actionable; failed signing publishes nothing.
notes: Tauri desktop shell and native installers deferred to 2026-10-01 per user direction

title: Produce Linux deb packages from a pinned WebKitGTK baseline
description:
## Why
A deb package gives Debian/Ubuntu users native dependency declaration and uninstall behavior, but Tauri v2 requires WebKitGTK 4.1 and the build baseline controls glibc compatibility.
design: Build the approved architecture on the oldest supported image selected by the ADR (Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12 are official Tauri examples). Declare runtime WebKitGTK/system dependencies, install the ACP sidecar in the bundle, and avoid PATH discovery. Keep the deb distinct from the portable AppImage.
acceptance_criteria: On clean supported Ubuntu and Debian VMs, dpkg/apt installs without undeclared dependencies, desktop launch completes the ACP smoke, package upgrade preserves user config, uninstall removes application files but not user data, lintian findings are resolved or documented, and CI rejects a bundle missing the sidecar/license payload.
notes: Tauri desktop shell and native installers deferred to 2026-10-01 per user direction

title: Produce signed and notarized macOS Tauri DMGs
description:
## Why
Direct macOS distribution requires a DMG built on macOS, Developer ID signing, and notarization. The nested mini-agent sidecar must be covered by the signing chain and retain executable permissions.
design: Add a macOS release job for every architecture approved by the ADR. Build the exact ACP-enabled sidecar and Tauri app on macOS; sign nested binaries before the outer app/DMG; notarize and staple; keep Apple credentials in CI secrets. Do not rely on shell-dotfile PATH because launched GUI apps do not inherit it.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh macOS VMs install each DMG, Gatekeeper accepts it without override, codesign verifies the app and nested sidecar, stapler validation succeeds offline after download, the app completes the ACP smoke from a path with spaces, uninstall guidance is documented, and failed signing/notarization publishes no asset.
notes: Tauri desktop shell and native installers deferred to 2026-10-01 per user direction

title: Scaffold a least-privilege Tauri v2 ACP sidecar vertical slice
description:
## Why
A desktop shell needs one proven end-to-end boundary before installer work. The existing ACP stdio server is the narrowest reusable boundary and keeps QuickJS, permissions, sandboxing, and provider logic out of the webview.
design: Under apps/desktop/, add the smallest Tauri v2 app and frontend that starts the bundled mini-agent sidecar with --acp over stdio, negotiates stable ACP v1, creates one session for an explicitly selected project directory, streams a prompt result, cancels it, and reaps the complete child tree on window close/crash. Use bundle.externalBin target-triple names. Grant only shell:allow-spawn for that named sidecar and fixed --acp arguments; expose no general shell command or arbitrary argument channel. Keep secrets/config in mini-agent's existing platform paths.
acceptance_criteria: A development build on each approved OS starts no shell, launches exactly one target-matched sidecar, completes and cancels ACP prompts, rejects malformed protocol output closedly, and leaves no child after normal/error/window-close paths. Capability tests prove arbitrary executables and arguments are denied. docs/ documents the module and process/security boundary.
notes: Tauri desktop shell and native installers deferred to 2026-10-01 per user direction

title: Optional Tauri desktop shell and native installers
description:
## Why
mini-agent already ships cross-platform CLI archives; Tauri is justified only if the project chooses a desktop GUI. Coordinate a minimal Tauri v2 shell, an ACP sidecar boundary, native packages for approved operating systems, and release integrity without weakening the existing CLI or sandbox contracts.
design: Treat the existing mini-agent process as an ACP stdio sidecar rather than moving agent logic into a webview. Put new code under apps/desktop/. Bundle exact target-triple sidecars with least-privilege Tauri capabilities. Platform packages must be built on their native or documented baseline runners and preserve GPL Corresponding Source delivery.
acceptance_criteria: The product/matrix decision is recorded; every approved platform child is closed or explicitly declined by that decision; bundled sidecar behavior is feature-equivalent across approved OSes; signed installer smoke tests and GPL/source checks pass; existing CLI release assets remain supported.
notes: Tauri desktop shell and native installers deferred to 2026-10-01 per user direction

title: Derive model tool guidance from the final registered tool set
description: The static SYSTEM_PROMPT advertises js, read/write/edit/grep/find_files/todo/task and the optional LSP paragraph even when --no-tools or --tools removes those tools. This can cause failed tool attempts and defeats capability-driven startup behavior.
design: Split generic behavioral guidance from per-tool guidance. Build the registered preamble from the exact eligible/final native tool set; append JS-first computation guidance only when js is registered, task guidance only when task is registered, and LSP guidance only when lsp_diagnostics is registered. Preserve shell guidance from the captured ShellCapability. MCP guidance must reflect collected MCP tools without exposing unavailable names.
acceptance_criteria: Preamble tests cover --no-tools, --tools read, --tools js, unavailable shell, disabled LSP, and an MCP-only allowlist. Every tool named in the resulting guidance is present in the built agent's tool definitions; JS remains the preferred computation tool whenever registered. cargo test passes.
notes: Implemented runtime-derived prompt guidance from the final registered tool names. JS-first computation, native file/task/memory guidance, LSP guidance, and shell capability guidance now appear only when the corresponding tool survived registration and allowlist filtering; --no-tools emits no named tool guidance. Focused builder/prompt tests and cargo fmt pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified runtime-derived prompt/tool parity, including JS-first gating, LSP-only guidance, and reserved MCP/built-in names.

title: Re-resolve workspace-relative shell capability after worktree rebind
description: The verified ShellCapability is pinned when startup resolves the configured shell. An explicit worktree switch rebinds Sandbox cwd and file authority but a workspace-relative configured shell executable can remain pinned to the old workspace, creating asymmetric execution authority.
design: Define whether relative shell configuration is workspace-scoped. If so, resolve and verify it against the newly captured WorkspaceBinding inside the existing transactional worktree rebind, publish the new shell capability only after every binding/context/sandbox step succeeds, and restore the prior capability on failure. Absolute/PATH-resolved shells should retain their verified image contract.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with workspaces A and B prove a relative shell switches from A to B only after successful rebind; failed B verification leaves A fully active; replaced executable images fail closed; normal resume/load/import that intentionally retain A do not re-resolve. Run focused shell/worktree tests serially, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and cargo install --path . --debug.
notes: Implemented transactional worktree shell rebinding. ShellCapability now retains provenance only for configured workspace-relative paths; explicit worktree rebind verifies and pins the corresponding image under the replacement WorkspaceBinding before permission or UI authority is published. Absolute and PATH-resolved shells remain startup-pinned. Added cross-platform success/failure/pinning tests, Unix replaced-image rejection, Windows write-sharing denial, session restore non-rebind coverage, and full authority rollback coverage. Verified cargo fmt, strict clippy, 15 shell-mode tests, 83 worktree tests, full serial cargo test (1568 passed, 5 ignored; worker bootstrap 7 passed), and cargo install --path . --debug.
close_reason: Implemented workspace-relative shell capability re-resolution with transactional rebind rollback and cross-platform identity tests; merged in PR #27 (95949b5a775f87133c9cbc18d72fde8de204db58).

title: Reuse JS skill services across agent rebuilds within one session
description: provider::build_agent_in_workspace reopens SkillRuntime and agent::builder::register_js_tool starts proposal, admission, and telemetry workers on every agent rebuild. TUI model changes/compaction and ACP prompts can therefore repeat storage/index startup and accumulate short-lived worker sets.
design: Create one workspace-bound, session-scoped JS skill service owner containing SkillRuntime and the proposal/admission/telemetry services. Capture it once for a normal UI/headless session and once per ACP SessionState, then pass Arc-backed handles through every build/rebuild. Never use a process-global workspace cache because mutable turn context must not cross concurrent ACP sessions. Teardown must be owned by the session and bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Counter tests prove an eligible session initializes skill storage/indexes and starts each service worker once across repeated rebuilds; --no-tools and JS-ineligible modes initialize zero; two ACP sessions receive distinct turn contexts; session teardown joins workers; failed initialization stays fail-closed without repeated startup churn. Run focused JS skill/ACP/UI tests serially, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and cargo install --path . --debug.
notes: Implemented one lazy workspace-bound SkillServiceOwner per UI/headless/ACP session. Agent rebuilds reuse SkillRuntime, turn gate/context, proposal budget, and proposal/admission/telemetry workers; ineligible or unavailable JS initializes nothing; failed initialization is cached; persistent service workers do not inherit turn cancellation. Added lifecycle, workspace rebind, failure-cache, zero-init, teardown, and ACP session-isolation coverage. Verified focused lifecycle/rebuild/ACP tests, clippy, full serial default suite, full serial default+skills suite, and cargo install --path . --debug.
close_reason: Merged PR #28 after 65/65 checks passed; session-scoped JS skill services now survive agent rebuilds without cross-session leakage or startup churn.

title: Bound or defer OpenRouter pricing refresh during startup
description: OpenRouter pricing refresh is awaited on the startup path. The default HTTP client has no request/connect deadline unless the user configured one, so DNS, connect, TLS, or a stalled response can dominate startup even when model prices are not needed to launch.
design: Trace the startup pricing call from initialization through HTTP client construction. Give it a short explicit connect/request deadline and preserve cached prices on failure, or move refresh off the critical path under an owned cancellable task. Do not make startup depend on a successful network refresh and do not log API keys, URLs with secrets, or response bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic delayed-server tests prove startup reaches agent readiness within the documented ceiling with cached or unavailable pricing; successful refresh still updates prices; cancellation/relaunch leaves no task or connection behind; custom provider timeouts retain their documented precedence. Record cold and warm startup timings, run focused provider/startup tests, full cargo test -- --test-threads=1, and cargo install --path . --debug.
notes:
Implemented owned opportunistic OpenRouter pricing/context refresh starting before feature initialization, skipped for ACP, preserving explicit/quick/catalog/resumed metadata precedence. Pending work aborts at readiness with 100 ms foreground join; a runtime reaper retains timed-out cancellation ownership. Response bodies are capped at 8 MiB. Focused startup tests: 20 passed; provider tests: 32 passed; process inventory passed. Full serial suite, debug install, and cold/warm timing remain.
Integration gate 2026-08-10: full serial suite and debug install passed. macOS is not valid Windows startup timing evidence; record the five-sample Windows cold/warm/default matrix from docs/benchmarks/windows-startup.md before closing.
Implementation is merged on main through PR #22 (commits 3f29a54 and 2006245 within merge 53d5e73). Validate only the combined main build; no individual branch remains to merge. Keep open for the recorded Windows cold/warm timing matrix.
close_reason: Verified fixed in feat/windows-shell-native-git by code audit

title: Keep picker state coherent across bracketed and clipboard paste
description:
Every UserEvent::Paste calls InputEditor::handle_paste, which mutates only buffer and cursor. Active picker query/filter state is updated only by handle_picker_key, so bracketed paste already makes the picker display diverge from the input; Windows Ctrl+V would inherit the defect.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a command or file picker in the TUI.
2. Paste ASCII, Unicode, or multiline text through bracketed paste.
3. Observe InputEditor buffer/cursor change while the picker query/filter remains stale.
design: Define one paste insertion operation used by bracketed paste, paste-burst newlines and Windows clipboard paste. Either update picker state from printable pasted text or deliberately close the picker before multiline/unsupported paste; document one deterministic policy. Paste must remain atomic and must never submit.
acceptance_criteria: ASCII, Unicode and multiline paste leave buffer, cursor and picker query/filter coherent; clipboard and bracketed-paste paths behave identically; multiline paste never submits; behavior without an active picker is unchanged. Run cargo test paste_burst -- --test-threads=1, cargo test picker_tests -- --test-threads=1, full serial cargo test and debug install.
notes: Confirmed root cause: UserEvent::Paste bypassed picker key handlers and mutated only InputEditor buffer/cursor. Added one bounded paste policy: searchable pickers accept up to 256 printable characters through existing insertion handlers; multiline, control-bearing, oversized, and rewind-mode paste closes the picker and performs one atomic non-submitting buffer insert. Added ASCII, Unicode, multiline, oversized, and no-picker regressions. Verified 30 picker tests, 5 paste-burst tests, clippy, full serial suite (1573 passed, 5 ignored; bootstrap 7 passed), and debug install.
close_reason: Merged PR #29 (d79e092): bounded searchable-picker paste replay preserves query/filter/cursor coherence; unsafe multiline/control/oversized paste closes the picker and inserts atomically. Focused, full serial, install, clippy, and 65-check CI gates passed.

title: Design race-safe checked workspace replacement on Windows
description: Windows NtSetInformationFile supports handle-relative atomic rename but has no destination file-ID compare-and-swap condition. An unconditional ReplaceIfExists implementation can clobber a user edit published after the final identity check, so existing-file EditTool and JS write_file replacement must continue to fail closed on Windows until a protocol can preserve the checked-replacement contract.
design: Investigate a bounded oplock or other supported Windows protocol. Do not use name-based ReplaceFileW rollback or deprecated TxF unless it can prove handle-relative containment, crash-atomic publication, and preservation of every raced target. Keep the safe unsupported result if those guarantees cannot be met.
acceptance_criteria: Native Windows adversarial tests deterministically replace the target after the last pre-publication check and prove the raced file is preserved; EditTool and brokered JS existing-file writes then pass on Windows; Linux/macOS exchange behavior remains unchanged.
notes: Design concluded: Windows FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION/MoveFileExW/ReplaceFileW provide pathname replacement but no expected-destination identity compare-and-swap operand. Oplocks coordinate breaks and can be broken by competing rename; TxF is deprecated and not a supported shared-writer solution. Existing-file workspace-relative native edit and brokered JS write_file therefore remain fail-closed on Windows. Implemented FILE_SHARE_DELETE on retained regular-file identity handles so races and the product's own later publication are not accidentally blocked; directory binding handles remain pinned. Added a deterministic Windows race-after-final-check test proving the competing target identity/content survives and no temp residue remains, plus an exact Windows CI discovery/run gate and scoped documentation. Local verification: cargo fmt, strict clippy, 6 focused workspace binding tests, 1573 serial unit tests + 7 bootstrap tests, and cargo install --path . --debug all pass. Native Windows execution is delegated to CI.
close_reason: Completed design and fail-closed Windows implementation via merged PR #30 (bc7bddb). Native Windows CI deterministically raced the target after the last identity check, preserved the competing identity/content, left no temp residue, and passed the full matrix. Microsoft APIs provide no supported expected-destination identity CAS, so existing-file native edit and JS write_file remain safely unsupported on Windows while create-only writes remain available.

title: Isolate residual Windows filesystem and process-global test failures
description: After accounting for path-test defects and the process-creation poison cascade, the reported full Windows run still includes session_storage_permissions_windows_reject_reparse_paths_without_mutation, successful_turn_persistence_still_commits_the_complete_turn, and edit_invalidates_only_the_owning_session_tracker. The pasted output lacks panic bodies, so these cannot yet be assigned a shared root cause. Re-run each serially, then under parallel load, capture the first assertion/error, and audit shared ZS_DATA_DIR/ZS_CONFIG_DIR/ZS_STATE_DIR plus junction cleanup and Windows replacement behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Each named test has a confirmed causal chain from a captured Windows failure; targeted serial and parallel repetitions pass; test-owned environment variables and junctions are restored on success and panic; any production filesystem correction retains reparse-point fail-closed behavior and read-tracker session isolation.
close_reason: Fixed Windows delete-sharing for retained atomic metadata, added Windows workspace-bound replacement, centralized panic-safe process-environment guards, serialized Windows production instrumentation, and added native Windows CI coverage.

title: Make renderer scroll redraw test independent of the host terminal size
description: scroll_triggers_chat_redraw assumes 40 lines overflow an 80x24 fallback viewport, but Renderer::terminal_size reads the real terminal whenever available. On a Windows console taller than the fixture, scroll_line_up is correctly a no-op and the dirty assertion fails. This is an environment-dependent test, not evidence of a Windows rendering defect.
acceptance_criteria: The test controls viewport geometry or derives enough content from the observed/injected geometry; it proves both that an actual scroll marks chat dirty and that a no-op scroll does not; it passes from terminals of different sizes and in headless CI on all three OSes.
close_reason: Renderer scroll redraw coverage now derives overflow from observed geometry and proves no-op scrolling remains clean.

title: Make file-picker and slash-add path tests portable on Windows
description: The Windows suite deterministically fails test_walk_files_includes_nested_dirs plus slash-add absolute/root tests. The picker test converts PathBuf values to strings and expects 'a/b', while Windows returns native separators. The slash tests use '/tmp/foo.txt' and '/' as absolute paths, but those are Unix fixtures and are not fully-qualified Windows absolute paths. The production APIs use PathBuf and should be verified with platform-native components rather than Unix string spellings.
acceptance_criteria: Picker assertions compare PathBuf components or otherwise accept native separators; slash-add tests construct a real absolute path for each platform and retain explicit Unix coverage where appropriate; all affected tests pass on Windows, macOS, and Linux without changing correct platform path semantics.
close_reason: Picker and slash-add path tests now use platform-native PathBuf/absolute fixtures; targeted tests pass.

title: Add artifact-level compliance smoke tests for package recipes
description: Build or faithfully stage the AUR, Conda binary/source, and Homebrew package outputs in CI and assert LICENSE, NOTICE, and SOURCE.md are present. Current policy validates source URLs, checksums, revisions, and install commands but does not execute every external package manager.
acceptance_criteria: CI verifies the installed compliance payload for every maintained package channel, with pinned or controlled package-manager inputs and platform-appropriate jobs.
close_reason: Added controlled offline artifact-staging smoke coverage for AUR, Conda binary/source, and Homebrew, wired into CI and metadata policy; 62 Python tests pass.

title: Stabilize Git worktree timeout tests under full parallel feature load
description: The default-plus-skills cargo test matrix (1,880 tests) reproducibly leaves concurrent_stash_before_exact_publication_is_never_captured_as_owned and timed_out_worktree_create_rolls_back_the_new_ref_and_registration failing under suite-wide load, while both pass when rerun individually. Investigate whether test deadlines/coordination or production cleanup need strengthening without weakening the worktree ownership checks.
acceptance_criteria: Both tests pass repeatedly in the default-plus-skills parallel suite and individually; timeout cleanup remains bounded and exact stash ownership remains fail-closed.
notes: A full parallel Windows suite also showed many worktree failures, but they followed failures in the process-global Windows creation boundary. Narsil traces worktree subprocess consumers into creation_guard. Re-run the Windows worktree subset after mini-agent-obqi is resolved before classifying every reported Windows worktree failure as an independent Git race; the original default-plus-skills load failures remain valid independent evidence.
close_reason: Repository-keyed stash gate plus timeout-first sandbox selection make both load-sensitive regressions deterministic; feature+skills targeted tests and the full suite pass.

title: Rewrite README around ZeroStack foundation and mini-agent code-as-tool architecture
description: Replace the implementation-first README with a proper project introduction that credits ZeroStack's minimal Rust foundation, explains mini-agent's added features, documents JavaScript code-as-tool and cross-platform parity, and explains the verified self-curated JS skill library with authoritative research references.
acceptance_criteria: README clearly credits and links ZeroStack; distinguishes foundation from mini-agent additions; explains why JS is used across Linux/macOS/Windows without overstating platform guarantees; explains proposal, verification, retrieval, evidence, promotion, quarantine, and rollback of learned snippets; preserves operator/developer links and build instructions; cited claims link to primary sources.
notes: README rewritten to credit ZeroStack's minimal Rust foundation, separate mini-agent additions, explain CodeAct/code-as-tool, define tested Linux/macOS/Windows JS contract versus platform assurances, and explain proposal/verification/retrieval/evidence/promotion/quarantine/repair/rollback for the agent-curated JS library. Primary links: ZeroStack, Apple CodeAct, QuickJS, Voyager.
close_reason: Implemented, documented, benchmarked, and verified by repeated affected feature suites plus the installed macOS containment canary.

title: Optimize macOS 26 JS worker cold start and cancel recovery
description: The reviewed macOS 26 reference pair records cold Ready p95 at 7.53s/7.27s and post-cancel recovery p95 at 8.77s/7.02s, above the initial 300ms/1s goals. Warm calls, 4 KiB IPC, memory, one-worker, and zero-idle-runtime goals pass. The measurements include the full one-time-image Seatbelt and guardian preflight/teardown and remain observational rather than security gates.
acceptance_criteria: Profile the containment-safe cold and recovery paths on a matched quiet macOS 26 host; reduce repeatable overhead without weakening the live preflight, guardian, one-time-image, or fail-closed guarantees; retain machine-readable before/after evidence and review any revised performance target explicitly.
notes: Replaced per-generation full debug-binary rewrite with descriptor-relative Darwin fclonefileat APFS COW publication, retaining independent hashes, inode/ACL/mode/source-stability/cleanup checks and an EXDEV/ENOTSUP secure-copy fallback. Matched 100-sample macOS x86_64 evidence: cold p95 6380.723ms -> 3794.123ms (-40.54%); recovery p95 6025.452ms -> 3676.008ms (-38.99%). Installed production lifecycle canary passed.
close_reason: Implemented, documented, benchmarked, and verified by repeated affected feature suites plus the installed macOS containment canary.

title: [REVIEW] Delete the unused retry::with_retry helper
description:
## Defect and impact
`src/retry.rs::with_retry` has no production caller; exact search finds only its own private tests. Production uses streaming/runner-specific retry paths. The generic helper and five tests are dead abstraction and maintenance noise.

## Exact scope
- `src/retry.rs::with_retry`
- only tests whose sole subject is `with_retry`

## Required implementation
1. Re-run exact `rg '\bwith_retry\b'` immediately before editing to avoid racing a new caller.
2. Delete the helper and helper-only tests.
3. Keep `RetryConfig`, `simple_jitter`, `is_retryable`, `retry_stream_chat`, and their production tests unchanged.
4. Do not consolidate or redesign remaining retry loops.

## Constraints / non-goals
No broad retry refactor, backoff semantic change, or removal based only on static analyzer output.

## Verification
`rg '\bwith_retry\b' src`; retry tests; `cargo fmt`; `cargo test`; `cargo install --path . --debug`.

## Duplicate search
All 274 Beads were searched for with_retry/dead retry helper. No matching issue exists.
design: Delete the dead generic helper rather than consolidating unrelated production retry loops.
acceptance_criteria: Exact reference search finds no with_retry definition or caller; only helper-specific tests are removed; RetryConfig/simple_jitter/is_retryable/retry_stream_chat behavior and tests remain unchanged; fmt, full tests, and debug install pass.
notes:
Source plan SIM-02: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-02-application-critical-review.md.
Deferred by owner to keep the finish-line focus on core software implementation; revisit on 2026-09-01.
close_reason: Implementation and documentation are merged into main; focused metadata checks, cargo fmt, full cargo test, and debug install pass.

title: [REVIEW] Isolate the research spike from the production Cargo workspace
description:
## Defect and impact
`AGENTS.md` calls `spike/` a research artifact and never a production target, but root `Cargo.toml [workspace]` includes it. Root metadata, lockfile, loop verification, workspace lint/tests, and CI churn therefore include a nonshipped harness with independent dependencies and target-specific manifest warnings.

## Exact scope
- root `Cargo.toml [workspace]`
- `spike/Cargo.toml`
- spike-specific crate selection in `scripts/loop.sh`
- contributor guidance that claims root workspace membership

## Required implementation
1. Capture root and spike `cargo metadata --locked --no-deps` package sets before change.
2. Exclude spike from the root workspace and make it an explicit standalone workspace/package so it remains runnable.
3. Remove production loop/CI logic that conditionally validates spike as a shipped root crate.
4. Preserve spike source and research instructions.
5. Assert root metadata contains only mini-agent and spike-local metadata only spike.

## Constraints / non-goals
Do not delete or productionize spike, consolidate its dependencies, change QuickJS behavior, or make production import it.

## Verification
Root and spike-local metadata commands; root `cargo fmt`; root `cargo test`; documented spike-local test/run; root `cargo install --path . --debug`.

## Duplicate search
All 274 Beads were searched for spike workspace isolation. Phase 6 Windows proof mentions spikes but no task owns removing the research crate from the production workspace. No duplicate exists.
design: Exclude spike from the root workspace and give spike its own explicit workspace boundary; preserve it as a standalone research artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Root cargo metadata contains only mini-agent; spike-local metadata contains only spike; root loop/CI no longer treats spike as shipped; spike source remains independently runnable; root cargo test and debug install pass without spike lock/lint/test participation.
notes:
Source plan SIM-01: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-02-application-critical-review.md.
Deferred by owner to keep the finish-line focus on core software implementation; revisit on 2026-09-01.
close_reason: Implementation and documentation are merged into main; focused metadata checks, cargo fmt, full cargo test, and debug install pass.

title: [REVIEW] Remove the unproved Nix packaging support surface
description:
## Defect and decision
The repository presents Nix as supported but has no Nix CI row or current install path. `release.nix` is impure and exports old names; `nix/package/zerostack.nix` expects missing Cargo homepage metadata, disables tests, and uses invalid quote characters in postInstall. Keeping apparently supported but unverified packaging is misleading belly fat. Decision: remove it now rather than create an unrequested pinned-flake/CI product commitment.

## Exact scope
- `default.nix`, `release.nix`, `shell.nix`
- `nix/overlay/*.nix`, `nix/package/*.nix`
- Nix expectations in `scripts/check-package-metadata.py` and tests
- Nix channel claims in `docs/agent/PUBLISHING_RELEASES.md` and other active user docs

## Required implementation
1. Make supported package channels explicit in metadata tests.
2. Remove tracked Nix package/overlay/dev-shell entry files.
3. Remove Nix release/install claims and validation expectations.
4. Preserve `/nix` filesystem runtime roots used for sandbox/toolchain compatibility.
5. Document that restoration requires pinned inputs, Linux/macOS CI, default-feature parity, and smoke of the exact store output.

## Constraints / non-goals
Do not remove runtime `/nix` sandbox access or alter Cargo/AUR/Conda/Homebrew packaging. Do not replace this with an unverified flake.

## Verification
Scoped stale file/reference search; package metadata/script tests; `cargo fmt`; `cargo test`; `cargo install --path . --debug`.

## Duplicate search
All 274 Beads were searched. Closed `mini-agent-efb` attempted Nix parity, but the current untested/stale files prove regression and it did not decide support removal. No open duplicate exists.
design: Choose the smallest truthful support policy: remove stale untested Nix packaging now; future restoration requires pinned inputs and exact-output CI/smoke on every claimed platform.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked Nix package/overlay/dev-shell entry files and active Nix release claims are removed; supported-channel metadata tests no longer infer Nix; /nix runtime sandbox compatibility remains; stale searches, package metadata tests, full tests, and debug install pass; restoration requirements are documented.
notes:
Implementation independently reviewed CLEAN and pushed on bead-jj7m-4 at e6ddb18 (based on required bead-jj7m-3 dependency). Removed all tracked Nix entry points; indexed release gate rejects renamed *.nix, flake.lock, and nix directory surfaces while preserving untracked local files and runtime /nix compatibility. Gates: 13 metadata regressions, metadata checker, 1084 applicable Rust tests, debug install/live smoke, crate package contains no Nix entries. Keep open until jj7m.3 external public-release blocker clears and both branches merge.
Deferred by owner to keep the finish-line focus on core software implementation; revisit on 2026-09-01.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text: 2026-08-09 local revalidation remains green: package metadata policy, 45 focused tests, cargo fmt, cargo test (1516 passed, 5 ignored plus 7 integration), and debug install pass. Closure still follows jj7m.3.

comments.text: Final verification 2026-08-09: tracked Nix package/overlay/dev-shell entry points and active support claims remain removed; runtime /nix compatibility remains intact. The indexed release-surface guard, package metadata checker, 51 focused metadata regressions, cargo fmt, Rust tests (two unrelated timing flakes each passed immediately in isolation), debug cargo install, canonical release matrix, and live installer smoke all pass.

title: [REVIEW] Pin release artifact actions to immutable commit SHAs
description:
## Defect and supply-chain impact
`.github/workflows/release.yml` uses mutable `actions/upload-artifact@v4` and `actions/download-artifact@v4` at every private handoff. Most other actions and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` use immutable commit SHAs. Release dependencies can therefore change without a repository diff.

## Exact scope
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` upload/download artifact sites
- workflow static/policy tests
- dependency automation configuration if needed

## Required implementation
1. Add a static test requiring full commit SHAs plus version comments for release `uses:` entries unless explicitly allowlisted.
2. Resolve/review current v4 commits and pin every upload/download use.
3. Configure/update dependency automation so SHA and comment move together.
4. Rehearse private artifact upload/download and final publication handoff.

## Constraints / non-goals
No behavior or artifact-retention change. Do not replace mutable tags with unverified SHAs or repin unrelated actions without review.

## Verification

title: [REVIEW] Scope repeated-read policy and history to one agent session
description:
## Defect and impact
`DENY_REPEATED_READS` and `READ_TRACKER` in `src/agent/tools/mod.rs` are process-global. `Startup::init_features` changes the flag globally and every ReadTool shares ranges. One session can block or reconfigure another, including concurrent ACP/agent builds.

## Exact scope
- `src/agent/tools/mod.rs::{DENY_REPEATED_READS,READ_TRACKER,track_read,untrack_read_path}`
- `src/agent/tools/read.rs::ReadTool`
- edit/write invalidation call sites
- tool registration in `src/agent/builder.rs`
- setting application in `src/startup.rs`
- `src/tests/tools_mod_tests.rs`

## Required implementation
1. Add two concurrent tool/agent fixtures using the same path but different settings.
2. Introduce a small owned ReadTracker with deny flag and tracked ranges, shared only by tools from one agent/session.
3. Inject it into read/edit/write and scope invalidation to that instance.
4. Delete global state/setters and rewrite tests to avoid global reset/serialization.
5. Verify edits invalidate only the owning session's ranges.

## Constraints / non-goals
Do not create a broad globals refactor. Edit-system, TODO, advisor, and subagent globals are outside scope without a concrete production defect.

## Verification
Concurrent tracker/tool tests; `cargo fmt`; `cargo test`; `cargo install --path . --debug`.

## Duplicate search
All 274 Beads were searched for repeated-read/read-tracker session state. Only a closed display off-by-one issue matched and is unrelated. No duplicate exists.
design: Own a small ReadTracker per built agent/session and share it only among that agent’s read/edit/write tools.
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent agents can use different repeated-read settings and read the same range independently; one session edit invalidates only that session tracker; process-global DENY_REPEATED_READS/READ_TRACKER and setters are gone; focused and full tests pass without serial global cleanup.

Restricted-harness full cargo test reached 1083 pass; remaining failures were environment-denied sockets/Seatbelt plus the known cross-branch subprocess-inventory drift that is resolved during integration. Bead remains in progress until integration and final aggregate gates.

title: [REVIEW] Execute positional interactive input as the first turn
description:
## Defect and impact
`src/startup.rs::Startup::dispatch_interactive` adds `cli.message.join(" ")` to session history, then calls `run_interactive` with `auto_trigger_msg=None`. The user turn is displayed/persisted but never sent to the model, leaving unmatched history and a no-op CLI experience.

## Exact scope
- `src/startup.rs::dispatch_interactive`
- `src/ui/mod.rs::run_interactive`
- `src/ui/app.rs::App::new` auto-trigger path
- startup/UI tests

## Required implementation
1. Add tests for positional interactive input, `-p`, empty interactive startup, and resumed session plus positional input.
2. Pass nonempty positional text through the established auto-trigger/normal turn path.
3. Remove eager history insertion from startup; the turn path must insert the current user message exactly once.
4. Assert model history contains only prior turns, while the current prompt is sent separately and persisted once after dispatch starts.

## Constraints / non-goals
Do not change `-p` semantics, add a startup-only runner, duplicate command classification, or alter empty interactive startup/resume ordering.

## Verification
Focused startup/UI tests; `cargo fmt`; `cargo test`; `cargo install --path . --debug`; tmux smoke launching the installed binary with a positional prompt and confirming a response.

## Duplicate search
All 274 Beads were searched for positional/initial prompt/input behavior. No matching issue exists.
design: Reuse the existing auto-trigger/normal turn lifecycle rather than maintaining a second dispatch implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A nonempty positional argument in interactive mode starts one normal model turn and is persisted exactly once; -p remains headless; empty input remains idle; resumed history precedes the new prompt without duplication.
notes: Source plan INT-02: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-02-application-critical-review.md. Implemented on pushed branch bead-1hq5-2 at 6c4f55b7629d67ae17bdad88c2c259ac695f096d. Positional interactive input now enters the established auto-trigger path, receives only prior session history, records once after runner start, shares pending-send/advisor/chat-history bookkeeping with normal submitted turns, and preserves -p/empty/fallback behavior. Verification: cargo fmt; focused startup/initial-turn/failure rollback tests; 1090 applicable Rust tests passed with only the known unrelated production_subprocess_sites_have_a_trust_classification test filtered on this main-based branch; cargo install --path . --debug; installed headless smoke returned hello; real tmux positional smoke returned POSITIONAL_FINAL_OK exactly once. title: js: wrap fetch host call in tokio::time::timeout to satisfy the blocking-host-call invariant
description:
WHAT: the fetch host function relies on reqwest's own internal timeout configuration instead of an outer tokio::time::timeout. CLAUDE.md invariant 6 requires the outer timeout explicitly, because the QuickJS interrupt handler fires only while JS bytecode is executing -- it cannot interrupt a host call blocked in network I/O. Every other blocking host call follows the required pattern; fetch is the lone deviation.

WHERE:
- src/extras/js/host.rs:~1707-1726 -- the make_fetch closure / FetchExecutor::execute() call site, which blocks the JS thread on network I/O.
- Correct reference patterns to copy: read_file at src/extras/js/host.rs:~1645, write_file at ~1682, spawn at ~1832 (which also races bridge.cancelled() via tokio::select!), and the shared helper block_on_host_call() at ~1380-1395.

WHY IT MATTERS: if reqwest's timeout is misconfigured or bypassed on some path, the JS thread hangs with no way to interrupt it, and the step deadline cannot reclaim it. Defence in depth on the one call that reaches the network.

NOTE: the SSRF policy itself was reviewed and is sound -- IPv4/IPv6 special-use blocking, IPv4-mapped handling, redirect re-validation and DNS-rebinding checks are all present and tested. Do not re-open that; this bead is only about the timeout wrapper.

HOW TO FIX: wrap the execute() call in tokio::time::timeout with a bound derived from FETCH_TOTAL_TIMEOUT (src/extras/js/host.rs:~844) and map elapsed to the existing FetchError::TimedOut, matching how spawn maps its timeout. Prefer routing through block_on_host_call() so the cancellation select! comes along with it.

HOW TO VERIFY: add an integration test that calls fetch() from JS against an address that black-holes the connection, and assert it returns the timeout error well before the step deadline and that the JS thread remains usable for a subsequent eval. Command: cargo test --locked --features js,sandbox fetch
notes: 2026-08-01: This remains the canonical outer fetch-timeout/cancellation issue and blocks Phase 6 effect-service extraction mini-agent-xic0.12; its behavior must survive the parent-broker refactor.
close_reason: Implemented and verified outer fetch timeout/cancellation in commit 59d52ef8

title: memory: /memory read daily silently ignores the YYYY-MM-DD argument and always reads today
description:
WHAT: the slash command hardcodes today's date for the 'daily' source, so a user-supplied date is accepted and then discarded with no error. The equivalent tool API honours it, so the two surfaces disagree.

WHERE:
- src/ui/slash/memory.rs:123 -- \"daily\" => Some(mem.daily_file(&mem.today)), ignoring parts.get(3). Compare the adjacent \"note\" arm at :124-127 which does read parts.get(3).
- Correct reference implementation: src/extras/memory/mod.rs:1199-1210 (memory_read tool) reads args.name, validates with is_safe_daily_name(), and only then calls daily_file().
- Same correct pattern again in Mem::edit at src/extras/memory/mod.rs:480-489.

FAILURE SCENARIO: user runs '/memory read daily 2026-05-15'. They get today's log, presented under today's path in the success line, with no indication the date was dropped -- so a missing historical entry looks like missing data rather than a UI bug.

HOW TO FIX: in the \"daily\" arm take parts.get(3), default to &mem.today when absent, and validate with is_safe_daily_name() BEFORE calling daily_file() -- daily_file() does no sanitisation and an unchecked name traverses out of the memory store (that is exactly why the tool path validates). is_safe_daily_name is at src/extras/memory/mod.rs:73 and will need to be reachable from the slash module. Also update the usage text at src/ui/slash/memory.rs:111-115, which currently documents '[name]' without saying it applies to daily.

HOW TO VERIFY: add a test in the existing #[cfg(all(test, feature = \"memory\", unix))] module in src/ui/slash/memory.rs -- write a dated log, invoke handle_read with that date, assert the dated content is returned; then invoke with '../../etc/passwd' and assert it is rejected rather than read. Command: cargo test --locked --features memory slash::memory

title: sandbox: emulate a Windows backend via restricted tokens + job objects (currently Windows has NO sandbox at all)
description:
WHAT: mini-agent has no sandbox backend on Windows. default_sandbox_backend() (src/cli.rs:7-13) returns 'bwrap' on every non-macOS target including Windows, and bwrap_path()/bwrap_exists() are hardcoded to None/false off Linux (src/sandbox.rs:72-88). So on Windows the policy is always RequiredButUnavailable. Now that sandboxing is default-on, Windows silently runs UNSANDBOXED (with a warning) -- and before the fallback was added it would have refused to start entirely. This matters more on Windows than elsewhere because the bash feature is compiled out there, making JS spawn() the only action primitive.

RESEARCH -- how comparable agents solve it (Aug 2026):
- AppContainer: strongest isolation, but default-deny on the host filesystem. OpenAI Codex evaluated and REJECTED it for agent workloads precisely because agents must read repos, toolchains and caches. Not recommended as the primary backend.
- Windows Sandbox (the VM): unavailable on Home edition, too slow for rapid command loops, requires explicit folder mapping. Rejected.
- Mandatory Integrity Control: only a vertical Low/Medium/High hierarchy; cannot express 'write here but not there'. Insufficient alone.
- RECOMMENDED -- restricted tokens (what Codex CLI actually shipped): create the child with CreateRestrictedToken using the WRITE_RESTRICTED flag, so writes must additionally pass a synthetic SID list; grant explicit ACEs for the workspace and configured writable roots only. Pair with a Job Object (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, process-count and memory caps) for lifetime/resource containment. Elevated mode can add dedicated local sandbox accounts plus Windows Firewall DENY rules for network isolation; unelevated mode derives a restricted token from the current user and works without admin.
- Known gaps to document, not solve: unelevated mode cannot stop writes to directories that already grant the Everyone SID; no registry isolation; network denial needs firewall rules and therefore elevation.
- Prior art to evaluate rather than write from scratch: the codex-windows-sandbox Rust crate (run_windows_sandbox_capture + helper binary, two-tier elevated/unelevated) and the nanosandbox crate (job objects + restricted tokens + AppContainer).

WHERE: add a 'restricted-token' (or 'winsandbox') backend arm in src/sandbox.rs next to the bwrap and seatbelt arms -- specifically a *_exists()/*_path() pair following src/sandbox.rs:67-111, a branch in wrap_command() (src/sandbox.rs:352-406) and a capability-matrix arm in capabilities() (src/sandbox.rs:279-341). Make default_sandbox_backend() in src/cli.rs:7 return it on target_os=windows instead of the current bwrap fallthrough.

ACCEPTANCE: on Windows, a default run reports a real backend and RequiredAndAvailable rather than warning about a missing bwrap; a child process cannot write outside the workspace and configured writable roots; killing the parent kills the job.

HOW TO VERIFY: extend the platform-paths CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml, which already has a windows-latest row) with a Windows sandbox-policy test mirroring the existing linux_sandbox_policy job. Locally on Windows: cargo test --locked sandbox:: and a test asserting a spawned child writing to a path outside the workspace fails with access-denied while a workspace write succeeds. Also assert capabilities() no longer claims network isolation unless firewall rules were actually installed.
notes:
2026-08-01: Keep separate from Phase 6 LPAC worker Beads mini-agent-xic0.26/.27. LPAC confines only a broker-only zero-authority QuickJS worker; this issue remains authoritative for workspace-capable general Windows subprocesses and gates Windows JS spawn, not Windows pure/effect-brokered JS availability.
2026-08-03 continuation: Implemented a unique per-launch WRITE_RESTRICTED SID, handle-bound ACL grants/cleanup, executable identity+digest lock, private desktop, creation-time bounded/UI-restricted Job, capped request feeder, parent-death ownership, exact hosted runtime probe, and z2mh default-on docs. Local evidence: cargo fmt/diff clean; source contract 1/1; subprocess inventory 27/27; cfg-Windows metadata harness passed; full restricted-host suite 1252 passed with 21 socket/Seatbelt environment denials and one timing test that passed in isolation. Required debug install is blocked by the Codex account usage limit; native hosted Windows execution is blocked by GitHub Actions billing. title: Flaky todo tests race on the process-global TODO_LIST
description:
tests::todo_tests::call_overwrites_previous_list fails intermittently (roughly 1 run in 3) under the parallel test harness. The todo tests mutate a shared process-global TODO_LIST static and call reset_todo_list() at test start, so two todo tests running concurrently clobber each other's state.

Pre-existing and unrelated to Phase 2/3 work; surfaced while verifying the b16 CI feature matrix. Matters more now because the matrix runs 8 feature rows across 2 platforms, so a 1-in-3 flake will fail some job on most CI runs.

Fix by serializing the todo tests against a shared mutex, or by making the tool take an injectable list handle instead of touching a global.
acceptance_criteria: tests::todo_tests pass on 20 consecutive full-suite runs with no serialization flag; the todo tool's list state is either injected or guarded so concurrent tests cannot interfere.
close_reason: Closed

title: [AUDIT] Remove process-global CWD races and blocking subprocesses from worktree operations
description:
## Problem
Git worktree merge/cleanup paths change process-global current directory and run blocking subprocesses from async workflows. Concurrent agent/tool operations using relative paths can execute in the wrong repository, while a slow Git command blocks an async runtime worker.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run two concurrent worktree operations in different repositories while another relative-path operation reads/writes the original workspace. Introduce a slow Git command/hook. Observe global CWD interference and async blocking risk.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/extras/git_worktree/mod.rs:1-30` — module comments acknowledge global CWD/blocking limitations.
- `src/extras/git_worktree/mod.rs:225-325` — merge/cleanup paths use process-global directory changes and synchronous commands.
- Audit every `set_current_dir`/relative Git invocation in this feature.

## Implementation scope
- Never mutate process-global CWD for worktree operations.
- Use `git -C <path>` or per-command `current_dir` and absolute/canonical paths.
- Use async subprocess execution from async contexts, with finite timeout/cancellation and bounded output.
- Preserve caller CWD on every success/error/panic path.
- Serialize only repository operations that truly conflict; allow independent repositories concurrently.

## Suggested approach
Centralize Git command construction with explicit repo/worktree path and bounded execution. Remove any CWD guard whose correctness still depends on global mutable state.

## Tests
Concurrent operations in two repositories; concurrent relative read in original workspace; command failure; timeout/cancel; hook delay; cleanup; paths with spaces/non-UTF8 where supported; assert `std::env::current_dir()` never changes.

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features git-worktree worktree_concurrent_cwd_isolation
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features git-worktree
cargo test --locked
```
Run relevant tests under a multi-thread Tokio runtime and, where feasible, a race-stressing repeat.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No production worktree path calls `set_current_dir`.
- [ ] Every Git command has explicit repository/worktree context.
- [ ] Async paths do not run blocking child waits and have finite cleanup.
- [ ] Concurrent regression tests prove relative operations stay in their intended workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Worktree merge/cleanup commands use explicit repository/path context without changing process-global CWD, execute without blocking async workers, have finite cancellation/timeouts, and pass concurrent relative-path regression tests.

title: [AUDIT] Bound loop validation subprocess time and captured output
description:
## Problem
Loop validation runs a configured subprocess with `.output()` and no timeout or output bound. A hanging validator or stdout/stderr flood can stall the agent indefinitely or exhaust memory in both headless and interactive modes.

## Steps to Reproduce
Configure loop validation as an infinite process, then as a command that floods stdout/stderr. Trigger validation. Observe no finite deadline and unbounded in-memory capture.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/extras/loop/headless.rs:102-128` — validation command uses unbounded `.output()`.
- `src/ui/event_handler.rs:427-450` — interactive path duplicates the same unbounded behavior.
- `src/sandbox.rs` / bounded process helpers from Bash/JS/hook work should be reused where suitable.

## Implementation scope
- Apply finite configurable/default deadline, stdout/stderr/combined byte caps, concurrent drain, and cancellation.
- Kill and reap the complete process group/tree on timeout, cancel, cap breach, or parent shutdown.
- Run through the selected sandbox/policy consistently with other process tools.
- Return structured status, truncation/timeout reason, and bounded diagnostic to loop logic.
- Unify headless/interactive execution semantics.

## Suggested approach
Extract/reuse one bounded process runner rather than maintain two `.output()` call sites. Pass explicit command/args/cwd/env policy without shell interpolation beyond the existing documented command contract.

## Tests
Success/nonzero exit; hang; ignored TERM; forked descendant; stdout-only/stderr-only/mixed flood; invalid UTF-8; cancellation; unavailable sandbox; headless/interactive parity; following validation succeeds after failure.

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features loop loop_validation_process_limits
cargo test --locked --no-default-features --features loop
cargo test --locked
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Validator runtime and memory use are finite.
- [ ] Output streams are drained concurrently with accurate bound diagnostics.
- [ ] Timeout/cancel/failure leaves no child or descendant.
- [ ] Headless and interactive paths use one tested policy.
acceptance_criteria: Loop validation commands have finite runtime and bounded concurrent output, kill/reap complete process trees on timeout/cancel/cap failure, and share identical headless/interactive semantics with deterministic tests.

title: [AUDIT] Detect and import exported JSONL sessions through the slash command
description:
## Problem
JSONL export has parser-level support, but the `/import` slash command treats any file beginning with `{` as one native Session JSON document. JSONL metadata begins with `{`, so native parsing fails and the command exits without trying JSONL. Exported sessions therefore cannot round-trip through the advertised UI.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Export a session in JSONL format.
2. Run `/import <exported-file>`.
3. Observe the command selects native JSON based on the first character and fails instead of invoking JSONL parsing.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/ui/slash/session.rs:79-109` — format detection selects native JSON solely from leading `{`.
- JSONL parser tests exist below the slash-command boundary and do not cover actual dispatch.
- `src/extras/export.rs` owns emitted JSONL format/metadata.

## Implementation scope
- Detect native Session JSON versus repository JSONL robustly without consuming/losing input.
- Produce clear errors for malformed/ambiguous files and enforce existing size/message bounds.
- Preserve message order, roles/content, supported metadata, and safe path/persistence behavior.
- Do not fall back from arbitrary malformed native JSON to permissive line parsing in a way that hides corruption.

## Suggested approach
Parse or inspect a bounded first JSON value/schema rather than one character. Dispatch based on validated format markers/shape, then require the selected parser to consume the expected document/lines.

## Tests
End-to-end session → JSONL export → `/import` → saved/reloaded session equality; native JSON import; pretty JSON; BOM/whitespace; malformed first/middle line; oversized input; ambiguous object; unsupported schema version.

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked --features export session_jsonl_slash_import_round_trip
cargo test --locked --features export
cargo test --locked
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] JSONL exports round-trip through the slash command.
- [ ] Native JSON still imports correctly.
- [ ] Detection is schema/shape based, bounded, and deterministic.
- [ ] Malformed/ambiguous data returns a precise error without partial session mutation.
acceptance_criteria: A session exported as JSONL can be imported through the user-facing import slash command with exact validated message order/metadata, while malformed/native JSON inputs retain clear deterministic handling.

title: [AUDIT] Persist clear, undo, and redo session mutations immediately
description:
## Problem
`/clear`, `/undo`, and `/redo` mutate only in-memory session state. If the process exits or crashes before another save, reopening restores old content and contradicts the command the user just completed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a persisted session with several turns.
2. Execute `/clear`, `/undo`, or `/redo`.
3. Exit immediately without another model turn.
4. Reopen the session and observe pre-command history is restored.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/ui/slash/session.rs:257-312` — history/undo mutations have no immediate persistence.
- Session save APIs and error reporting should define whether command success is transactional.

## Implementation scope
- Persist each successful mutation before reporting command completion.
- Keep in-memory and disk state consistent if persistence fails: roll back mutation or surface a failed command with explicit recoverable state.
- Preserve undo/redo stack semantics and private atomic writes.
- Avoid unrelated autosave redesign.

## Suggested approach
Use a shared mutation-and-save helper that snapshots prior state, applies one command, saves, and restores on save failure. Keep each command's behavioral semantics intact.

## Tests
Clear/undo/redo followed by immediate reload; empty/no-op cases; repeated undo/redo; save failure; process exit simulation. Assert live history, saved history, and stacks match.

## Verification
```bash

```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Immediate reload reflects clear/undo/redo exactly.

- [ ] Undo/redo stacks remain coherent across restart.

title: [AUDIT] Roll back failed user turns before persisting session state
description:
## Problem
On a failed turn the event handler saves the session before the app rolls the turn back in memory. The disk snapshot retains a user prompt and possibly partial state that the live UI removed. Reopening the session resurrects this ghost turn.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a persisted interactive session.
2. Submit a prompt and force provider/tool failure.
3. Let the UI report/roll back the failed turn.
4. Restart and reopen the session; observe the failed prompt remains on disk.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/ui/event_handler.rs:276-289` — error path saves session first.
- `src/ui/app.rs:883-892` — rollback happens afterward.
- Session storage helpers define the atomic/private write boundary.

## Implementation scope
- Establish one transaction/order for failed-turn mutation and persistence.
- Remove the failed user turn and any partial assistant/tool messages before the persisted snapshot is taken.
- Apply to provider error, tool error where turn rollback applies, cancellation, stream failure, and persistence failure semantics.
- Preserve successful-turn save behavior and undo/redo state consistency.

## Suggested approach
Move rollback into the state transition that handles terminal failure, then persist the resulting authoritative state once. Avoid a second compensating save if a single ordered transition is possible.

## Tests
Provider failure before output, partial streamed output then error, cancellation, tool failure, save failure, and successful turn. After each, reload from disk and compare exact history/undo state with live state.

## Verification

- [ ] Reload cannot resurrect a removed prompt or partial response/tool interaction.
- [ ] Rollback occurs before the authoritative save.
- [ ] Successful turns and persistence errors have deterministic tested behavior.

title: [AUDIT] Restrict PlanWrite exceptions to authorized workspace-contained plan files
description:
## Problem
The permission checker grants special PlanWrite behavior based only on the final filename. Paths such as `/tmp/PLAN.md` or `$HOME/PLAN-private.md` can receive the exception even though they are outside the workspace/authorized plan root.

## Steps to Reproduce
Request a PlanWrite to an external path whose basename matches the plan naming rule. Observe the path classification ignores containment and can bypass normal external-write authorization.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/permission/checker.rs:284-309` — PlanWrite permission behavior.
- `src/permission/checker.rs:751-755` — `is_plan_file` checks only the final filename.
- Reuse hardened path authorization/atomic write semantics from existing filesystem work.

## Implementation scope
- Require both an allowed plan filename and canonical component containment in the configured workspace/plan root.
- Handle nonexistent targets by validating the nearest existing parent and remaining components.
- Reject final/parent symlink escapes and path replacement races at the write operation.
- Keep ordinary external-write prompting behavior available when the path is not eligible; do not silently reinterpret it as PlanWrite.

## Suggested approach
Make plan classification accept an authorized root/path context and return a typed decision. Do not use raw prefix checks or canonicalize only once far before mutation.

## Tests
Workspace plan root, descendant, sibling-prefix, `/tmp/PLAN.md`, home `PLAN-private.md`, `..`, symlinked parent/final target, nonexistent in-root file, and swap race. Assert denied cases do not modify external sentinels.

## Verification

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Eligible paths are component-contained under the authorized root.
- [ ] Symlink/nonexistent/race cases use hardened path semantics.
- [ ] External lookalikes follow normal permission policy and produce no unauthorized write.

title: [AUDIT] Bound continuation retries after stream EOF without a terminal event
description:
## Problem
A model stream can end cleanly without a terminal completion/error event. The runner accepts EOF, then requests continuation without charging the turn/retry budget. Repeated empty or malformed streams can loop indefinitely and repeatedly call the provider.

## Steps to Reproduce
Use a fake provider whose stream returns EOF immediately (or emits only nonterminal fragments) on every request. Run the agent with a small `max_turns`; observe continuation can repeat beyond that bound.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/agent/runner.rs:434-477` — EOF is accepted without requiring a terminal event.
- `src/agent/runner.rs:645-682` — no-completion continuation retains the full turn budget.
- Compare prior continuation budget hardening so the new accounting composes rather than duplicates.

## Implementation scope
- Define terminal-event expectation and classify clean EOF without terminal completion as a retryable protocol failure or bounded continuation.
- Charge a shared finite budget for each additional provider stream attempt.
- Return a typed/user-visible error when exhausted; include no secrets/raw provider payload.
- Preserve valid tool-driven continuations and normal completed streams.

## Suggested approach
Track stream-attempt/continuation count in the same outer budget state as turns and token limits. Require progress or a terminal event before resetting any retry allowance.

## Tests
Immediate EOF repeated; partial text then EOF; tool call/result then EOF; malformed item then EOF; terminal completion; transient first EOF then successful retry; exact provider call count at exhaustion in interactive/headless paths.

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked runner_eof_without_terminal_event
cargo test --locked runner_continuation_budget
cargo test --locked
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every nonterminal EOF attempt consumes a finite documented budget.
- [ ] Exhaustion stops provider calls with a stable diagnostic.
- [ ] A transient EOF can recover within budget.
- [ ] Normal completion/tool continuation behavior is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated clean EOF or malformed nonterminal streams consume a finite retry/turn budget and end with a typed diagnostic; normal terminal completion and legitimate continuation behavior remain unchanged.

title: [AUDIT] Correlate parallel tool results by call ID instead of one mutable name slot
description:
## Problem
The runner tracks only one mutable `last_tool_name`. If a stream emits two tool calls before their results, the first result can be attributed to the second call and the next result is treated as unknown/dropped. This corrupts events/history and can mislead continuation logic.

## Steps to Reproduce
Feed the runner a stream containing tool call A, tool call B, result A, result B (and an out-of-order B/A variant). Observe attribution uses a single slot rather than a per-call correlation.

## Evidence / affected code
- `src/agent/runner.rs:54-93` — stream item/event correlation types and helpers.
- `src/agent/runner.rs:495-555` — mutable tool-name tracking and result handling.
- Closed `mini-agent-jlu` only fixed a result with no preceding call; it did not support multiple outstanding calls.

## Implementation scope
- Track outstanding calls by protocol call ID, preserving name and any metadata needed for events/history.
- Resolve each result exactly once, independent of arrival order when the provider supports it.
- Define deterministic behavior for missing ID, unknown ID, duplicate result, and stream termination with pending calls.
- Apply identical behavior to interactive/headless runner paths without duplicated state machines.

## Suggested approach
Maintain a bounded map keyed by call ID and make event conversion consume the matching entry. If a provider type lacks result IDs, explicitly serialize that provider or preserve a bounded FIFO only where the protocol guarantees order; do not silently pretend one slot supports parallel calls.

## Tests
Two and three outstanding calls; in-order/out-of-order results; duplicate/unknown result; same tool name with distinct IDs; pending call at EOF; interactive/headless parity.

## Verification
```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked runner_parallel_tool_result_correlation
cargo test --locked runner_unknown_tool_result
cargo test --locked
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ToolResult event/history name and call identity match the originating call.
- [ ] Parallel and out-of-order sequences do not overwrite pending metadata.
- [ ] Unknown/duplicate/missing-ID cases are explicit and do not consume another call.
- [ ] Both runner paths use the tested behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Every tool result is attributed to its exact call ID/name under multiple outstanding and out-of-order calls; unknown/duplicate results are handled deterministically without dropping a valid pending call.

title: MISSING-FEATURE: No token budget enforcement across continuation iterations
description:
## What is wrong
While max_tokens is passed to the model and token usage is tracked via events (usage.input_tokens, output_tokens), there is no enforcement of context window limits or token budgets across continuations. Each continuation iteration can potentially use the full context window again, and there's no tracking or enforcement of cumulative token usage. The model could theoretically use 2x, 3x, or up to 11x the context window across the outer loop iterations.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Context window is 200k tokens. User runs agent with max_tokens=180k. First continuation uses 180k, second uses another 180k from the same 200k window. Model overwrites earlier conversation context. Or, context window overflow silently truncates early messages.

## Fix
Track cumulative input/output tokens across continuations. Before calling continue_prompt_injector, check if adding the current continuation would exceed the context window. If so, trigger compaction or abort gracefully.

## Verification
Integration test: set context_window to 100k, trigger multiple continuations, verify cumulative token tracking, verify that an error or compaction is triggered if window is exceeded.

## Location
/Users/ahrens/projects/mini-agent/src/agent/runner.rs:398
close_reason: Implemented: enforce cumulative input/output token budget across continuation streams and add regression coverage

title: BUG: Tool name not tracked correctly when tool result arrives for unknown tool
description:
## What is wrong
When a ToolResult is received, the tool name is retrieved via last_tool_name.take().unwrap_or_default() at line 437. If a tool result arrives without a corresponding tool call (e.g., out-of-order stream items or first item is a result), last_tool_name is None and unwrap_or_default() produces an empty string. The event at line 454 sends a ToolResult with an empty name, and the history at line 458 includes a tool result with undefined tool association. This produces confusing logs and history entries.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Stream items arrive out of order: ToolResult before ToolCall. Event shows: ToolResult { name: '', output: '...' }. History shows unattributed tool result. Model doesn't know which tool produced the result.

## Fix
Validate that last_tool_name is Some before processing a ToolResult. If None, either: (1) log an error and skip the result, or (2) extract the tool name from the ToolResult structure itself if available.

## Verification
Unit test: send a ToolResult stream item without a preceding ToolCall, verify that either an error is logged or the result is skipped, not silently attributed to an empty name.

title: BUG: Tool result extraction silently produces empty output for non-text content
description:
## What is wrong
When a ToolResult is received (line 432-459), the output is extracted by iterating over tool_result.content and only including ToolResultContent::Text blocks (line 440). If a tool result contains only non-text content (e.g., structured data, images, or other media types), the output string remains empty. The empty output is then sent as an AgentEvent::ToolResult at line 453 and added to tool_interactions at line 458 without any warning or indication that the result was empty. The model receives a tool result with no visible output, which may confuse it or cause it to retry the same tool.

## Exploit / failure scenario
A tool that returns a structured JSON result (not wrapped in text) produces an empty output event. The model sees '[ToolResult]: read_file' with no content, doesn't know what the file contains, and may either retry the read or produce an incorrect response based on missing information.

## Fix
When tool_result.content contains no text blocks, either: (1) log a warning indicating the result was empty and send it with a note, or (2) format non-text content as a string representation (e.g., 'json: {structured_data}'), ensuring the model always receives useful feedback.

## Verification
Unit test: create a ToolResult with only non-text content, pass through the extraction logic, verify output is not empty or that a warning is logged.

## Location
