title: js: spawn's permission subject is a lossy space-join of argv, so approvals do not faithfully represent what runs
description:
WHAT: js spawn() builds the string shown to the permission layer by joining the command and its arguments with single spaces. That mapping is not injective: argv [\"git\", \"commit\", \"-m\", \"fix bug\"] and argv [\"git\", \"commit\", \"-m\", \"fix\", \"bug\"] produce an identical subject string, and an argument containing spaces or shell metacharacters renders as though it were multiple arguments. The permission subject is then evaluated by the same layer that handles BashTool, whose subjects really are shell strings.

WHERE: src/extras/js/host.rs:1809-1815 -- permission_command is built with std::iter::once(cmd).chain(args).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\" \") and passed to permission_bridge.check(\"bash\", &permission_command).

SCOPE / WHAT THIS IS NOT: this is an approval-fidelity and audit-fidelity defect, NOT a proven sandbox escape. The arguments are passed to exec directly (src/extras/js/host.rs:1816-1824 uses sandbox.wrap_command with exec \"/bin/zsh\" \"\"), so embedded metacharacters are NOT interpreted by a shell -- do not file this as command injection. The risk is that a human or a rule approves a string that does not correspond one-to-one with the argv actually executed, in either direction.

FAILURE SCENARIO: a stored allow-rule written against the BashTool's shell-string grammar matches a joined spawn subject whose real argv differs, or a reviewer approves what looks like two flags but is a single argument containing a space.

HOW TO FIX: give the permission layer the structured argv rather than a pre-joined string, or shell-quote each element when composing the subject so the rendering round-trips. If the check signature must stay string-based, quote arguments containing whitespace or metacharacters so the subject is unambiguous, and keep BashTool's own subject construction unchanged.

HOW TO VERIFY: add a test asserting that spawn(\"echo\", [\"a b\"]) and spawn(\"echo\", [\"a\", \"b\"]) produce DIFFERENT permission subjects, and that an allow-rule authored for one does not authorise the other. Command: cargo test --locked --features js spawn
notes: 2026-08-01: Acceptance is absorbed by Phase 6 typed effect-service Bead mini-agent-xic0.12. Do not implement a competing permission-subject format; close this issue together when mini-agent-xic0.12's distinct-argv approval tests pass.
close_reason: Absorbed by A12: versioned canonical JSON spawn subject preserves argv boundaries; focused collision/allow isolation tests pass.

title: [HARDENING] Bound timed-out system DNS resolver work for JS fetch
description: The bounded JS fetch resolver times out its Tokio lookup future, but the operating-system getaddrinfo work may continue after cancellation. Repeated adversarial timeouts could temporarily accumulate resolver worker work even though no destination I/O occurs before validation. Evaluate a resolver backend with cancellable bounded workers or enforce an explicit global concurrency/backpressure budget around resolution without weakening SSRF checks.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated timed-out DNS resolutions have a deterministic bound on live resolver work and recovery; cancellation never permits destination I/O; SSRF/rebinding tests and js,sandbox remain green.
notes: Implemented on origin/bead-vbnv at 22bac7a. Added a process-wide four-slot DNS budget whose owned permit moves into the actual non-abortable ToSocketAddrs blocking closure, so timeout, cancellation, caller drop, and Tokio runtime shutdown cannot release capacity before OS resolution finishes. Late results are discarded before permission/destination I/O; overload shares the three-second deadline and recovers after underlying completion. Evidence: isolated js+sandbox 1034/1034; default 1272/1272; DNS concurrency/cancellation/timeout/runtime-shutdown/replacement tests; SSRF/fetch regressions; fmt/diff clean; debug install; installed headless hello; independent adversarial-security re-review CLEAN. Bead intentionally remains in progress until integration/merge.
close_reason: Implementation is already integrated on all-beads-integration with its focused regression coverage and recorded verification.

title: INCOMPLETE: Unknown stream item types silently ignored without logging
description:
## What is wrong
The stream processing loop at lines 399-544 has a catch-all `_ => {}` pattern at line 542 that silently ignores unknown MultiTurnStreamItem variants. If rig introduces a new stream item type that requires special handling (e.g., new content type, error condition, or state change), it will be missed entirely. No log message or event is generated, making debugging difficult.

## Exploit / failure scenario
rig library adds MultiTurnStreamItem::CacheStatus indicating model is accessing prompt cache. The catch-all at line 542 silently drops this item. Caller doesn't know cache was used, can't adjust strategy or logging. Cache performance metrics are invisible.

## Fix
Replace the catch-all with explicit handling for each known variant, and add a catch-all that logs a warning: `_ => { tracing::warn!("unknown stream item variant: {:?}", item); }`

## Verification
Add test: construct a mock unknown stream item, pass through loop, verify a warning is logged to tracing with the unknown item information.

## Location
/Users/ahrens/projects/mini-agent/src/agent/runner.rs:542
close_reason: Implemented: explicitly handle known stream variants and warn with details for unknown items, with tracing capture coverage

title: PERF: Chat history file grows unbounded without pruning or size limit
description:
## What is wrong
The append_entry function (lines 18-40) loads all existing chat history from disk, appends one new entry, and saves. There is no pruning, rotation, or size limit. The file grows indefinitely with every chat entry. Over time, the chat_history.json file could grow to megabytes or larger, and every subsequent write loads the entire history into memory before appending and saving.

## Exploit / failure scenario
User runs 1000 chat turns over a month. chat_history.json grows to 10MB+. Each new chat entry requires loading and re-saving the entire 10MB file. Appending becomes slow and memory-intensive. If file is corrupted (as handled at line 25-29), a large backup file is created but original data is lost.

## Fix
Implement rotation: keep only the most recent N entries (e.g., last 10000), or implement a size-based rotation (e.g., rotate when file exceeds 5MB). Or, change to an append-only log format where each write appends a line without loading the full history.

## Verification
Create a test that appends 1000 entries and measures file size and append time. Verify file size remains bounded or grows sub-linearly.

## Location
/Users/ahrens/projects/mini-agent/src/session/chat_history.rs:18
close_reason: Implemented: bounded chat history to the newest 10,000 entries with a 1,000-append regression test for pruning and file size

title: INCOMPLETE: Silent channel send failure in JS engine thread
description:
## What is wrong
When the JS engine finishes a step, it sends the reply via req.reply.send() with error silently ignored (let _ = ...). If the reply channel's receiver (reply_rx in tool.rs) is dropped before the send (e.g., the tool task is cancelled), the send fails silently. While this is acceptable if the caller doesn't care, it masks potential issues where the caller is still waiting on reply_rx (though tool.rs does handle channel-closed errors).

## Exploit / failure scenario
JS tool call starts → reply_rx.await is waiting → caller task is cancelled/aborted → reply_rx is dropped → JS thread finishes and tries to send → send fails silently → no error logged or observed.

## Fix
Log the send error even if ignored: `if let Err(e) = req.reply.send(...) { tracing::debug!("JS engine reply channel closed: {}", e); }`. This helps with debugging and makes the failure visible in logs.

## Verification
Cancel a JS tool call mid-flight and check logs to see if the send error is logged.

## Location
src/extras/js/engine.rs:11
close_reason: Implemented: log closed JS engine reply channels on cancelled and completed requests

title: Memoize overlay prompt rows; stop cloning prompt strings into every bottom snapshot
description:
- Priority: P4
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: While a permission or chain prompt is open the loop refreshes on every spinner tick (10/s) and after every event, and each refresh word-wraps the prompt text twice (`sync_input_height` -> `input_visible_height` -> `overlay_prompt_rows`, then `draw_bottom_in_frame` -> `overlay_prompt_rows` again), allocating a `Vec<String>` each time, and `bottom_snapshot` clones the `tool`/`options`/`question` `CompactString`s just to compare them — even when the plan is `Skip`. For a multi-KB command preview that is ~20 wraps/s and 10 string copies/s for an unchanged screen.
- WHERE: src/ui/renderer.rs:1714-1737 `overlay_prompt_rows` -> `permission_prompt_rows` (518) / `prompt_block_rows` (565); callers 1628-1631 (`input_visible_height`) and 2763 (`draw_bottom_in_frame`); 2605-2644 `bottom_snapshot` with `tool: pp.tool.clone(), options: pp.options.clone()` (2616-2617); loop refresh at src/ui/app.rs:2645-2647 `if self.permission_prompt.is_some() || self.question_prompt.is_some() { self.refresh()?; }`.
- HOW: Add `prompt_generation: u64` to `Renderer`, bumped wherever `permission_prompt`/`chain_prompt`/`chain_but_mode`/`expanded` change (they are `pub` fields; wrap the writes in setters or bump in `bottom_snapshot` when the pointer/len differ). Cache `overlay_prompt_rows` in `RefCell<Option<(u64 /*gen*/, u16, u16, Arc<Vec<String>>)>>` keyed by `(prompt_generation, cols, rows)`; make `PromptSnapshot::Permission/Chain` carry the generation instead of the strings.
- VERIFY: `cargo test --bin mini-agent -- permission_prompt control_c_and_d_abort_permission_prompt picker_overlays_stay_in_band --test-threads=1`; `FrameStats.bottom_full_paints` for a run with an open prompt and 10 spinner ticks must stay at 1 as today.

title: Do not open two empty render frames on every event-loop iteration
description:
- Priority: P4
- Dimension: simplification
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: `run_inner` opens a frame for MCP notices even when `take_notices()` is empty and `drain_tui_diagnostics` opens one even when there is no receiver or nothing queued. Each open/close does an atomic epoch load, `frame.clear()` + `extend_from_slice(SYNC_BEGIN)`, a `mem::take` and a length check — twice per iteration, and iterations run per token during streaming (hundreds/s). Cheap individually, pure waste in aggregate and noise around the paint counters.
- WHERE: src/ui/app.rs:2440-2450: `let notices = manager.take_notices(); self.renderer.frame(|renderer| { for notice in &notices { renderer.write_line(&sanitize_output(notice), C_ERROR)?; } Ok(()) })?;`; src/ui/app.rs:2684-2709 `drain_tui_diagnostics`: `let receiver = self.tui_log_rx.as_mut(); self.renderer.frame(|renderer| { if let Some(receiver) = receiver { for _ in 0..16 { let Ok(message) = receiver.try_recv() else { break }; ... } } let dropped = crate::logging::take_dropped_tui_diagnostics(); ... })`; frame cost at src/ui/renderer.rs:1117-1165.
- HOW: `if !notices.is_empty() { self.renderer.frame(...) }`; in `drain_tui_diagnostics` return early when `self.tui_log_rx.as_ref().is_none_or(|rx| rx.is_empty())` and only then open the frame (dropped-record warnings can only exist when the channel was full, i.e. non-empty).
- VERIFY: `cargo test --bin mini-agent -- tui_diagnostics diagnostic notice --test-threads=1`; `FrameStats.writes/flushes` for an idle loop must stay 0 (empty frames already wrote nothing, so no byte-level change is expected).
close_reason: Implemented on main in the 2026-10-20 vb5vw wave (perf/<lane> merge), with the bead's pinning tests.

title: Gate the plan-event future box like the MCP one (4 large heap futures per keystroke)
description:
- Priority: P4
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: Each keystroke allocates four "measured large" boxed futures: the batch handler, `handle_plan_event` (which returns `false` on its first line whenever no plan is pending), `handle_standard_user_event` and `handle_key_event_with`. title: Write each JS protocol frame with one syscall (length-prefixed buffer)

title: Avoid two PathBuf allocations per directory entry in the bound walker
description:

- WHAT: `BoundWalker::next` builds `relative_path` and `approved_path` (two heap PathBufs) for every entry before the skip/ignore/hidden/file filters run, so a 100k-entry walk (the entry budget) performs 200k allocations even when most entries are filtered out by name. - WHERE: src/agent/tools/find_files.rs:1203-1204 in `impl Iterator for BoundWalker`: `let relative_path = frame.relative_path.join(&name); let approved_path = self.approved_root.join(&relative_path);`.

Note the borrow of `frame` (`self.stack.last_mut()`) — take the scratch buffers out with `std::mem::take` for the duration of the entry.
- VERIFY: find_files/grep/list_dir tests in src/agent/tools/find_files.rs (`cargo test --bin mini-agent -- find_files --test-threads=1`), grep tests above, `grep_skips_directories_matching_grep_deny_rules`. title: Keep HistoryCountCache from retaining a second copy of the child's history
description:
- Priority: P4
- Dimension: memory
- Confidence: medium
- WHAT: The per-run incremental estimate cache stores a full `Message` clone for every history message it has measured, so each in-flight child run holds a duplicate of its own chat history (tool results included) for the run's lifetime — +H bytes per child, e.g. +1 MiB per child with a 1 MiB history, x N parallel children.
- WHERE: src/agent/runner.rs:1906 `struct HistoryCountCache(std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<(Message, u64, u64)>>>);`; src/agent/runner.rs:1958-1969 in `incremental_request_estimate`: `Some((cached, ..)) if cached == message => keep = index + 1` ... `measured.push((message.clone(), message_wide, message_narrow));`.
- HOW: Store a fingerprint instead of the message: `(u64 hash, u64 wide, u64 narrow)` where the hash is computed by a `Hasher`-based walk of the `Message` (role discriminant, per content item: variant tag, text bytes, tool call id/name + canonical args via a hasher-generic version of the existing `hash_canonical_json` at runner.rs:197-235, image/audio data length only). Equality check becomes hash comparison; the stated invariant (an edited/reordered prefix is re-measured) is preserved up to 64-bit collision. Document the trade (one hashing pass over the prefix per call, ~1 ms/MiB, instead of memcmp) and keep `serializations` counting unchanged.
- VERIFY: src/extras/subagents/builder.rs `prepared_request_is_serialized_once_for_context_guard_and_usage_ledger` (2352) and `incremental_prepared_estimate_equals_full_serialization_across_turns` (2413) pin estimate equality and serialization counts. Add a test that mutates a message in the middle of the history between calls and asserts the estimate still equals the full serialization (prefix invalidation), and a size assertion that the scratchpad cache holds no `Message` (e.g. `size_of::<CacheEntry>() <= 24`).

title: Do not count chars of self-bounded tool results in ToolResultSpillHook
description:
- Priority: P4
- Dimension: cpu
- Confidence: high
- WHAT: The spill hook decodes the whole result (`chars().count()`) before checking whether the tool is self-bounded or the result is small, so every `read`/`shell`/`grep`/`find_files` result (up to 1 MiB) is fully UTF-8 walked and the count thrown away. ~0.3 ms per large result, on every tool call of the most common tools.
- WHERE: src/agent/runner.rs:106-110 in `impl AgentHook for ToolResultSpillHook::on_event`: `let output_chars = result.chars().count(); if crate::session::tool_result_is_self_bounded(tool_name) || output_chars <= crate::session::TOOL_RESULT_SAVE_THRESHOLD { return Flow::cont(); }`.
- HOW: Check `tool_result_is_self_bounded(tool_name)` first, then `if result.len() <= TOOL_RESULT_SAVE_THRESHOLD { return Flow::cont(); }` (bytes >= chars, so a byte length under the threshold implies the char count is too), and only then compute `output_chars`.
- VERIFY: src/agent/runner.rs `oversized_tool_result_is_spilled_before_the_next_model_call` (6722), `self_bounded_read_keeps_all_400_lines_in_live_and_replayed_history` (6833), `large_third_failure_preserves_sanitized_error_notice_and_spill_correlation` (7063). No new test needed beyond a unit test that a 12_000-byte multi-byte result is still measured in chars (e.g. 6_000 two-byte chars must not spill).
